on behalf of the enf group. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, this is a very unpleasant dilemma to deal with. on the one hand, the european commission has a good idea: to relax the emission requirements for light vehicles. volkswagen or not, we must admit that the constraints on the european automobile industry are enormous, and in a context of international competition, unlimited opening of trade borders, industrial collapse and exploding unemployment, let us admit that the commission is defending our interests for once. on the other hand, the commission is taking its preferred route: bypassing parliament. it is true that our institutions must be based on trust, transparency and accountability, and this parliament should have been able to take on its bureaucratic excesses. but the time is critical, the economic war has indeed begun, we must act, which is why we will oppose this objection.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the decision taken last october is outrageous. in the process, heads of state and the commission have granted pollution permits to car manufacturers. these will now be able to exceed the pollution standards by 110% until 2020 and by 50% thereafter. it is scandalous and now the services of parliament are saying that it is illegal. in other words, it is a total violation not only of european legislation but also of the european parliament, which is the co-legislator of pollution standards to protect the health of citizens and serve the general interest. we're not in the service of the automobile lobby! instead of being complicit in the lies of the car industry, it is time for parliament, the member states and the commission to take the side of consumers, citizens and the planet. this outrageous decision must be rejected as early as next month. i would urge the member states and the commission to do the same and to look at the establishment of genuine independent type-approval controls and real tests under real conditions as soon as possible.
madam president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioner, the scandal which rocked the german car industry last september has revealed a worrying imbalance between emission standards and industrial reality. i share the concern of the drafters of this motion for a resolution about the public health costs of pollution and the inadequacy of the standards in force. the text, however, offers a further twist to an industry already in a state of disarray, by postulating the dogma that the race to growth without pollution is within reach, if the right advice from political ecology is followed. a dogma that has been around for a while let us reiterate that this scandal has benefited american industry and has been detrimental to european industry. let us also reiterate that the reduction of polluting emissions will be achieved by reducing international flows, relocating the economy, a certain form of 'globalization' that no one - starting with political ecologists - wants to mention here. the commission's text is, in the final analysis, the lesser evil, because the better is the enemy of the good.
madam president, we all agree that the automobile sector must make a serious effort to limit the emission of polluting gases into the atmosphere, including nox emissions. the tests carried out so far in laboratories have lacked transparency and honesty, and this is unacceptable, because our citizens need to know the truth about the quality of the air they breathe. this is why the introduction of real driving tests, which are mandatory for all car manufacturers, is a major step forward. but as for me, i will oppose that objection. a vote in favour of the objection to the commission's act would considerably delay the introduction of these tests, which are both better and much more reliable than the previous ones and which do not yet exist anywhere else. it would therefore be irresponsible, both for the environment and for the automobile industry, to postpone the introduction of these tests until the greek calendar. we want to strike a balance between protecting the health of our citizens and preserving the future of the european automobile industry. the adoption of the objection would then be the absence of an immediate solution and the status quo, whereas the rejection of the objection would be the beginning of the solution. in four years' time there will be a compliance review, which will allow us to be even more demanding in terms of reducing emissions from the automotive sector, but this will only be possible by accompanying the sector in this transition and ensuring that the values are strictly respected. it is a question of the confidence that must be restored in our fellow citizens and in the future of our automobile industry, which is an important pillar of our economy. we expect the commission to take strong measures in this respect, to control better the setting up of these tests and to make them more independent.
madam president, doing what we say and saying what we do is a simple code of conduct to maintain the trust of those we represent. one month after cop 21 and its ambitious targets, how can we accept the commission's implementing act which falls below the euro 6 standard on the grounds that it is too difficult to achieve? the automobile industry is in the news today because its emissions are significantly higher in real life than in the laboratory, even though for the past four years it has been bragging about ever cleaner cars. customers and the general public in contact with vehicles no longer want to have to suffer such levels of pollution. and we're not living in a lab! so, the recognition of real-world tests to seriously estimate the pollution level of a vehicle is very good, but above all do not lower the level of requirements. in order to combat the deaths of drivers due to speeding, has the maximum speed been increased? no, it's the opposite. the french minister for the environment has committed, following the decision of the technical committee for motor vehicles (ctvm), to review this implementing act at political level by the relevant ministers in the council. this would give member states the opportunity to reach a better compromise which would guarantee compliance with european standards. by accepting the postponement of our vote in february, we are giving you the opportunity to show that you too can do what you say you will do.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text to amend the regulation on the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. although the plan has some shortcomings, particularly in relation to the waste caused by the technique of sending boats to feed tuna with mackerel or stocks which benefit only a few tuna-farms, the text is intended to support traditional fishing methods for bluefin tuna. i am in favour of these fishing techniques, which are environmentally friendly because they are very selective and require very little energy, and which should benefit from a special advantageous regime.
in writing. ‒ the aim is to transpose the iccat convention (international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas) and to defend the prerogatives of the european parliament by proposing the codecision procedure, in the face of the european commission's request for the possibility of adopting delegated acts. it's the lesser of two evils. however, this report allocates quotas, which is not good for the mediterranean fisheries. however, other traditional fishing methods, such as mackerel, should be able to benefit from a favourable specific regime. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it aims to ensure the long-term conservation and optimum use of fisheries resources for sustainable fisheries in europe.
in writing. ‒ this is the transposition of a convention of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccta or iccat) on the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks. the commission has asked for the possibility of adopting delegated acts, but the rapporteur defends the co-decision procedure in order to maintain parliament's prerogatives. i voted in favour of this text which calls for an increase in the quotas allocated to small-scale fishermen using traditional and selective fishing methods, a decision which would protect both stocks and jobs, as my colleague sylvie goddyn had requested in committee by tabling several amendments.
in writing. ‒ since the aim is to strengthen the role of parliament vis-à-vis the commission on these tuna conservation issues by transposing the iccat convention into european law and since this plan aims to protect traditional fishing methods for bluefin tuna which are very selective and environmentally friendly, i am voting in favour of this report, although some problems such as the exclusion of small-scale fishing or the effects of the quota allocation system are still unresolved.
in writing. ‒ this multiannual plan for the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean focuses on the transposition of the iccat (international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas) convention. although bluefin tuna stocks have been restored, some issues remain, such as the allocation of quotas, which remains unfavourable to small-scale fisheries. nevertheless, the european commission wants to protect traditional, environmentally friendly fishing methods for bluefin tuna, such as madrague, which should benefit from a special favourable regime. i am committed to the defence of the environment and small-scale fishing and i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by mr gabriel mato on the multiannual plan for the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. this report aims to transpose into union law the measures of the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and mediterranean adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccst) between 2012 and 2014. iccat is an international organisation responsible for tuna management, to which the european union is a contracting party. iccat recommendations are binding acts which need to be transposed into union law. the ices recovery plan provides for the following measures: limitation of fishing in certain areas and at certain times, the new minimum size, measures relating to recreational fishing, measures relating to livestock and reinforcement of inspection measures. they are valid until 2022.
in writing. ‒ this legislative report responds to the binding recommendations of the cicta (regional fisheries management organisation to which the eu is a party) on the recovery of bluefin tuna stocks in the atlantic and mediterranean. in 2006, iccat launched a multiannual action plan to replenish stocks, which will end in 2022. it provides for a reduction in catches from 2007 to 2011, limitations on fishing by zone and period, and a new minimum size. the aim is also to strengthen the international inspection programme through new monitoring techniques, such as the use of stereoscopic cameras to assess the state of stocks. the report stresses, however, that it is essential that these rules apply equally to european operators and to those in third countries. i share these conclusions and have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i supported this report which aims to transpose into eu law the measures adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icct), to which the eu is a contracting party. the purpose of this regulation is to ensure the uniform application of the rules on bluefin tuna fishing and farming capacity within the eu, and thus to ensure a level playing field for all operators.
in writing. ‒ bluefin tuna remains critically endangered in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean. of course, the introduction of quotas has improved the situation, but overfishing is still a threat, with quotas being the subject of fierce competition between large tuna vessels and small fishermen. a balance must therefore be struck between safeguarding the marine ecosystem and preserving small-scale fisheries. this is the meaning of the measures in the multiannual recovery plan for bluefin tuna in the eastern atlantic and the mediterranean, adopted by the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccst). in this context, particular support and attention will be given to small-scale gear such as traditional fishing gear ('almadrabas'), which has a very low impact on marine ecosystems due to their low level of energy consumption and bycatch and their high level of selectivity.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to support the transposition of the international convention for the conservation of atlantic tunas. the rapporteur, however, suggested curbing the commission's eagerness by defending the codecision procedure rather than delegated acts. the european parliament's negotiating position is thus strengthened, which i support and consider to be a democratic guarantee. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate because it is about protecting traditional fishing methods, which are more concerned with protecting the environment.

in writing. ‒ the eu is a contracting party to the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icta). in 2006, iccat adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan, which will end in 2022. to restore stocks, the recovery plan provides for a gradual reduction in the level of total allowable catches from 2007 to 2011, limitations on fishing in certain areas and during certain periods, a new minimum size... in view of the positive evolution of the stock situation, iccat decided to increase the total allowable catch (tac) slightly to 15 821 tonnes, of which 9 372,9 tonnes were allocated to the union, compared to 13 400 tonnes in 2014. the aim is to transpose into union law the decisions of iccat concerning fisheries conservation and management in its area of competence. i am voting for this text.

in writing. ‒ the report was intended to integrate all the measures on bluefin tuna adopted at international level since 2012 into a single regulation. it should be noted that the treaty entrusts the council and it alone with the task of fixing quotas for all species, so there was no question here of negotiating the quantities of catches authorized. the report has enabled the implementation of particularly stringent management and control measures, following the bluefin tuna crisis, where we saw the biomass of the species fall dangerously. for example, observers will have to be on board all ships without exception. today the stock has returned to an encouraging level in european waters and international scientific bodies have authorised an increase in quotas in 2015. this is a demonstration of the effectiveness of the safeguard measures implemented so far. finally, we voted almost unanimously for a plenary amendment calling for quotas to be set in a fair way between artisanal fishermen and others. for bluefin tuna, as for all species, it is essential that the diversity of fisheries be preserved.

in writing. ‒ since the 2008 financial crisis, many legislative initiatives in the area of eu financial services have been launched with a view to restoring financial stability. the report welcomes these measures and the future creation of a 'capital markets union', pretending to believe that such a union will solve investment problems, when the lack of investment is in fact linked to the weakness of demand for business, which stems from the wage and budgetary austerity policies imposed on the countries of the european union. the proposed capital markets union is in fact aimed at changing the european financial system from the current financing model based mainly on bank credit to a model based on market finance. under this model, banks can resell these debt securities as financial securities on the capital markets (securitisation), which allows them to lend out of their risk pocket, while pocketing bank fees. this securitisation was a major contributor to the 2008 financial crisis. i object to this text, which is clearly drafted by the banking lobby.
in writing. ‒ the balz report provides little in the way of legal elements and concrete proposals. the report generally contains the commission's communications. we can agree with him on two main points: concern about the complexity and abundance of european regulation, and the project for a european and public rating agency for sovereign debts. on the other hand, we are opposed to the idea of breaking the link between the member states and their national banks, i.e. the completion of the banking union. the reforms initiated by commissioner hill in the run-up to the cmu also raise questions about their purpose, the influence of american market players on europe. with these various points in mind, i decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the balz report is a rather hollow text on the challenges of financial regulation since the 2008 crisis and the capital markets union projects. it merely gives an account of the agreed places and of the proposals which follow the trend of the texts proposed by the commission, with few legal elements or new proposals. he is also concerned about the increasing complexity of regulation and the need for harmonized, coherent and non-redundant regulation. but we cannot follow him on the need to break the link between sovereign states and banks at national level, i.e. to complete the banking union. it makes no mention of the need for a real banking separation, which is now at a standstill. on capital markets union, we are both in favour of diversifying the means of financing and reserved for securitisation or for real access to markets for most smes, which cannot access markets anyway. for these reasons, it is preferable to abstain on this text.
in writing. ‒ the balz report is a set of points and does not bring anything new to the table. it lists the commission's proposals on financial regulation and capital markets union. some positive points are to be noted, such as its concern about the increasing complexity of financial regulation that weighs on the activity, or about the creation of a public rating agency. however, it follows the commission on the need to break the link between states and banks in difficulty by promoting the banking union, the limits of which were seen in italy during the rescue of four local banks. nothing is proposed on the necessary banking separation. on the contrary, we are again being given the opportunity to discuss the capital markets union, which would relaunch securitisation in order to finance smes on the american model. however, smes themselves admit that they would prefer to favour bank financing over securitisation, which in the united states is mainly the responsibility of large public funds. i therefore abstained on this text, which seems very empty and does not add much.

in writing. ‒ this report for a digital single market act uses the digital economy to advance federal europe at the expense of states in different areas of sovereignty. it provides for greater harmonisation of vat for online mail (single rate), concentration of transactions by a few european operators and unification of copyright and intellectual property rules to prohibit zone blocking. the text, however, refuses to deal with such important subjects as the dismantling of european telecommunications equipment manufacturers in favour of the chinese and the americans or the lack of investment due to competition, especially in digital terms, in rural or peripheral areas. finally, nothing is said about the problem of personal data which differs according to european or american rules, especially when we know the risks with espionage cases. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ the digital market, on the internet, is a huge reservoir of potential growth. it has grown rapidly in recent years: more and more of us are shopping, renting and watching movies on the internet. however, the digital market is under-exploited by our businesses in europe, and the reason is very simple: there are barriers that prevent the emergence of a common, european digital single market. today, it is sometimes impossible to get a product delivered because of where we live, impossible to watch a video from abroad. we have just voted a key text in the european parliament which calls for all these obstacles to be removed. this will enable our companies to compete directly with the giants of america or asia. it's good for our economy, and it's good for our jobs. but we must not lift the barriers on any condition. the internet must remain a space of freedom, but not a zone of lawlessness. so i want to develop a european-style digital market, where we protect copyright, where we hold the big video and music platforms accountable for the content they broadcast.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the digital single market. this strategic guideline, which may seem abstract, is followed by the adoption of 16 important and very concrete european initiatives. the challenge is to make the european union one of the leaders of the fourth industrial revolution, with the creation of a genuine cross-border e-commerce market. if completed, this project will boost the union's competitiveness, have a positive impact on growth and employment, and significantly relaunch the single market. this process will also contribute, provided that we decisively close our digital skills gap, to making our society more inclusive, by offering new opportunities to european citizens, consumers and businesses, while stimulating trade and the sharing of innovation. to achieve this, a key word is trust, both from consumers and businesses. this also raises the issue of an adequate regulatory environment, in particular for platforms and intermediaries, outlined in the text. finally, it highlights the potential offered by the sharing economy, without being too evangelical: we recall the challenges it represents for the legislator.
in writing. ‒ the digital single market is one of the main priorities of the juncker commission. on 6 may, it unveiled its action plan to build this market. the report by kaja kallas and evelyn gebhardt urges the commission to act in all areas of its strategy and even beyond. it called for full harmonisation of the legal framework for online sales in order to better protect consumers and improve consumer confidence. it also places the european union in a context of innovation and support for young firms, which are essential for european dynamism. however, the report gives too little weight to culture and creators, which are as much a source of wealth for europe as start-ups. it contains ambiguous provisions on geo-blocking and platform liability, while it opens up important discussions on portability, copyright, audiovisual services, and that europe must specifically affirm the role of digital in the dynamism of cultural creation. for these reasons, and despite these reservations, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the creation of a digital single market which will enable europe to strengthen the competitiveness of its industry in the face of the global digital giants. the eu must get on the digital bandwagon as soon as possible, catch up with the us and build a legal and economic environment that is conducive to the creation of future european digital champions. the creation of a digital single market is accompanied by prospects for economic growth, many jobs but also greater benefits for consumers. i supported this text, which combines the development of a digital economy with the protection of copyright, intellectual property and better tools to combat counterfeiting on the internet. the union must fully embrace the digital path, offering immense opportunities for growth, a stable legal framework and preserving our cultural industries.
in writing. ‒ this text is a flagship document of the legislature as it provides the european parliament's support for the commission's communication on the digital economy. the digital economy is here used as a pretext for advancing the federalisation of europe in areas of sovereignty: taxation: in the name of market fluidification, it provides for greater harmonisation of vat in the area of online shipments, moving towards a single rate, to develop cross-border purchases; concentration of operators in a few large european-level operators, which would make it impossible for states to regain their sovereignty in this strategic industry; unification of copyright and intellectual property rules to prohibit zone blocking. i therefore vote against this text.

i'm the reporter. madam president, madam commissioner, although it is very late, i am very pleased to be able to bring up in a debate this evening this directive on the presumption of innocence, on which we have been working for many months and on which we have finally reached an agreement, and i might even say a good agreement, after some difficult negotiations. this agreement sets out an ambitious legislative text on this great principle of criminal law, for the respect of our rights of defence for all of us, european citizens. on 31 march last, ladies and gentlemen, you gave me a clear mandate. the position of our parliament was strong and firm. it called for greater protection for suspects or accused persons, an ambitious directive to protect the rights of europeans and a directive harmonising national provisions upwards rather than downwards. the right not to be publicly accused by the public authorities before a judgment is rendered is enshrined in this text. i will give you a recent example: during the charlie hebdo attacks in my country, a young high school student in my constituency, mourad hamyd, was accused of having participated in the attacks, while he was quietly attending a mathematics class. his name was all over the news, all over the media, all over the networks, when he was totally innocent. his name was tarnished, he was involved in horrible attacks, it was a traumatic experience. the european directive proposes to prohibit any public statement or official decision by public authorities which would present or even imply that a suspect is guilty before trial. the text contains clear definitions of public declaration and the concept of public authority. secondly, and this is a victory for parliament, the directive contains a new article on the way in which suspects are presented, who may, at the hearing or in public, be behind glass walls or partitions, handcuffed, with handcuffs, dressed in prison clothes, and this way of presenting people can fully suggest the guilt of the person who is gambling and undermine his right to the presumption of innocence. from now on, we will have to ensure that suspects or accused persons are not presented in a way that might suggest their guilt. finally, the directive fully enshrines the great principle in dubio pro reo, according to which any doubt as to the guilt of a person must obviously benefit that person, and where there is doubt as to the guilt of the person, the person must be acquitted. finally, the fact that the burden of proof rests with the prosecution is a principle of criminal law, and it is self-evident. in the text, some people wanted to make it possible, at some point, to reverse the burden of proof as a principle. this was one of our battles, or even our red line, and we managed to go ahead and make sure that this element exists only in limited cases, where there is a presumption of guilt. the directive also enshrines the right to remain silent and makes the right to silence an absolute right, which is a real breakthrough in this area. it seems obvious, but in some cases silence can be used as such against a person as an inducing element, here too, of his guilt. the directive enshrines the right to be present at the trial and, lastly, with regard to the taking of evidence, a paragraph refers to the national rules on the admissibility of evidence and the fairness of proceedings. we have fought for an additional recital and this is a real first in a european text, since there is a clear reference to article 3 of the echr and to the case law, which states that when evidence is obtained through torture, it totally deprives the whole procedure of fairness.
on behalf of the enf group. madam president, the presumption of innocence is a fundamental right, but france does not need the european union to protect it. article 9 of the 1789 declaration does this better than any directive written in obscene jargon. i believe that criminal proceedings should be a matter for the sovereignty of the member states alone. the union is in any case incapable of protecting this fine principle without damaging it. the commission proposal for a directive is a good example of this. article 5 of the convention, for example, allows for the burden of proof to be reversed, with the burden of proof being on the accused rather than on the accuser. in my opinion, this is contrary to the presumption of innocence. even more disturbingly, its recital 17 allows for the use of coercion to compel suspects to provide information. why not torture while we're at it? amendments will no doubt remove these errors, but the damage has already been done in principle. the union is really nothing but a europe of banks and lobbies, and it will never understand anything about freedom, which is fundamentally alien to it.

in writing. ‒ the objection is raised by keith taylor, an english environmentalist. the committee also welcomed the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all types of transport. the rapporteur stresses the importance of breastfeeding, which is desirable but not always possible. it also calls for a review of the maximum permitted sugar content and a total ban on glyphosate. the referral of the text to which the objection relates will not necessarily produce the desired effect and will only delay progress, in particular certain information on packaging. in addition, efsa is due to produce two opinions on composition and authorised pesticides in 2016. those opinions shall give rise to revisions of the delegated act. it should be noted that baby food products are the most regulated and controlled products. it is almost certain that a well-meaning mother who does not want to buy specialized products exposes her child to more pesticides (e.g. 10 times more in breast milk or uncontrolled on fresh products) than with so-called highly standardized industrial products. the manufacturers are already prepared to implement it and this text will not harm babies any more than it does now, on the contrary. i vote against the objection.

president-in-office of the council.– madam president, i would first of all like to thank this parliament for holding this important and very timely debate to discuss the humanitarian situation in yemen. let us face it, yemen is too much of a neglected, even forgotten, crisis. it is absolutely necessary that we devote attention to what has been described as a humanitarian crisis of catastrophic proportions, surpassing all others when measured by the number of people in need of immediate assistance. in spite of repeated international condemnation, we are witnessing continuous disregard for the very basic principles of international humanitarian law and human rights law. civilians and civilian infrastructures are being targeted by all parties to the conflict on an almost daily basis. we are particularly concerned by the recent attacks on médecins sans frontières (msf). their facilities in yemen have been attacked, leading to casualties which are yet another example of the violations of international law that occur during this war. the intensity of the humanitarian crisis is constantly on the rise. humanitarian organisations estimate that 21.2 million yemeni people – that is 82% of the total population – are in need of humanitarian assistance; 14.4 million are suffering from food insecurity; 14.1 million are in need of health care and 19.3 million lack access to water and sanitation. the european union has been actively contributing to efforts aimed at resolving the current conflict and restoring basic rights for ordinary yemenis. we are doing so on several tracks. on the humanitarian front, the commission increased its emergency assistance for yemen by eur 17 million in december, bringing the total amount of commission support in the crisis to eur 52 million for 2015. some member states already contribute to emergency and humanitarian assistance and more will follow. the funding benefits the most vulnerable people, including internally displaced persons, refugees, migrants trapped in yemen and those affected by the pre-existing nutrition and food crisis, all of whose situations have deteriorated due to the conflict. the european union will continue to call on all parties to allow access for delivery of humanitarian aid. however, the level of humanitarian funding is only one aspect of the problem. we know this. with a population dependent on imports for 90% of its basic needs, the lifting of all restrictions on commercial imports is equally important. in this respect the european union is working very closely with the united nations and other partners to expedite the implementation of the united nations verification and inspection mechanism to allow the flow of humanitarian and commercial goods into yemen, to which it is contributing eur 2 million. the second track is political. the escalation of hostilities in the second half of 2014, and more prominently since march 2015, has gravely obstructed the achievements and the implementation of the yemeni transition and have left the country on the brink of a humanitarian disaster. the european union, as stated in the conclusions of 20 april and 16 november 2015, strongly believes that the solution to this crisis must be a political one. achieving an inclusive political settlement, fully in line with the framework provided by the gulf cooperation council (gcc) initiative, the outcomes of the national dialogue conference and relevant united nations security council resolutions is the only sustainable way to alleviate the plight of the yemeni people. after united nations facilitated talks in geneva in june, a second round was held in bern, switzerland in december 2015. the european union is closely coordinating with the united nations to continue playing a helpful role with the parties to ensure that the third meeting can take place in the coming days. the conflict has now involved a number of regional players. we encourage all relevant actors to play a positive role towards a lasting political solution of the crisis. one of the main concerns of the european union remains the implementation of immediate steps leading to a durable ceasefire. previous ceasefires have failed to take hold due to multiple violations by the parties and it is crucial that the parties implement confidence-building measures, including the full respect of international human rights and humanitarian law and the release of political prisoners. permanent access for humanitarian and emergency assistance to reach the suffering population, in particular in the city of taiz, but also in saada and other affected regions, must be guaranteed. in yemen’s dramatic situation, ensuring accountability for violations is an important part of the process to achieve a lasting settlement in the current conflict. the united nations human rights council adopted a compromise resolution on 2 october 2015 on technical assistance and capacity building for yemen in the field of human rights, which sets the conditions for a national commission of inquiry, which the eu expects to work independently. i reiterate our call for the independent investigation of all alleged violations of international human rights law and international humanitarian law. the european union looks forward to the high commissioner’s oral update at the council’s 31st session and to a comprehensive written report during its 33rd session.

mr president, the threat of terrorism is global, global, internal and external. in the face of this threat, we need unity, will and, above all, action today - not tomorrow, not the day after tomorrow, but today - and action in four directions. first, we must control, like all the great powers of the world, and effectively guard our borders. secondly, we must make it compulsory for european countries to exchange information. if not, we tell stories. thirdly, we must put a common european defence policy on the rails, because the threat is at the doorstep of europe. fourthly, we must have a foreign policy strategy to try to find solutions to conflicts, particularly in syria and libya. in conclusion, i say to you, if we can do all this as 28, let us do it, but if we cannot act as a whole, then let us decide to act as a few: let a few countries take the initiative to move forward. i hope that in this respect france and germany will regain the inspiration and vision which the european union is sorely lacking today.
mr president, in the face of terrorism, the member states can no longer act alone. the union must ensure the coordination and coherence of national policies, because european security is at stake. in the face of terrorism, the socialists and democrats are calling for more europe. more europe, this requires systematic sharing of information between the police, judicial and intelligence services of the member states. europol, with its new counter-terrorism centre, must become a fully-fledged european agency. the fight against terrorism also means tackling its financing. the strengthening and harmonisation of the powers of financial intelligence units and the improvement of the efficiency of the european system for freezing terrorist assets are all measures which must be taken as soon as possible. finally, in the face of the growing recruitment of young europeans by the islamic state, we must tackle the roots of terrorism through a systematic policy to prevent radicalisation. europe and its member states must invest more resources in developing and financing preventive measures, from the local to the european level, at school, in neighbourhoods, in businesses, but also on the internet. we have a burning obligation to demonstrate, through our public policies, that our young people - all our young people - have a place in our society. we must forcefully recall our common values of respect and solidarity with all the religions, including the muslim religion, which make up our european community.
in writing. several proposals have been announced by the commission. the establishment of a european border guard corps, a targeted reform of the schengen code for systematic checks at the external borders of the union, an extension of ecris to criminal records of non-europeans. i have been asking for these proposals for a long time now. but why so much time and lives wasted before they are done? in my report on the prevention of radicalisation, which was voted on 25 november, i included many other measures. i hope that the commission and the member states will commit themselves to the introduction of criminal liability for internet giants who do not cooperate in the face of the mass dissemination of terrorist propaganda content. strong measures to combat the financing of terrorism must also be put in place. the responsibility of certain gulf countries for financing terrorism must be brought to light. we also need a european tfts, a system for detecting terrorist financing channels, modelled on the agreement we have with the united states. what we have lacked so far is political will! let us not abandon european citizens to terrorists and let us act!

in writing. a process is under way to open discussions with new zealand and australia, which could lead to free trade agreements. although it is essential to help strengthen the union's ties with these two partner countries, the agricultural aspect of such agreements is very sensitive and the european union should not sell its agriculture on the altar of diplomacy. at a time when our livestock sectors, which produce meat and dairy products, are going through an unprecedented crisis, it would be dangerous to open up the european market to such direct competitors. let me give you some figures: new zealand is the world's largest exporter of dairy products and the second largest exporter of milk powder. it is the fifth largest exporter of beef in the world. australia is the world's second largest exporter of milk and the third largest exporter of beef. other sectors are also affected, such as large crops and sugar. i therefore call on the european commission to concentrate on the agreements currently being negotiated and not only to limit agricultural concessions as much as possible but to encourage the exclusion of our sensitive products.
in writing. a process of opening up negotiations is under way and the launch of negotiations for free trade agreements between the european union and australia and new zealand will open up new prospects and opportunities for our businesses. in order to prepare for these future negotiations as well as possible, it is essential that the european commission should carry out, as soon as possible, comprehensive and precise impact analyses in order to be able to anticipate the effects of such agreements on our market. the aim will be to negotiate ambitious and balanced free trade agreements in a spirit of reciprocity and mutual benefit. in view of the opening of these negotiations, i would like to stress at this stage that agricultural products will be a very sensitive subject in these future discussions. the most sensitive products will need to be excluded from negotiations or at least, where appropriate, specific quotas or appropriate transitional periods will be introduced. it will also be essential to obtain the recognition and protection of our protected geographical indications. finally, i would point out that australia and new zealand each have their own specificities and that separate agreements will have to be negotiated in this respect.

in writing. ‒ one year after the ratification of the association and free trade agreements between the union and georgia, moldova and ukraine, economic and trade links with these countries of the eastern neighbourhood have been strengthened. while progress has been made in terms of economic development and stability, reforms remain in the area of individual freedoms and human rights and in some state institutions. in ukraine, corruption remains endemic. the judicial system in georgia is not sufficiently independent, as evidenced by the lack of transparency in the appointment of prosecutors and investigators. in moldova, the financial sector needs to be completely overhauled. the european union will of course continue to provide assistance to these countries as they progress in the areas of democracy, the rule of law and the fight against corruption. at the same time, it is urgent to convince russia to stop meddling in the conflicts in georgia, moldova and ukraine and to stop interfering with their european aspirations. finally, it should be remembered that this rapprochement and closer cooperation with these countries does not presage systematic accession to the european union.

in writing. ‒ following the terrorist attacks on 13 november 2015 on french soil, france called for the solidarity of the other european states by using the mutual defence clause provided for in article 42 (7) of the treaty. this clause states that in the event of an armed attack on the territory of a member state, the other states must give it aid and assistance by all means in their power. the member states, by accepting this request, have shown their solidarity with france in the fight against terrorism outside the union's borders. the resolution welcomes france's request and the member states' willingness to cooperate in defence matters. the text also stresses the progress made in the cooperation of the eu member states in the fight against terrorism. i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ this resolution follows france's decision to invoke the eu treaty's mutual defence clause (article 42 (7)) to seek the assistance of member states in the face of the threat of the islamic state. this article, invoked for the first time since it entered into force in 2009, provides that 'if a member state is the object of armed aggression on its territory, the other member states have an obligation to assist it by all means'. following france's request, all the countries of the european union expressed their support, symbolizing europe's unity against terrorism. this resolution deals with the scope of this article, the implementation arrangements and the role of the union institutions. i supported this and voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report takes stock of the activities of the committee on petitions in 2014. since the entry into force of the lisbon treaty in 2009, the charter of fundamental rights has had binding legal force. the right to petition is therefore recognised as a fundamental right (article 227 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union) and allows citizens to raise concerns with the european parliament about problems related to the implementation of european policies. in 2014, 2714 petitions were filed (6% less than in 2013) and 1607 were deemed admissible. some 80% of the petitions were dealt with during the year and a few triggered infringement proceedings before the court of justice. the majority of petitions concern justice, fundamental rights, the environment and the internal market. the main objective of this report is to clarify the rules on the admissibility of complaints, in order to offer citizens better protection of their rights when the union is competent. i have supported this report because i believe that the right to petition is an important element of the rule of law.

mr president, commissioner, are you familiar with the havana charter? i don't know, man. however, this charter was signed in 1948, after the war, at the initiative of the united nations, to think of trade for peace and to set trade rules with a view to peace and the pursuit of this peace. the principles are quite clear: balance of payments equilibrium (surpluses of some people cause deficits of others; no one can be locked in their deficit), fair labour standards, authorisation of state aid where sovereignty and independence are at stake, authorisation, and therefore also of subsidies in certain circumstances, and prohibition of dumping. it is very clear that today china is not a market economy. it protects itself, pursues a policy of self-interest for its own development and may not necessarily be concerned with the interests of others. we must build a fair trade with it, and this fair trade must be based on the principles of the havana charter. china is the european union's largest imbalance in the balance of goods. we must find the basis for a new sustainable trade balance with china and this must be done within the framework of the united nations and not the wto.

in writing. china signed an accession protocol with a series of commitments to become a market economy after joining the wto in 2001. this agreement allows other wto members to apply the non-market economy status to this country. it thus allows the introduction of protective measures against chinese imports. while china has only met one of the 5 criteria set by the eu for recognition of its market economy status (mes), the european commission recently indicated that it would consider this possibility by december 2016. it is well known that large parts of the production of goods and services in china are heavily subsidised by the state. however, community law provides a strict framework for cases where such aid is authorized. under these conditions, granting the sem to china would have a devastating impact on the european economy. several studies show that this 'dumping' permit would overwhelm the european market with chinese products at low prices, leading to a significant fall in eu industrial production with consequences for gdp and employment. in the end, it is most urgent to wait for china to make profound reforms before considering granting it sem.
in writing. the question of whether china should be granted market economy status will mark the year 2016. first of all, i would like to stress that china is not a market economy because it does not meet the five criteria defined by the european union. this is also evidenced by the many anti-dumping measures currently in force against china. i take this opportunity to stress the need and urgency of modernising our trade defence instruments without weakening them. while we are constantly trying to revive growth in europe, the granting of market economy status to china would be catastrophic for european jobs and industry. that is why we must continue to pursue our objectives of combating unfair competition and strengthening our businesses, especially our smes. we will be watching closely the impact assessment which will be published by the commission in a few weeks' time and its proposal this summer. we reiterate our insistence that the european union should not be isolated and should coordinate with the major international trading partners and wto members. finally, we must already be thinking about ways of mitigating the effects of possible retaliatory measures.

member of the commission. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i made a commitment to you some time ago, in a previous debate, to provide the answers you expect quickly to the challenges posed by tax fraud and tax evasion. the package we adopted last week is the fulfillment of that promise. this debate is an opportunity for me to present this answer and it also confirms, in line with the measures adopted last year - you remember our two packages of march and june - that it is possible to act quickly and clearly on corporate taxation. i would like to begin by welcoming the decisive role played by the european parliament in these matters. your assembly has given valuable support to the commission in redefining the contours of a fairer, more transparent and more efficient tax system in terms of content, but also in terms of political impetus. this subject could not and would not progress without your commitment. our institutions, the commission and parliament - as you know - are often in sync. what's the point? the absolute need to adopt concrete measures to combat abusive tax optimisation and to strengthen tax transparency, which is our common objective. the measures advocated in various reports presented to this house last year by the committee on economic and monetary affairs (econ) and the special committee on taxation and other measures similar in nature or effect (taxe) have highlighted these convergences and, not surprisingly, many of the measures contained in the package reflect - you can and will see - the recommendations made by this house. so i'm very happy to be here this morning, in tune with you, but now let's get to the actual package. our desire for reform is based on a very simple and deeply shocking fact: some companies today do not pay their fair share of taxes, or do not pay any taxes at all. this is a situation which has become, for many of our fellow citizens, absolutely unbearable. this strategy, which i would call a bypass strategy, takes advantage of an international and european tax system which is clearly no longer suited to today's economy, that is to say an economy which is global, mobile and complex. to respond to this state of affairs, to combat this inadequacy, the package i am presenting to you is based on four pillars. first, the taxation of companies is an actual taxation, not a theoretical one. it's very simple: companies have to pay their taxes where they make their profits. secondly, a qualitative leap for tax transparency. thirdly, a healthy and fair tax competition and, finally, a fine link between the internal dimension of the european union, which we must address, and the external dimension, which we must also take into account. i'm going back to these pillars, in that order. firstly, the effective taxation. the initiatives presented last week will ensure that companies are effectively taxed. this means that in reality there must be a close link between taxation and the place where profits are generated. we shall do this, with your support, through two instruments: a directive and a recommendation. we have first drawn up a proposal for a directive on tax evasion. i do not want to go into the details of the provisions here, but the proposed initiatives will, in particular, firstly prevent companies from transferring their profits to subsidiaries located in low-tax states, then prevent companies from circumventing certain legislation limiting the deductibility of interest by using so-called 'hybrid' instruments or entities and, finally, to counter the practices of certain companies which transfer their assets from one state to another in order to avoid paying tax on those assets. these measures - as you can see - are in line with the recommendations made last year by the econ and taxe committees. we are indeed following your own works. this directive is supplemented by a recommendation to prevent any abuse of tax conventions. you are familiar with these practices: some companies set up artificial structures to gain access to the most favourable tax treatment under various tax agreements with other member states or with third countries. our recommendation provides guidance to member states on how to make their tax treaties more resilient to tax treaty shopping. the second pillar is decisive and fundamental in my view. that is the fight i want to fight during this mandate, namely tax transparency. the directive on the publication of information by country is at the heart of our action. this text is a manifestation of our commitment to a real revolution in tax transparency within the union. in concrete terms, the measures i am presenting to you this morning will enable the exchange of key information on certain companies between the tax administrations of the member states. what's this about? i want to be specific. the proposals for directives implement the oecd recommendations on the publication of financial information on a country-by-country basis. you know the challenge: it is to enable administrations to better control irregular transfers of profits between companies. we therefore propose today that you transpose the standards as recommended by the oecd. it's a first step. i know that many of you want to go further in terms of transparency and make country-by-country reports of companies public. i will put it in the simplest way possible - and you already know this - and that is my wish too. i have said this on several occasions in this house and outside it, and i have long tried in my political practice not to have double talk. i am therefore in favour of publishing information on a country-by-country basis. the commission will be submitting a proposal in the spring on this point. what's the problem? our services are studying the best approach to take. we have conducted a public consultation, we are conducting an impact study and the problem must be the following: is there a contradiction between this increased publicity which you want - as i, as many others, as other members of the commission, you know that some have spoken on this matter - and the competitiveness of our companies and their ability to invest? if so, and if there is this contradiction, it will take a while. if not, we must move forward with determination. that's what this impact study should say. you know my wishes and my intentions, but at the same time i think that we must act on this matter with a great deal of pragmatism and not be guided by ideology. transparency and competitiveness are two objectives which we must pursue together. third pillar: we want to restore healthy and fair tax competition between companies within the internal market. i am talking about competition between economic actors, such as companies, and between member states. let us first look at what is happening at the corporate level. there is a profound imbalance in the tax burden between smes and multinational companies. when i talk about some companies - i'll be more specific now - multinationals have the means to practice aggressive tax planning. that doesn't mean that all of them do, i don't want to be in an intent lawsuit. i am simply saying that they have the means, with the legal services they have and with their own internal organisation, to do so. it is therefore smes, which represent the hard core of the european productive fabric, that are disadvantaged. in other words, there are significant distortions of competition to the detriment of companies that pay their fair share of taxes. we estimate that the tax burden of smes is up to 30% higher - a considerable figure! - than that of multinational companies. this situation is unacceptable and cannot continue. the commission's proposed measures therefore directly target the increasingly aggressive tax regimes of multinational companies that have the means to evade tax. the package will also restore fair tax competition between member states by protecting their tax bases. this is the principle of base erosion and profit shifting (ebitb), which you know. some member states have already taken action on tax evasion and have adopted measures to counter its effects, but others have not followed up or to be more than lenient not yet followed up and this has resulted in a particularly unfair situation where anti-abuse measures taken by some member states are in fact undermined by more permissive legislation that is taken elsewhere. the package i am presenting to you will therefore allow the member states to return to a level playing field within the union, and this is a necessity. finally, the last pillar: we are developing a genuine external strategy for the european union. our initiatives are designed to provide a global response to a global problem. let us be frank: we need a common approach at european level to the outside world, complementing the internal measures that will be taken by the member states. our new strategy therefore addresses the risk of external fiscal erosion and, to this end, encourages greater cooperation between the union and its international partners. i am thinking first of all of the non-cooperative third countries, which represent a real threat to the balance of the internal market. the commission intends to work with its international partners to promote good international tax governance. that's what's happening at the oecd. that's what's happening in the g20. i say this firmly: we will not hesitate to take a hard line against those states which persist in the wrong direction. as you can see today, the package presented to you is a strong one, with a series of solid and coherent measures. our new european strategy proposes the establishment of a european list - and i emphasize the two words - of non-cooperative third countries. so far, as you know, i have taken the initiative to have a list that is, i would say, a kind of best of, a medley of national lists with their inequalities. some have no non-cooperative states, others have 85. some have certain criteria and others have fewer or different criteria. it was not satisfactory, but at the same time it made things move. this has led to debate and to the evolution of a number of states which have felt that they were being targeted and which have already been removed from the list. i do not want to name names, since there was virtuous behavior. however, the european list i am proposing would be based, as the european parliament has suggested, on objective and fair criteria decided by the member states, as well as on a permanent dialogue with these countries: effective taxation of companies, tax transparency, sound and fair tax competition, and external strategy. so these are the four pillars of the anti-tax evasion package that we are presenting to you. i would now like to say something perhaps a little more technical, but behind the technique there is often policy, more specifically in relation to implementation. the package allows for a comprehensive and coordinated implementation of the oecd recommendations. what are the parameters we have to deal with? in simple terms, we must avoid the effects of variable geometry, since not all eu member states are members of the oecd, and we must take account of the specific features of our internal market. a common approach was therefore essential to avoid a partial or disparate application of the ebitb measures, which would de facto doom our package to failure. in addition, some specific initiatives go beyond the ebitb recommendations. it is also because we have been nourished by the debates in this house and the discussions in the council, and it is also because we are a union, with a stronger integration than a system like the oecd. in our previous discussions, some in this house had questioned the competitiveness and economic attractiveness of the union. i would like to reassure them and tell them that the initiatives proposed this morning are not hostile to this. on the contrary, i believe strongly that transparency and competitiveness go hand in hand. the provisions i am proposing will avoid a patchwork of national legislation which would seriously damage the internal market and thus the economic activity of european companies. all of this is shaping taxation in europe to be favourable to companies that play by the rules and not favourable to those that play by the rules. so clearly these are the first things we should give priority to. a few words to conclude, first to look ahead to what awaits the commission, to what awaits you in 2016. this anti-tax evasion package, which is - as you can see - very ambitious and very comprehensive - is probably the most ambitious and comprehensive package ever proposed by a commission and examined by your assembly. but it is only the beginning of a series of initiatives that we will be presenting, that i will be presenting to you in the coming months. we will have another big date this year: you know that 2016 will be the year of the rebirth of the accis, the consolidated common platform (ccctb in english). the ccctb has the merit of providing a comprehensive answer to the problem of profit transfer within the union, while offering businesses an optimal framework for their economic exchanges. so i want to keep, or rather pick up the pace on this project. the commission services are currently working on a proposal which must be a proposal in stages, because we have seen that a one-stop-shop approach has not convinced the council and what i want, as always, in tax matters is to marry the desirable with the possible. the only way to do this, ladies and gentlemen, - and i must say this - is by agreement between us, but also by consensus between the member states, since you are familiar with the decision-making process in this area, which requires unanimity. some may regret it. that is the way our institutions are set up and of course we must respect that sovereignty. but one step at a time! the commission is reaffirming its commitment to the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion more than ever with the package we are discussing today. i have already said this before, and i hope i will say it again with greater force: we must fight these forms of economic inefficiency which give rise to social injustice. the most honest actors, the taxpayers, are now unfairly bearing the costs of these distortions and there is a considerable amount of money lost to growth, to public services, to hospitals, to safety, to schools, to public transport and to the economy in general. we need to inject more fairness and transparency back into international taxation and into our own european taxation. the measures presented in 2015 were already a very significant step forward in this direction. i would like to mention in particular the long-awaited directive on the automatic exchange of information on tax returns, to which your parliament has made such a great contribution. the package we have just adopted is a further major step along this demanding but essential path. i sincerely hope that parliament and the commission will continue together in the coming months to make tax transparency and fairer international taxation what we want it to be: a reality.

in writing. ‒ this report calls for the codification of the body of rules gathered around the schengen status quo. historically, from emperor justinian to emperor napoleon, every attempt to codify has been made in an effort to ensure the succession of rules, to enshrine great principles. so it is not a question of bringing my stone to a building which i would rather see dismantled and consigned to the dustbin of history. i therefore naturally vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it makes it easier to read this legal document. i would also like to emphasize that coding is a well-known and recognised technique in our country, and that this type of initiative makes it easier for citizens to find themselves in the texts in the application, which are sometimes difficult to read.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which supports the commission's proposal to codify the regulation establishing a community code on the rules governing the crossing of frontiers by persons. it is therefore in the interests of transparency and legal clarity that this new regulation would replace the various acts which are incorporated into the schengen borders code. the content of the code shall be preserved; it is a simple coding operation. the conditions of application related to the absence of controls at the eu's internal borders, the types of controls, the special circumstances, the modalities for exceptional reintroduction of controls and the responses to serious threats are thus being re-codified. this codification operation provides the legal clarification necessary for the implementation of the schengen borders code.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, determined to maintain the schengen agreements and borders. without the free movement of citizens, the union would be nothing but a single market. i won't compromise. nationalism and identity rhetoric lead to deadlock. to solve the migration crisis, as well as to combat terrorist risks, european countries must come together and strengthen their common border policy, not dismantle it. the return to national borders would only increase isolation and condemn everyone to impotence. those who tried to take greece out of the euro zone are now proposing to take it out of the schengen area. this is unacceptable. greece is not responsible for its geographical location which makes it a preferred arrival point for refugees from the middle east. is there a need for a border management policy? i know. but it must be done at the external borders of the union and with european border guards! the european union is now at a crucial stage: if schengen falls, so will it. together we will be stronger, without cooperation we will remain powerless.

in writing. ‒ undocumented work must be discouraged and combated. the establishment of a european platform for cooperation between the competent authorities of the member states is an important step forward in this field. i therefore voted in favour of an important report which respects the powers of the member states and the principle of subsidiarity.
in writing. ‒ whatever the good reasons for the creation of this platform, namely the fight against social fraud and the decrease in tax revenues, this form of imposed cooperation represents a new interference in the internal affairs of states. moreover, it is recognised that the most relevant actions are at national level, so that cooperation at european level will have only a very marginal impact on this phenomenon, which is constantly increasing in a crisis context and whose scale varies widely from one member state to another. a european platform would at best be another useless structure financed by taxpayers' money, which would be more useful elsewhere, at worst another harmful bureaucracy. i therefore vote against this proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the creation of a european platform to strengthen cooperation in preventing and discouraging undeclared work. beyond being illegal, undeclared work is detrimental to the smooth functioning of our society, as it does not contribute to our health and social redistribution systems. the amount of the costs or the administrative complexity are often cited as justification for the switch to undeclared work. i myself am fighting against the excessive taxation of labour and against the administrative overload which our country is unfortunately suffering from, in order to revive growth. but this is another debate, and we must not forget the figures: undeclared work accounts for about 20% of european gdp, sometimes even more in some countries not known for breaking tax records. so we must fight undeclared work for the sake of our companies and their law-abiding employees, for the sake of our living together.
in writing. ‒ undocumented work and sham self-employment have a significant budgetary impact and serious consequences for employment, productivity, skills development, pension rights and adequate social benefits, and the stability of social security systems. the existence of a cross-border dimension of this type of fraud requires action by the european union, whereas there is no formal structure to enable member states, responsible for combating undeclared work, to cooperate at european level. the resolution also calls for the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's citizens are not left behind in the process of deciding on the future of the eu. this tool, by pooling resources and means, will make it possible to combat this problem more effectively, while promoting the regularisation of the jobs concerned. that is why i supported the report by georgi pirinski.
in writing. ‒ i supported this report which calls for the establishment of a european platform to combat undeclared work, i.e. paid activities which are not reported to public authorities. this type of work has negative consequences such as severe exploitation situations, unfair competition disrupting the internal market and significant losses for the social security systems of the member states. a european platform would allow for the collection and sharing of reliable information on good practices and persistent problems; it would also develop cooperation in the definition and implementation of effective law enforcement. it is also essential that action be taken upstream, including the reduction of administrative and tax rules for our companies, in order to boost employment and growth.
in writing. ‒ undeclared work is equivalent to 18% of the eu's gdp and accounts for 8% to 30% of economic activity, depending on the member states. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's social security system is properly functioning. to build the european union, we must instead converge towards high social standards and the guarantee of the rights of all european workers. the fight against undeclared work is therefore a priority. i congratulate my socialist colleague, mr pirinski, on his report which foreshadows the creation of this european platform. it will include the social partners in a broad way in order to prevent and discourage such practices. the platform, which will involve all member states, will be designed to 'prevent, detect and combat undeclared work'. the aim of the directive will also be to encourage, rather than merely to impose, the legalisation of undeclared workers. this is a significant step forward and deserves to be welcomed, let us continue in this direction with a genuine european social agenda. the social europe in action is what our citizens expect.
in writing. ‒ in principle, the fight against illegal work remains a matter for the states, and its effectiveness depends to a large extent on the involvement of the social partners. the main actions of the platform will be to enable the exchange of information and good practice, to monitor actions at national level, and to encourage the training of relevant staff. whatever the good reasons put forward, namely the fight against social fraud and the reduction of tax revenues, this form of co-operation represents a new form of interference in the internal affairs of states. moreover, it is recognised that the most relevant actions are at national level, so that cooperation at european level will have only a very marginal impact on this phenomenon, which is constantly increasing in a crisis context and whose scale varies widely from one member state to another. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ following the adoption in january 2014 of a european parliament resolution calling for the strengthening of cooperation between national labour inspectorates against undeclared work, the commission proposed in april 2014 the creation of a european platform in this area. after several months of negotiations, the european parliament and the council agreed to set up this platform. in addition to measures to strengthen cooperation and operational measures between national labour inspectorates such as joint investigations, the platform will also cover fictitious self-employment. however, following the negotiations between the council and parliament, states will no longer be obliged, contrary to the commission's initial proposal, to participate in all the activities of the platform and will be able to choose to implement its recommendations. once again, the member states have refused to build a real social europe. i voted for this report, however, because i believe it is a first step in the fight, at european level, against undeclared work, which deprives many workers of the most basic social rights in terms of social protection and security.

in writing. ‒ this report on the mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy finds that efforts by member states are relatively modest, mainly because of the flexibilities granted to them. these have in fact limited the correct application of european directives. although it is regrettable that the issue of biodiversity is being dealt with in a financial approach, we appreciate the importance attached by the rapporteur to reconciling respect for the environment with economic development. it is essential not to impose too heavy requirements on member states, which are already suffering from the environmental dumping of the emerging countries and the united states. that is why i voted for this text.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament has delivered its opinion on the mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy. i voted in favour of this balanced report, which aims to fully implement the nature directives and support the european biodiversity strategy by 2020. it is important to remember that nature conservation and economic development are not mutually exclusive: the loss of biodiversity is detrimental to nature, to people and to the economy. to combat biodiversity loss, the european union needs to be able to measure the state of biodiversity with scientific indicators. this is one of the prerequisites for achieving the objectives of the strategy by 2020. it is important that the agricultural and forestry sectors are involved in achieving the objectives, which is why this report proposes a multilateral and participatory approach.
in writing. ‒ this strategic own-initiative report is parliament's contribution to the european commission's mid-term review of the eu biodiversity strategy (habitats and birds directives). the report notes a general loss of biodiversity. at the same time, we opposed the reopening of the texts, which would lead to a weakening of the legislation and a damaging legal instability. member states need to pay more attention to the implementation of existing rules to achieve the 2020 targets. i have been particularly active in this dossier in calling on the european commission to take adaptation measures for large carnivores (e.g. wolves) in order to preserve livestock in mountain areas. i also felt it was essential to call for better integration of local and regional actors, including farmers, in order to define a coherent biodiversity policy, which takes into account the activities of socioeconomic actors and the particularities of the territories. i think that this report sends a clear message to the european commission with recommendations that are in the right direction, and i voted in favour of it.
in writing. with this vote, the european parliament wanted to reiterate its commitment and support for a strong eu strategy for biodiversity. at a time when our biodiversity is under serious threat from pollution and climate change, the european union and its member states need to show more political will by setting ambitious targets. it is therefore particularly relevant to underline the importance of innovation, research and development in achieving these objectives.
in writing. ‒ biodiversity is essential not only for the functioning of ecosystems but also for preserving air and water quality and for pollination. the european union has set itself the objective of halting biodiversity loss and restoring ecosystem services by 2020. it is therefore important that member states implement better the eu's habitats and birds directives and that the union increases funding for biodiversity and takes action to strengthen the coherence between its agricultural, energy and environmental policies. finally, effective and proportionate penalties must be introduced for non-compliance with the european nature protection directives.
