sir, we're recording this information.
the agenda calls for the joint discussion of:- council and commission statements on the refugee emergency, external border control and the future of schengen (2016/2259 ((rsp)) - council and commission statements on compliance with the international principle of non-refoulement (2016/2535 ((rsp)) - council and commission statements on the financing of the refugee facility in turkey (2016/2525 ((rsp)) - council and commission statements on the resurgence of racist hatred and violence against refugees and migrants in europe (2016/2563 ((rsp)).
madam president, the causes of the influx of migrants are well known. first of all, disorganization, with the help of the west and the united states of america, of countries like iraq, syria and libya. secondly, the rhetoric of the european union and certain member states or political forces, which for ideological or political reasons are constantly calling for more migration to europe, is a rhetoric that is not heard, and mrs merkel's appeal has been heard. but mr pittella and mrs harms have just made some very moving speeches, except that if mr pittella and mrs harms go home and find migrants who have entered their homes unwittingly, i think they will call the police and lock their doors in double locks and shut their windows. it is also the laxity of the european union, because we always say - it is a purely verbal incantation - that those who have no right to be considered political refugees - and that is the vast majority of migrants, ladies and gentlemen, as you well know - must return to their country of origin. oh, how interesting! in my country, for example, france, it has been proved by one of our highest financial and judicial institutions, the court of auditors, that 95 per cent of those denied asylum, whose application has been carefully examined for months, years, with all sorts of levels of appeal, remain in france or, when they are returned to the border, for example, the franco-belgian border, they return the next day to the country from which they were allegedly expelled. the principle of non-refoulement is absurd when applied to countries that are safe. therefore, neither article 33 of the geneva convention nor article 19 of the european charter precludes the return of people from safe countries who come to us only for economic reasons.
the question is "blue cardboard". madam president, do you think that the migrants waited for mrs merkel's permission to leave the place where they could no longer live, subjected to terror, bombs and deprivation of liberty? do you think they waited for that authorization?
mr president, the european refugee facility in turkey is a fraud. the european union is going to pay 3 billion euros to turkey in the hope of settling the 2 million syrian refugees there. turkey does not, however, intend to comply with this agreement. the proof: president erdogan came to strasbourg in 2015 to challenge the union by criticizing european civilization and calling on the turks of france to refuse to integrate. the truth is that erdogan is willingly letting syrian migrants leave turkish ports for europe. he rejoices in our calamity, and he feeds the migratory wave that overwhelms us. the union is inherently weak because it is an off-the-books bureaucracy cut off from the soul of the european peoples. she'll lose her $3 billion without getting anything in return. the solution is to abolish the schengen agreement. each state must regain control of its borders to stop the flow of migration and treat turkey as an equal. if i take my country as an example, i would say that france will defend its interests much better when it is outside the schengen area, and even outside the european union.
mr vice-president, mr minister, we share the commission's commitment to the refugee crisis, whether it is to move towards a dignified and shared reception of asylum seekers, to improve our border management or to strengthen our cooperation instruments with our partners. all these devices are welcome. the question is the financing of these measures and therefore their sincerity. the agreement on the 2016 budget signed two months ago has exhausted most of the budgetary margins. the commission itself admits that we are now condemned to financial manipulations, and i quote: 'creative'. these creations do not meet any ordinary procedure, and the facility for turkey is an example of this. the union's budget is being strengthened, but without touching the ceiling of the multiannual financial framework. the heads of government can thus make it appear, with a rather hypocritical message, that the union is not being strengthened. the europe-haters in this house feed on these half-truths, these false appearances. mr president-in-office of the council, tell your colleagues to stop making europe feel ashamed. each council is given more responsibilities for the union, but what about the means of implementing them? we have an opportunity this year to seize it with the obligation to revise the multiannual financial framework. we can raise the union's budget to its responsibilities. since we have spoken this morning with commissioner moscovici about the important progress on taxation of multinationals, why not consider this tax at the level of the union? we would thus put an end to the sterile competition which is destroying our national tax systems and we would significantly reduce national contributions to the union budget.

this closes the voting.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the application of the safeguard and anti-circumvention clause for agricultural products in the eu-moldova association agreement. these clauses apply where the european branch is affected and not the national branches of the member states which are not protected. moreover, the changes made by this text are minor; i would like to ask the commissioner whether he is aware of the fact that the commission has not yet taken a decision on the amendment. finally, the adjustment of customs duties to deal with the problem of large imports is too small to be effective.
in writing. ‒ the eu-moldova association agreement includes an 'anti-circumvention mechanism' and a 'safeguard clause'. thus, if there is an unforeseen and significant increase in imports with serious detriment to the european industry, the clause allows for a suspension of any further reduction in customs tariffs on the product concerned or their replacement by the most favoured nation customs duty. we can only welcome such a reservation in regard to free trade. unfortunately, the most favoured nation clause is still far from sufficient. moreover, it is clear that this arrangement, more cosmetic than practical, is never used. voting in favour of this text would therefore be to endorse a protection policy which is too minimalist. that is why i, together with my colleagues from the national front, have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement because it will facilitate the monitoring of the implementation of a common trade policy between the eu and moldova in the interests of transparency and the reduction of corruption.
in writing. ‒ agricultural products imported from moldova are mainly oilseeds, fresh nuts, apple juice, wines and cereals. the association agreement with moldova contains a safeguard clause: if there is an unforeseen and significant increase in imports with serious detriment to the 'european production' branch, the clause allows for a suspension of any further reduction of customs tariffs for the product concerned or their replacement by the most favoured nation customs duty. there is also an anti-circumvention clause: when the volume of imports of certain agricultural products exceeds a ceiling with a doubt about their origins, the clause allows the preferential customs duty to be replaced by the most favoured nation (mfn) customs duty. these clauses are similar to those already in place in many free trade agreements. these clauses can only be applied where the 'european industry' as a whole is affected: the branches of production in each state are therefore not protected. that's why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ this report concerns the safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism for the eu-moldova association agreement. the clauses of this agreement apply when it is a european branch and not a national branch, which means that the productions of each state are not protected. the objective of placing flat tariffs on the npf rate is clearly too low for a real resolution on imports. in reality, the agreement is only intended to facilitate adjustment, not to prevent it. the amended text does not in any way enrich the safeguard clause and the anti-circumvention mechanism of the eu-moldova association agreement. in view of their reaction, the clauses of this agreement have no protectionist ambition. the changes are very minor and do not improve the text in any way, which is why i shall abstain on this vote.

in writing. ‒ on 27 june 2014, following a five-year negotiation process, the european union and the republic of moldova signed an association agreement. the latter has since been applied provisionally but remains incomplete in two essential respects: the anti-circumvention mechanism and the safeguard clause. the anti-circumvention instruments allow for the temporary suspension of preferential duties for certain products provided for in the agreement when the maximum import volumes are reached. more protective, safeguard clauses allow the suspension of trade preferences for a product if it is imported into the union in such increased quantities that it causes or threatens to cause serious injury to union producers of similar products. the european parliament was consulted to approve the introduction of these two schemes. without expressing an opinion on the political and strategic merits of an association agreement with moldova, whose political landscape is fragmented, i supported the introduction of such instruments, already present in a number of agreements concluded by the union, in order to preserve the balance of the european market. more generally, however, i regret that the commission makes only very limited use of the safeguard measures provided for in trade agreements.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the ratification of the marrakesh treaty, based on the petitions received by the european parliament. the aim of the marrakesh treaty, to which the european union is a signatory, is to facilitate access to published works for the blind and visually impaired. i fully support the ratification of this treaty, since today less than 10% of the world's works are made available in accessible forms for the visually impaired. the ratification of this treaty by the member states will make up for this shortfall and will be effective once the revision of the european copyright framework is completed, as the european commission plans to do in 2016. this resolution was adopted by a large majority, which i welcome.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the ratification of the marrakesh treaty. the aim of the directive is to create exceptions to copyright to facilitate the reproduction, distribution and making available of published works in formats designed to be accessible to blind or visually impaired persons. this also applies to persons with physical disabilities who are unable to hold or handle a book. the european union and its member states signed the treaty in april 2014, but it will not enter into force until 20 ratifications have been made. it seems that seven member states of the union have blocked the ratification of the treaty. at the moment, the council of the european union would like to include the provisions of the treaty in the new copyright directive, rather than ratify the treaty. but the revision of this directive could take time...
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it aims to encourage the ratification of the marrakesh treaty. this is an interesting treaty because it aims to create exceptions to copyright to facilitate the reproduction of works in formats accessible to blind or visually impaired persons.
in writing. - i voted for this ratification. the marrakesh treaty allows for exceptions to copyright to facilitate the reproduction, distribution and making available of published works in a format designed to be accessible to blind or visually impaired persons, and to persons with physical disabilities who are unable to hold or manipulate a book. the treaty will not be able to enter into force until it has been ratified by 20 member states, but at the moment seven member states appear to be standing in the way of ratification.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this resolution which calls on the council to ratify as soon as possible the marrakesh treaty to facilitate access to printed texts for the blind and visually impaired. only 5% of all published books exist in braille. for several years now, associations have been campaigning to put an end to this "hunger for books" which introduces profound inequality from school. but the real point of the story is that seven member states, germany foremost among them, are holding back and preferring to wait for the revision of the copyright directive. the european machine is therefore blocked, since the commission would have to ratify the treaty on behalf of all the member states. that's a good example of what i'm denouncing. france must disobey and ratify this treaty for her people without delay.
in writing. ‒ in order to facilitate the ratification of this treaty, i voted in favour of this resolution. i approve of its content in favour of the disabled. it would allow exceptions to copyright for these individuals, making it easier to make published works available in formats that are appropriate to them. i therefore vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the european union and its member states signed the marrakesh treaty in april 2014 to create exceptions to copyright to facilitate the reproduction, distribution and making available of published works in formats designed to be accessible to people who are blind or visually impaired. this also applies to persons with physical disabilities who are unable to hold or handle a book. at the moment, the council of the european union would like to include the provisions of the treaty in the new copyright directive, rather than ratify the treaty. but the revision of this directive could take time. the marrakesh treaty illustrates europe's failure to defend the disabled. it has not yet been ratified, probably because it restricts copyright. it therefore goes against the interests of important people: authors, publishers, translators. it is therefore proposed that we vote in favour of ratification.
in writing. the vote is to ratify the marrakesh treaty adopted in 2013. the latter provides for exceptions to copyright to facilitate the reproduction, distribution and making available of published works in formats designed to be accessible to blind or visually impaired persons. this also applies to persons with physical disabilities who are unable to hold or handle a book. i decided to vote in favour of this text, which slightly limits the excessive expansion of copyright.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the council and the member states to speed up the process of ratifying the marrakesh treaty to facilitate access to published works by the blind, visually impaired and other print disabled. the aim is to enable the crossborder exchange, within the union and between the union and third countries, of books in braille or large print, digital or audio-digital books with special navigation tools, produced under copyright exceptions. the european union signed the treaty in 2014, and each member state must sign and ratify it before it can be applied. the current french government is making ratification conditional on the amendment of the 2001 european disability exemption directive and is thus blocking this process, which i regret. the world health organization estimated in 2010 that there were more than 26 million people in all of europe who were blind or visually impaired. however, only 5% of all books published in developed countries and less than 1% in developing countries are produced in accessible formats for people with disabilities.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the ratification of the marrakesh treaty, calling on the council and the member states to speed up the process to ensure respect for the right of persons with disabilities to access education and culture, as well as the protection of intellectual property rights.
in writing. ‒ i supported the request for ratification of the marrakesh treaty. to date, 79 countries have signed the marrakesh treaty to facilitate access to published works by the blind, visually impaired and other print disabled, but it needs to be ratified for its provisions to enter into force. european citizens have rightly called on us, through a petition to the european parliament, to speed up the process. we have therefore taken it upon ourselves to press for ratification to be accelerated. this shows the effectiveness and the role of the petition as a relay for european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the marrakesh treaty to facilitate access to published works by the blind, visually impaired and other print disabled. the treaty currently has 79 signatories and the european union signed the text on 30 april 2014. however, each member state must now also ratify the treaty and the process is long. with only 1% to 7% of the world's published works made available in accessible formats, it is urgent that all parties ratify the treaty as soon as possible to ensure non-discriminatory access to cultural goods.
in writing. ‒ the marrakesh treaty aims to create exceptions to copyright to facilitate the reproduction, distribution and making available of published works in formats designed to be accessible to blind or visually impaired persons. this also applies to persons with physical disabilities who are unable to hold or handle a book. the treaty will not enter into force until 20 ratifications have been made. it seems that seven member states of the union have blocked the ratification of the treaty. the marrakesh treaty illustrates europe's failure to defend the disabled. it has not yet been ratified, probably because it restricts copyright. the resolution put to the vote is intended to facilitate ratification of the treaty. i vote for it.

in writing. ‒ the cultivation of monsanto's soybeans is part of the colonization of europe by foreign interests: the properties of this soybean serve only the interests of monsanto and, in the short term, those of industrial farmers. all three of these gmos are glyphosate-tolerant. efsa has ignored the reasoned objections of several member states, while its assessment of gmos is widely criticised. we have tabled amendments in plenary to ask that authorisations be granted in the form of delegated acts, with the aim of finding out who are against 'democratic control' of the placing of gmos on the market. i therefore very logically voted in favour of the objection to the placing on the market of genetically modified fg72 soybean.
in writing. ‒ as regards my general position on gmos, i am against the precautionary principle which prevents research in europe. i am also astonished at the hypocrisy of banning the marketing of these products which europe then allows itself to import. however, i voted against the marketing of this pesticide-resistant variety, because it is considered by many research centres, including the one in lyon, as a variety which could be dangerous.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposes to authorise three new gm soya beans from bayer cropscience and monsanto. all three are glyphosate-tolerant, with a different characteristic for the two monsanto gmos: different fatty acid composition for the gmo mon 87705 × mon 89788 and tolerance to dicamba (a pesticide) for the gmo mon 87708 × mon 89788. these properties only serve the interests of monsanto and industrial farmers (again, this is not proven). as in previous cases of gmo authorisation, the evaluation provided by efsa remains clearly unsatisfactory. unfortunately, objections to implementing acts are only symbolic and do not bind the commission, and the amendments tabled by my group to make objections binding and to recall that the commission does not even wait for the end of objection procedures to publish gmo authorizations have unfortunately been rejected. their rejection, recorded by roll call voting, thus shows the hypocrisy of elected officials who are in reality against "democratic control" of the placing of gmos on the market. however, it should be possible to issue authorisations for gmos by means of a delegated act and not by means of an implementing act.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection from the parliament to the commission concerning a marketing authorisation for products concerning genetically modified soybean fg72. in fact, despite repeated warnings from the member states and the concern of consumer protection associations, the european food safety authority - which has a bad name - is still trying to market this modified soybean, for the sole benefit and in the sole interest of monsanto. it should be noted that this genetically modified fg72 soybean is clearly tolerant to glyphosate, a total herbicide that monsanto markets under the brand name "roundup", which remains the most widely used herbicide in the world and which, according to recent studies, has tumourogenic and toxic effects. once again the commission is showing its willingness to submit to the big industrial groups, to the detriment of europe's economic interests but also of food safety and health in europe.

in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed to authorise the marketing of three new types of genetically modified soya beans from the us company monsanto. it is in this context that this objection is intended to signal parliament's opposition to the placing on the market of these three genetically modified organisms (gmos) tolerant of glyphosate. one of them also shows tolerance to the pesticide dicamba. if this objection does not force the commission to abandon the marketing of these gmos, we consider it essential to support it in order to show parliament's disapproval of the commission and efsa whose assessments are unsatisfactory and do not take account of the comments of the member states' authorities. that is why i voted for this objection.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution by a member of the european parliament (mep) from the socialist and democratic group concerns the draft commission decision in favour of authorising the use of glyphosate-tolerant gmo soybean fg72 in food and feed products. the rapporteur argues that glyphosate is a herbicide classified as a 'probable carcinogen' by the international agency for research on cancer (iarc). however, this justification is questionable. on the one hand, the draft decision of the european commission follows the positive opinion of the european food safety authority (efsa). its conclusions are based on a large number of studies, including those of iarc, and scientific data, as the authors explained in an exchange of views with meps last december. secondly, the commission has respected its mandate within the framework of its implementing powers deriving from european legislation, approved by the european parliament. i regret that this ideologically motivated resolution does not take account of the many precautionary measures voted by the european legislator in this area. for these reasons, i voted against this objection.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this motion for a resolution on emissions from passenger and light commercial vehicles. this proposal follows the volkswagen scandal, which revealed the considerable differences between pollutant emissions in the laboratory and those in real driving conditions. it should be remembered, however, that the cars involved have, on the other hand, emitted less carbon monoxide, a much more harmful gas. the resolution is a misguided strategy, since it seeks to impose additional, restrictive and costly standards on an industry already in crisis. i therefore opposed this text.
in writing. ‒ the issue of vehicle emissions has returned to the forefront of european politics with the volkswagen case. the commission's strict standards for actual pollutant emissions do not yet require real driving conditions (rde) tests. the limit values established in a 2007 regulation are reviewed by internal procedures within the commission: the requirement of this motion for a resolution was therefore to request a new regulation, to be submitted by 1 april 2016, to impose tests in real conditions at the earliest. this race to standard is questionable for two reasons: first, europe is becoming the least industrially-friendly region in the world. secondly, technical standards are a cataplasm on a wooden leg in the fight against air pollution, because the eu is also increasingly encouraging the flows that generate these emissions. this text is therefore a unilateral requirement of the political environment, imposed on european industry alone, with serious consequences for a sector in crisis. that is why i objected to this objection.
in writing. ‒ this objection follows the revelation of considerable differences between laboratory and real driving emissions (rde) for volkswagen diesel engines. the commission's stringent emission standards do not yet require such tests, so the text calls for a new regulation to be presented by 1 april 2016 to require real-world tests as soon as possible. the first recital recalls the numerical cost of air pollution (estimated at eur 940 billion per year) as a dogma, and justifies the need for increasingly stringent and costly technical standards. these requirements are questionable for two reasons: europe is becoming the least industrially-friendly region in the world; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment. this text is therefore a unilateral requirement of the political ecology, imposed on european industry alone, with serious consequences for a sector already in crisis. that's why i objected.

in writing. ‒ following the volkswagen scandal, the commission has responded by proposing to make the real-world emissions testing of diesel cars more stringent by reducing the difference between the regulatory emission limit which is tested in the laboratory and the value of emissions produced in real driving conditions. this measure, together with the european commission's ambitious new legislative package, shows the commission's determination to do everything possible to increase the reliability of the european automotive sector in terms of compliance with environmental standards. if this objection had been voted by the european parliament, the process of introducing new tests in real driving situations would have been delayed by two years. but we must act quickly. our aim is to reduce emissions of polluting gases while giving the european automobile industry time to adapt to these new conditions and to remain competitive on the international market.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution aims to oppose the european commission's draft decision on vehicle emission limits, in the context of euro 6 european legislation. the introduction of real driving tests, foreseen in this project, is a giant step unique in the world. nowhere else, not even in the united states, are vehicle emissions standards this ambitious. tomorrow, our citizens will breathe cleaner air and live in a less carbon-intensive environment. i therefore oppose this objection, which would be tantamount to postponing the application of the standards for another two years, which i consider to be counterproductive. the rules can be improved, but the protection of citizens cannot wait. the automobile manufacturers are engaged in a global industrial battle in which europe has its champions. the european automotive sector alone accounts for 12.1 million direct and indirect jobs on the continent. given that the role of the european parliament is to ensure that the rules are respected, while ensuring a transitional period which allows our companies to adapt without losing their competitiveness, i welcome the rejection of this objection.

in writing. ‒ following the volkswagen scandal, the commission, which was aware of the fraud well before the case broke, was forced to change the methods of vehicle approval and the conditions for pollutant emission tests. but the commission has reversed its own standards, under pressure from the car industry lobby worried about having to play cards on the table on their emissions. it did so by abandoning its own pollution thresholds, particularly for diesel, and by adopting 'guidelines' which permit exceedances of up to twice (more than 110%) the thresholds laid down. the way in which these tolerances were adopted is a scandal, since the commission has used an internal legislative procedure which only allows parliament to oppose this gift to the fraudulent manufacturers. i therefore opposed this double legislative gambit, which has been made at the expense of the anti-pollution standards already adopted, european democracy and the health of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection under rule 106 on emissions from passenger and light commercial vehicles. the volkswagen scandal revealed considerable discrepancies between laboratory and real driving emissions of pollutants for diesel engines. the commission's strict standards for emissions of pollutants do not yet require such tests. the requirement of this resolution is to request a new regulation, to be submitted by 1 april 2016, to mandate real-world testing at the earliest. the first recital refers to the cost of air pollution and justifies the need for increasingly stringent and costly technical standards. these requirements are questionable for two reasons: europe is becoming the least industrially-friendly region in the world; the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment. this text is therefore a unilateral requirement of political ecology, imposed on european industry alone, with serious consequences for a sector in difficulty.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because it requires, in a too hasty way, that a new regulation be ready by 1 april 2016 to impose pollution controls on diesel engines in real driving conditions and not in laboratories. i agree with the commission that the european parliament should be given the opportunity to express its views on the commission's proposals, and i am convinced that the commission will be able to do so.
in writing. ‒ dominique martin voted against this text. it follows the volkswagen scandal which revealed the discrepancies between pollutant emissions from laboratory tests and those under real driving conditions. the commission is setting unrealistic and unrealistic emission requirements, unilaterally demanding a political environment that is harmful to european industry, with serious consequences for a sector already in crisis.
in writing. ‒ the revelations about the polluting emissions of volkswagen vehicles and the suspicions that other manufacturers have been subjected to have raised legitimate indignation. a major sector of the european economy, largely supported by the public authorities during the crisis, has knowingly organised massive fraud to circumvent anti-pollution standards. the european commission has taken a crucial decision on this matter, without referring it to the member states or the european parliament: to give in to fraud in the automobile sector. rather than punishing those who do not comply with the prescribed standards, it prefers to raise the maximum level of permitted polluting gases (including nitrous oxide). in the wake of cop 21, the commission, one of the three pillars of its europe 2020 strategy being sustainable growth, is giving in to the car lobby without consulting it. to your relief, the tests will have to be conducted in real driving conditions. however, the arbitrary authorization given to manufacturers to exceed the permitted ceilings by 110% is unacceptable. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ the resolution opposes the adoption of the commission's draft regulation on vehicle emissions under the real driving emission (rde) package. the regulation allows derogations from the euro 6 emission limits for nox (nitrogen oxide), which leads to a lowering of the anti-pollution standards. increasing the nox emission limits for diesel vehicles will have serious consequences for the health of european citizens. air pollution causes more than 400 000 premature deaths a year in the european union and causes significant health costs of between €330 and €940 billion a year. in france, air quality causes more than 42 000 premature deaths and costs between 34 999 and 103 497 million euros per year. no2 emissions (mostly from diesel vehicles) are responsible for more than 7700 deaths a year in france. i am voting for this text, which opposes the harmful plans of the committee.
in writing. ‒ the volkswagen case has brought the issue of vehicle emissions back to the forefront of european politics. the commission's strict standards for actual pollutant emissions do not yet require real driving conditions (rde) tests. internal procedures in the commission are revising the limit values established in a 2007 regulation: the resolution called for a new regulation to be submitted by 1 april 2016 to require testing in real conditions at the earliest. i dispute this race to the standard for two reasons: firstly, europe is becoming the least industrially-friendly region in the world. the technical standards also show a contradiction in the fight against air pollution, as the eu is increasingly encouraging the flows that generate these emissions. i note that this text is a unilateral requirement of the political environment, and that is the sole responsibility of european industry, with serious consequences for a sector in crisis. so i objected to this objection.
in writing. this motion for a resolution on emissions from passenger and light commercial vehicles follows on from the volkswagen scandal. the revelations had implicated the company in falsifying its tests on pollutant emissions in the laboratory and in real driving conditions. the text recalls the cost of pollution (estimated at €940 billion per year), which would justify the introduction of ever more stringent standards. however, this text places the cost of this ecological burden on the european industries alone, which are already badly damaged. so i decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this objection to the draft regulation on emissions from passenger cars and light commercial vehicles. the objection, raised by the far left, the socialists, the greens and the centrists, would have unduly delayed the process initiated by the commission to replace laboratory tests with real driving tests. with this text, europe will become the first continent to have real-world emissions tests, which are much more accurate than laboratory tests, whose theoretical values are still far outdated. these new tests will provide greater visibility and legal certainty for car manufacturers who need to plan for the long term for their investments in emission reduction and environmental protection. they will also provide more reliable information to consumers on the pollution of the vehicles they buy. the regulation provides for new thresholds adapted to real driving. these thresholds will be gradually tightened.
in writing. ‒ in response to revelations of volkswagen's rigged tests, an objection to a change in the rules for measuring car emissions has been lodged. i voted against this objection, which in no way takes account of the new binding text, which everyone already considers to be a great step forward towards more efficient testing and respect for the environment.
in writing. ‒ the commission has decided to raise the emission limits for new cars, particularly diesel cars. it was the end of october, right after the volkswagen scandal. this has made many environmental ngos grin their teeth. in their desire to destroy european diesel know-how, the greens made it their mission to oppose this text and put an objection to the vote. but what they forgot to say is that the volkswagen scandal and the revised thresholds are two totally unrelated matters. the truth is that we made the choice to move towards tests in real driving conditions from 2017, and no longer in the laboratory where emissions and consumption were already lower. i even asked for it in my cars2020 report, back in 2013. it is both a way of regaining the confidence of motorists and of meeting our commitments to reduce vehicle pollution. but to do so, industry needs clarity and stability in legislation to invest in cleaner technologies. that objection was rejected, in a common sense move.
in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of the objection against the european commission's delegated act to increase the tolerance for polluting emissions from cars. parliament could have vetoed the commission's proposal to introduce a margin of tolerance of 2.1 for nitrogen oxide emission thresholds. unfortunately, this objection was not voted by the required majority, which i regret, and the commission's original proposal will therefore be implemented. but now we must look to the future and do everything we can to reduce this margin as quickly as possible, so that eventually it will be 1 if possible by 2020. this is not only a matter of respect for democracy and the european legislator, but also of the quality of air in europe, a major health and environmental issue. the work is also far from over with regard to real-world emissions testing (rde): now that the commission's delegated act has been adopted, i will be particularly vigilant about the proper application of rde tests, which is a prerequisite for the effective entry into force of pollution standards.
in writing. ‒ i am shocked by this vote of the european parliament. european manufacturers have already had almost 10 years to adapt to the new nitrogen oxide (nox) emission standards since parliament voted them in 2007. they have no excuse and parliament should have been tough on the manufacturers who, unlike others, have not invested in high-performance technologies and sustainable jobs. the commission's comitology decision was in clear breach of eu law by allowing manufacturers to exceed the legal nox thresholds by more than twice by 2020. we, the environmentalists, want to save our fellow citizens from respiratory problems rather than indulge the shareholders of the car manufacturers as the majority of the parliament has just decided.
in writing. ‒ i supported the commission's proposal to introduce a compliance factor for new real driving emissions tests. the proposal allows a temporary exceedance of the legal emission limits by 2.1 (exceeding 110%) until 2020 and by 1.5 (50%) after that date - to take account of any initial shortcomings of the new measurement system. this is already a marked improvement on the current situation, which is an overrun of around 400%. the commission also provides for an annual review clause to reduce the second compliance factor to 1 by 2023 at the latest and has committed to activating it systematically. i would also remind you that the vehicle typeapproval system is currently being revised. we will have a say in this and we will ensure that monitoring and the independence of the controls are strengthened. finally, i wanted to avoid the rejection of this text in order to ensure a rapid and realistic reduction in the levels of nitrogen oxide emissions currently emitted under real conditions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which calls for the rejection of the commission's draft regulation on emissions from passenger and commercial vehicles. the draft regulation aims to raise the limit for the emission of nitrogen oxides (nox) from diesel cars by up to 110%. in the context of volkswagen's emissions fraud, such an upward reassessment of the emission thresholds for carcinogenic pollutants is unacceptable. the majority of meps, however, chose to reject this resolution on the grounds that the commission regulation provides for tests under real conditions on vehicles. a paradoxical decision which does not guarantee adequate protection of the health of europeans.
in writing. ‒ when the volkswagen scandal broke a few months ago, the european parliament reacted firmly with a committee of inquiry and an unequivocal condemnation of the fraud orchestrated by the german manufacturer, concealing the real emissions of its vehicles. however, at this session, the right wing, by its vote, gave in to the lobby of the car manufacturers at the expense of the health of its citizens. the commission's proposal to create a right to pollute more was approved by meps, who voted against the objection of the left and environmentalists. the emissions of nitrogen oxides - fine particles that have been shown to be carcinogenic - could be 110% higher under real conditions than the legal emissions in the laboratory. public health justifies our refusal to create a right to pollute ever more. although industrial activity remains a key factor, it must adapt to respect both health and the environment. you can count on me to continue to fight for the preservation of air quality.

in writing. ‒ following the scandal of anti-pollution test fraud in the automotive sector, which primarily concerns the german manufacturer volkswagen, the european commission has proposed a draft regulation to raise the existing greenhouse gas emission standards for light vehicles. manufacturers have until 2020 to comply with the new legal standards for nitrogen oxides emissions, adopted in 2007, and during this period, to be type-approved, cars are allowed to emit up to 2 times more nitrogen oxides (nox) than the future legal standard. the european commission is not content with not punishing car manufacturers, who have had almost 10 years to comply with the standards, but intends to reward them for their bad practices in this area. this so-called resolution of objection tabled by my group, together with the greens and the s&d, alde and efdd groups, was intended to oppose this proposal for a regulation and to ask the commission to review its copy by 1 april 2016. i regret that a majority on the right of the european parliament, led by the fn members, voted against this resolution, which was rejected, thus favouring the interests of the automobile industry.
in writing. ‒ this text deals with the negotiations on the agreement on trade in services (tisa or acs). the aim of the agreement is to promote international trade in services and to create international regulations for such services. the aim of this text is, among other things, to make people believe that these international standards can be created while retaining the right to regulate or that it is possible to allow the personal data of europeans to circulate while protecting them. in addition, in the name of the frontier-free market, this treaty would have serious consequences for the sovereignty of the states. i am deeply opposed to the implementation of this treaty, which is a real danger to french public services and french businesses, and i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ tisa aims to establish a free trade agreement, similar to tafta (transatlantic free trade agreement) and tpp (trans-pacific free trade agreement), and is more specifically concerned with services. it is currently at the negotiating stage and includes the eu, the usa, norway, switzerland, canada, australia, new zealand, israel and turkey, chile, colombia, costa rica, mexico, panama, paraguay, peru, taiwan, hong kong and south korea and pakistan. the stated aim is to establish global standards for trade in services and a wide free trade area. in reality, it is mainly a question of dismantling part of the national public services by putting them in competition with private service industries. as i am, together with my colleagues from the national front, absolutely opposed to this world without economic frontiers which allows multinational companies to dictate their laws to states, and ultimately to the people, i naturally voted against it.
in writing. ‒ under negotiation, the tisa is a free trade agreement and "world standards" on trade in services, comprising no less than the eu, the usa, norway, switzerland, canada, australia, new zealand, israel, turkey, chile, colombia, costa rica, mexico, panama, paraguay, peru, taiwan, hong kong and south korea, pakistan. the aim is to remove barriers to trade in all services. the agreement therefore aims to prevent governments from introducing regulations if they impede the activities and profits of large service industries. public services will thus be put in competition with private services with the exception of the royal powers: justice, the army, the police, diplomacy. basic services such as health, education or water are considered economic services and may therefore be open to the market. public services will be put in competition with services provided by private companies in the same niche and will therefore be gradually 'dismantled' as the public rail service is today with the sncf. not to mention the lack of privacy protections.
in writing. ‒ i was of course strongly opposed to voting on this report which gives recommendations to the commission on the negotiations on the trade in services agreement (tisa). as a reminder, this agreement, which mainly concerns the us and the eu negotiating on behalf of the member states, aims to reduce barriers in the services market - 'barriers' being the deliberately chosen term as a pejorative, but which in reality refers to genuine protective standards. once again, in the name of the frontier-free market and the interests of the all-powerful multinationals, the report advocates, for example, unbridled competition in the telecommunications sector, which, as we know, would be to the detriment of european industries and consumers, and especially french. tisa is also a real danger to french public services and french companies and that is why it is scandalous that the states have no latitude in these negotiations which risk creating precariousness to the detriment of all sectors such as education or health. once again, the logic of the market seems to take precedence over the well-being of citizens, which is why the enf group called for the immediate halt of the tisa negotiations in this vote.
in writing. ‒ the agreement on trade in services (tac) is a free trade treaty which aims to reduce tariffs on services considerably and to harmonise global standards. the main danger of this agreement is that it puts public services, which are carried out in the public interest, in competition with private services which are required to be profitable. with the exception of the royal powers, namely the judiciary, the police and the army, education, health or water will be concerned. even if the member states of the union will benefit from the harmonization of customs duties, since the ones we set are far below those of the other signatory countries, the deregulation of public services will be extremely harmful to the most vulnerable among us who will not have enough money to pay for their children's schooling or to pay for social security. we are not fooled by the so-called red lines which the commission is not supposed to cross, because the european soviet union, destroyer of national identities and jobs, will stop at nothing to satisfy the demands and needs of the big multinationals. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted its position on the international agreement on trade in services. the agreement is being negotiated by 24 parties, including canada, the united states, japan and the european union. together they account for 70% of world trade in services. the union is the world's largest exporter of services. this agreement will benefit companies which will be able to export services more easily. this will generate growth and jobs. parliament stressed the importance of preserving european economic, social and environmental standards in these negotiations. certain services such as audio-visual, health and water must be excluded from this agreement. we must also be sure that our partners are fully reciprocal. we must be in a win-win situation. if we are to open our borders to trade in services, we must ensure that each side respects the same rules in the context of fair competition. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report proposes the european parliament's recommendations in the context of the negotiations for the international agreement on trade in services (tisa). the agreement brings together 24 parties (including the eu) and represents a third of the wto's members and 70% of world trade in services. while the revision of the wto general agreement on trade in services (gats) has stalled, due in particular to the blockage of the brics (brazil, russia, india, china), states in favour of strengthening trade in services began negotiations in 2013 on an gats. the european commission is negotiating on behalf of the union and its 28 members. we ask the european commission to exclude public and audiovisual services from liberalisation and guarantees on consumer rights and labour standards. finally, we believe that more transparency and better access for european companies to public contracts in third countries is needed. i supported this report because i believe that this agreement can open up new markets to stimulate our economy and our smes and must preserve our public and audiovisual services.
in writing. with this vote, the european parliament has set out strong guidelines for the european commission for the further negotiations on the agreement on trade in services (tsa). the agreement on trade in services is aimed at strengthening international rules and opening up markets in services such as digital, financial and transport services. i considered it particularly necessary to ensure that the conclusion of this trade agreement actually promotes growth and employment in europe and contributes to the competitiveness of our companies. in this context, it is of course essential to pay particular attention to smes.
in writing. ‒ this european parliament resolution is a clear message to the commission in charge of negotiating the agreement on the european union. the main objective of this agreement is to remove certain barriers to trade, on average 50% additional cost on products of european exporting companies. the agreement on trade in services should help defend and better protect european businesses abroad and support the internationalisation of smes. it must also allow for greater reciprocity in market access, some of our trading partners and wto member states having very protective and exclusive legislation. in this sense, it is important that the european union should have a european business act, modelled on the american business act, to give preference to eu companies on the community market, where necessary. at the same time, it is important that states can continue to protect public health, education and audiovisual services. the commission is therefore not authorised to make commitments on these dossiers. it is on the basis of compliance with all the recommendations set out in this resolution that our parliament will ratify or not the tisa agreement.
in writing. ‒ tisa is less well known than ttip - which provides for greater liberalisation of trade in services by updating the existing multilateral framework and adapting it to the context of the digital revolution ‒ is no less dangerous. its contents are negotiated in the greatest opacity. the report adopted by parliament on wednesday 3 february sets out a number of red lines and protective barriers. tisa cannot encourage tax evasion, social dumping or the lowering of labour standards. personal data must be protected, while public and cultural services must be excluded from this agreement. on the question of public services, i had pushed this strict exclusionary position through the intergroup on public services. i regret, however, that we were not able to agree on the need for positive lists, which are more protective than negative lists. the commission must now hear this vote by the elected members of the european parliament. if this is not the case, parliament has a veto right and may, as a last resort, oppose the adoption by the assembly of the final agreement submitted to it.
in writing. ‒ the tisa treaty, in the name of the principle of free trade and international trade in services, is to abolish what remains of regulation by states. the provisions of the act will put public services in competition with private services, with the exception of the royal authorities (justice, army, police, diplomacy). as the protection of personal data risks being undermined by the growing exchange of information, public services could be dismantled, as was the case with the railway in france. i reject the proliferation of good intentions, which have disastrous consequences, as in the case of the transatlantic treaty, and i have chosen to protect french public services and companies by opposing this text.

in writing. ‒ the trade in services agreement (tisa) aims to reduce as much as possible the barriers preventing companies from carrying out their service activities in another country. this is the extension of the general agreement on trade in services (gats) which was established in 1995. the right and the social democrats authorized the opening of these secret negotiations by a vote in the european parliament in 2013. in addition to the united states and the european union (on behalf of its 28 member states), 22 countries are currently involved in the negotiations. according to the wto definition, services concerned are all services in all sectors. the report does, however, propose the setting up of certain safeguards on public and audiovisual services, non-existent services (i.e. future environmental services), social security systems, water and health. but these safeguards are entirely hypocritical, since they are based on the european concept of public services, which advocates systematic competition. i maintain my opposition to this agreement and vote against it.
in writing. ‒ tisa, which aims to establish a free trade agreement, is more specifically about services, as are tafta and tpp. it is currently at the negotiating stage and includes the eu, the usa, norway, switzerland, canada, australia, new zealand, israel and turkey, chile, colombia, costa rica, mexico, panama, paraguay, peru, taiwan, hong kong and south korea and pakistan. the stated aim is to establish global standards for trade in services and a wide free trade area. it is in fact aimed above all at dismantling part of the national public services by putting them in competition with private service industries. as i am absolutely opposed to this world without economic frontiers, which allows multinational companies to dictate their laws to states and ultimately to the people, i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. the adoption of tisa would be a real legal chernobyl for our public services. the aim is to negotiate, in the utmost secrecy, the total liberalisation of services. the stated aim is clearly to strip the state of all economic competence. thus, certain services, such as water, education or health, could be subject to market laws and open to competition. this redding report obviously validates this process without a frown (is that surprising when one knows the pedicure of its rapporteur ?). this agreement, if adopted, would strip governments and people of all their fiscal and regulatory sovereignty, in favour of multinational corporations. it is therefore the counterpart of the transatlantic treaty's tertiary sector. i voted against this report, of course.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the negotiations on the services agreement under discussion between the european commission and 23 wto member countries. this text recalls the european parliament's guidelines and red lines in this area, including the essential maintenance of the quality of our standards and public services, which must be safeguarded. the eu is currently the world leader in trade in services but also an already very open market. the negotiations under way should enable our companies, and in particular smes, to expand further on international markets and to protect certain particularly vulnerable sectors of our european economies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the recommendations to the european commission on the negotiations for the agreement on trade in services, which aim to improve international regulation. the importance of such regulation is all the more emphasized by the very large majority which supported the recommendations.
in writing. ‒ i supported the report by my colleague viviane reding, former commissioner, on the trade in services agreement (tisa). the agreement is currently being negotiated by 23 members of the world trade organisation (wto), including the european union. in a globalised economy, services are becoming increasingly important and are a fundamental part of the economies of eu countries. the eu is the world's largest exporter of services (24% of the world market and a trade surplus of €170 billion), with tens of millions of people working in this sector in europe. this report is perfectly balanced and stresses above all the need for reciprocity and the fact that europe is a fairly open market in services and that now it is the other countries that must open up and use the same rules as we do.
in writing. ‒ in her report, viviane reding makes recommendations to the commission for the negotiation of this treaty, which are all red lines that the commission should not cross. as with all trade negotiations conducted by the commission, the tisa negotiations are characterised by a lack of transparency. this agreement on the liberalization of services between the european union and 22 partners does, however, entail many risks for european services. this resolution of the european parliament does not mean that the european commission is being given a blank check. on the contrary, it calls for greater transparency and for action to be taken against tax evasion and social dumping. the personal data of europeans must also be effectively protected. the european parliament calls for the exclusion of public services and audiovisual services from the scope of the agreement. as for cultural services, he advocated a "cautious approach". the report also calls for the preservation of the legislative capacity of the member states, rejecting the principle of standstill and cliquet clauses. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which does not express an opinion for or against the agreement on trade in services (acs or tisa in english), but which sets out the red lines for the european commission to follow during the negotiations. public services and audiovisual services must be clearly excluded from the future agreement and our cultural diversity must be protected. it is also about preserving the right to regulate of states and our legislation on data protection. but we must also keep the aim of reaching an ambitious agreement and remain aggressive in terms of market access. the european union is a leader in trade in services and the european market is already very open. we must therefore not liberalize further through these negotiations but win reciprocity, because it is essential that our companies have access to the markets of our partners. we will continue to follow these negotiations closely in order to defend the interests of european businesses and citizens.
in writing. ‒ tisa is, alongside tafta and ceta, the third free trade agreement currently being negotiated by the european commission. parliament decided, by this resolution, to set the red lines for the negotiations. this text provides a solid basis for defending fair trade. the commission now has a mandate from parliament to protect workers and consumers. transparency is required and citizens should have access to all information. tisa will not in any way facilitate social dumping, tax evasion or weaken our social and environmental standards. it will also have to exclude public and cultural services, while guaranteeing the protection of the personal data of our citizens. finally, this agreement will not restrict the right of the states to legislate, either by means of normative cooperation or by means of standstill and catch-up clauses. this resolution increases the pressure on the negotiators. the european parliament will vote on whether to ratify the agreement. if one of our red lines is crossed, tisa will not have my vote!
in writing. ‒ the tisa treaty is strategic. the aim is to deregulate the services market. public services will be put in competition with services offered by private companies in the same niche and will therefore be gradually 'dismantled'. international data flows will make europeans' private data travel all over the world (as it already does). data protection is therefore not a priority for them. audiovisual services, the media and publishing are excluded from the agreement. the eu is already very open in services, and it would be a matter of opening up other markets. the customs duties are 6% in the eu, 15% in canada and japan and 25% in south korea, so the rapporteur has every reason to be optimistic. this document follows the same strategy as the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip) with no different results. i vote against it.
in writing. ‒ this resolution concerns the european parliament's recommendations on the negotiations of the 'trade in services agreement', better known by its english acronym, the famous tisa. this agreement, like ttip and ceta, aims to increase trade liberalization, in this case in services. it has been negotiated by 50 states, including the european union, since march 2013 and 14 rounds of negotiations have already taken place in the greatest opacity. in a sign that the citizens' mobilization against these agreements is beginning to bear fruit, several amendments by the gue-ngl were adopted: the obligation for the parties to ratify the ilo conventions, the safeguarding of universal services, especially for island regions, and a mechanism for suspending the agreement in the event of violations of labour law. however, in addition to the lack of transparency in the negotiations, many problems remain: insufficient safeguards for public services, lack of oversight of financial services, the impact of the liberalization of the digital economy on data protection not taken into account enough... we in the igc have fought against this agreement, which is a continuation of all-round liberalization for the benefit of multinationals and against the interests of the people. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted against these resolutions on the strategy on gender equality and women's rights for the period after 2015. i am in favour of measures to ensure equal pay, but i am opposed to measures to introduce quotas, particularly in company boards, which are real constraints and do not always reflect the personal aspirations of women. in addition, requests for new proposals for gender equality have crept into the text, while the current texts are not yet being implemented.
in writing. ‒ this resolution calls on the commission to review its strategy on 'equality between men and women'. it deals with gender equality, feminization of boards of directors, women's rights, etc. however, there are some positive aspects to be noted: the need, for example, to take into account the different cultural contexts in different countries and regions, and the respect for the sovereignty of the states in the choice of legislation on wages... nevertheless, it is clear that the general orientation of the document contains a very ideological aim, namely the feminization of all sections of society without regard to the complementarity of the two sexes. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this debate as the committee had recommended in the background.
in writing. ‒ i support actions aimed at ensuring equal pay, in particular, provided that it is a question of aligning women's wages with men's and not the other way around. i am opposed to all quota arrangements, particularly in the boards of directors of companies. these mandatory quota policies turn women into adjustment variables to satisfy administrative constraints and deny their personal skills and aspirations. i finally supported the motion for a resolution which was the most respectful of the principle of subsidiarity and the cultural diversity of the member states, while aiming at fair pay for women: the proposal of the group of the european conservatives and reformists. i voted against the other proposals which call on the commission to propose new measures against gender equality when we are voting against it in every area to the point of absurdity. the promoters of the deadly gender ideology are never far away.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution which ignores common sense by asking the commission for new commission proposals on gender equality, even though the current texts on the subject are not being applied. the legislative overriding will not ensure equal treatment in particular in terms of pay. it is also up to the member states to propose solutions, especially since the socio-cultural circumstances in this area differ greatly from one nation to another. i am also opposed to the principle of quotas for women on boards because i believe it is an insult to the ability of women to rise to the highest positions on the basis of their merits and talents alone. women should never be reduced to the status of victims, as is unfortunately the case in some passages of the beijing declaration. however, i welcome the fact that the importance of respecting equality between men and women, taking into account their differences and complementarity, is being recalled.
in writing. - confusing equality with egalitarianism, this motion for a resolution uses absolutely ridiculous data to highlight the inequalities suffered by women: parttime work without even knowing whether it is desired or suffered; the employment rate, lower among women than among men without knowing whether it is explained by the desire of some of them to remain inactive in order to take care of the education of their children. although we are fully in favour of equal treatment in terms of pay, for example, and it is essential to combat all forms of discrimination and violence against women, i voted against this motion for a resolution which does not provide any solution to the problem.
in writing. ‒ equality between men and women must become a reality within the european union. we need to put in place an eu strategy for equality between men and women after 2015 that is in line with the principle of subsidiarity. we cannot continue to see cases of discrimination against women. the european union must be a model in this area if it is to be able to export these values worldwide. i voted in favour of this resolution.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am pleased to see that the debate today is about the key role of local and regional authorities in the development of our territories and, above all, about cities as a source of growth and employment, and therefore deals with urban policy. as you know, in 2015, 40 percent of the population of the european union lived in cities. an effective urban policy is a necessity. i would like to draw your attention to the concerns of certain regions of the union which have seen, since the financial crisis, a widening of the development gap between urban and rural areas. this is even more true in the case of the outermost regions, which - as you know - have many handicaps. cohesion policy must therefore retain its original spirit of territorial solidarity, which it is important not to call into question. the complementarity between the different territories is a reality, and this requires a transversal approach, guided by the principle of subsidiarity, both at european level and at the level of each member state.

author. madam president, on the occasion of the spring of peace in 2011, almost half of the bahraini population took to the streets. they were mostly shiites, an oppressed majority, but their demands were democratic and social. they failed to find an answer, and saudi arabia intervened to restore order. ngos estimate the number of political prisoners at 3,000. this country has the second largest prison population in the arab world. the general population is seeing its freedoms curtailed. the fight against terrorism is also being used here. the country seemed on the way to abolishing the death penalty, but ten death sentences have just been handed down. the loss of nationality is also exploited, with more than 208 cases in a few months. if the bahraini authorities are truly willing to embark on the path of reform, it is time they implemented the 26 recommendations of the independent commission of inquiry and put an end to the practice of torture and the convictions obtained on this basis. progress is judged on the facts and at this point, the least we can say is that in bahrain we are not going in the right direction.

on behalf of the enf group. mr president, the case of the eures platform, the european network of employment services, is moving forward. in doing so, the negative points appear more clearly behind the apparently positive reasons for the proposal, which are the transparency of the labour market, the technological leap in networks with automatic matching of offers and cvs associated with new services, or the increased coordination of trade between member states. but in fact, through what you call, with humour, 'areas of labour shortage or surplus', it is possible to reveal a major hidden danger: that of clearly indicating to potential economic competitors the areas of strength or weakness of europe. the holding of categorical targeted listings by private and public law bodies may be agreed at member state level, but at european level it constitutes a major economic weapon as well as a powerful surveillance tool. it is therefore at the level of states and in the framework of targeted international partnerships that trade can take place in favour of workers who are chosen for their skills and who move freely.

in writing. in the name of the sacrosanct 'free movement', the eu wants to set up a structured cooperation network allowing all citizens access to all job opportunities. the parliament's proposal mentions, in bulk, the strengthening of cooperation between the public employment services (spe), the integration of non-governmental organisations, an improvement of eures, the creation of a european coordination office... clear problems are emerging: logistical (matching offers and requests at european level poses obvious problems, especially in times of crisis), financial (matching offers and requests will be expensive) and above all human because eures, this "european employment pole", promotes blackmail on mobility, according to which an unemployed person would not want to work if he is not ready to take up an offer in europe, wherever it may be. rather than institutionalizing job insecurity and uprooting, support should be given to smes, which account for 90% of jobs in europe, and the conditions for job creation should be created in the member states. an individual, much to the commission's displeasure, will always prefer to work close to home!

in writing. ‒ this report is a draft recommendation on the proposal for a council decision authorising austria and malta to accede to the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters. this convention simplifies the service of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters in other signatory states. it is an effective instrument that streamlines global judicial relations. austria and malta have expressed their wish to join, and the eu must respect their sovereign choice. that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ the hague convention simplifies the service of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters in other signatory states. since it applies only to relations with non-eu countries, it simplifies global judicial relations. austria and malta have expressed their wish to join, so i did not oppose it. the convention does not allow membership of international organisations. however, following the adoption of regulation (ec) no 1393/2007 of the european parliament and of the council of 13 november 2007 on cross-border service of documents (the 'regulation'), the union has acquired exclusive external competence in this area, in accordance with article 3 (2) tfeu, which states that 'the union shall also have exclusive competence to conclude an international agreement where such conclusion ... is likely to affect common rules or alter their scope'. it is on the basis of this article that the decision in question was put to the vote of the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ with the adoption of regulation (ec) no 1393/2007, the union acquired exclusive external competence in the field of membership of an international organisation. the text calls for austria and malta to be authorized to accede to the hague convention of 15 november 1965 on the service abroad of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters. twenty-six member states already apply the convention and overall the convention has been widely adopted (eu, china, russia, switzerland, etc.). the convention is an effective instrument which streamlines global judicial relations. in theory, this authorization to join is to strengthen the eu, but in reality we must respect the sovereign will to join expressed by austria and malta. so i decided to vote for it.

in writing. - i voted in favour of the uspaskich report. the hague convention of 15 november 1965 establishes a system for the service of judicial and extrajudicial documents in civil and commercial matters in other signatory states. it should be clarified that it applies only to documents intended for or emanating from countries outside the european union. twenty-six of the 28 member states already apply the convention. the two member states which have not yet applied it, namely austria and malta, have expressed their wish to join. since the hague convention of 15 november 1965 has proved its usefulness in the crossborder service of documents and since it is in the interest of both the european union as a whole and the two member states in question to have a uniform system in this area in their relations with third countries, it is proposed that parliament give its consent to the decision authorising the accession of austria and malta to the said convention.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this proposal for a regulation on a european network of employment services, workers' access to mobility services and further integration of labour markets. the system is facing many problems. firstly, it would tend to encourage the "brain drain" which would increase inequalities between the different european areas (east, west, north, south). secondly, more than an obvious logistical and resource problem, this network would trigger the uprooting of workers and the precariousness of employment. finally, the eures system for job mobility would encourage blackmail against mobility and would pose major difficulties with regard to unemployment benefits. i am deeply opposed to the single market in employment and i opposed this text.
in writing. ‒ this text is consistent with the eu's plan to create a single labour market based on one of the founding pillars of the eu, namely the free movement of workers. in this case, the aim is to set up a structured cooperation network allowing all european citizens to have access to all job vacancies. the measures mentioned include strengthening cooperation between public employment services, integrating non-public bodies (trade unions, chambers of commerce), improving access to the eures portal and creating a european coordination office (to collect information from the national offices, train its staff and make surpluses and shortages in the different regions). the employment and social innovation programme (easi) is funding this scheme. i voted against this report because i believe that this system encourages the uprooting of workers, that it imposes the single european labour market as the only alternative to unemployment and that it institutionalizes the precariousness of employment.
in writing. ‒ since the free movement of workers is one of the eu's tenets, the establishment of a structured cooperation network allowing all european citizens access to all job opportunities appears to be a favourable mechanism for the achievement of a single labour market. among the many problems raised by this report is the risk that the system in question will increase inequalities between southern and eastern europe and northern and western europe by encouraging 'brain drain'. worse, eures "european job centre" would encourage blackmail of mobility, whereby an unemployed person would not want to work unless he or she is ready to take up an offer in europe, wherever it may be; the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's social security system is in place. finally, it encourages the uprooting of workers, imposes the single european labour market as the only alternative to unemployment and institutionalizes the precariousness of employment. that is why i voted against this report.
