in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the van bossuyt report entitled 'towards better regulation of the single market'. this own-initiative report aims to examine ways of improving internal market regulation in order to make it more effective. it analyses how to make the whole policy cycle more efficient in the interests of smes and consumers, taking into account the existing tools of the single market (impact analysis, consultation process, implementation, monitoring and problem solving, enforcement of legislation, ex post evaluation and review). the report recalls that improving the regulation of the internal market is a shared responsibility of the eu institutions. it also states that good legislation requires effective and efficient work throughout the policy cycle, and in particular stresses the importance of transposition and implementation of the regulation (which are an integral part of the means to enjoy the benefits of the single market). it also stresses that a single market that supports production, innovation and trade promotes growth.
in writing. ‒ improving the regulation of the european single market is essential to allow business development and enhanced trade. this improvement can only be undertaken if all the european institutions concerned are committed to the reform of the regulation. this text, which i voted for, examines the various possibilities for improvement available to the european parliament and the other institutions. it is therefore part of our commitment to simplify the regulation of the internal market.

in writing. ‒ the european single market is a major tool which, in order to foster growth and job creation, needs improved and simplified regulation. that is why i voted in favour of the report which sets out the means by which these objectives can be achieved. we therefore call for the quality of impact assessments or the consultation process with economic and civil society actors to be improved. finally, it is clear from the text that improving the regulation of the single market does not mean eliminating or reducing the ambition of certain rules, particularly in the field of consumer protection. simplification and efficiency must be the guiding principles of all public action, serving the actors that make the single market work.

in writing. ‒ education is a fundamental human right and a public good which must be accessible to all. that said, if there is one area where european cooperation works, it is in higher education, apprenticeship and youth training, particularly through the erasmus programme. since its inception in 1987, there have been many programmes which have enabled millions of young europeans to move and pursue higher education abroad. these programmes have undoubtedly contributed to european integration, facilitated the personal and critical development of students and improved the learning of new languages, thus helping to prepare them for the world of work. today there seems to be a need to encourage mobility in vocational training. this is what is being proposed in particular in the framework of the erasmus+ programme and i fully support this initiative of the commission. youth unemployment is a real challenge and its solution is a societal challenge. let us encourage young people to find work placements and to study abroad, and they will come back richer with a european culture which we must preserve and export.
in writing. ‒ this report on erasmus+ is quite satisfactory, and i am pleased that my colleagues have incorporated in it the realistic proposals i had tried to put to the committee, including the need to rely on the chambers of trades and crafts to promote vocational training. other good elements are included, such as the essential involvement of small and medium-sized enterprises in the construction of learning paths; the commission has also proposed the recognition of school curricula between countries, in particular through the system of 'credits'. i will, however, have some reservations. first of all, i am not sure that increasing mobility alone will solve the problem of unemployment, especially youth unemployment. i believe that a number of sensible measures must be taken beforehand: ensuring that education is adapted to the needs of the labour market, in particular by refocusing guidance counselling; acquiring basic knowledge: i would remind you that, according to the latest joint report by the council and the commission on the follow-up of the et2020 strategic framework, 22% of 15-year-olds in the eu have a mathematical deficit and 18% have a serious deficit in reading.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the common rules for the application of the external dimension of the cfp. the european union is an important market for fishery products, being the main importer of these products with a consumption of 11% of world fishery production. the text reaffirms that multilateralism and international cooperation must be the preferred platforms for the effective and sustainable management of global fisheries resources. the external dimension of the cfp needs to be consistent with its internal dimension of the union in order to carry an ambitious vision. in bilateral agreements, the focus should be on environmentally, economically and socially sustainable fisheries. the external dimension of the cfp must be based on fair and mutually beneficial relations, but also on reliable data on fish stocks. i supported this report, which recalls that the union must promote, within the external dimension of the cfp, very high environmental and social standards such as the promotion of sustainable aquaculture or the inclusion of instruments to protect workers and guarantee decent working conditions.
in writing. ‒ the main objective is to know the impact of the external dimension of the european union in order to determine whether the fisheries are environmentally, socially and economically sustainable. the so-called 'external' fisheries, outside european waters, account for 25% of european products. it is therefore essential to ensure that our fishermen have the best possible conditions for their work, while respecting marine biodiversity. the report states that trade relations with any country engaged in illegal fishing will be interrupted and the eu will pay only 35% of access fees, compared with 65% before. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund for volvo trucks. the report aims to provide eur 1.793 million in aid for the reintegration into the labour market of 500 of the 647 workers made redundant by volvo group trucks operations, its four suppliers and subcontractors in sweden. it is interesting to note that the report mentions competition from asian manufacturers as the main cause of these redundancies, while the eu spends its time negotiating free trade agreements with these countries, thus increasing the rope to hang us. indeed, china has become the world's number 1 commercial vehicle producer with a market share of 34,1%. if the egf is a sham designed to timidly mask the consequences of the union's trade policies and to relieve large companies of their responsibilities, this aid seems useful for the reintegration of workers who do not have to suffer the free trade whims of the european commission.

in writing. i voted in favour of this first eu amending budget for the financial year 2016, which provides for the creation of a permanent mechanism for emergency humanitarian aid in the eu. this measure will help to alleviate the refugee crisis in greece, the first country in the union to be affected by it. there was no previous mechanism for internal humanitarian aid within the union, unlike in third countries, and it was in the context of the current humanitarian emergency in the union that an allocation of eur 100 million in commitments and eur 80.2 million in payments was proposed. this amount, which is mainly intended for civil society working on the ground, will complement and support the member states' response to this crisis.

mr president, in parallel with this objection, i myself had proposed, on behalf of the enf group, an objection to the renewal of the authorization of glyphosate, an initiative which was not followed by the other groups, who preferred to present a joint text. however, we have seen today that there are great divisions within the political groups. i therefore maintain that the european commission has exceeded its powers in proposing to renew the authorization of glyphosate for several reasons. the scientific background and the study by the international cancer research centre urge us to be cautious of a product that is likely to cause cancer and is everywhere. this caution should be at the heart of the commission's thinking, as the european ombudsman reminded him. finally, it is not acceptable to postpone publication of the list of co-formulants which increase the toxicity of the product to an unknown date. commercial formulation and co-formulants are at the heart of all the concerns. the vote today, however, is so far from the spirit of the text and the whole point of the objection.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text on the objection to the renewal of the glyphosate authorisation because i consider that the value of this objection is only symbolic. the text, as finally voted, advocates a seven-year authorisation of glyphosate and suggests very few restrictive provisions, whereas this product has been repeatedly identified as very dangerous, both for consumers and farmers. i therefore voted against this text, which, moreover, does not take account of the precautionary principle and does not oblige the commission to act on parliament's requests in this area.
in writing. ‒ i regret that the european parliament did not follow our committee on the environment, public health and food safety, which had called for a ban on glyphosate. the european right has succeeded in poisoning the european citizens for another seven years. glyphosate, which was declared a "probable carcinogen" by the world health organization (who) in march 2015, remains the world's best-selling herbicide. several european countries, including denmark, the netherlands, and sweden, have decided to ban or restrict its use because of its possible effects, ranging from birth defects to autism to kidney problems. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road, rail and inland waterway. the urgent need in the very short term is to help producers using glyphosate by offering them alternative solutions. this requires support based both on the use of the least dangerous products and, above all, on the development of bio-controls and a gradual change in production models.
in writing. ‒ meps from the national front had tabled an objection to the european commission's authorisation of the renewal of glyphosate, an active substance considered carcinogenic by the who and found in high concentrations in food. glyphosate is the basis of a herbicide that is widespread in france and widely used. i maintained my position by opposing the new text of the objection proposed in strasbourg. the house also welcomed the commission's proposal to limit the use of the product to professionals, such as farmers. nevertheless, the renewal period of 7 years finally decided upon does not encourage the chemical industries to look for alternatives, while the health of our farmers and consumers is at stake! i would have liked to have voted for an immediate ban on this substance, but the crisis in our agriculture is serious enough not to put further pressure on french farmers. however, the original text has been profoundly altered, and we have to object to this objection, which has been distorted from its original meaning.
in writing. ‒ because of the lingering concerns about the carcinogenic and endocrine disrupting properties of glyphosate, i voted to reduce the duration of use to 7 years, instead of the 15 initially proposed, and for professional use only. this timeframe is to allow the executive to launch an independent study on the overall toxicity and classification of glyphosate and to clarify the hazardous nature of the substance. nevertheless, the european union must stop legislating chemical molecule by chemical molecule and would be more effective in acting globally on harmful substances through a single regulation. this approach would have the benefit of increasing the understanding of standards and adaptation of users of these substances. finally, it is necessary to ensure that the application of these standards is the same throughout europe and that it does not encourage technological dumping between eu member states.
in writing. ‒ in the name of the precautionary principle with regard to a product that the international agency for research on cancer has described as carcinogenic, i support the objection to the renewal of the approval of the active substance glyphosate. the arguments put forward by the scientific community such as the german heinrich böll foundation which this year established a high exposure of the most vulnerable groups to glyphosate show that the commission, by authorising this antibiotic substance while the fight against the widespread use of antibiotics is a recurring topic in european regulation, has exceeded its areas of competence, which legitimises this objection.
in writing. ‒ many of our colleagues, before voting on this resolution, were probably unaware, before the subject was put on the agenda, that glyphosate is a non-selective herbicide absorbed by leaves and having a widespread action, formerly produced under a patent, this patent, we were told, having fallen into the public domain in 2000. but that wasn't the point. in the debate in this house on whether or not the commission should renew the approval of the substance, two opposing arguments were put forward, one guided by the precautionary principle and advocating non-approval, while the other believes that the scientific studies carried out on the harmfulness of the product are sufficient to allow its dissemination. i am not an expert on the subject myself, so i took the precautionary approach and voted against the approval, even if i had to reconsider my position if further conclusive studies were to show that this caution was not necessary.
in writing. ‒ i opposed this text which, although originally objecting to the renewal of the approval of glyphosate, has in the end led to its authorisation for a period of 7 years, and only suggests some restrictive provisions. it did not, for example, ban the use of glyphosate in public parks and gardens. i would remind you that the international agency for research on cancer has previously described glyphosate as a 'probable carcinogen', a caution which the european food safety authority does not share. the risks associated with glyphosate are well established, particularly in its commercial formulations. given the divergent views on this issue between iarc and efsa on the subject, the doubt persists and calls for the precautionary principle to be respected.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the objection to the renewal of the authorisation of glyphosate because i consider that the value of this objection is purely symbolic. the text, as finally voted, advocates an authorisation of glyphosate for seven years and suggests very few provisions to restrict this product on the market, despite the fact that it has been repeatedly identified as very dangerous both for consumers and for farmers. i therefore voted against this text, which does not take account of the precautionary principle and does not oblige the commission to act on parliament's requests.
in writing. ‒ in this motion for a resolution, a left-wing majority wanted to object to the renewal of the authorisation of glyphosate. i do not think that the commission has any right to interfere in the negotiations on the gatt agreement. in addition, without a technically and economically viable alternative, this decision would have a counterproductive impact in terms of health and environmental safety. i therefore welcome the adoption of the amendments which we tabled with my colleagues from the epp group, in order to preserve the competitiveness of the agricultural sector while guaranteeing a high level of health security. we propose to reduce the duration of authorisation from 15 to 7 years, to take account of the lack of consensus among scientists, but also the time needed for agricultural professionals to adapt to possible regulatory changes. we also call for stricter controls on the use of glyphosate, limiting it to professionals, strengthening farmers' training and banning its use before harvest. finally, we must be able to revise the authorisation at any time if new scientific evidence justifies the product being banned. in view of these facts, i supported this resolution.

in writing. ‒ declared probable carcinogen by the world health organization (who) in march 2015, glyphosate remains the world's best-selling herbicide. this dangerous product is present in more than 750 herbicides and was recently detected in 44% of european citizens who have never been in direct contact with the herbicide: it is simple, a good part of our food chain is contaminated. despite this, the european food safety authority (efsa) has found the carcinogenic risk of glyphosate to be "unlikely". but the studies used by the commission are "at best" sponsored by the agrochemical industry, and at worst written by the industry. in the face of this risk, it is our responsibility to apply the precautionary principle and to withdraw dangerous molecules from the market. the urgent need in the very short term is to help producers using glyphosate by offering them alternative solutions. this requires support based both on the use of the least dangerous products and, above all, on the development of bio-controls and a gradual change in production models. i therefore voted against the text to the commission to re-introduce glyphosate on the market for 7 years.
in writing. ‒ glyphosate is a systemic, non-selective herbicide that destroys all plants. it is now the most widely produced herbicide in the world, with its use increasing 260 times in the last 40 years from 3 200 tonnes in 1974 to 825 000 tonnes in 2014. as a result of this widespread use, "glyphosate and/or its residues have been found in water, soil, food, non-food products and the human body (including urine and breast milk)". in march 2015, the international agency for research on cancer (iarc) classified glyphosate as a "probable human carcinogen" (group 2a). but in november 2015, the european food safety authority (efsa) stated that it is unlikely that this substance poses a carcinogenic threat to humans. strangely, efsa has always refused to make these studies public, on the grounds that their publication would be detrimental to commercial interests. the resolution called for the publication of these studies and for the authorisation of glyphosate not to be renewed. unfortunately, the right wing's intrigue has led to the passage of an amendment allowing glyphosate for another seven years. in these circumstances i shall vote against.

in writing. while the un international cancer research centre (composed of some of the world's most renowned experts, whose independence is guaranteed) had given an unfavourable opinion on glyphosate (considered to be probably carcinogenic), efsa (a european agency whose impartiality is relative and whose opinion is based only on studies carried out by industry) decided to give the substance in question the benefit of the doubt. scientific studies show that glyphosate, which is part of monsanto's roundup, leads to an increase in rare cancers in male rats exposed, thus eliminating the random bias. the meta-studies conducted all conclude, however, that the molecule is dangerous. considering that this report is aimed at not renewing the authorisation of glyphosate and concerned about the precautionary principle, i decided to vote in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the kalniete report. the report is divided into four main parts: defending europe's states, societies and values; the union's first objective is to ensure the security of its citizens and its territory, while preserving its values and its model of society and defending its fundamental interests; stabilising europe's wider neighbourhood the union must assume its responsibilities by closing the security gap in its neighbourhood and in the neighbourhood of our neighbours and by respecting its enlargement commitments; become a more present actor in a multipolar world the union should aim to become a 'decision-maker' that sets effective rules for global multilateral governance, which requires strengthening cooperation with regional actors on global threats, maintaining a comprehensive approach to foreign policy (building synergies between different 'external policies'), but also building on the union's fundamental principles and interests; interact with the union, national parliaments and european citizens; parliament called for the introduction of a review clause (every five years) and stressed the importance of the european parliament and national parliaments, which should ensure joint control.
in writing. ‒ the attacks in brussels on 22 march have once again demonstrated the importance of further developing european security. the adoption of the pnr is another step in the right direction. the high representative of the union for foreign affairs and common security policy is responsible for the conduct of european security policy, but the european parliament has a role to play. as such, i voted in favour of this report which sets out parliament's contribution to the high representative's strategy on security. we thus make the defence of the union's states, societies and values our priority, together with the stabilisation of the union's neighbourhood and the strengthening of the union's presence in a multipolar world. the resolution also calls for the establishment of a european union defence and security policy, and calls for better interaction between the european parliament, on the one hand, and national parliaments and european citizens, on the other.
in writing. following the adoption by the eu of a european security strategy, which identifies a series of threats to the union's security interests, this report endorses the strengthening of security measures and proposes the strengthening of the union's defence capabilities. despite some positive elements on the defence of human rights and the union's values, the report supports an advanced militarisation of europe, with increases in member states' military budgets, to the detriment of other policies, and considers, among other things, that the usa is the eu's main strategic partner, all reasons which justified my vote against this report.
in writing. the report takes the pretext of the current developments in the world, the tensions and crises that are taking place there, to call, surprisingly, for the construction of a federal europe whose defence policy and diplomacy would be entirely subordinated to nato. i, for my part, am in favour of a free and sovereign france, determined to defend the interests of the french people against any outside power. i am therefore clearly not in a position to support a text which is so ideologically harmful and obsolete, and which is not at all up to the challenges of the contemporary world. i therefore vote against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this contribution by the european parliament to the new eu comprehensive security strategy, led by federica mogherini, high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. in the field of defence, we call on the eu to strengthen its autonomy, complementing nato's fields of action. stabilising europe's wider neighbourhood must also be a priority. the european union and its member states must also be made more present in a multipolar world marked by constant threats. finally, interaction at all levels (the union, national parliaments and citizens) will be the condition for the success of this new global strategy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which is the european parliament's contribution to the review of the eu's global strategy on foreign and security policy to be presented by the high representative in june. it is crucial that the union identifies and affirms its strategic interests on the international stage. the union's priority must be to stabilise crises in its neighbourhood. the union must be more involved in its neighbourhood to ensure its security. as such, i supported this text which calls for the union and the member states to improve their defence capabilities and to devote at least 2% of gdp to defence spending by 2024. it is essential that the union should have greater strategic autonomy and develop a genuine european intelligence capacity. it is necessary to recall that the union has set itself the objective of being the world leader in multilateral governance and in respecting and promoting international law. it must continue to promote effective multilateralism based on the rule of law. in view of the rapidly changing challenges facing the union, the text calls for the strategy to be reviewed every five years.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report: foreign policy is a competence of the states. the eu does not need to add to the confusion in an already unstable area such as central asia.

in writing. ‒ the countries of central asia are of considerable strategic importance to the european union. a review of the union's strategy towards the region is necessary to strengthen bilateral and multilateral relations with all the countries that make up the region. it is important to develop action plans adapted to the specificities of each partner, given the differences between these countries. it is also very important to strengthen the promotion of the rule of law, democracy and fundamental rights in the region. i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the review of the union's strategy for central asia in 2015. the first point is to recall the union's strategic, economic and political interest in strengthening relations with the countries of central asia. the text calls for closer ad hoc collaboration, closer monitoring of the use of funds and a concrete action plan with measurable criteria to assess progress made or to be made. democracy, human rights and the rule of law must be the union's top priorities in the region. it is regrettable that very little progress has been made in the area of democracy and the rule of law, particularly in the areas of freedom of expression, women's rights and freedom of the press. i supported this text which calls for intensifying economic and trade relations with these countries. it also involves greater cooperation in the energy sector, since central asia is a potential additional source of energy security for the union. finally, it is essential to strengthen the union's cooperation with central asia in the security field in order to combat terrorism effectively.

in writing. - zika virus is an emerging virus transmitted by mosquitoes. after an initial outbreak in 2007 in micronesia, it has now spread to the south american continent, and in 2016, who "declared the zika virus outbreak a public health emergency of global concern". in addition, a causal link between zika virus infection during pregnancy and microcephaly is strongly suspected, although not yet scientifically proven. the resolution also supports "the call by the united nations for the repeal of laws and policies that restrict women's access to sexual and reproductive health services and rights in violation of international standards". but the resolution also stresses "the need for further research into the possible link between microcephaly and the larvicide pyriproxyfen", (manufactured by a monsanto partner to protect against rabies). i am voting for this text, which does not exclude any possible explanation.

in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the zika virus outbreak. in february, the who declared the epidemic a public health emergency of global concern. a growing number of preliminary studies suggest that zika virus is one of the causes of microcephaly - a condition in which babies are born with smaller than average skulls and delayed brain development - as well as guillain-barré syndrome. currently, there is no specific treatment or vaccine. the consequences of this virus can be life-changing for the victims, and it is urgent to take all the necessary measures to combat it, to help the most affected regions and to prevent its spread in europe. in particular, research should be conducted on preventive measures, treatments and the suspected link between the virus and microcephaly. i welcome the commission's decision to mobilise eur 10 million for this purpose. finally, awareness-raising and information work is needed, both among citizens and healthcare professionals.

commission very much welcomes the resolution on bosnia and herzegovina. i would like once again to congratulate the rapporteur, cristian preda, on his high-quality report and to thank all the members who have actively participated in the debate, not only today, but also in committee, and have shown a keen interest in bosnia and herzegovina’s european future. the commission takes note of this resolution and will take parliament’s views into account, including those expressed today. we specifically share parliament’s view that the country’s authorities need to continue with their determination in pursuing socio-economic reforms, including their effective implementation and making steady progress towards the european union. this would be particularly necessary to enable the council to decide whether to seek the commission’s opinion on the merits of bosnia and herzegovina’s application. at the same time, the commission is also looking to the country’s authorities to ensure the functionality of the coordination mechanism on eu affairs and to adapt the saa, following croatia’s accession to the european union. let me also mention that the commission has taken note of parliament’s call for internal reform within the country based on several principles such as decentralisation and federalism. however, in line with our approach to all enlargement countries, including past eu enlargements, the commission reiterates that the european union has no competence regarding the internal structure of a state. what matters is the capacity of a country to meet all its obligations as a future european union member. it will be up to bosnia and herzegovina’s authorities and citizens to decide how best to comply with the european union membership requirements. likewise, i would like to emphasise that, as is the case with any country aspiring to the eu, the commission will particularly insist that the country fully abide by the principles of non—discrimination against its citizens, irrespective of their ethnicity, belief or gender, in line with the european union acquis. finally, i would like to stress that the commission will spare no effort in supporting bosnia and herzegovina on its path towards the european union. this also applies when it comes to using eu money efficiently and in a sustainable targeted manner, but there has to be a national strategy in the relevant areas. that is what we are discussing with the bosnia and herzegovina authorities: there has to be an idea of how to best use the money in order to ensure not only that it will have an impact on the country, but also that it will provide the necessary european added value. the commission will keep parliament informed in the coming months on further i'm the reporter. madam president, we are here tonight in the house to debate the draft directive on the protection of professional know-how, know-how, confidential commercial information, all those things commonly known as 'business secrets'. we are in particular responsible for discussing among ourselves the agreement reached in the trilogue on this important draft directive. this is the first time that we have had the opportunity to present the result of the trilogue agreement in plenary. the main objectives of this directive are to combat economic and industrial espionage and the looting of our european companies, to protect our innovation and research and to defend our european competitiveness. of course, the aim is to provide a common legal basis, common european rules for all economic operators in the european union, in order to ensure a stable and secure legal framework. it is a question of combating the legal fragmentation which currently exists in the european internal market, which we must of course complete and improve its functioning. the patchwork of different national legislative systems, which are disparate, leads to instability and legal uncertainty. the idea is therefore to have the most uniform protection possible at european level of those trade secrets, professional know-how, know-how, strategic and commercial information which are of value, which represent the intangible heritage of our companies and which are important for their economic development and for the development of our jobs in europe. we have been keen to support these main objectives together in the european parliament, particularly in the legal affairs committee. we were of course also concerned - and were fully determined in this respect - to ensure that the protection of trade secrets could not in any way affect the exercise of fundamental freedoms, such as the fundamental rights of freedom of expression and information, the foremost of which are, of course, freedom of the press and pluralism of the media, and which are also, for example, the right of workers to be represented by trade union representatives, who may be made aware of trade secrets, or the right to professional mobility. after a very long period of work - more than 18 months of work in three parliamentary committees - we have managed to agree on these major priorities and to substantially amend, transform and improve the original proposal for a directive as presented to us by the european commission. we have transformed it, we have improved it, in particular, and especially in a spirit, i would say, of very positive, very constructive and genuine collegiality on the part of the members of the committee on legal affairs, and then of the european parliament's negotiating team, who went to discuss, negotiate, engage in a sometimes quite violent confrontation with the council, strengthen fundamental freedoms, strengthen protection, of course, in terms of freedom of expression and freedom of information, which must be granted both to journalists, especially investigative journalists, and to whistleblowers whose activities must be able to be exercised freely and conscientiously. and it is thanks to the extremely positive contribution of all the fictitious rapporteurs who, together with me, were very active participants in the negotiating team that we obtained, in the negotiations with the council, a text which took up 100% of the recommendations and red lines of the european parliament. it is therefore now a balanced text, which protects not only what is essential for our companies, their professional know-how, their intangible heritage which is so valuable for their economic development, but also the fundamental freedoms and the exercise of the profession of journalist and the activities of whistleblowers. i therefore call for a frank and massive support for this balanced and fair text which we have drawn up together.
member of the commission. – madam president, i would like to thank the legal affairs committee and warmly congratulate the rapporteur, ms constance le grip, and the shadow rapporteurs for the excellent and successful work on the trade secrets protection directive. both the work and the constructive spirit in the negotiations facilitated reaching satisfactory compromise and hopefully, if this house votes in favour tomorrow, the swift adoption of the directive at first reading. trade secrets are an important part of businesses’ intellectual capital in the knowledge economy. trade secrets are widely used to obtain a competitive advantage, to undertake research and development activity or to innovate in general. for instance, secret know-how is licensed every day between business partners as part of technology transfer deals, and trade secrets are essential for success. every patent first started as a trade secret. this widespread use of trade secrets is general to all businesses, but smes value and rely on trade secrets even more than larger companies. valuable trade secrets, however, become worthless if misappropriated by others. the risk of such misappropriation is real and could come from cyberattacks, economic espionage and unreliable partners in extended supply chains, for instance. the new eu rules will provide for effective eu-wide means of redress against such trade secret misappropriation. eu businesses will have better tools to fight against unfair and dishonest behaviour that threatens the value of their intellectual capital. this is an important step forward in allowing our creators and innovators to get profit from their hard work and intellectual efforts. let me be clear: this directive is not about promoting secrecy in business, it is about trust. thousands of eu companies, most of them smes, are innovating out there, sharing confidential information. the new eu rules will contribute to building such trust, as they will ensure that the risk of sharing information diminishes. this directive is also about the fairer and deeper single market, one of the priorities of this commission. a deeper single market, because the new rules will provide for more predictability and legal certainty. they will also result in a simpler legal framework facilitating the life of enterprises. companies will no longer need to research and analyse 28 different and disparate national laws; they can count on a harmonised approach. at the same time, rules will reduce unfair competition from rogue competitors who are cutting corners by not respecting the rules. a fairer single market means saying ‘no’ to hacking, cheating and economic espionage as business practices. this directive is not only about protecting businesses holding trade secrets; it is also about placing limits on the protection of trade secrets, avoiding abuse and ensuring full respect for disclosing obligations established by transparency rules. it is not here to protect potential illegal behaviour of companies. on the contrary, it serves to safeguard fundamental rights and freedoms and the legitimate interest of citizens, consumers, employees, honest competitors, journalists and public administrations. a significant added value of this directive lies in achieving the right balance between the different interests in this area. the european parliament has been decisive in improving the clarity of the proposal in this regard. thus, considering the overall compromise that has been achieved by the co-legislators and the benefits and significant added value for enterprises and citizens at large, the commission welcomes and endorses the agreed compromise deal.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of the data protection package after four years of legislative work. on the one hand, it will protect the personal data of europeans, especially in relation to multinational companies. we have taken care to strengthen the rights of internet users by giving them greater control over their data: the right to erasure, information on how their data is processed, controls on the transfer of data from europeans to third countries, strictly limited possibilities for profiling, sanctions for violators. the reform will give the eu the highest standards of privacy protection in the world, which, given its demographic and economic weight, will influence standards in the rest of the world. secondly, because technology provides new means of surveillance for the police and the judiciary, it was essential to build a foundation of guarantees for the rights and freedoms of citizens, while allowing the security forces to exchange information more quickly and efficiently. we have struck the right balance between protecting the fundamental rights of citizens and enhancing the effectiveness of police and judicial cooperation throughout the european union.
in writing. ‒ this codecision report concerns the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data by the european institutions and bodies and the free movement of such data. it establishes the european data protection supervisor (edps) and lays down the rules to ensure the confidentiality of personal data. i have supported this report because i believe it is essential to ensure that internet users have control over their personal data.
in writing. ‒ i voted decisively in favour of this major data protection reform, which allows us to adapt to contemporary digital developments. citizens are publishing more and more personal information and digital companies have started collecting it on a large scale. this meant that the legislation, which had been inadequate since 1995, had to be updated! this reform of european legislation obliges companies to inform their customers in case of data hacking, allows the transfer of data in very limited cases and, above all, establishes a right to be forgotten and a right of citizens to see the information that is collected about them.

in writing. ‒ after five years of negotiations, this report on the protection of personal data was finally adopted, despite the reluctance of the states. the reform will replace the current 1995 data protection directive with a general regulation to strengthen and adapt data protection. this report is the fruit of a long battle waged by the european parliament. it will, in particular, strengthen the participation of individuals in the protection of their own data, clarify definitions and provide greater legal certainty. the powers and functions of the supervisory and data protection authorities are also strengthened. this regulation also emphasises the application of the principles of necessity and proportionality in the transfer of personal data. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this codecision report makes legal proposals to strengthen the protection of personal data within the union, particularly when used to fight crime. it also aims to build trust between law enforcement agencies so that they can exchange personal data in their possession to fight crime. i also believe that there is a need for strict standards on the use of data for police and judicial purposes and that the rights of citizens in this respect must be respected. i therefore supported this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted decisively in favour of this major data protection reform, which allows us to adapt to contemporary digital developments. citizens are publishing more and more personal information and digital companies have started collecting it on a large scale. this meant that the legislation, which had been inadequate since 1995, had to be updated! this reform of european legislation obliges companies to inform their customers in case of data hacking, allows the transfer of data in very limited cases and, above all, establishes a right to be forgotten and a right of citizens to see the information that is collected about them.
in writing. ‒ this directive establishes a framework of guarantees for the rights and freedoms of citizens, while modern technologies now allow the use of advanced means of surveillance of the population by the police and the judiciary in order to ensure their safety, in the context of the terrorist threat that we know. while it is important to be able to prevent attacks and crime by strengthening police and judicial cooperation within the european union, it is also essential to protect the fundamental rights of citizens in parallel. failure to protect the data of suspects, witnesses or victims may threaten their security, their right to privacy or to a fair trial. that is why i voted for this package of laws and measures that regulate access to this data by security forces, while harmonizing the processes for processing and transferring this data between the 28 countries of the european union for an easier exchange of information, in order to counter cross-border criminal initiatives.
in writing. ‒ i have approved the rapporteur's recommendation on the proposal for a directive on sovereign files, which complements existing national rules on the processing of data for criminal purposes. this directive lays down minimum rules on data protection other than those covered by the regulation, which deals with commercial uses. the text provides a framework for the processing of data used in the context of police and judicial activities and which may be useful for investigations and prosecutions. i believe that if the first version was unacceptable because it did not respect the essential balance between the protection of personal data and their necessary use for security purposes, the version at second reading, which is the result of an agreement with the member states, seems to me to be much more balanced, in that it corrects the risks to the operational capabilities of the law enforcement agencies.
in writing. ‒ this directive guarantees the protection of personal data of persons involved in criminal proceedings, whether as witnesses, victims or suspects. it will also facilitate the exchange of information between national police and judicial authorities. the directive also provides clear rules for the transfer of personal data by law enforcement agencies outside the european union. on the one hand, this directive is designed to protect personal data; the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. so, another attack on national sovereignty. i therefore naturally voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ in early 2012, the commission proposed a reform package comprising a regulation establishing a general eu data protection framework and a directive addressing the processing of personal data for the purpose of fighting crime. by strengthening the right of users to be informed about what is being done with their data, these two texts will give european citizens greater control over their privacy and make them masters of their own data, ensuring that they consent to the processing of their data and guaranteeing them remedies against any misuse of their data. the adoption of these measures will also make them applicable to all undertakings. foreign companies, especially the giants of the digital economy, who want to process the data of european citizens will therefore also have to comply with the new european requirements. this legislative package thus makes it possible to reconcile a high level of protection for citizens with increased fairness of competition in strategic economic sectors. i therefore vote in favour of both texts.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of the european pnr is to collect personal data of air passengers entering or leaving the european area: identities, itineraries, travel agencies, means of payment, baggage information and specifics related to meals and health. officially, this massive data collection is to help fight terrorism and certain serious crimes. however, we are very hostile to the pnr for three reasons. firstly, it is a freedom killer because it seriously infringes the privacy of passengers by transmitting to the states a very large amount of private information which will be kept for five years. secondly, it is ineffective and the perpetrators of the latest attacks could not have been detected with this tool. rather than monitoring passengers, almost all of whom are innocent, it would be better to exploit the many intelligence tools that already exist and that could be very effective. thirdly, it is a nuisance to national sovereignty because its disguised aim is to save the schengen area by creating an 'air schengen'. we are radically opposed to this ineffective and freedom-threatening initiative.
in writing. ‒ the european pnr is a freedom killer because it seriously infringes the privacy of passengers. it is also ineffective because it does not make it possible to combat terrorism effectively. the european pnr also undermines national sovereignty, as it aims to save the schengen area by creating a sort of schengen airspace. finally, the european pnr is intended to be disclosed to the united states, whereas the latter will not in turn disclose their us pnr to the european union. it is obvious that such cooperation without reciprocity is unacceptable, since it is more akin to feudalism than to genuine international cooperation.
in writing. ‒ after the terrible attacks in the european union, including those in paris in 2015 and brussels in 2016, and after long and difficult negotiations, hampered in particular by socialist and green mps, but also by the front national mps, the european parliament finally voted on the passenger name record. the pnr requires air carriers to communicate passenger data, including name, address, travel dates and itineraries, and identity card numbers to the european states concerned by a flight to or from a state which is not a member state of the european union. this tool is essential in the fight against terrorism. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ after much debate, parliament finally adopted the passenger name record (pnr) directive, which has become all the more necessary in the light of recent developments. this directive is central to enhancing passenger safety, particularly in the prevention and detection of terrorist attacks or serious crime, thus ensuring a safer common area. while we can welcome the positive signal of this vote, i regret the role played by the member states in this matter, which have considerably reduced the european scope and coordination of the pnr. three shortcomings in particular: firstly, rather than creating a single european file, as parliament wanted, which would gather data on all passengers, the member states opted instead for 28 national files, 28 'silos' of pnrs; secondly, the exchange of data and information is not automatic but at the discretion of states; thirdly, the legislative scope of the text leaves the door open to possible differences in application, since it is a directive and not a regulation. despite these shortcomings, this report is a step forward for security in europe and will hopefully serve as a starting point for further european integration on the subject in the future. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this directive.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague constance le grip on the protection of undisclosed know-how and business information (business secrets) against their unlawful acquisition, use and disclosure. any confidential commercial information which gives a competitive advantage to a company can be considered a trade secret (trade secrets include manufacturing secrets, industrial secrets and trade secrets). the unauthorised use of such information by anyone other than the holder is considered to be unfair practice and a breach of business secrecy. trade secret is substantially different from ipr, which confers exclusivity. the holder of a trade secret does not have an exclusive right to its creation. its competitors and other third parties can therefore freely discover, develop and use the same formula. the commission proposal sets out the measures, procedures and remedies which should be available to the holder of a trade secret in the event of unlawful acquisition, use or disclosure of that secret by a third party.
in writing. ‒ the directive on the protection of trade secrets that we have adopted provides a more precise framework for what we call 'trade secrets'. contrary to the criticisms that have been made about the infringement of citizens' freedom of information, the directive guarantees the respect of business secrets revealed before the courts, but respects the balance with the fundamental right to freedom of expression. by adopting a common definition of trade secret, we also avoid the risk of legal vacuums. i therefore voted in favour of this directive, considering that its contributions were not only fair but essential to ensure at the same time respect for the freedoms and activities of undertakings.
in writing. this report concerns a proposal for a directive on business secrecy, introducing a harmonised system for the protection of business secrets and know-how in the european union. trade secrets are legal instruments that allow companies to protect certain of their business information and to conceal it from third parties (journalists, civil society) but also to impose confidentiality on employees and their representatives. for example, trade secrets have been regularly invoked in the united states with regard to the composition of products used for the extraction of shale gas, despite the risks these products pose to the environment. in addition, trade secrets are often invoked against journalists, trade unions or whistleblowers who publish information on illegal business activities, such as tax evasion. the directive thus puts the protection cursor on the side of the companies and endangers the freedom of expression of journalists and whistleblowers who act in the public interest. i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of new rules to help companies that have suffered theft or misuse of trade secret data to obtain redress. in fact, one in five companies is the victim of theft of trade secrets every year. by voting for this text, the european parliament is promoting a safe and reliable environment for companies that need to see their know-how fully protected. freedom of expression and information are therefore fully protected. in this sense, the text does not infringe on the freedom of the press and the work of journalists, particularly in their investigations but also in the protection of sources, is protected.
in writing. ‒ contrary to what has been said on social media, this directive is a balanced text that both ensures additional protection for smes and protects journalistic investigation and journalists' sources. the aim of this directive is to respond to the growing risks to which smes (especially the most innovative ones) are exposed as a result of globalisation, in the face of unfair practices of the misappropriation of trade secrets, while at the same time combating unfair competition and ensuring greater harmonisation and transparency within the union. my political group in this parliament has helped to ensure that all the provisions are in place to guarantee and safeguard the right to freedom of expression and information. this is the first time that a legal text specifically mentions and protects whistleblowers. the directive thus guarantees journalists full protection when their action is used to denounce an illegal practice and, more broadly, when it is motivated by the defence of the general interest (public safety and health, consumer and environmental protection, etc.). i voted for this text because it meets a genuine expectation of security for smes and guarantees freedom of expression and information in the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this directive. while the original proposal of the european commission was far too vague and dangerous, the socialist and democratic group considerably improved it during the debate. the text presented to the european parliament is therefore a satisfactory and balanced compromise. it aims to protect companies, especially smes, against industrial espionage while guaranteeing a high level of protection of freedom of information. by excluding freedom of the press from the scope of this directive and introducing safeguards to protect whistleblowers, parliament has helped to balance this text which will actually improve the situation of those who act in the general interest throughout the european union.
in writing. ‒ a 'trade secret' is information that companies protect to preserve, for example, their manufacturing secrets. while the original draft had significant shortcomings, meps fought to amend the directive because of the risk of putting whistleblowers at risk. the final text introduces new rights for citizens and journalists. the text states that the alleged disclosure of business secrets is the result of the "exercise of the right to freedom of expression" and states that the directive cannot achieve "respect for the freedom and pluralism of the media". for whistleblowers, we are also creating new protections: "revealing wrongdoing, inappropriate behaviour or illegal activity" in order to "protect the general public interest" cannot be considered as a breach of business secrecy. this text is an important step forward. it will protect the production processes of companies, while providing protection for whistleblowers and journalists. however, there are still areas of uncertainty and the european socialists call on the commission to extend this progress: we ask for a comprehensive text on the protection of whistleblowers!
in writing. ‒ the aim of this directive is to protect the business secrets of european companies, including smes, against economic espionage. the text proposed better protection for whistleblowers, which i of course supported. i am of course in favour of greater protection of our companies, and especially our smes, against economic espionage. france is a leader in many advanced fields such as aviation and information technology, and these companies must be able to exercise their know-how without fear of a potential threat of espionage. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ in the midst of the panama papers scandal, the european parliament voted by a large majority in favour of the 'business secret'. the directive will allow companies to protect and conceal certain information and impose confidentiality clauses on their employees and representatives. in other words, large companies will be able to hide crucial information such as health or environmental information! for example, the chemical composition of products used for shale gas extraction is considered a trade secret in the united states. this directive therefore represents a direct threat to whistleblowers, journalists, trade unionists and employees of companies. the european parliament has made some progress, but it remains hypothetical until a text that actually protects whistleblowers is adopted. it was 'promised' by the commission for june. the vote on the two texts should have been tied. i voted against this directive.

in writing. ‒ turkey is a key partner for the european union, particularly in managing migration flows to european countries. i also welcome his commitment to the fight against terrorism and i support the decision of the turkish government to allow the coalition forces to use its military bases. however, i cannot accept that turkey should use the current crisis to get parliament to continue the process of accession to the european union. while turkey is far from meeting the convergence criteria for considering membership, and even though it is a major player in the middle east and not in europe, my position remains unchanged. i therefore voted against the resolution and i would like to express my disappointment at the european parliament conceding what, for the moment, should not be conceded.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the 2015 report on turkey, presented by the european commission in november 2015. i would like to remind you that the current cooperation between the union and turkey in the management of the migration crisis must be dissociated from the negotiation process for the country's accession to the union. in particular, although turkey is a "key strategic partner" for the european union, the overall pace of reforms in the country has slowed down in recent times, with worrying regressions in freedom of expression and the independence of the judiciary. the 2015 report on turkey also indicates that the kurdish peace process is a major issue. the negotiations on the reunification of cyprus are also linked to turkish policy. if there is a positive development in relations between cyprus and turkey, it will not change the fact that i am still opposed to turkey's accession to the european union.
in writing. ‒ as every year, parliament adopted a report on the situation in turkey in the context of its application for eu membership. in this text, parliament deplored with rare firmness the setbacks in respect for democracy and the rule of law and the regressions observed in certain areas (independence of the judiciary, freedom of expression, respect for human rights against academics, journalists and hdp activists, etc.). the kurdish question in particular is dealt with at length: abuses by the security forces are denounced and the turkish government is called upon to assume its responsibilities in order to resume negotiations with a view to reaching a lasting solution. - what's the deed? but at the same time, the text adopts a mediocre position, which is sometimes absurd, particularly in the fight against terrorism. it is recalled that the pkk is on the union's list of terrorist organisations, which justifies the unjustifiable. 113 members voted for the amendment i tabled to remove the pkk from this list. the trade dimension is also present, with a call for "turkish interests to be taken into account" in the negotiations on the itcp. the eu and turkey have reached an agreement on migration. a curious balancing act that led me to abstain.

in writing. ‒ the report is based on the role of the private sector in the development of african countries in particular. he believes that the aid needed should be more than $2 billion, all of which would potentially come from our national coffers, unless public-private partnerships are further developed. it is stated that taxpayers would probably not be inclined to pay this... the report is entirely focused on the concept of unlimited growth, with the consequent increase in demand for energy, food and water, without, of course, indicating any recipe for answering these very serious questions. the only option offered is perpetual growth and economic success, with private investment, the ultimate goal being growth without limits, while we know that this is impossible... i voted against this text, of course.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which follows the commission's communication proposing a framework for action to strengthen the role of the private sector in developing countries. the private sector provides 90% of jobs in developing countries and is therefore a key partner in the fight against poverty. it also has a role to play as an investor in sustainable agricultural production to meet the challenge of feeding 9 billion people by 2050.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it is obsessed with public-private partnerships (ppp). i am opposed to ppps, which are almost always a boon for large private groups, at the expense of sound management of public money.
in writing. - i voted against this bill. this report aims to promote the role of the private sector in the development of the least developed countries (ldcs). he points to some structural obstacles, such as bureaucracy and even corruption. however, it advocates objectives which are difficult to achieve in terms of public aid to the ldcs. in addition, the draft report advocates increased use of intergovernmental bodies, which is not an appropriate solution.
in writing. - the report starts with a biased finding. the private sector is said to generate 90% of jobs and income in developing countries. but what jobs and at what cost? the report notes the weakness of public resources, which are hampered by imf loans. rather than promoting real public policies in these countries, it advocates public-private partnerships. these contracts entrust a private operator with the supervision of the works and the operation of a collective equipment. behind the legal novelty, there is a powerful tool for expropriating citizens and public power. worse, the report calls for private participation in the design of public development policies. finally, the report calls for diplomats on the ground to be trained, like vrps, to sell the concept to african countries. in the end, we are left to hope that the private sector will reduce land grabbing. i vote against it.
in writing. ‒ the report provides for more than €2 billion in aid for the private sector in african countries. the dogma of (unlimited) growth is also reaffirmed, linked to that of sustainable development. endless growth is a liberal myth, our infinite desire will collide with our finite resources. furthermore, i believe that sustainable development is a charm that masks the madness and damage of the project. finally, the panel that oversaw the research and development programme includes 250 multinationals, which have few rules other than that of making a profit. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the report estimates that development aid for african countries should exceed usd 2 billion and be financed through public-private partnerships. the development envisaged is purely illusory and no investment is proposed to solve the serious problems (food, water, energy). we are voting against this text which calls for the financing of projects which will only benefit multinational companies and which will only aggravate the problems of land expropriation, corruption and loss of sovereignty of african states.
in writing. ‒ this report is incomplete: nothing on natural resources, important issues for developed countries and multinationals, very little on land expropriation or corruption, etc. i therefore vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes measures to involve the public and private sectors in the development of developing countries. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the deva report on the private sector and development. the private sector provides 90 per cent of jobs in developing countries. it is therefore a key partner in the fight against poverty. it also has a role to play as an investor in sustainable agricultural production to meet the challenge of feeding 9 billion people by 2050. given the capacity of the private sector to generate inclusive and sustainable growth in developing countries, businesses, associations and employers' and workers' organisations in particular are playing an increasingly active role in the field of development, both as a source of funding and as partners of public authorities, non-governmental organisations (ngos). a recent evaluation of eu private sector development assistance between 2004 and 2010 confirmed the commission's significant contribution to private sector development in partner countries and identified ways to improve future programmes and strategies, in particular with a view to focusing on decent job creation and mainstreaming private sector participation in all eu support activities.
in writing. ‒ the private sector is, as we know, essential for development. it is responsible for most of the economic activity through its role as an investor and job creator. in developing countries, the private sector provides almost 90% of jobs and is an important partner for public authorities, ngos and donors. i therefore voted in favour of this text to support the european parliament's work on development aid and to enable the proposed strategic framework to be put in place to strengthen the role of the private sector, and thus achieve inclusive and sustainable growth.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which stresses the importance of private sector actors for development, particularly in countries beyond europe's borders. the annual global expenditure in developing countries is not high enough and has so far been over-supported by the taxpayer. participating in development in areas where it is needed is a win-win for all: for the people and the states that are not yet sufficiently integrated into the world economy, but also for our european companies that will find new levers of growth in the developing countries. finally, the role of the european investment bank (eib) must be emphasised in order to increase its involvement in the project financing effort.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which highlights the link between the private sector and development policy. it is essential to recall that the private sector accounts for 84% of the gdp of developing countries and is therefore an essential player in development policy and the fight against poverty. the text recommends the development of a long-term strategy with the private sector, particularly in order to stimulate and increase investment. these private sector partnerships should be based on shared values and priorities, with specific development objectives, and managed in cooperation with partner countries. a second focus developed in this report is support for the local private sector in developing countries by supporting microenterprises which often face significant regulatory constraints. the aim is to encourage european and international businesses to contribute to the sustainable development goals and the implementation of internationally agreed standards. i supported this text because it states that public-private partnerships established within a specific framework, structured, transparent and with a clear distribution of responsibilities, constitute important opportunities for the development of the partner countries, particularly in terms of employment and investment.
in writing. ‒ this report addresses the issue of private sector development assistance to africa. it states that the consequences of these investments should be growth for the private sector. this growth would then be unlimited and that is what underlies the whole package. the text is in fact intended to copy the european economic model in africa and i am aware of all the harmful consequences that this can have. i therefore follow the approach of my colleague louis aliot, who voted against it in committee by voting against it in my turn.
in writing. ‒ the management of 'public' development aid (oda) is increasingly being transferred to the private sector due to budgetary constraints. in fact, development policies are increasingly being handed over to the interests of private investors. while the report calls for increased public investment in education, access to clean water and health, it also encourages the development of public-private partnerships (ppps). the partnerships in the field of education are even welcomed, when they must be "profitable" and there is no need to remind us of the detrimental effects of such practices. it is even proposed to increase public technical assistance to the private sector for the setting up of these ppps, and to train the european union delegations in the country for this purpose. the integration of the private sector and neoliberal logic into the design of official development assistance is dangerous, to say the least, for the recipient countries. the developed countries would do better to meet their commitments (0.7% of gnp) which are 45 years old and still not met, with rare exceptions. i voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report which, although not binding, seeks to prevent member states from being able to refuse certain types of adoption, in particular children from gpa.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution, which responds to petitions addressed to the european parliament, claims to defend the best interests of the child, particularly in the area of adoption. the resolution incorporates an amendment voted in the peti committee which abolishes the possibility for states not to recognise adoptions contrary to their own law. in fact, this resolution entails the mandatory recognition of adoptions by same-sex couples and children of gpa, adoptions prohibited by most european states as being against their public order. in addition to a clear denial of sovereignty, this resolution violates the rights of the child by opening the way at european level to the acceptance of practices harmful to its well-being and balance. i therefore voted against this resolution.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution must make it possible to apply the best interests of the child in all areas, including in the field of adoption. this also applies to the parents' right to maintain contact with the child. the resolution includes an amendment which removes the possibility for states not to recognise adoptions contrary to their public policy. thus, if an adoption is recorded in one member state, it may be recorded in another. this may in fact lead to the compulsory recognition of adoptions by same-sex couples or children from gpa. the resolution does call on the member states to regulate the recognition of crossborder adoptions, but i would like to point out that this is not an eu matter and is entirely a matter for national policies. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the compulsory recognition of adoptions by other member states could lead to the compulsory recognition of adoptions by same-sex couples, of children from gpa, which i oppose. point 22 calls on the member states and the commission to regulate the recognition of crossborder adoptions. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution, which is supposed to protect the best interests of the child in all circumstances in the european union, is in fact aimed at removing the possibility for member states not to recognise adoptions contrary to public policy. the text could therefore oblige the national authorities to recognise adoptions by same-sex couples or children born of surrogacy. it would be absolutely scandalous to subject the peoples of europe to customs which are not their own. that is why i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ coordination of the judicial systems of the member states is essential to ensure the best interests of the child in cases of divorce of transnational parents. the brussels iia regulation is a european legal instrument designed to help international couples resolve transnational disputes on divorce or child custody. there is clearly a problem in the implementation of this regulation which is preventing it from achieving its intended objective. this regulation should serve the parents to resolve their disputes while safeguarding the best interests of the child. states must support the communities most vulnerable to social exclusion through more preventive approaches. i voted in favour of this resolution, which aims to guarantee the same european standards for all children and families in legal proceedings. this resolution also shows that petitions sent by our fellow citizens are duly examined by the european parliament.
in writing. ‒ this resolution recalls the main principles of child protection and judicial cooperation in the eu, the role of social services in child protection, judicial proceedings relating to child custody, child placement and adoption, and any cross-border dimension related to the subject. the report calls on member states to integrate monitoring and evaluation systems into their national coordination framework on crossborder cases involving children. it also advocates the creation of specialised chambers in family courts and stresses the importance of offering children a sense of closeness to their cultural background. i have supported this report because i believe that in the context of the migration crisis, where more than 10 000 children are missing, it is essential that our states strengthen their cooperation in order to protect their children's interests.
in writing. ‒ the principle of free movement allows millions of europeans to live and, in some cases, to start a family in a state other than their own. in the event of separation, difficulties may arise when one of the spouses decides to return to his or her member state of origin, as national laws on parental custody are still not harmonised at european level. in view of the principle of the protection of the best interests of the child, it is therefore urgent that the european union and its member states improve their judicial cooperation on this issue, as we have long been calling for.
in writing. ‒ the compulsory recognition of adoptions by some member states could lead to the compulsory recognition of adoptions of children raised by same-sex couples or children from gpas, for example. however, these particular adoptions are often prohibited by most member states in the name of public policy. however, the resolution adopted in the peti committee on 14 march 2016 includes an amendment which removes the possibility for states not to recognise adoptions contrary to their interpretation of public policy. although the resolution stresses that there is no automatic recognition, it also calls on the states and the commission to regulate the recognition of cross-border adoptions. that is why i voted against this text, which does not respect the sovereign choices of states and which contributes to the spread of practices that endanger the family and the natural foundation of our societies.
in writing. ‒ vote against: the compulsory recognition of adoptions by other member states could lead to the compulsory recognition of adoptions by same-sex couples, children from gpas, etc.
