in writing. - a breakup is never easy. especially when it involves a child. but when one or both parents come from another country, the complexity of the issue of custody becomes clear. citizens have sent numerous petitions to the european parliament on disputed decisions on child custody, abduction and placement cases. the resolution therefore calls for better coordination of legal services in the member states, particularly in crossborder cases. it is developing very concrete solutions, such as a common definition of 'habitual residence'. but don't stop there. social services are essential for the care of children and their parents. the text therefore criticises the policies of austerity and cuts which ultimately harm the child himself in the first place. another concrete example: it asks that in the case of child placement procedures (when the parents are dead or deemed incapable of acting) a sufficient period be determined so that the child's extended family members, sometimes in another country, have time to present themselves and propose to adopt the child. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ this report was a generally cautious report in that it was not binding. in other words, it did not oblige a member state to recognise automatically an adoption by another country. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to carcinogens at work. we must also ensure that the laws of the states are respected in matters of the family. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ this resolution adopted by the peti committee on 14 march 2016 includes an amendment that removes the possibility for states not to recognise adoptions contrary to their public policy. the compulsory recognition of adoptions by other member states could lead to the compulsory recognition of adoptions by same-sex couples, children from gpas, etc. and these particular adoptions are often prohibited by most member states in the name of public policy. however, the motion for a resolution adopts a cautious wording, particularly in paragraph 22: it merely emphasizes that there is no automatic recognition and calls on the states and the commission to regulate the recognition of cross-border adoptions. i shall vote against it, however.
in writing. ‒ the compulsory recognition of adoptions by other member states could lead to the compulsory recognition of adoptions of children from gpa. these particular adoptions are often prohibited by member states in the name of public policy. the member states are sovereign in this area, so i am voting against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which focuses on child protection and judicial cooperation within the eu, the role of social services in child protection, judicial proceedings relating to child custody, child placement and adoption, and any cross-border dimension related to the subject. it calls on the member states to designate specialised chambers within family courts or crossborder mediation bodies to deal with cases concerning crossborder children.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on child protection and judicial cooperation in crossborder custody and adoption disputes. more cooperation in crossborder family matters is needed. legal cooperation between member states needs to be improved and the european commission needs to help provide clear information to all european citizens about legal procedures relating to children, such as parental rights in different european countries. children should not pay the price of a lack of cooperation from member states; their interests must be protected.
in writing. ‒ this text claims to safeguard the best interests of the child in all areas, including in the field of adoption. it also concerns the right of parents to maintain contact with their children. however, it has an important con­triction: the removal of the possibility for member states not to recognise adoptions contrary to public policy. the compulsory recognition of adoptions by other member states could lead to the compulsory recognition of adoptions by same-sex couples, children from gpas, etc. and these particular adoptions are often prohibited by most member states in the name of public policy. i therefore vote against this text.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament is preparing an own-initiative report on the creation of a european pillar of social rights, which will serve as a framework for examining performance in the social and employment field in the light of changing forms of work and societies and, more generally, as a guide for the new convergence process within the euro area. the european parliament, pursuant to rule 137 of its rules of procedure, asks the european economic and social committee to deliver an opinion on this matter. in the interests of continuing dialogue with civil society and european economic and social actors, i voted in favour of this consultation, which will enrich the content of the own-initiative report prepared by the parliament's employment committee.

in writing. ‒ the eesc is the european institution representing the european socioeconomic community. its members are appointed by the member states. unfortunately, it has only an advisory role. the 350 members of the eesc represent trade unions, employers' organisations, ngos, the agricultural and craft industries, the professions and consumers. the social economy is also represented. it is the european equivalent of the french economic, social and environmental council. the treaty on the functioning of the eu provides for consultation on certain matters. in this text, the european parliament asks the eesc to deliver an opinion on the creation of a european pillar of social rights. this seems to be the least of it and i think it is an important subject, although i am doubtful about the consequences, especially as i consider that the opinions of the eesc are not sufficiently used and taken into account. nevertheless, it is an important form of consultation of the social partners. i am in principle in favour of his views and of a wider consultation of 'civil society', especially when it comes to the rights of which they are the main actors. i voted in favour of this consultation in the hope that it will open up new prospects, including for that other europe to which i aspire more than ever.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the agreement we have reached, which gives real powers to the european railway agency (era). in concrete terms, the commission will now be able to issue safety certificates for railway undertakings and authorisations for rolling stock at european level, while continuing to draw on the expertise and know-how of national authorities. the afe will also develop the european traffic management system so that trains can run in several countries with different infrastructures without having to change control, braking or signalling systems. finally, the tfa will also be responsible for harmonising the approximately 11 000 national safety rules. in the fight against climate change, europe has a great tool to promote rail mobility, which is much more environmentally sustainable.

in writing. ‒ following discussions, the european union railway agency will be able to eliminate the need for multiple authorisations, have a greater role in the development of the european rail traffic management system (ertms), establish a one-stop shop , making the agency the only entry point for all applications, and conclude cooperation agreements between the agency and national safety authorities. finally, the agency's management board will also establish rules on the prevention and management of conflicts of interest and procedures for cooperation with national judicial authorities. there are many concerns about these prerogatives, not least the fact that the agency will certainly be much more easily subjected to pressure than national agencies taken separately. worse, the agency will now be able to dictate its choices to the states and bypass national railway safety agencies for the entire railway sector. i have therefore decided to reject the council's proposal and to vote in favour of the rejection amendment tabled by the efdd group.

in writing. ‒ this technical report is part of the fourth railway package, adopted by the european commission in 2013, which aims to fully liberalise the transport sector in europe with a view to creating a single market. the aim of this report is to give the european railway agency the responsibility to promote interoperability between member states by imposing common safety rules on them. the interoperability of transport means, in particular, the possibility of trains running unhindered on railway networks located in different member states. as a result, the national railway agencies will soon become mere branches of the european agency. the commission will therefore be able to impose its choices on the member states and to bypass the national agencies. i have of course opposed this report, which contributes to the creation of a single transport market which undermines the sovereignty of the member states of the union. that is why i voted for the rejection amendment.

in writing. ‒ as part of the technical pillar of the fourth railway package, this legislative report aims to strengthen the remit of the european railway agency (era). the aim of this agency is to remove the remaining administrative and technical barriers in the railway sector. it also aims to further develop and ensure the proper functioning of a single european railway area. to this end, it should ensure a high level of railway safety and interoperability and monitor the development of national railway rules to support the achievements of national railway safety and interoperability authorities and promote the optimisation of procedures. the agency will be responsible for issuing authorisations to place vehicles and types of railway vehicles on the market and for issuing single safety certificates for railway undertakings. i personally worked on this report during the last mandate 2009-2014 and, considering that the european railway market requires better coordination and harmonisation at european level and that this requires the strengthening of the afe's competences, i supported this report.

in writing. ‒ by harmonising the technical and safety rules for rail transport, this directive is further deepening the technocratization of the european union. the aim is to improve 'the technical compatibility of infrastructure, rolling stock, signalling and other parts of the railway system and to simplify the procedures for authorising rolling stock for use on the entire european rail network'. the agreement should therefore allow railway undertakings and equipment manufacturers to achieve further economies of scale. this is supposed to help avoid any 'hidden discrimination' against companies wishing to enter a market (i.e. in practice the outsourcing and privatisation of railway equipment companies). it will also significantly reduce the volume of national rules in areas where harmonised regulation at union level has been put in place, meaning that transport policy will no longer be in the hands of the states but of the commission. i am voting against this text.

in writing. ‒ the resolution aims to put an end to a wave of scandals concerning the manipulation of financial indices, in particular the libor and euribor interest rate benchmarks. by manipulating these indices, banks were able to influence the prices of loans and other derivatives to their advantage. i voted in favour of this new european regulatory framework which guarantees a high level of protection for investors and consumers in the use of financial indices, by preventing fraud and manipulation which can have disastrous consequences (inflation of consumer goods prices such as petrol or mortgage rates).
in writing. ‒ the libor and euribor manipulation scandals have prompted european authorities to legislate on indices used as benchmarks for financial instruments. the idea of the regulation is to make their calculation formula transparent and to regulate the 'governance' of their suppliers in order to prevent conflicts of interest and subject them to some form of control by regulators, while respecting a principle of proportionality linked to the sum of indexed products they represent. it is also intended to allow the use of indices issued in third countries, provided that they comply with a list of criteria to ensure their reliability, defined by iosco. this text is a step forward and entrusts the national regulators with the main control functions. i therefore voted in favour of this text, despite the likely complexity of its implementation.
in writing. ‒ the libor and euribor manipulation scandals have prompted the european authorities to legislate on the subject of benchmarks, in addition to the sanctions component, which fall under the market abuse directive. the idea of the regulation is to make their calculation formula transparent, to frame the governance of their suppliers in order to prevent conflicts of interest and to subject them to some form of control by the regulators. the report identifies three categories of indices: critical indices (more than eur 500 billion of indexed products), significant indices (more than eur 50 billion) and non-significant indices. some indices are not taken into account, but it is planned to allow the use of framed third country indices. although i regret the complexity of the text in its implementation, it is nevertheless a step forward, especially since it entrusts the main control functions to the national regulators. so i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the repeated scandals of libor and euribor manipulation have led european authorities to regulate the methods of calculating indices, exchange rates and commodity prices, with the aim of making them much more transparent in order to limit manipulation. the text sets out more or less strict obligations depending on the amount of the derivatives underlying these indices. the text is clearly a step in the right direction: in addition to increasing transparency in financial markets, the report entrusts the main functions of supervision to national regulators, thus not limiting the sovereignty of the member states. that is why i voted for this text.
in writing. ‒ the libor and euribor manipulation scandals have prompted the european authorities to legislate on the subject of benchmarks, in addition to the sanctions component, which fall under the market abuse directive. the proposal includes making the formula for calculating these indices more transparent, setting out the governance of their providers and subjecting them to some form of control by regulators. this text is a step forward and entrusts the national regulators with the main control functions. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ benchmarks are indices used as a reference price for a financial instrument or contract. the most well-known european indices are libor and euribor, which serve as benchmarks for, for example, interbank interest rates, oil price valuation and stock market indices. the manipulation of benchmarks can have devastating consequences for the european economy. so we have to ensure their integrity. under this regulation, administrators of all benchmarks will be required to register with the european securities and markets authority (esma) and to publish a declaration of compliance specifying the use of their benchmark and its reliability. they will also have liability (code of conduct) and record-keeping constraints, as well as audit and review requirements. the regulation also requires reciprocity for indices from third countries. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this legislative report concerns the introduction of a common framework to ensure the accuracy and integrity of indices used as reference points in the union's financial instruments. its main objectives are to improve governance and ensure that administrators avoid conflicts of interest, to improve the quality of input data and the methods used, to ensure that contributors to the benchmarks are subject to adequate controls, and to ensure adequate protection for benchmark users by improving transparency, ensuring adequate rights of appeal, and ensuring relevance. considering that improving the process of calculating benchmarks and increasing transparency is essential to avoid conflicts of interest, i supported this report.
in writing. ‒ the text aims to make the formulae for calculating indices used as benchmarks for financial instruments more transparent, following the libor and euribor manipulation scandals. the indices concerned may be conventional stock market indices (e.g. cac 40), indices on rates (monetary, foreign exchange), on the price of raw materials, or even on meteorology or energy prices. indices produced by central banks and press companies (trade newspapers) are largely exempt. indices with an objective calculation formula (stock exchange rates) are less controlled, because they are less manipulable. it is also intended to allow the use of indices issued in third countries, provided that they comply with a list of criteria to ensure their reliability, defined by iosco. the text, which is rather complex in its implementation, would have benefited from a less restrictive definition of the critical indices. but as it is a step forward and gives national regulators the main control functions, i voted in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ the text aims to provide a framework for the main benchmarks for financial instruments and contracts. in the wake of the libor and euribor scandals in 2008, the commission wants to prevent any further controversy over manipulation or conflict of interest. the report therefore focuses on the critical indices (cac 40), on rates (monetary, foreign exchange) and on the price of raw materials (e.g. meteorology, energy prices). the aim is to define the governance of their suppliers and to promote the transparency of calculations. this is therefore a step forward in this area. the rapporteur also leaves the power of control to the national regulators. for all these reasons, i voted in favour.
in writing. - i voted for this text. this report follows the libor and euribor manipulation scandals. it complements the market abuse directive. it aims to control price indices (stock market indices, commodity price indices, etc.) by making their price formula transparent and by controlling the providers of such indices (in particular to limit the risks of conflicts of interest). the various indices are classified by degree of sensitivity. the applicable level of control depends on the degree of sensitivity of the index concerned. indices produced by central banks and press companies are not covered by this report. this text is the result of a long legislative process: the commission's initial proposal dates from september 2013. it was put to the vote of the european parliament in may 2015. the final report is disappointing because of the narrow definition of the indices to which it applies. we welcome the regulation and the broad powers granted to national legislators. the latter are granted the bulk of the control powers.
in writing. ‒ a benchmark is a value or indicator calculated on the basis of a representative set of data or information. it is used to value financial instruments or contracts, or to measure the performance of an investment fund. the london interbank offered rate (libor) and the euro interbank offered rate (euribor), which serve as benchmarks for interbank interest rates, are examples of benchmarks. any risk of manipulation of benchmarks can undermine market confidence, cause significant losses for investors and, above all, distort the real economy. the commission and parliament's report propose improving the control and governance of the referral process to avoid manipulation. the report stresses the need to combat conflicts of interest and ensure transparency. but these few efforts pale in comparison with the manipulation of these indices that has already occurred in the past. in particular, the text does not propose the creation of alternative indices measuring the real economy rather than speculative forecasts. i vote against it.

in writing. ‒ the libor and euribor manipulation scandals have led european authorities to look at indices used as benchmarks for financial instruments, in addition to the 'sanctions' component of the market abuse directive. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be able to grant a derogation to the member states in respect of the use of the financial instrument for the period from 1 january 2014 to 31 december 2015. the text distinguishes three main categories of indices: critical indices (over eur 500 billion), significant indices (over eur 50 billion) and non-significant indices. each of these is matched by bonds and only libor and euribor remain in the category of critical indices. indices produced by central banks and press companies (trade newspapers) are largely exempt. indices with an objective calculation formula (stock exchange rates) are less controlled, because they are less manipulable. the text would probably have been better if it had adopted a less restrictive definition of critical indices, but it is a step forward and gives national regulators most of the control. it is likely that the text will be difficult to implement, but it is a step forward in terms of transparency and objectivity of calculations, allowing markets to function better. i vote for it.

in writing. ‒ libor and euribor are overnight lending rates indices on the interbank market, which have been gradually used as benchmarks in millions of contracts between individuals (credit loans, mortgages). in june 2012, the libor scandal erupted around the manipulation of these rates by banks, aimed either at optimizing their market operations or to display apparent solidity and credibility. the scandal demonstrated that benchmarks in financial instruments and contracts were subject to conflicts of interest, poor governance and the risk of fraudulent practices. the commission proposal aims to establish a common regulatory framework to strengthen governance and transparency, and thus prevent these fraudulent practices, while ensuring a high level of protection for consumers and investors. more generally, it is the integrity of indices that needs to be restored in order not to undermine market confidence, distort the real economy or cause serious losses to investors and consumers. i therefore voted in favour of this report which supports the proposed direction and aims to ensure the accuracy, robustness and integrity of benchmarks.

in writing. ‒ the european aviation safety agency (easa) has the main function of being the certification authority for aeronautical products. in addition to the fact that the commission, through this agency, eventually wants to take over most of the functions of the national aviation authorities, in particular in the area of control of the airspace of the member states, the easa is in conflict with other international bodies, such as eurocontrol. the question then arises as to the real purpose of this agency, which is increasingly encroaching on the powers of eurocontrol and is more respectful of the sovereignty of states than the easa. in addition, between 2013 and 2014, the agency's budget increased by 8,47%, with two thirds of this budget coming from private sources, raising the question of independence in the agency's decision-making. the report's lack of determination to highlight these major problems led me to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ the agency's final budget for the financial year 2014 was eur 131.179.098, an increase of 8,47% compared to 2013. the report also notes that the agency has adopted a confidential safety reporting procedure which addresses information provided by whistleblowers regarding alleged aviation safety failures and irregularities reported by outsiders. there were 66 cases related to this procedure in 2014. finally, the aim of the agency is to eventually allow european control over national aviation authorities and i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ the centre's main mission is to carry out information and expertise missions on human diseases. it was particularly active in 2014, with the outbreak of the ebola virus in west africa. a third of its workforce has been mobilized to help solve the crisis. however, although the centre reacted quickly, it did not carry out its protection mission. for example, while the organization criticized the ineffectiveness of temperature screening at airports (to detect products that are dangerous to humans), it did not call for the end of flights from infected areas. that is why i voted against the report.

in writing. ‒ the european chemicals agency is responsible for the proper enforcement of chemicals legislation, for example, it is responsible for authorising chemicals such as plasticisers suspected of being endocrine disruptors and nanomaterials, and has hundreds of thousands of products under its control. however, only 6% of its budget comes from the union, the rest from the chemical industry which applies for authorizations: a problematic situation in that it creates a dependence which is necessary to achieve its objectivity. finally, its 2014 activity highlighted some surprising and completely forbidden practices: for example, in a letter dated 20 april 2016, it plans to reopen 700 files to verify their completeness and to give applicants a "reasonable time" to complete them, which is quite astonishing considering that these are potentially dangerous products for health and the environment. that is why i could not give echa discharge.
in writing. ‒ the agency's final budget for the financial year 2014 was eur 114.112.193, an increase of 6,37% compared to 2013. the report recalls that, in accordance with the reach regulation, the agency is funded by fees paid by industry for the registration of chemicals and that in 2014 the agency was fully funded by fees collected for its activities under the reach and clp regulations. in reality, only 6% of its budget comes from the eu and the rest comes from the chemical industry applying for authorisations. if one can at first sight think that this saves the general budget, i think in reality that this system creates a problem of dependence and lack of objectivity of the agency. i therefore voted against.

in writing. ‒ this resolution addresses attacks on hospitals and schools in war and armed conflict zones, which constitute violations of international humanitarian law. such attacks are on the rise in many parts of the world, as the recent attacks in aleppo have shown. the infrastructure, sanitation and schools, should remain neutral and protected areas even in times of armed conflict. these serious violations of international law must be investigated in a transparent, independent and impartial manner. in this resolution, parliament also reiterated its position in favour of a european arms embargo on countries responsible for serious violations of international law, including saudi arabia. the eu is the leading donor of humanitarian aid. this represented 1% of its budget in 2015. this aid should be increased and accompanied by significant efforts by the member states. some european states have a heavy responsibility, including in the sale of arms, which could have been underlined in the resolution, as well as their direct or indirect participation in these conflicts. i voted in favour of this resolution, which was drafted by my greek colleague and friend from syriza, kostas chrysogonos, who was one of the main drafters.

on behalf of the enf group. mr president, since 1989 the european union has signed fisheries agreements with mauritania. the last one was on 10 july 2015 and will apply for four years. this is a good agreement, because it allows european vessels to fish in mauritanian waters, while respecting a sustainable fisheries objective. it thus limits the volume of fish allocated to freezer trawlers to 247 000 tonnes, compared with 300 000 tonnes under the previous agreement. in return, the eu will pay €55 million per year to mauritania, compared with €67 million in the previous agreement. however, mauritania is a poor state, ranking 161st in the world on the human development index. the commission notes that the 2015 agreement provides for an additional financial contribution of eur 4,125 million per year, compared to only eur 3 million in the previous agreement. the 2015 agreement also maintains the obligation to recruit 60% of the seafarers from mauritania. it is therefore a fair agreement that serves european interests while respecting mauritania. i hope that this agreement will mark a new beginning in our relations with mauritania, relations which have lacked mutual trust in recent years. i wish to do so for two reasons in particular: first, as a frenchman, because mauritania is a french-speaking country and a friend of france. i myself went to nouakchott on an official mission a few years ago and was received admirably. i hope so, secondly, for our collective security, because mauritania is an exemplary partner in the fight against islamist terrorism, and we have every interest in supporting such a reliable ally.

in writing. ‒ codification is the process of grouping together normative texts of various kinds into collections for the purpose of simplification, clarity and transparency. the text before us aims to codify regulation (ec) no 597/2009 on the defence of europe against subsidised imports from countries not members of the european community. this regulation lays down european rules establishing countervailing duties to offset any subsidy granted, directly or indirectly, to the manufacture, production, export or transport of any product from a third country, the marketing of which on the eu market causes injury to competitors. but it also gives the commission full power to amend, suspend or repeal countervailing measures or to provide for total or partial exemption from countervailing duties. these non-democratic technocratic procedures prevent europe from practicing the solidarity protectionism which is the ecological and social emergency of our time. i vote against it.

in writing. ‒ this eu-liberia partnership agreement on sustainable fisheries is to allow access to liberian waters for eu fishing vessels. the new agreement was signed on 5 june 2015 for a period of five years. this is the first fisheries agreement with liberia. it concerns 28 tuna seiners (16 spanish and 12 french) and 6 surface longliners (spanish). in return, liberia will receive eu funds, namely eur 715 000 in the first year; eur 650 000 in the second, third and fourth years; eur 585 000 in the fifth year, based on a reference tonnage of 6 500 tonnes, and the sectoral policy corresponds to half of these amounts. the eu's share will gradually decrease as the share of shipowners increases. in addition, it was decided that shipowners should endeavour to take on board three qualified liberian seamen per vessel and, overall, 20% of the seamen on board should be of acp origin. overall, this agreement seems fair, especially as the country is emerging from a period of civil war and the aftermath of the ebola epidemic, and this will make it possible to achieve a real agreement on co-development. so i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ territorial cohesion is a fundamental objective of the european union, enshrined in the treaty of lisbon. cohesion policy 2014-2020 therefore focuses on an integrated and territorialised approach to foster economic, social and territorial cohesion. two new tools have been introduced to achieve this: local development led by local actors (lda) and integrated territorial investment (iti), which will account for around 5% of the cohesion policy budget (€16 billion). although it is still too early to make a real assessment, ruža tomašić's report provides a first assessment of the problems, challenges and prospects associated with these tools. the lack of trust between different levels of government or the weak capacity of local governments to develop comprehensive strategies for their territories are thus identified. these tools should help to overcome these problems by promoting a more rational use of european funds, without creating administrative complexity, which is still far too present. the approach proposed by dlal and iti should be part of future cohesion policy debates. i voted for this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which recalls that the new territorial development tools are innovative instruments in cohesion policy and that they represent a qualitative leap in the ability of local actors to better coordinate grants and plan more limited local initiatives. these two new tools are integrated territorial investment (iti), which allows for better combining the flow of funds from several programmes, and local development led by local actors (ldaa), which aims to strengthen synergies between local actors in order to better target actions. the iti and the lag are therefore vectors for better territorial governance in the context of cohesion policy. i supported this text because it recalls the need to define strategies and to delegate responsibilities and resources wisely to local decision-making levels. in order to be more effective, the involvement of regional and local actors, from the earliest stages, is essential to ensure effective local action, particularly in the fight against youth unemployment and the financing of smes.
in writing. ‒ these new investments could help to reduce regional disparities in cohesion policy, in particular by addressing the financing and cash flow problems of smes and youth unemployment. in france, the scope of the iti's intervention is geographically aligned with the city's policy. so more money will be poured into the suburbs and peri-urban areas. however, it must be admitted that the increase in budgetary transfers in the european union will not reduce the competitiveness deficit of our smes due to the unbridled globalisation. moreover, the implementation of these new territorial development tools is essentially based on a bottom-up approach whereby local and regional actors gain autonomy and weaken the power of national authorities even further. these new territorial development tools, which are intended to respond directly to local needs and challenges, are a means for the european union to extend its fields of action in urban policy, which are the exclusive competence of the member states. i am voting against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted abstention on the report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on community statistics relating to balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment. although a number of measures are designed to strengthen reporting and publication obligations in order to improve the transparency and level of detail of statistics, the purpose of this text is to provide the commission with a large amount of strategic information on financial flows. in addition, the study of these statistics is intended to contribute to the economic governance imposed on the member states. finally, they are intended to certify the conformity of the economic policies of the member states with the general guidelines of the union, which is unacceptable to us.
in writing. ‒ while this report proposes to improve the finesse of statistics on financial flows into and out of the eu, it is a question of entrusting the commission with a very large amount of strategic information on financial flows. moreover, these statistics are not just for scientific purposes. their primary purpose is to serve as a means of economic governance imposed on the member states. they help to certify the consistency of the economic policies of the member states with the union's broad guidelines, as well as with the legal obligations deriving from the union's economic governance framework. i abstained.
in writing. ‒ these statistics are part of the general framework of the union for monitoring economic developments in each member state and in the union as a whole. i believe that in a world where international capital flows have increased and become more complex, the production of reliable statistics on balance of payments, international trade in services and foreign direct investment is essential for the monitoring of macroeconomic imbalances. these tools will help to ensure better traceability of these flows and to combat tax evasion. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ this report follows the interinstitutional negotiations on the amendment of regulation (ec) no 184/2005 on statistics on financial flows into and out of the eu. the objective is to strengthen reporting and publication requirements to improve the transparency and level of detail of statistics by integrating into the reports recent regulatory innovations related to the fight against money laundering and tax evasion, such as the public registers of beneficial owners established by the anti-money laundering directive. however, this report does provide the commission with a great deal of strategic information on financial flows, especially since these statistics serve more than a scientific purpose: they also serve to strengthen the economic governance imposed on the member states. i could not therefore vote in favour of this report, despite its original draft which was not without relevance.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament adopted the giegold report on balance of payments statistics by a very large majority. it calls for greater transparency in international capital flows. it is essential that balance of payments data should no longer be manipulated by the trusts or certain opaque financial companies in tax havens. from now on, it will be possible to see the starting and ending points of investment flows. eurostat and the member states will now have to publish data on capital flows in a clear and accessible way. eurostat and the member states will also include data from future registers on final beneficiaries of trusts in capital flow statistics. these changes will shed much-needed light on the murky world of investment flows. transparency on direct investment flows also needs to be improved. coordination between the member states and the european commission must now aim at improving statistics to better understand whether direct investment creates jobs or merely serves to take over companies. i naturally voted in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which recalls the importance of the union's mountain regions. these regions rarely receive specific attention in cohesion policy, even though they make a decisive contribution to european objectives in a multitude of areas. the text calls on the commission to take account of the specific features and strengths of mountain regions and to draw up a programme for european mountain regions. the coordination of the union's policies, strategies and programmes which have direct consequences for mountain areas must be strengthened. greater coherence will be achieved for the benefit of employment and economic growth in mountain areas, but also for sustainable growth, the environment and accessibility of these mountain areas. i supported this text, which calls for special attention to be paid to the development of smes, to improve the marketing of agricultural products, to promote better access to public services, but also to concentrate european efforts on the use of renewable energies in these mountainous areas. there is an urgent need for a more coherent and better coordinated european policy towards mountain regions in order to exploit their full potential.
in writing. ‒ i am opposed to the establishment of macro-regional strategies that limit the scope of action of national governments. the european union is seeking to expand its sphere of influence by strengthening its relations with local authorities. as such, member states are almost never mentioned, although they are the essential partners for the success of any crossborder cooperation project. the macro-regional strategy in the alpine, carpathian and ionian regions is simply aimed at strengthening the european commission's project for a new territorial architecture, which in the short term may threaten the sustainability of cross-border cooperation based on healthy relations between nation states. i am voting against this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (eu) no 575/2013 as regards the derogations applicable to commodity traders. the proposed amendment would allow commodity traders to benefit from an extension until 31 december 2020 of the derogations from the requirements of the crr on large exposures and own funds. these derogations avoid forcing these investment companies to increase their own funds to continue their activities. however, they represent a significant risk for commodity markets, in particular through the massive use of derivatives which can cause very high volatility and cause prices to fluctuate without any fundamental reason, while having negative consequences for the real economy. i therefore believe that the very fragile state of our financial system should encourage the commission to regulate these activities rather than ask for additional time.
in writing. ‒ the proposed amendment will allow commodity traders to benefit from an extension until 31 december 2020 of the derogations from the regulation's capital and large risk requirements. the commission considers it necessary to extend the derogations already provided for, taking into account the time needed to complete the review of investment firms and to develop, adopt and implement the legislation that could result from that process. the companies concerned represent a significant risk to commodity markets, in particular through the massive use of derivatives which can cause very high volatility and cause prices to fluctuate without any fundamental reason, while having adverse consequences for the real economy. it therefore seemed to me detrimental to the financial stability of our economies to leave the commission room to do work that should have been done well before the 2008 financial crisis. the very fragile state of our financial system should encourage the commission to regulate these activities, even if it is too cautious, rather than asking for three years' additional time. i voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution which applies to credit institutions and investment firms trading in raw materials. it is necessary that this review should lead to the establishment of a prudential framework appropriate to their situation. in order to ensure a stable legislative framework for investment firms, the already provided for derogations should be extended until 2017, taking into account the time needed to complete the review of investment firms and to develop, adopt and implement the legislation that may result from that process.
in writing. ‒ the amendment proposed by this report would allow commodity traders to benefit from an extension of the derogations from the requirements of the crr, the application of which could force them to significantly increase their own funds requirements to continue their activities and, consequently, increase their costs. the commission considers that the exemptions already provided for in the crr need to be extended in order to avoid such a situation. the very fragile state of our financial system should prompt the commission to regulate these activities, even if it is too cautious, rather than asking for an additional 3 years, especially in an area where prices can be so volatile, and especially since it should have already acted after the 2008 crisis. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ this report on exemptions for commodity traders should allow them to benefit from an extension until 31/12/2020 of the derogations from the requirements of the crr on large exposures and capital. the current framework for investment firms is under review. however, i do not think that legislation resulting from this process will be achieved before the expiry of the current derogations, i.e. on 31/12/2017. this could force commodity traders to significantly increase their capital requirements to continue their activities and could therefore increase the costs of doing so. the commission therefore considers it necessary to extend the derogations already provided for in the crr, since article 498 of the crr required the commission to report to parliament on the prudential regimes applied to commodity dealers 'by 31 december 2015 at the latest'. these companies represent a significant risk to the commodity markets (due to the use of derivatives) and i think that there should be no delay when this work should have been done much earlier. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the aim is to extend until 31 december 2020, without updating, the derogations granted to commodity dealers under the prudential framework defined by the crr and the capital requirements directive 2013/36/ec. in fact, according to article 498 of the crr, the commission was required to submit a report to parliament on these derogations before the end of 2015, which was not done. given the extreme volatility of commodity markets, i believe it is wiser to regulate these activities as soon as possible in order to avoid the risk of a large-scale financial crisis. i am therefore not in favour of postponing these derogations in the state until the end of 2020, and i voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ this council text reforms europol's governance and powers. the text establishes a monitoring group on governance, set up by the national parliaments and the parliamentarians of the competent committee of the european parliament. however, the european parliament's powers remain strictly limited. this is demonstrated by the way in which the executive director of europol is appointed: by the council from a list of names drawn up by the member states. his appointment shall be subject to an advisory opinion of the european parliament. the text formalises and clarifies europol's powers in the area of internet surveillance and the processing of personal data. the latter can now receive and transfer personal data from private individuals. it may also carry out analyses from ongoing surveys under the 'integrated data management' system. however, europol shall be subject to the control of a data protection officer internally and to the control of the european data protection supervisor externally. the processing of certain categories of data is also strictly regulated. the fight against organised crime is a priority. we do not, however, support the extensive powers granted to this quasi-federal police.

in writing. ‒ with a budget of 350 billion for the period 2014-2020, cohesion policy is one of the eu's main policies in budgetary terms. in theory, cohesion policy is supposed to reduce economic, social and territorial disparities between regions and complement other european policies in the fields of education, employment, energy, the environment, research and innovation. unfortunately, the european institutions are increasingly turning it into a means of submitting to the union's economic policies, in particular structural reforms, the implementation of the european semester and, therefore, austerity in general. so we are turning our backs more and more on the original objectives. the resolution supports this drift and calls for its implementation to be accelerated, while at the same time simplified to take account of delays in payment and the slow completion of current programmes. the gue/ngl tried during the negotiations to challenge these adverse developments. but it didn't work. the epp and s&d both voted in favour of the amendment on structural reforms. i have chosen to abstain in order to take account of the need for such funding for projects, particularly regional projects, but by refusing to endorse this new approach.
mr president, if these reforms are presented and adopted quickly, they will finally enable europe, but above all the states, and especially those which the geography of europe has placed on the external borders of the union, to manage and welcome in a responsible, solidarity-based, humane and dignified way the people who are fleeing war and violence. the first package of measures with the major reform of the dublin regulation is probably the most significant, and we have been calling for it for many months. so, if the commission has basically fulfilled a significant part of the contract with the negligence i bring, echoing cecilia and other colleagues, on the reception of unaccompanied minors , it is now time to make a clear appeal to the states, because the blockage of the states leads to the fact that, in the end, all the work on the "asylum" package that took place and negotiated from 2008 to 2012 has been so unfinished that after just two years, we are forced to reform it. this persistence in blocking and delaying is deadly both for refugees and for citizens, our fellow citizens who expect something else from europe.
mr president, the dublin regulation is not new. we know that this system is inefficient, unfair and expensive. the current crisis highlights these failures and reminds us that it is urgent to rethink them. however, the commission has not made this choice. i understand the reason, but i don't share it. i can think of two words to describe this proposal: re-busting and red rag. why re-arm? the dublin system had to be shaken to its foundations and will be maintained. the commission adds a touch of solidarity by providing for a specific relocation mechanism in the event of a crisis. but the basic mechanism of distribution is the same, and it's flawed. the commission does indeed envisage significant financial penalties for those who are unwilling to comply, but if this fine is intended to act as a deterrent, it is legitimate to think that this financial solidarity is realistic. unless the amount of financial penalties fixed also serves as a red cloth and is useful in diverting attention from certain objectionable provisions in the new regulation. i am thinking in particular of the quasi-punitive measures envisaged to combat the secondary movements of claimants. i am also thinking of the primacy of the concepts of 'safe third country' and 'first country of asylum' before any designation of the member state responsible for the examination. the dublin system's golden rule of first country of entry is not only maintained but strengthened. this mechanism will therefore continue to pose a number of logistical challenges in frontline countries to ensure individual examination, appeal procedures and a dignified reception of these populations. there is no easy solution to this problem, but i am not sure that the proposed calculation is the right one. the risk is that we end up with an unchanged dublin system, or worse, with reduced rights for applicants and even less readable arrangements for the states.
in writing. the commission finally puts forward a proposal to revise dublin. unfortunately, this is only a re-write, which does not call into question the foundations of the present system. we cannot accept that the criterion of irregular entry remains applicable. first-entry countries should become registration countries only, so that they no longer have to process asylum applications from everyone who arrives on their territory. the 'equity mechanism' should therefore not only apply in case of emergency, but on a permanent basis. finally, while the proposal to sanction countries which refuse solidarity is welcome, there must also be guarantees that these sanctions will be effectively applied. what is needed is a harmonisation and europeanisation of asylum procedures at european level, to create a unified and effective european asylum system. we must also advocate the creation of a genuine european asylum agency to oversee this new system and process asylum applications in a centralised way. the commission is proposing the creation of such an agency, but not in the same framework and not with the same powers. we will fight throughout the parliamentary process to improve this proposal, which does not meet our expectations.

for the greens/efa group mr president, dams are a real heritage for every european country. they have not only produced electricity but also shaped landscapes, changed valleys, and altered the flow of rivers. the challenges are therefore not only energy-related, but also strategic and safety-related for the population basins that have adapted to the river's course. in the case of renewal of concessions, the question is not whether the operator should be public or private, since it will pay the same fees anyway. the question is rather what added value a new concessionaire will bring and, above all, how the concessionaires will work together to manage the shared valleys. a great danger is looming with the renewal of concessions and their competition. the fragmentation of concessions and the lack of a comprehensive approach could threaten the proper management of a resource as vital as it is dangerous. accidents are rare but avoidable if the dams are well coordinated from upstream to downstream by grouping the dams in the same concession. my question is simple: will the commission favour concession contracts by dam or will it follow the obvious but necessary logic of grouping by valley?

author. madam president, what has been happening in djibouti for years is very worrying, and recent events are not reassuring. after revising the constitution to run for a fourth term in the presidential elections, president guelleh declared a state of emergency: murderous repression of the opposition, self-censorship of the only government press, extreme poverty, violence against women, and lack of respect for human rights. the only thing that could remind us that djibouti is supposed to be a democracy is the regular holding of elections - elections so rigged that president guelleh's scores no longer even create the illusion of democracy. in fact, it is still expected that european election observation missions will be able to be carried out. the african union, following these observation missions, recommends the establishment of an independent electoral commission to put an end to the democratic charade. the geography of djibouti makes it a strategic point that france has happily taken advantage of for years, since it has installed its main military base abroad. i have no doubt that my country is partly responsible for the political situation in djibouti, but so are other foreign powers: germany, china, japan and the united states also have military bases there. that is why i am calling not only on europe to act, but also on the countries militarily involved, so that they play their best role and not the one they have always been confined to playing, that is to say, defending their own interests. it's high time we put an end to hypocrisy.
author. madam president, according to many diplomats, and especially those of the countries that have military bases, and there are more and more of them, djibouti would be an anchor of stability. the reality is quite different. despite its considerable strengths, djibouti is ravaged by economic underdevelopment, widespread social misery and political gridlock, and the word is weak. this resolution is itself a revolution. i thank all those who contributed to it. in this resolution, we denounce in particular the growing repression in that country and, in particular, the one that followed the massacre of buldhoqo on 22 december 2015, in particular against those who dared to denounce the facts. we denounce the electoral masquerade of the presidential elections on 8 april. yes, all scores above 80% are, in general, tainted with irregularities. in fact, even the african union has acknowledged a number of irregularities. finally, we are here to echo the voices of those courageous djiboutian women who have begun a hunger strike to denounce the rape of which they are victims by members of the army, with impunity. we are calling for an independent international investigation. yes, there is an urgent need to lift the heavy weight of lead that weighs on this country and which the djiboutian people are paying for.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the automatic and compulsory exchange of information in the tax field. the text proposes the introduction of country-by-country reporting in order to combat aggressive tax optimisation. the purpose of this reporting will be to enable member states' tax administrations to ensure that multinational corporations' profits are taxed where they are realised. this reporting is therefore a tool in the fight against letterbox companies or fictitious or abusive addresses. it should also be noted that it is the member states which will be obliged to take the dissuasive sanctions in the event of non-compliance and which will derive the tax benefit from this.
in writing. - the rosati report is a first step which i welcome. however, in another text voted by the european parliament we have already obtained a similar public accounting report which is blocked in a scandalous way by the council. then there is the threshold: this country-by-country reporting will only apply to multinationals with more than €750 million in net annual turnover. we have fought to change this threshold, which de facto exempts 90% of multinationals. we have tabled an amendment to this effect, with the aim of lowering it to €40 million, the threshold corresponding to the definition of a 'large undertaking' in european law. it is incomprehensible that a section of the house, the conservative and liberal groups, refused to vote for transparency for all multinationals over €40 million. they voted in favour of this threshold last july; in the meantime, the panama papers have confirmed the need for force if necessary. the time was not right to slow down europe's fight against fraud and tax optimisation.
in writing. ‒ country reporting will be a tool in the fight against letterbox companies or fictitious or abusive addresses. it is the member states which are obliged to take the dissuasive sanctions in case of non-compliance and which will derive the tax benefit from this. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that european countries must unite to fight tax evasion, particularly that of multinationals. the lack of coordination in tax matters benefits big business and prevents europe from acting. i welcome this resolution which requires companies with a total turnover of eur 750 000 000 or more to complete a country-by-country declaration for their fiscal year.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report requiring automatic and mandatory exchanges of information in the tax area for companies with a turnover of more than eur 750 million. this report is a first step in the fight against tax optimisation or tax evasion. this is the translation into european law of an oecd agreement approved at the g20 last november. it requires multinational companies to report to tax administrations only, country by country, their main tax information: nature of activity, employees, turnover, profit before tax, total tax due, corporate taxes paid.
in writing. ‒ this report sets out parliament's position on the proposal for a council directive imposing country-by-country reporting in the fight against aggressive tax optimisation. the purpose of this provision is to enable the tax administrations of the member states to ensure that multinational corporations' profits are taxed where they are realised. the proposal for a directive would make it compulsory to report turnover, profit before tax, tax paid, etc., by country, in each jurisdiction where multinational groups operate. i voted in favour of this measure, which makes the automatic and compulsory exchange of information a tool in the fight against letterbox companies or fictitious or abusive addresses, especially since the text provides that it is the member states which will be obliged to take the dissuasive sanctions in case of non-compliance, and which will derive the tax benefit from it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text which contains the proposal for a directive to impose country-by-country reporting. the directive will make it possible to combat the abusive tax optimisation practices of certain multinationals, while protecting smes. it will allow member states to ensure that the profits of large companies (the proposed threshold is €750 million in turnover for the parent of the group, a sufficiently high threshold to avoid imposing new constraints on smes) are taxed where they are made. multinational companies would be required to report in each country their turnover, profit before tax, tax paid, employees, assets, or subsidies received. where appropriate, member states will be empowered to take dissuasive sanctions. finally, it would also constitute a tax advantage. the only disadvantage of this proposal for a directive is that the european commission is the primary recipient of the information and can decide whether or not the reporting should be made public. this point could potentially compromise business secrecy.
in writing. ‒ the rosati report sets out the european parliament's position on the proposal for a directive requiring country-by-country reporting in the fight against aggressive tax optimisation. this reporting enables member states' tax administrations to ensure that multinational corporations' profits are taxed where they are made. the proposal for a directive would make it compulsory to declare by country turnover, profit before tax, tax paid, employees, assets, subsidies received in each jurisdiction where multinational groups operate. for this main reason, i voted, through this report, to continue the legislative process.
in writing. ‒ the directive on the automatic and compulsory exchange of information in tax matters is part of the european commission's legislative package to improve tax transparency following the revelations of the luxleaks scandal. the european parliament was consulted on this text. the european commission is proposing that multinational companies with a turnover of €750 million or more provide the tax authorities of the member state in which they operate with a country-by-country declaration. this statement contains the turnover, profit before tax, profit taxes, number of employees and share capital of the multinational enterprise. this information will then be automatically and compulsorily exchanged with the other authorities of the member states concerned by the multinational. this directive is a major step forward in the fight against tax optimisation. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this consultation report concerns the revision of the rules on administrative cooperation in the field of taxation. this exchange of information between the tax authorities of the member states would become mandatory and automatic. the text proposes that multinational groups of companies provide certain information (amount of turnover; profit before tax; number of employees; share capital; intangible assets) annually for each tax jurisdiction in which they operate. all multinational groups with a turnover of more than eur 150 million (oecd standard) must complete this country-by-country declaration. i supported this report because i believe that multinational groups of companies should be transparent with regard to european tax jurisdictions.
in writing. ‒ the end of tax fraud and evasion requires the introduction of public country-by-country accounting reporting. the rosati report is a milestone, as it provides for the automatic and mandatory exchange of information between member states' administrations and aims to require multinationals to declare, country by country and to tax administrations only, their main information. i welcome this step forward, which for the time being will only apply to multinationals with a net annual turnover of more than €750 million. we have fought to change this threshold, which de facto exempts 90% of multinationals, without being heard for the time being, even though the panama papers scandal shows a general awareness. i am therefore concerned about the provisions introduced by the council in the directive on administrative cooperation, which weaken the general scope of the text.

in writing. ‒ in a different context from the financial globalisation we are experiencing, where capital flows freely from one end of the planet to the other, we would not even ask ourselves the question of tax optimisation, its morality, its legality and its harmful consequences. but in reality, even if the european level of decision-making is not satisfactory, we must act. that is why i voted in favour of mr rosati's report, which is part of the fight against tax evasion or aggressive tax planning by multinationals. it is no longer acceptable - it never was - that large corporations with huge profits, aided by armies of lawyers, escape taxation, while captive taxpayers, smes and citizens, are crushed by it. the so-called 'country-by-country reporting', i.e. the obligation to declare to the tax authorities the profits made by each country, taxes paid or due, turnover, staff numbers, etc., as well as the automatic exchange of this information between administrations should make it possible to detect suspicious behaviour. there are many negative aspects to this report, such as the role of the commission. but since the parliament's opinion was only advisory, this did not justify a different position.
in writing. following the revelations about the panama papers, a message of firmness must be sent to tax evaders. it's a social justice issue that i care about above all. that is why i supported this text, which is one of the three proposed in the 'moscovici package' against tax evasion presented last january, and which aims to require multinationals to declare, country by country, to tax administrations only, their main tax information: nature of activity, employees, turnover, profits before tax, total tax due, corporate tax, etc. for the socialists, the aim was to lower the threshold currently set for exempting multinationals below 40 million, not 750 million as proposed by the commission, thus exempting 90% of multinationals. we will continue to fight to raise this threshold and to achieve a country-by-country public ratio. conservatives and liberals must stop turning a deaf ear to the calls of our citizens for the firmness that seems needed now more than ever; it is simply unacceptable to go in any other direction.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution, which aims to provide solutions to the many cases of fraud detected in the labelling of fish in the retail sector. it is essential that consumers are able to know the commercial name of the species (as well as its scientific name), the production method and the gear used for fishing, the catch area and finally whether the product has been frozen beforehand. the text therefore provides for measures to increase transparency and traceability of products, such as the implementation of a public database indicating all the trade names for each species or the creation of an external structure that will certify information (voluntarily submitted) related to fishery and aquaculture products.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution calling for a reliable european fish labelling policy. several studies have shown that fishery products sold on union markets are often incorrectly labelled. such deception of consumers cannot be tolerated. they should be able to have full confidence in the whole supply chain of fishery products to the union market and it is our duty to protect them against such fraudulent practices. we call on the european commission to assess the benefits and feasibility of a robust eu-wide labelling system and to consider measures to improve the traceability of fishery and aquaculture products. the labelling must contain comprehensible, verifiable and accurate information to enable the consumer to make an informed choice. such a system would be beneficial for the development of coastal communities as it would highlight the best practices of fishermen as well as the quality of the products. this would also reduce dependence on trade in imported fishery and aquaculture products, thus consolidating the european market.
in writing. ‒ studies by the european commission and non-governmental organisations have identified cases of concern of incorrect fish labelling; i therefore supported this report which calls for consumer confidence in the product they consume to be strengthened and for them to have access to sound and reliable information. more than 70% of fishery and aquaculture products sold on the european market come from imports; in this sense, it is important that they meet the same traceability standards as european products and therefore be fully traceable. a traceability system for all fishery products sold in shops or restaurants in the european union would help prevent fraud and provide consumers with access to sound and reliable information.
in writing. ‒ i joined my colleagues in the committee on fisheries in pushing for the adoption of an oral question and a resolution on the traceability of fishery and aquaculture products in the catering and retail trade. a few months ago, a new scandal broke out over labelling. far less damaging than that of the horse, concerned the fraudulent designation of certain species labelled as more "noble" species. the scandal, however, has revealed the shortcomings in terms of traceability and consumer information. now the labels must indicate the fao zone where the fish was caught. but is it really clear to a consumer that a fish caught in the bay of biscay can come from brittany? in addition, labelling must be a traceability tool. i would like to make a few comments on the report by mr de gucht, which i think is very important. finally, i would like to see a european eco-label based on criteria which are formulated in a democratic and objective manner.
in writing. ‒ a study by the ngo oceana has revealed cases of mislabelling of fish served in restaurants in brussels, including in the european institutions. about one third of the fish tested were mislabeled. this study shows that the traceability of fishery products is not guaranteed, as there is no reliable labelling. the european eco-labelling system must be kept on a vigilant footing, as it could supplant the labels of the member states. labelling and the creation of labels, with the aim of improving the traceability and quality of products, is in line with what we are asking for. but we cannot accept a single european label which would effectively deprive the states of their right to create more stringent labels which would better protect consumers. i chose to abstain.
in writing. ‒ this resolution by the parliament's committee on fisheries concerns the traceability of fishery and aquaculture products in the catering and retail trade. studies have shown that fishery products on eu markets, in restaurants and even in the canteens of the parliament and the commission are often mislabeled. the labelling policy would improve the recognition of fishermen's best practices and the quality of products sold to consumers, and could enhance traceability and transparency of information for consumers. the union's maritime and fisheries fund is in a position to finance this and could in particular allow for the establishment of an independent structure certifying information on the labels of fishery products. this report, the main provisions of which remain optional, seems to me to be a step in the right direction for fishermen and consumers alike. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ this resolution, proposed by most political groups, deals with the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals to be achieved. the text proposes measures based on prohibitions, regulations, taxation, environmental incentives, often with few constraints: nothing is said about countries which refuse to submit to such constraints, such as the united states or china. similarly, the fact that the amount of waste and miscellaneous releases (soil erosion, carbon dioxide emissions, etc.) increased by 28% in the united states between 1975 and 1996 is not mentioned, nor is the crucial notion of natural resource limits. the resolution also calls for the european sustainable development strategy to be the subject of a broad consultation involving national parliaments, local authorities and civil society, which seems to be a no-brainer. the measures proposed in this resolution are insufficient and poorly targeted; so i voted against it.
