in writing. ‒ this resolution underlines the commitment of the 2030 agenda to sustainable development, which aims to eradicate poverty and redefine and modernise development strategies. meps stress the importance of consulting all stakeholders, including national parliaments and local authorities, in the process of drawing up the new eu sustainable development strategy. considering that it is essential to establish close cooperation between all stakeholders at the level of the european union and the united nations in order to assess the achievement of the sustainable development goals and to coordinate joint policies and programmes, i supported this resolution.
in writing. the 2030 agenda for sustainable development was adopted on 25 september 2015 by the united nations. it has 17 sustainable development goals. i supported this resolution on monitoring and progress in implementing these objectives because it encourages the establishment of a comprehensive strategy up to 2030, including internal and external policies.
in writing. ‒ in 2000, the un member states committed themselves to 15 years to achieve the "millennium development goals" to eliminate extreme poverty and hunger in the world and to ensure primary education for all. one year after the deadline, although we are still far from the objectives, it is clear that the international community has made significant progress. global poverty has been reduced, access to safe water has been expanded, and the number of children in primary school has increased. a new international framework for development policies must now be developed. for the european union, the world's largest provider of development aid, it is important to pursue an even more ambitious development strategy, and to focus on the issues that have emerged or intensified over the decade, such as the increase in inequalities and the challenges of climate change.
in writing. ‒ this text on the 2030 agenda and the objectives to be achieved in terms of sustainable development only highlights the inability of conferences, summits and meetings on this subject to change the concrete situation. prohibitions, regulations, taxes, environmental incentives have obviously not prevented man from consuming the stocks that the planet had built up over millions of years. the resolution requires countries to report on the 2030 agenda, including on the basis of indicators related to the sustainable development goals. in view of the inadequacies and shortcomings of this approach, i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i vote against: these are generally measures based on prohibitions, regulations, taxation, environmental incentives, with unfortunately very few constraints.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution because it represents a new step in the european union's commitment to sustainable development. it provides the necessary clarification of responsibilities but also encourages the development of new synergies between the european institutions in favour of the environment. these measures are the basis for a more effective and coordinated programme to achieve the ambitious targets set for 2030.
in writing. ‒ the resolution calls in particular for the european strategy for sustainable development to be the subject of a broad consultation involving national parliaments, local authorities and civil society. i support that, which is why i am voting in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls in particular for the european union to have a united position at the next un high-level political forum on sustainable development and to strengthen policy coherence for development.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the resolution on the follow-up and progress of the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals. the house also welcomed the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'common carrier' to cover all transport services, including the carriage of goods by road, and to extend the scope of the directive to include the carriage of goods by road. it is therefore disturbing to talk about sustainable development in these conditions. the text refers to the countless summits, texts, ranging from the un to the various gas factories of the european institutions. all the measures advocated, while they may be beneficial, have obviously not solved the problems so far, especially since countries such as the united states and china are not included.
in writing. - i voted against this text. it is drawn up by the majority of the political groups in parliament (epp, s&d, ecr, alde, efdd, gue) and aims to bring european citizens closer to the sustainable development objectives set out in agenda 2030. it called on the commission to develop a communication on the hlpf (high level political forum on sustainable development) to be held in september 2016. the text also aims to organise a broad consultation involving all civil society actors. the proposals are therefore a sham and do not address urgent situations such as the health crisis in greece, which is experiencing a sharp rise in infant mortality.
in writing. - i voted against this bill. this motion for a resolution is the initiative of the majority of the political groups in the european parliament. it aims to establish objectives in terms of sustainable development (economic development compatible with respect for the environment) for the needs of the 2030 agenda. this document will define the multiannual development strategy of the european union. the resolution calls on the commission to produce a comprehensive document on the progress made by 22 states, including four member states, in protecting the environment. this communication will be used at the un forum on sustainable development, scheduled for september 2016. we are not opposed to the necessary protection of the environment. however, the very notion of sustainable development is based on the idea of a 'world government' which we reject. we also have doubts about the effectiveness of measures taken by supranational bodies in the field of sustainable development.
in writing. ‒ the un has been working since september on renewed sustainable development goals, a roadmap for the next 15 years, through specific common development indicators. a meeting in july will discuss the progress of the work. while the commission and the council are discussing it, the european parliament has still not been consulted, a symbol of the low regard accorded to democracy in brussels. the resolution calls for the commission's proposal for an eu position on this work to be made public and for parliament to be duly consulted and involved. the text supports the objectives of eradicating poverty. it highlights the remarks of un experts on the need for resources in national statistical offices. otherwise, how can we establish reliable indicators of development? our concerns about tafta and other treaties for multinationals are irreconcilable with these objectives. they were therefore rejected. the text is very flawed, particularly on the paris agreement on climate change, and tends to defend the questionable idea of a necessary common eu position at the un, disregarding the sovereignty of states. i am voting in favour of the resolution to show my support for the work of the un.
in writing. ‒ the resolution is based on the concept of sustainable development. this unreasonable notion attempts to unite ecology with economic interests, with the practical inertia inherent in it. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the resolution calls in particular on the commission to produce a communication ahead of the sustainable development forum, scheduled for september 2016, to be held at the un with all member states. in the main, these measures are based on prohibitions, regulations, taxation and environmental incentives, with, unfortunately, very often little constraint. all these measures, while beneficial, have obviously not prevented the destruction of the planet and its resources, since it is also known that countries, such as the united states and china, are not affected by these measures. although we can only agree with the alarming observation made about the state of the planet and the plundering of resources by the industrial economy and the dogma of infinite growth, it is not desirable to support this resolution insofar as it ends up endorsing the hypocrisy of the world's leaders on these issues.
in writing. ‒ the resolution calls for the european sustainable development strategy to be the subject of a broad consultation involving national parliaments, local authorities and civil society, which seems to be a no-brainer. the most interesting amendment, therefore, comes from the gue and concerns concern about the threat of ttip, ceta, tisa. but as is often the case, support for this political group seems out of place. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the state of play of the 2030 agenda, which puts sustainable development and the fight against climate change in a common framework for both developed and developing countries. the resolution calls in particular on the european union to negotiate a united position in view of the forthcoming united nations high-level political forum on sustainable development (unhcp). it also calls for greater coherence in development policies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which calls for the european union to have a common and coherent position at the un high level political forum in july. the eu's participation in this high level political forum is crucial for the review of the implementation of the sustainable development goals adopted by the united nations in september 2015 (the 2030 agenda). it should also be noted that in this resolution the european parliament calls on the european commission and the eeas to come forward with concrete proposals on how to integrate policy coherence for development more effectively in the implementation of the 2030 agenda. it is a political priority for me to ensure the coherence of the actions of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament's role is to monitor the work of the european institutions and to participate in the development of their guidelines. in the context of the achievement of the objectives of the united nations 2030 agenda, i voted in favour of a resolution calling on the european commission to propose a comprehensive sustainable development strategy with a detailed timetable up to 2030 and also asking it to present a communication on the monitoring and review of this 2030 agenda, in order to understand the structure of its implementation at the level of the european union and its member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the follow-up and progress of the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals. this resolution reflects the position of the european parliament in view of the united nations high level political forum on sustainable development (unhcp) to be held in july 2016. the purpose of this forum is to assess needs and adopt the roadmaps needed to implement the 2030 agenda. in this context, the commission should propose a comprehensive sustainable development strategy and present a communication on the follow-up and review of the 2030 agenda. it will also be necessary to ensure that the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework (mff) reflects the commitments made by the union in agenda 2030. presenting a common and coherent position on sustainable development is important for the credibility of the european union. it should also effectively integrate policy coherence, in particular through regular dialogue with all stakeholders to ensure effective cooperation between the institutions. finally, there is a need to increase the democratic control of the european parliament in the implementation of agenda 2030.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which calls for the union to have a united position at the next un high level political forum on sustainable development and to strengthen policy coherence for development. the 2030 agenda and the sustainable development goals constitute a new international commitment to poverty eradication and new strategies for development policies. the aim is to emphasize the need to make development policies coherent with each other, both at european level and at international level, with the united nations, for example, and all other donors. i supported this text because it also recalls the need for the union to ensure that the review of the multiannual financial framework (mff) is an opportunity to take account of its commitments in the 2030 agenda.
in writing. ‒ the resolution, considering that optional labelling schemes only generate confusion (recital l), calls for mandatory indication of origin in a very broad way. there is a small caveat: in the light of this resolution, the draft national provision on indication of origin, which france recently notified to the commission and the member states, in accordance with the procedure established by regulation no 1169/2011, could well be considered as a 'best practice' to be shared, or even extended to the whole internal market through a specific implementing act adopted by the commission. i voted for this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution following an oral question on the compulsory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance for certain foodstuffs. the text calls for the mandatory indication of origin to be extended to a very large extent, given that optional labelling schemes only generate confusion. i strongly support these measures which help to inform european consumers more precisely. transparency about the country of origin or place of provenance of a foodstuff is a right for all citizens. we also recall that 'origin' cannot be reduced to a simple question of costs for enterprises, but must on the contrary be a lever in favour of the primary sector in particular. it is an instrument which can encourage an agricultural sector already badly affected by the european crisis which our farmers are suffering in france and elsewhere.
in writing. ‒ the resolution, considering that optional labelling only creates confusion, calls for the mandatory indication of origin of certain food products to be extended. i voted in favour of this resolution which improves tracing.
in writing. ‒ this resolution calls on the commission to follow up on its obligations to implement the standards, in accordance with article 26 (5) of regulation no 1169/2011 of 25 october 2011. the resolution calls for the mandatory indication of origin to be extended to a very large extent, as voluntary labelling schemes only create confusion. i voted in favour of this measure, which is aimed at extending the obligation to trace products to all consumers and thus ensuring the protection of consumers as well as smes who are committed to the quality of their products.
in writing. ‒ i welcome this resolution which encourages the member states of the european union to make it compulsory to indicate the country of origin or place of provenance for certain foodstuffs, such as dairy products and meat. in the past, my country has always fought for the respect and protection of the indication of origin of its own products in international trade - i am thinking in particular of our wines, our champagne and our cheeses - and it is only logical to extend this protection to other products and to all the countries of the union. such protection not only protects the interests of the industries of the member states but also contributes to the necessary protection of consumers and, in the case of foodstuffs, to the welfare of animals.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution which calls for the country of origin indication for certain foodstuffs to be made compulsory, given the inefficiency of optional labelling. i believe that this is a necessary measure to protect the food security of the citizens of the member states. in particular, regulation (eu) no 1169/2011 gives member states the right, depending on local practice and the circumstances, to have non-prepacked food regulations. respect for the traditions and sovereignty of the european nations, but also the guarantee of the protection of this food safety standard, even in the event that ttip is implemented.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the mandatory indication of the country of origin on dairy products, meat and processed meat. i think it is essential that consumers are fully informed about what is on their plates. transparency throughout the food chain is an absolute necessity. strict labelling of dairy products, meat and processed meat should be made compulsory in order to improve food traceability. we must learn the lessons of the horse meat scandal. the resolution calls on the commission to draw up a proposal to make the country of origin labelling of certain foodstuffs compulsory.
in writing. ‒ this resolution aims to respond to the various reports published by the european commission on the issue of labelling in relation to regulation (eu) no 1169/2011 and the various resolutions adopted by the european parliament, the latest of which was dated 11 february 2015. this resolution, unlike the 2015 resolution, does not only cover meat used in processed foods, but also milk for consumption and milk used as an ingredient in dairy products and other types of meat. it also mentions eggs and egg products. the resolution calls for the compulsory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance of these foodstuffs. it therefore calls on the european commission to draw up legislative proposals in these areas. although i am not opposed in principle to mandatory labelling, i believe that it poses real challenges in terms of means, control, cost and implementation. in addition, in terms of international trade, such a measure could hinder our products for export, even though it could promote consumer information, traceability and citizen consumption in relation to imported products. considering all the evidence, i abstained.
in writing. in line with the expectations of french consumers and farmers, and taking into account the economic feasibility of such a measure, i voted in favour of this resolution which should allow for better traceability of dairy products, meat and processed meat.
in writing. ‒ the demands of european consumers for food labelling are clear and unambiguous. according to a 2013 commission report, more than 90% of europeans believe that mandatory labelling should be applied to processed products. 88% of them think it is necessary for meat, and 84% for milk. the introduction of such a measure would be a major step forward, both in terms of transparency in the food chain and consumer information. this could help to avoid food fraud scandals, such as the one involving horse meat in 2013. the new resolution, which follows a series of texts adopted by parliament on mandatory labelling, should encourage the european commission to make a legislative proposal on this matter as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i am afraid that the mere use of voluntary indication of the origin of products creates two categories of consumers: those who will have the choice of the product they want and those who will not. so we have to reconcile consumers with their food after the various food crises we have experienced. that is why i voted in favour of the resolution on the compulsory indication of the country of origin or place of provenance for certain foodstuffs. farmers and processors already have an obligation to trace. i therefore want to strike a balance between the interests of consumers and the competitiveness of our businesses. it seems to me that a mandatory common european framework would be less distortive than a voluntary one.

in writing. - everyone wants to know what they eat and where it comes from. i'll go first it's not even politics anymore, it's common sense. that is why i have always supported the compulsory indication of the country of origin in this house. today's resolution calls for this to be compulsory for all meat and milk, including when these products are used as ingredients in food. i would have liked to have added the slaughter methods, but i am in full support of this proposal as it stands. opponents of this measure argue that it would lead to additional costs for the agri-food sector, which is far from being confirmed by studies, let alone by reality, where voluntary schemes exist. my country is also preparing to set up an experiment in this field. it is true that labelling is not a guarantee against fraud and cannot replace necessary checks. but it is a question of informing the consumer while leaving him, as far as his financial means allow him, the freedom to choose. perhaps this is what is frightening: that this free choice may lead systematically and massively to a national and local preference, which would de facto call into question the dreams that some people have of a totally globalised agricultural market.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament today adopted by a large majority yet another resolution calling on the european commission to speed up the revision of the consumer information regulation to make it compulsory to indicate the origin of meat and milk used as ingredients in prepared dishes. three years after the food and health scandal of 'horse lasagna', the european commission is still unable to give a positive answer to 70% of european consumers who are calling for this information to be compulsory. the european commission objects to this by claiming that the cost of the new system would be 20% to 50% higher than the current price. these figures are more than exaggerated. the mandatory traceability system for fresh meat is working and can easily be extended to meat in prepared dishes. all studies show that such traceability and transparency would not be costly. the commission must stop its false pretenses and delaying manoeuvres: it is time for action. i welcome the experimental approach taken by the french government and we must call on the european commission to extend this scheme to all the member states. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution in favour of country of origin labelling, particularly for meat, in particular to avoid the recurrence of new scandals, such as those linked to horse meat or other cases of food fraud. the text is balanced in that it responds to strong consumer demand and takes account of the problems associated with the risk of increased costs and administrative burden for businesses having to apply the legislation.
in writing. ‒ meps had already called on the commission in february 2015 to adopt rules to make it mandatory to indicate the origin of meat in processed foods. it is may 2016 and jean-claude juncker and his team have still not moved. worse, health commissioner andriukaitis reiterated that the commission would do nothing about mandatory labelling. i am disappointed that the amendment by the environmentalists calling for animal-derived foods to be labelled as containing gmo residues has been rejected. transparency is important for consumers, but the conservative majority rejected this amendment. it also rejected our amendment requiring that the origin of meat be labelled as soon as it exceeds 10% of the composition of a prepared food. this would have involved quiches, lasagnas or ravioli. this vote is a step in the right direction despite the attempts to sabotage the conservatives who tried to pass amendments to remove the reference to 'mandatory' labelling, but failed.
in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution calling on the european commission to come forward with legislative proposals to make the indication of the country of origin or place of provenance for certain foodstuffs compulsory. it is time to provide a clear and effective response to french and european consumers who, according to several studies, want to know the origin of the food they consume. the voluntary system is not enough, more than one product in two in france does not indicate the place of origin. the european commission must act to ensure transparency and traceability throughout the food supply chain. that is why i have reiterated my support for mandatory labelling of processed food products to indicate the country of origin or place of provenance of the meat. we also call for the mandatory labelling to be extended to other foodstuffs and propose that labelling for drinking milk and lightly processed dairy products (such as cheese and cream) and lightly processed meat products (such as bacon and sausages) be considered as a matter of priority. this resolution is a strong message that reflects the interest of consumers to be better informed so that they can make informed choices about their food.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which calls for the introduction of mandatory country of origin labelling for meat, processed meat, milk and milk used as an ingredient in dairy products. the resolution comes as a commission report shows that 84% of eu citizens believe it is necessary to indicate the origin of milk and 88% consider such labelling necessary for meat. mandatory labelling would help to maintain consumer confidence in food products, in particular french products, which meet high quality criteria, make the food chain more transparent and increase the added value it generates for farmers and the whole sector. i supported this resolution because it allows further reflection on the question of the labelling of meat and milk. however, it is essential to take account of the increase in costs and administrative burdens in order to strike a balance between the interests of our consumers and the competitiveness of our businesses.
in writing. ‒ this resolution deals with the country of origin labelling of certain foodstuffs, such as milk or meat, in processed foods. the stated aim is to ensure transparency in the food chain and to restore consumer confidence, which has been shaken by several scandals, including the horse meat fraud in 2013. in fact, despite the scandals, the european commission still defends labelling on a purely voluntary basis. this approach has shown its limitations and the aim here is to achieve mandatory labelling for so-called 'minor' types of meat (other than beef, pig, sheep, goat and poultry meat, for which mandatory labelling already applies), milk, unprocessed food, single ingredient products and ingredients which constitute more than 50% of a food. the epp has tried in every way to weaken this resolution by using the usual argument of the cost to smes, whereas in my view they will be the first beneficiaries and transparency is in any case a point on which we should not compromise under the pretext of weakening the market. i voted for this resolution and i welcome its adoption by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the application of council directive 2010/18/eu of 8 march 2010 implementing the revised framework agreement on parental leave. the aim here is to assess the implementation of parental leave legislation in the various member states. despite some measures that deserve our support, such as the reduction of administrative barriers to easier access to parental leave, the possibility of extending the scope of parental leave or the special attention to be paid to children with disabilities, this report has many problems of substance. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right to vote. it should also be noted that this text proposes real interference in family affairs by seeking to remedy the low participation of fathers in parental leave and to increase the employment rate of women substantially, whereas this should be the choice of each family. we believe, on the contrary, that the economic difficulties facing european citizens are not linked to and should not be compared with family life.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the text by my colleague marie arena. today, in the european union, workers can take parental leave when a child is born or adopted. however, the conditions for access to this right and the financial compensation vary considerably between member states. it is clear that men and women are not equal when it comes to parental leave. it is essential that member states address this imbalance in order to achieve a true work-life balance for both sexes.
in writing. ‒ under the pretext of the best interests of the child, the value of the role of parents, social policies for families, it is in reality the political will to achieve an employment rate of 75% for women that is expressed here. the report states that unemployment and precariousness are the result of economic difficulties. i voted against this biased report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, as the committee had recommended in its report. i am surprised, however, that europe is suggested to have any real competence in this area. such an initiative may lead to misunderstandings and frustrations.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to assess the implementation of parental leave legislation in the different member states, in order to ensure 'gender equality' and fairness in the distribution of family tasks between men and women. in concrete terms, the report proposes to simplify the transposition of european legislation, which constitutes a further attack on the sovereignty of the member states and on the principle of subsidiarity. it also interferes with the family and intimate life of couples, bringing economic difficulties and family life into competition. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ it goes without saying that family law, child education and social and family security benefits must remain the responsibility of the member states. i am not, however, opposed to the union's initiative to encourage member states to take measures to promote the taking of parental leave. i believe it is essential to guarantee women the right to work and be mothers. all too often, it should be remembered, economic and occupational pressures cause women to forgo maternity leave. balancing work and life is not easy, as we all know. i would like to remind you, however, that the family is currently under attack from all sides, with the recognition of the gpa, adoptions by homosexual couples and attacks on traditional marriage. the family is the natural and fundamental element of society. we have to protect her. in this sense, encouraging parental leave for educational purposes is a first step. the second would be to establish a genuine parental wage.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report to assess the implementation of parental leave legislation. first of all, it should be remembered that the child must live with the mother and the father. this diversity is reflected in the level of social security benefits in the member states. the rapporteur himself acknowledges these differences in social models, but he calls for harmonization, particularly by means of a real infringement of the family and personal life of the insured, since he calls in particular for the individualisation of parental leave and the non-transferability of a significant part of it. i find this stance shocking, particularly because it challenges the freedom of each couple to make their own decisions, and, worse, the freedom of women to decide whether to work or stay at home to raise their children. the real objective of this report is to achieve the targets set by the europe 2020 strategy, which calls for 75% of women in the labour market. women are thus reduced to a mere economic adjustment variable, to the detriment of their true freedom.
in writing. ‒ parental leave is very important in order to enable parents to accompany their children during their youth. it promotes family relationships and child rearing. it also promotes equality between men and women in their roles within the family structure. council directive 2010/18/eu on the implementation of the revised framework agreement on parental leave states that all workers are entitled to four months of parental leave. it is important that all member states comply with the requirements laid down in this directive. member states should also exchange good practice so that the directive fully encourages both parents to take parental leave, not just women, which is the current trend. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the framework agreement on parental leave, tabled by maria arena. it is more necessary than ever to affirm the need to apply common european rules on parental leave. in general, i welcome the extension of the minimum duration of unpaid parental leave from four to at least six months and the introduction of european rules on a minimum of two weeks paternity leave. the differences in parental leave are still too great between the countries of the union. this report is a step in the right direction in terms of conditions for access to this right, in particular by requiring member states to guarantee equal access to parental leave and incentives to encourage fathers to take it. moreover, at a time when financial compensation for parental leave varies considerably, the report calls on member states to review their systems with a view to achieving a level of adequate income replacement that is both decent and incentive.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report concerns the directive implementing the framework agreement on parental leave. it aims to achieve a balance between parental and professional life within the european union. the rapporteur proposes that paternity leave be extended to two weeks in all member states and that parental leave be used flexibly, with both parents being entitled to it under the same conditions. since french legislation already allows for 11 days of parental leave, i supported this report.
in writing. ‒ there is a great asymmetry in the implementation of parental leave today. the rights vary from one state to another depending on the sectors of employment public or private and the type of contract. and many eu member states still do not offer the possibility of paternity leave. ensuring a minimum set of european rules and harmonising these rules at european level would allow for greater equity and a better balance between the professional and private lives of men and women across the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the arena report on the revised framework agreement on parental leave because it is important to find a better work-life balance for all parents and to facilitate their reintegration into the labour market after the birth of the child. it is necessary to adopt common rules on minimum parental leave at eu level. i therefore supported this report in order to make parental leave available to all workers, regardless of the type of employment contract. furthermore, it seems to me that encouraging fathers to take parental leave is a way of strengthening the principle of equality between men and women in employment, which is enshrined in european legislation and defended by the epp group, and of avoiding discrimination against women in the labour market.
in writing. ‒ vote against: we believe that the economic difficulties faced by european citizens, which lead to unemployment and precariousness, are not linked to and should not be compared with family life.
in writing. ‒ the report by ms arena could have been limited to a few points: the need to further improve the reconciliation between private and professional life, but through non-legislative initiatives and the exchange of good practice; the assertion that social protection is the sole responsibility of the states; the finding that most national legislation on parental leave goes beyond the minimum european requirements, which are therefore not decisive; the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the programme. it could have avoided idle ideological considerations and contradictions: recognition of parents' autonomy and full responsibility in their organisation (this is welcome), but wanting to limit this autonomy by binding prescriptions and non-transferability of rights, or aiming for further harmonisation and strengthening the role of the commission. but i voted against this report mainly because it is basically there to promote a high female employment rate: 75% by 2020. first workers, secondarily mothers for the reproduction of the workforce. i believe in the crucial role of women and the family in society, including in their specific and irreplaceable functions, and i support a policy which would give them complete freedom of choice.
in writing. despite the speeches of european leaders in favour of 'fighting all forms of discrimination, including gender-based discrimination', it is clear that in reality we are far from the gender equality that socialists want. that is why i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mrs marie arena, because, although only 2.7% of fathers in europe take parental leave today, it is essential to combat this imbalance which contributes to the economic and social dependence of women and prevents their emancipation. a review of the parental leave directive is therefore essential and should include: a strengthening of incentives such as decent financial compensation for the length of leave, keeping a significant part of parental leave as non-transferable, improving access to affordable childcare services, or increasing the length of parental leave and the period during which it can be used. finally, there is an urgent need to revise the maternity leave directive and adopt a directive establishing a minimum of two weeks of parental leave, at the risk of europe disappointing its citizens again.

in writing. - i voted against this bill. the report aims to assess the implementation of parental leave legislation in the various member states. we oppose the desire for uniformity which emerges from this text, which aims to ensure gender equality and a fair balance in the distribution of family tasks between men and women, emphasizing the economic contribution that greater participation of women in the labour market would represent. we oppose this affront to the sovereignty of the member states and the disregard for the principle of subsidiarity. we oppose the interference with the family and even the private life of european couples by the individualisation of parental leave and the non-transferability of a significant part of it. although we are in favour of the possibility of extending the scope of parental leave, of special attention to children with disabilities and of adequate remuneration, we dispute that these measures hide a political will to achieve the objectives set by strategy 2020, namely a female employment rate of 75%. we are opposed to economic difficulties upsetting the balance of family life.
in writing. ‒ the 1996 parental leave directive currently in force provides that all workers are entitled to a minimum of four months of unpaid parental leave, of which one month is non-transferable (to the other parent). the report proposes to go further, taking into account the persistent gender pay gap. in fact, since men are paid more (+16.2% on average), it is often women who take this leave. the question of paid leave is therefore of paramount importance. the report advocates, without giving details, an "adequate and decent income that is an incentive". he advocates more generally a better reconciliation between work and private life. he proposed in particular that leave be reduced to a minimum of six months and that atypical contracts such as the zero-hour contract, which was very popular with mrs merkel and mr cameron, be covered. it also proposes to set and extend the age limit for children to be entitled to parental or carer's leave if they are disabled. he's requesting a soft resumption at the same station. the commission also stressed that the commission had not listened to parliament's requests for improvements in maternity and paternity leave. i vote for this request for social harmonization upwards.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to propose new directives on maternity and paternity leave, but also to revise parental leave legislation, in particular as regards its duration, remuneration and transferability. the adoption of a text which revises the legislation in force is welcome, since there are now many differences in the arrangements for parental leave.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the arena report and in favour of three points which i considered essential and for which i had to remain faithful to french laws in this area. in france, fathers can take paternity leave for 11 consecutive days (18 days for multiple births) within 4 months of the birth of the child, in addition to the 3 days of leave for childbirth. the law on marriage for all of may 18, 2013 allows same-sex marriage. it opened up new rights for marriage, adoption and inheritance. it allows for joint adoption of a child by both spouses or for the spouse's child to be adopted. parental authority is thus shared by both spouses, which gives them access to all parental rights, including parental leave. finally, since january 2015, in order to reduce the professional penalty for mothers, the duration of parental leave for a first child is 6 months maximum for a single parent and 1 year in the case of both parents taking leave.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on parental leave. there are currently disparities in the transposition of the european directive on parental leave in the member states; in some member states, for example, a worker will be less likely to take leave if he is employed under a fixed-term contract. there is also a persistent gender imbalance, with fathers making little use of their parental leave rights. it is therefore necessary to implement measures to strengthen the use of parental leave and to promote effectively a better reconciliation of work and private life. in particular, fathers should be encouraged to make greater use of parental leave, which would help to reduce discrimination against women in the labour market. equal career opportunities for men and women would also help to achieve the 75% employment rate target set in the europe 2020 strategy. finally, i think that the commission should improve and strengthen the provisions on parental leave for parents of children with disabilities or with serious or long-term disability-related illnesses.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which calls for better implementation of the common rules on minimum parental leave. in 2013, the union adopted a directive on the application of the framework agreement on parental leave. the text calls on the member states to guarantee working parents, particularly fathers, their right to take parental leave. today, only 10 percent of fathers take at least one day of parental leave. the commission is therefore asked to carry out a detailed analysis of the state of application of the directive in the member states, but also to call for the right of both parents, regardless of gender, to be guaranteed. it is essential to remember that the right to parental leave must not be conditioned by the nature of the employment contract.

in writing. ‒ this report deals with the application of the parental leave directive, which is one of the elements of the union's policies for equality between women and men. it contributes to a better balance between private and professional life and a better division of family tasks and promotes the return to employment for those who decide to stop working to take care of their young children. but while all member states have adopted parental leave, there are significant differences between the states and at least a limited number of fathers benefit from it: only 10% of them and taking them into account from day one. this leave remains poorly paid and not fully covered. given the gender pay gap, it is still more economically advantageous for the mother to stop working. this directive should be reviewed to take account of these elements, in particular with regard to his remuneration. as usual in the case of women's rights, the national front voted against. i voted yes.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this text on the implementation of directive 2011/36/eu of 5 april 2011 on preventing and combating trafficking in human beings and protecting victims from a gender perspective. the report aims to combat human trafficking and, in particular, the various forms of exploitation of women: pimping, begging, clandestine domestic work, forced marriage, organ trafficking and illegal adoptions. women and girls account for 80% of the registered victims of trafficking. while this objective is obviously commendable, the final text is not. the text proposes to regularize the victims of trafficking in the member states where they reside by creating safe channels for legal migration. the report also calls for the punishment of clients for prostitution, whereas it would seem more useful to actually crack down on pimps who are not deterred by the light sentences imposed on them. finally, it should be noted that the penalties imposed on criminals are by no means deterrent and therefore do not serve to impede the activity of these criminal networks. for all these reasons, i opposed this report.

in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report gives an account of the development of virtual currencies, the main danger of which, in addition to the dematerialization of money, which is supposed to be tangible, is the emergence of an international currency market independent of the power of central banks and therefore of states. it is also feared that one of the motivations for large international banks to invest in virtual currencies is the possible establishment of an interbank market managed exclusively by them. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which welcomes the dematerialization of money through so-called virtual currencies. however, they pose a great danger, as they are totally opaque to transactions conducive to criminal activities such as money laundering, terrorist financing or tax fraud and/or evasion. moreover, although they remain marginal today - with "bitcoin" holding 90% of the shares of this market for "only" 5 billion euros - these virtual currencies raise the risk of creating a foreign exchange market independent of the power of central banks, and therefore a fortiori, of states. eventually, the result would be an interbank market run exclusively by the big international banks and thus the unlimited and unrestricted submission of all to the power of money. however, i would be less categorical about distributed ledger technology (dlt), which, if used correctly, offers tremendous potential, for example in terms of crowdfunding.
in writing. ‒ there are two main dangers of virtual currencies. first, they give rise to an international currency market independent of the power of central banks and thus of the states. second, transactions made with these currencies allow for complete anonymity. they are thus used mainly on the 'black market' for money laundering, terrorist financing, tax fraud and evasion and other criminal activities. these currencies have no real basis, are not subject to any regulation and are mainly used to finance criminal activities. distributed ledger technology allows large amounts of transactions to be processed reliably and very quickly. its potential is expanding beyond the financial sector. this technology also presents an opportunity for public bodies by simplifying and securing e-government services and data protection. i shall vote against this report, which presents virtual currencies as a means of making a positive contribution to the development of the economy and of peoples.
in writing. ‒ this report provides an overview of the development of virtual currencies and the underlying technology that enables them to operate. virtual currencies are presented as a means of making a positive contribution to the economic development of our nations. we believe that they are a real danger because they are completely outside the control of central banks and governments. in addition, virtual currencies offer complete anonymity to those who use them to carry out transactions; they are therefore mainly used to finance criminal activities. because we are opposed to the use of these virtual currencies, which are not subject to any regulation, i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ virtual currencies are digital representations of a value that are not issued by a bank or a public authority. they are not necessarily linked to a fiat currency but are accepted as a means of payment. there are more than 600 virtual currency systems. the most well-known of these is bitcoin. the commission has also concluded that the measures provided for in this regulation are in accordance with the opinion of the committee established by article 15 (1) of regulation (eu) no 1095/2010. they also entail certain risks linked to the lack of governance, which leads to insecurity and consumer protection problems, as well as volatility and legal uncertainty. the report does not call for immediate legislation on virtual currencies but proposes a thorough impact assessment before any new legislation in this area. the report calls for the creation of a task force on virtual currencies and distributed ledger technology led by the commission and composed of regulatory and technical experts. the aim is to eventually create a proportionate regulatory framework that does not constitute a brake on innovation. i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - i voted for this report. the aim is to provide financial assistance of eur 5.1 million to the 2 132 employees of the french road haulage company moryglobal. the latter was liquidated in 2015. the report does not in any way call into question the harmful effects of the free movement of workers and the posting directive. the posting of workers directive allows an employer to pay the social security contributions of the home country of an employee from another member state. in france, this difference in social contributions is about 30%. the road transport sector employs the majority of posted workers in france. in addition, road cabotage, which consists in the possibility for a european carrier to deliver goods between two cities in a member state in which it is not established, aggravates this social dumping. these considerations aside, we support this report. we want these former employees to be able to benefit from this welcome material support.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this request for the waiver of the parliamentary immunity of gianluca buonanno. the member, who was allegedly the victim of telephone threats received from an anonymous correspondent on his mobile phone number, has initiated criminal proceedings before the vercelli court. for the purposes of the investigation (access to telephone records) and for reasons of legal certainty, gianluca buonanno's immunity must be waived. i approved that request.
in writing. ‒ on 14 april 2015, gianluca buonanno was allegedly the victim of a threatening phone call received from an anonymous correspondent on his mobile phone number. mr buonanno then brought criminal proceedings before the vercelli court. for the purposes of the investigation, the deputy public prosecutor of the vercelli court submitted an application for permission to obtain from telephone companies data concerning the recordings of a number used by a member of the european parliament. the immunities of members of the european parliament and the constitution of the italian republic, which in article 68 makes any telephone tapping of a member subject to the authorisation of the chamber to which he belongs, must be taken into account. access to telephone records, as in this case, is treated as a telephone tapping. as a precaution, the deputy prosecutor of the vercelli court preferred to extend parliamentary privilege also to cases where the member is the alleged victim of a crime. this request for waiver of immunity will allow the author of the threats to which mr buonanno has been subjected to be unmasked and brought to justice. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the legislative resolution, the committee's proposal, the amendments and the motion for rejection. this report concerns decisions 2015/1523 and 2015/1601 establishing provisional measures in favour of italy and greece in response to the influx of migrants. sweden received a total of 170 104 asylum seekers in march 2016. it therefore wishes to benefit from provisional measures suspending its reception obligations. we would not be able to support the swedish government. the council has always advocated the acceptance of migrants by the member states through the introduction of quotas. so this turn of events is inappropriate. in addition, the return of migrants by sweden will lead to their relocation to other member states. nor do we support the motion for rejection of the swedish request, tabled by 40 members. this motion calls for strict application of migrant quotas to the member states. clearly, the european union's migration policy is at an impasse. it is urgent to return to the states their prerogatives in immigration control.
in writing. ‒ this is a text calling for the distribution of immigrants in europe, to alleviate sweden, which has welcomed these populations in turn (170 000 in march). more than 40 meps have demonstrated to force member states to accept quotas. i am opposed to this text, firstly because the commission has nothing to impose on the member states and secondly because this allocation does not work. finally, sweden has supported highly unreasonable migration policies and these steps only bind sweden. i therefore voted against these texts.
in writing. ‒ the eu's principle of quotas for the distribution of migrants is odious. it is not working, and it is contrary to the principle of the sovereignty of nations. there is no point in introducing provisional measures to deal with the problems of the common asylum and immigration policy. the member states must be given the power to develop their own policies in this area.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which aims to allow sweden, overwhelmed by the influx of migrants, to temporarily escape its obligations in the field of migration policy. last year, sweden was the member state with the highest number of asylum seekers per capita. in march 2016, it received a total of 170 104 applicants, including 73 331 children, including 36 181 unaccompanied minors. i opposed an amendment by the greens which proposed that sweden should not be granted these emergency measures.
in writing. ‒ like many eu countries, sweden has been faced with a massive influx of migrants to its territory. in one year, the number of asylum seekers in the country increased by 60%, which led to a deterioration in reception conditions and in fact a deterioration in the functioning of the asylum application system in sweden. for these reasons i voted in favour of the interim measures on international protection for sweden to adapt to the reality of the situation in the country. the way to deal with this migrant crisis is to be pragmatic and not dogmatic.
in writing. ‒ sweden is the eu country that receives the most asylum seekers and refugees in proportion to its population. that member state has requested a temporary derogation from the commission in order not to implement its relocation obligations for one year. the aim of this interim measure is to enable the swedish authorities to rebuild their reception capacities (in particular in the fields of education, health and housing), in order to be able to fully meet their european commitments. sweden has no intention of stopping receiving people in need of international protection, especially as asylum seekers and many unaccompanied minors arrive in sweden every day outside the framework of relocation measures. i have decided to vote in favour of the commission's proposal to grant this temporary derogation. it would be incomprehensible to punish one of the few countries in the union which already hosts a large number of refugees and which wants to receive more, but under better conditions, while other member states continue to shamefully refuse to fulfil their obligations to receive and to trample on calls for solidarity.

in writing. ‒ sweden is the country that has taken in the most refugees in recent months in proportion to its population and this is what the swedish government is using today to ask to suspend its participation in the relocation mechanism for asylum seekers from greece and italy to other states. the commission rejected this request and came back with a compromise: to suspend this mechanism for one year. the rapporteur, ska keller, first proposed a straightforward rejection of this temporary exemption but this was not adopted in the vote in the libe committee. since the beginning of this humanitarian 'crisis', i have been insisting that the member states should show solidarity as demanded by the citizens of europe. the latter must stop focusing on national interests and take responsibility for the urgency of the situation, and this should continue to concern sweden. granting it an exemption would send the wrong signal to the other member states, which would refuse any effort at solidarity. the gue/ngl tabled an amendment rejecting this exemption which was not adopted. i therefore voted against this resolution, which takes up the commission's compromise proposal.
in writing. ‒ in the context of the negotiations on the transatlantic treaty between the european union and the united states, the issue of the protection of europeans' personal data is more than ever at the centre of the debate. however, in its judgment of 6 october 2015, the court of justice of the european union annulled the commission's decision on the adequacy of the levels of protection provided by the safe harbour principles, published by the us department of commerce. the commission and the us government have mentioned a 'privacy shield', but the joint resolution which tends to support this idea seems optimistic about the possibility of getting the americans to change their minds on this point. i therefore supported the first resolution which criticises the lack of provisions on privacy. i voted against the final motion for a resolution, which only deals with principles and considerations in very general terms and does not require sufficient guarantees. the protection of our citizens' personal data is paramount.

in writing. ‒ the fight against poverty is a key objective of the european union in the europe 2020 strategy. it is clear that there is a gender dimension to this phenomenon. in fact, worldwide, more than 65 million women live in poverty, compared with 57 million men. this difference may be explained by the persistent inequalities between men and women, particularly in terms of work and role within the family structure. too often women are discriminated against in relation to men in accessing a profession. this is just one example of the many discriminations faced by women. the report explains that gender inequalities can lead to a greater propensity for poverty among women than among men and that these inequalities must therefore be addressed. that is the main message of this report. i therefore voted in favour of this report, even though i do not agree with some of the points in it.

in writing. ‒ this report aims to provide guidance on how to tackle one of the most well-known problems of the european single market: its fragmentation. combined with the crisis, which saw the number of unemployed in the union rise to 22 million in 2015, this represents a shortfall of almost €1 trillion. by removing unnecessary barriers, non-tariff barriers, and promoting greater legislative and regulatory harmonisation, rapid results could be achieved in competitiveness, sustainable growth, research, innovation, consumer protection, job creation and investment, in particular for infrastructure, as well as the flourishing of smes and the most innovative companies in the union (in particular by facilitating their access to finance). while the report is not yet a legislative one, it is nevertheless a strong political message from meps to the commission and the member states to move towards greater integration. this is an initiative that can only be welcomed and encouraged, which is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ the single market, beyond its symbol for european integration, remains a vehicle for growth, competitiveness, innovation and employment, provided it adapts and responds to new developments. it is an asset that must be used in the best possible way to strengthen the european economy, consolidate its strengths and unlock its potential. unjustified obstacles to this should therefore be removed. the house therefore affirms its support for the general objectives of the commission's strategy for the single market in goods and services and calls for a more modern and innovative, deeper and fairer single market. our resolution covers many aspects such as the adaptation of the single market to the digital revolution, the importance of adequate consumer information and country of origin labelling, and the need to ensure a high level of consumer protection both online and offline. i was generally satisfied with the final text, and i therefore supported it.

mr president, nuclear disasters are one of the worst threats to mankind. the 1986 chernobyl and 2011 fukushima accidents must be taken very seriously; the european parliament is therefore rightly concerned about the safety of the ostrovets nuclear power plant, which belarus is currently completing construction with a view to starting operation in 2018. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the costs of the plant. this test is a necessary precaution. it was carried out after fukushima on 145 reactors in the european union and on 20 reactors outside the union. the 2013 resolution has thus developed a nuclear safety culture in europe that belarus would be well advised to respect. this is all the more desirable since the ostrovets power station is located only 50 kilometres from vilnius, the capital of lithuania. nuclear safety is also the subject of international cooperation organized under the control of the international atomic energy agency by the treaty of 17 june 1994. this international cooperation will of course be continued in the context of the europe of nations, which i wish to see. the legitimate concern about the safety of ostrovets must not, however, be used by the union to attack russia once again. belarus is an ally of russia, which deployed a military air base there in 2015, and it is known that russia financed the construction of the ostrovets power plant. i therefore ask the union not to take advantage of this case to further damage our relations with russia.
member of the commission. – mr president, let me first thank all members for their interventions which show how high the stakes really are when it comes to energy safety and security. by way of wrap-up, i would like to pick up on a few of the wider issues raised during the debate, but first on the ostrovets case. let me underline what i said at the start: the commission will continue to use all the instruments at its disposal to ensure the highest possible safety standards in the eu and internationally. that is non-negotiable, as i already said. that is why our priority is now to ensure the timely implementation of ostrovets nuclear safety stress tests in line with european specifications. as always, the commission will keep this house fully up to date with any developments as and when they happen. but let me be clear. many of the solutions to the questions raised in this debate lie in the need to end energy isolation and complete europe’s internal energy market. for lithuania, as well as for all baltic states, this means that we need to continue working towards their full integration into the european energy market. the good news is that we are making progress. we recently saw the start of operations for the electricity interconnections of lithuania with poland and sweden. thanks to the litpol link and nordbalt, the level of interconnection of the baltic states with the rest of the european grid has substantially increased, from 4% in early 2014 to approximately 22%. on gas, work is under way on the game-changing gas interconnector poland-lithuania. gipl, as it is called, is the first gas interconnector between the eastern baltic sea region and continental europe. when complete in 2019 it will end the region’s gas isolation, further diversify gas sources, routes and counterparts, and ultimately help to reduce prices for consumers. much of this progress is thanks in large part to the baltic energy market interconnection plan, which brings together all the baltic states to cooperate on integrating the region into a european network. this is an example to others on what we can achieve under the energy union. but we must build on this progress. our next challenge is to ensure the synchronisation of the baltic states and other isolated regions with the rest of the eu market. our vision is of an energy union based on solidarity and trust, which speaks with one voice to our external partners and which, ultimately, provides the secure and sustainable energy europe’s citizens need. that is why the energy union is a top commission priority and why our focus is fully on implementation. we look forward to working hand in hand with the european parliament to make it a reality.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which is intended to send a signal to the member states to ratify, as soon as possible, the additional protocol to the framework convention on tobacco control of the world health organisation. if this text is to become legally binding, it must be borne in mind that a minimum of 40 ratifications are required. however, at present only 17 countries worldwide have ratified it, including only five european states.
in writing. ‒ in 2003, a who framework convention on tobacco control was signed at the world health assembly. the who protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products was signed on 20 december 2013 subject to its conclusion at a later date. the protocol calls for action to combat smuggling, illicit manufacture and counterfeiting of tobacco products. the aim is to protect public health and to recover tax revenues. the text calls for the granting of licences, the monitoring and tracing of products, the control of the whole manufacturing and transport chain and the introduction of sanctions against infringers. unlike the european union's texts, this protocol respects the sovereignty of the parties, imposes principles but not the precise way of implementing them, and requires proper international cooperation. i regret that it is the european union and not the member states that are signing this text, but i can only agree with the objectives and the text of this protocol, which i therefore voted in favour of.

in writing. ‒ a who framework convention on tobacco control was signed at the world health assembly in 2003, followed by a protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products, signed on 20 december 2013. the protocol calls for the fight against smuggling, illicit manufacture and counterfeiting of tobacco products, in order to protect public health and to put an end to a major shortfall in tax revenues for the member states, by means of product tracking and tracing and closer control of the manufacturing and transport chain. i therefore voted in favour of this text, which constitutes a definitive acceptance of the measures recommended by the protocol: it calls for proper international cooperation which preserves the sovereignty of the states, and lays down a number of principles but leaves the states free to decide how to apply them.
in writing. ‒ i wanted to support this report on the protocol to the who framework convention on combating illicit trade in tobacco products. signed in 2003 at the world health assembly, this convention, and especially the protocol that followed in 2013, allows cooperation in the fight against smuggling, manufacturing and illicit trade in tobacco, objectives closely linked to public health issues, but also, for states, tax revenues. this report will make it possible, in particular, to grant licences, to set up product monitoring and tracing and thus to establish effective control over the production and transport of tobacco products, with possible penalties where appropriate. moreover, unlike the european texts on the subject, which tend to deny the sovereignty of the member states, the protocol ensures the cooperation of sovereign nations in good faith, in particular by allowing them to decide how they implement the principles to which they have adhered in the who convention.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report 'eliminating illicit trade in tobacco products: protocol to the who framework convention'. in 2003, a who framework convention on tobacco control was signed at the world health assembly. the who protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products was signed on 20 december. it called for action to be taken against smuggling, illicit manufacture and counterfeiting of tobacco products. the aim is to protect public health and to recover tax revenues. the text calls for the granting of licences, the monitoring and tracing of products, the control of the entire manufacturing and transport chain and the introduction of sanctions against infringers. unlike the european union texts, this protocol respects the sovereignty of the parties, imposes principles but not the precise way of implementing them and requires proper international cooperation.
in writing. - i voted for this report. it is part of the anti-smoking campaign run by the world health organisation (who). the objectives are clear: to combat smuggling and illicit manufacture of tobacco products while protecting public health. a protocol to combat illicit trade in tobacco products was signed at the world health assembly on 20 december 2003. this protocol is part of the who framework convention signed in 2003. in concrete terms, this text sets specific objectives such as the monitoring and tracing of products, the control of the entire distribution and transport chain, etc. it is particularly distinct from european legislation in that it respects the sovereignty of the parties to the agreement and leaves them free to choose the means of implementing the objectives set.
in writing. ‒ tobacco is trafficked in its production, transport and consumption. the world health organisation (who) estimates that 12% of the 6 000 billion cigarettes sold worldwide each year are illicitly traded. the fight against this practice is above all a public health measure. the aim is to prevent existing or potential consumers, particularly minors, from having access to cigarettes at very low prices. fighting the illicit tobacco trade also means safeguarding the public finances of the states. for europe, the tax gap is estimated at over €10 billion per year. the proposed protocol provides the tools to secure the tobacco supply chain through a series of measures such as the establishment of a global tracking and traceability regime and the creation of a global focal point for the exchange of information. in order to strengthen public health and the fight against tax evasion, i therefore give my consent to the ratification of this protocol by the european union.
in writing. - i voted for this text. this report is in line with the protocol to the framework convention on tobacco control of the world health organisation signed on 20 december 2013 to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products. it aims to strengthen judicial cooperation between member states in criminal matters. it is undeniable that the illicit trade in tobacco represents a considerable shortfall in tax revenue for the member states. these losses are estimated at €10 billion per year for each member state, while legal tobacco sales bring them €90 billion annually. in addition to these financial considerations, there are the known health risks of smoking.
in writing. ‒ the szejnfeld report called on the european parliament to give its consent to the ratification by the european union of the world health organisation (who) protocol to eliminate illicit trafficking in tobacco products. the protocol is complementary to the who framework convention on tobacco control. it is to be welcomed that more and more states are pursuing voluntary public health policies to combat smoking (increased taxes, pictorial warnings, neutral packaging, etc.). however, tobacco traffickers are thriving as a corollary: 12% of the 6 000 billion cigarettes sold worldwide each year are illicitly traded, which also encourages tax evasion. this trafficking has implications for the revenue of states, depriving them of the room for manoeuvre needed to meet their public health objectives. the who protocol, in this context, provides a number of essential tools to combat this global phenomenon: international monitoring regime, increased traceability, creation of a central point for the exchange of information. in the inta committee and then in the plenary, i therefore supported the union's ratification of this protocol, which is fully in line with its more comprehensive strategy against tobacco trafficking.
in writing. ‒ the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control (who fctc) is the first global health treaty. it was developed in response to the global tobacco epidemic and aims to tackle some of its causes, including the illicit trade in tobacco products. a protocol to eliminate illicit trade in tobacco products was established in 2012 and signed by the union in 2013. in fact, in europe about one out of every ten cigarettes is sold illegally. the illicit trade in tobacco is a criminal activity that poses a serious risk to public health and undermines the success of tobacco control policies by facilitating access to products. it also causes the union to lose huge revenues in terms of taxes and customs duties, estimated at over eur 10 billion. the agreement of the european parliament is necessary for the union to ratify this protocol. i vote for it.

in writing. ‒ the world health organisation framework convention on tobacco control (who fctc) is the first global health treaty. the text entered into force on 27 february 2005 and now has 180 parties. it aims to secure the supply chain for tobacco and tobacco-related products through the establishment of a global tracking and traceability regime. it contains provisions on controls on licences, record keeping, internet sales, duty-free sales and international transit. it also covers offences and means of recovery and should allow for better international cooperation. the ratification of this protocol is part of the european union's overall strategy to combat cigarette smuggling, adopted in 2013. by ratifying the protocol, the union will facilitate its implementation and contribute to the effective fight against the illicit trade in tobacco, a major public health problem. i voted in favour of this recommendation.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the draft council decision on the conclusion of the third revision of the agreement of the united nations economic commission for europe concerning the adoption of uniform technical prescriptions for wheeled vehicles. the unece, which has existed since 1947 to encourage economic cooperation between member states, aims to harmonize approvals and regulations on motor vehicles and spare parts. while i can understand the advantages of such harmonisation (a vehicle type-approved in one part is automatically type-approved in the other), which allows for a certain rationalization in view of the issues of safety or environmental protection, i reject the underlying objective, namely global technological harmonisation. the threshold for a majority of votes in the unece has just been raised, in particular to attract countries such as china (which still does not have the status of a recognised market economy) and india. moreover, these differences in rules allowed states to create non-tariff barriers, which is not without advantages in the case where the country in question has more demanding standards, in particular environmental standards.

in writing. ‒ this non-legislative report looks at the possibility of enhanced cooperation between 23 member states on the matrimonial property regime of international couples. this is a sensitive issue as national legal systems differ across europe on this issue. if enhanced cooperation must always be a last resort after attempting to reach agreement with all the member states, if cooperation with all 28 member states is impossible. i would like to remind you that enhanced cooperation is very much governed by the european treaties in order to respect the rights of citizens of the member states which do not participate in this cooperation. considering that more than 14 million european citizens live in a member state other than their home state, and that they face tedious administrative procedures in the event of international marriages, and that there is a need to alleviate these administrative obstacles, i supported this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of my colleague mr preda's report. in august 2015, the european commission (ec) published its fifth biannual report on policy coherence for development (pcd), shortly before the adoption of the 2030 agenda for sustainable development, which includes the objective of 'strengthening policy coherence for sustainable development'. the union has frequently reaffirmed its political commitment to the dpc, but it has yet to find the means to put this commitment into practice. previous european parliament reports have made a strong contribution to advancing the concept of the dpc by institutionalising a permanent rapporteur on dpc in the committee on development, by affirming that dpc falls within the political competence of the european parliament and by putting forward concrete proposals to move forward with the implementation of the concept at union level. the main objective of this report is to take stock of the progress made by the european commission, to identify areas where the existing mechanisms for the cpd in the union can be improved and to stimulate the debate on the future of the concept at union level.
