the rapporteur. madam president, i was given six minutes, and i will try to respect your time. commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the mobility of citizens in the european union is not an illusion. it is real and that is why the european union has 16 million multinational or international couples. these couples own property i.e. car, house or have bank accounts in various countries. if there is a problem, it is, so far, a real struggle to find a jurisdiction which is effective and accepted and, on the other hand, to achieve a fair sharing of responsibilities. these two regulations will put an end to the legal uncertainties that these couples face, with, of course, the costs of divorce proceedings and separations or in the event of death, and, above all, will put an end to the conflicting decisions that sometimes arise from these legal difficulties. these texts will apply to married couples as well as to those who have entered into a registered partnership. it was very difficult for these couples to know which court would have jurisdiction to settle disputes concerning their property in another member state, as the rules vary widely from one eu country to another. for this reason, when these regulations are adopted, spouses or partners will be able to choose, under certain conditions, the court which will be called upon to give a ruling. this may be the law of the country of residence or the country of nationality of the spouses or partners. this is a very clear arrangement and at the same time it is very flexible. the law chosen will be the law applicable to all assets, even if they are located in different countries. however, i would stress that these legal rules of each country will be properly applied and that the principle of subsidiarity will be properly respected. the two regulations do not concern the definition of marriage or the definition of partnership, and the rights and obligations arising from a marriage or registered partnership will continue to be governed by national law. thus, a member state which does not recognise registered partnerships will be entirely free not to adjudicate a dispute arising on its territory, particularly in view of the consequences of the separation or death of registered partners. it may therefore refer the case to the courts of another member state which recognises the partnership. the negotiations on these two regulations have been very delicate, as you well know. since the member states must reach unanimous agreement on family law, the procedure for enhanced cooperation was needed to resolve this situation, which caused a great deal of suffering. i can tell you, or rather confirm, that 18 member states have agreed to introduce and apply these various provisions among themselves. parliament gave its approval at the last plenary session in june 2016 to the decision to use enhanced cooperation for these two regulations. the two regulations, namely the regimes of marriage and registered partnership, were voted on by a large majority last week in the committee on legal affairs. so there was no major difficulty. there is an amendment which is a bit cosmetic, which calls for the original definition of member states to be completed and become 'the member states participating in enhanced cooperation'. this is a clarification which will have no legal effect. in any case, this addition is in my view somewhat unnecessary and superfluous, but in any case it does not influence the decision on the substance. i therefore inform you that my group and i have decided to recommend and vote against this amendment because we believe it is essential not to call into question the whole of the agreement negotiated with difficulty by the 18 member states participating in enhanced cooperation. in conclusion, madam president, commissioner, i would like to say that tomorrow's vote in favour of these two regulations is absolutely important, because it will allow the estimated timetable to be kept, so that the texts can be adopted at council level by the member states participating in this collegiate approach to enhanced cooperation as soon as possible. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, let us not forget that there are a number of couples, that is to say, some 16 million couples, which equals 32 million people. if you count two parents for each of these 32 million people, you get a sense of the number of families and people involved.
on behalf of the enf group. madam president, according to the brussels commission, there are nearly 16 million international couples in the european union. in any event, the union is using this as a pretext to intervene twice in family law. the first concerns the applicable law and the recognition of decisions in matters of matrimonial property regimes. but there is already the hague convention of 14 march 1978 on this subject. it would be better to encourage the states to ratify it rather than to compete with a european regulation. the second text concerns the recognition of decisions on registered partnerships. however, it poses a fundamental problem, since each state has its own conception of partnerships within a couple. the aim of imposing recognition of foreign partnerships will therefore, sooner or later, be to circumvent national rules in this field. that is why 10 of the 28 states have refused to accept these two bills, and that is why i will vote against them.

the rapporteur. madam president, i do not know whether this will be the last word, but at least for tonight, probably, on this subject. i want to publicly thank the council, its departments and those of the european commission for putting an end to six years of what i would call inequalities. why do i use that term? in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution, in which our assembly endorses an agreement reached in february this year between the european union and monaco on the establishment of an automatic exchange of information on the bank accounts of residents of both signatory parties, which will start in 2018 for information collected since 1 january 2017. the formal signing of the agreement is expected this summer. the agreement provides for the application of enhanced measures equivalent to those in place in the union since march 2014. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the financial institutions in question are in a position to provide the information requested by the commission. the agreement is a necessary new step in the fight against tax evasion and avoidance, since it will be more difficult for a person to conceal money that is liable to be taxed. tax administrations will be able to identify the taxpayers involved, administer and strengthen their tax laws in cross-border cases or assess the likelihood of tax evasion. this agreement is similar to the agreements with switzerland, liechtenstein and san marino, which i also supported.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the protocol to the agreement between the european union and monaco providing for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts. this agreement complements those concluded with switzerland, andorra, liechtenstein and san marino, providing for equivalent measures. the importance of automatic exchange of information has been recognised internationally as a means of combating cross-border tax fraud and evasion. in this context, the organisation for economic co-operation and development (oecd) was tasked by the g20 to develop a single global standard for the automatic exchange of financial account information. it is through effective bilateral cooperation that we will succeed in combating and ending tax evasion. this type of agreement not only meets an economic need but also an expectation of the citizens of the union.
in writing. ‒ on 22 february 2016, the european union and the principality of monaco signed an agreement on the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts, as part of the series of agreements between the eu and neighbouring states aimed at increasing cooperation in the fight against tax evasion and tax fraud. for the record, these agreements were one of the conditions set by luxembourg and austria to end their banking secrecy two years ago. the aim was to avoid tax havens at the eu's doorstep, where fraudsters could take refuge. the automatic exchange of information will still cover the income of accounts but also their balance and the proceeds of the disposal of assets. we have supported the previous agreements with switzerland, liechtenstein, andorra and san marino. the one with monaco is obviously symbolic, and it should also be supported. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to transpose into eu law the recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (icsta) concerning bluefin tuna. in 2006, iccat adopted a multiannual bluefin tuna recovery plan which will end in 2022. the total allowable catches (tacs) for bluefin tuna were progressively reduced from 2006 onwards, reaching their lowest level in 2012. the tacs for bluefin tuna in the area of the north sea and the north-east atlantic, as set out in annex i to regulation (ec) no 1967/2005, are set out in annex i to regulation (ec) no 1967/2006. the measures taken in recent years have therefore borne fruit. the significant improvement in bluefin tuna stocks is the direct consequence. i welcome this and invite the commission to continue to work closely with iccat to ensure sustainable exploitation of bluefin tuna.

in writing. ‒ multiannual management plans are the main instruments for fisheries management under the common fisheries policy. they make it possible to plan a set of measures, including fishing opportunities, in the long term. this management plan is the first to be drawn up under the rules of the new common fisheries policy (reformed in 2013), which requires, inter alia, the management of fish stocks at maximum sustainable yield (msy). this file has been very difficult. parliament and the council negotiated in a trilogue for 10 months before reaching an agreement. the agreement reached is balanced. it is also a means of unblocking the management plans for the other maritime basins, which were conditional on an agreement on this first new generation plan. i therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. - i voted for this report. we support this draft, which has been amended substantially by the committee on fisheries of the european parliament. in this case, the aim was to insist on taking account of the studies of the international council for the exploration of the sea on the stocks of cod, herring and sprat in the baltic sea, which are severely affected by overfishing. the draft also takes account of another requirement of the parliamentary committee: that of the transmission to parliament of documents relating to decisions taken by the commission in the context of delegated management. through this management system, the european commission was able to exercise considerable decision-making powers, particularly in the area of technical measures. the satisfaction of these demands is in line with our expectations.
in writing. ‒ due to intensive fishing, these fish species are in danger. the basic idea of the project was that the commission should have a lot of technical measures at its disposal. the commission had planned to implement the multiannual plan without waiting for the report of the international council for the exploration of the sea. the amendments seemed to me to be in the right direction, in that they put the expertise of this council back at the centre of the debate. it seems to me to be a precautionary measure. i also welcome the fact that the commission is finally obliged to inform parliament when it is preparing to adopt delegated acts. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the report tackles the problem of overfishing, which is putting the baltic sea stocks of cod, herring and sprat at risk. the commission wishes to act quickly, without waiting for the latest opinions of the international council for the exploration of the sea. however, as amended by the members of the committee on fisheries, the report insists that the most recent studies of the international council for the exploration of the sea be taken into account. it is also provided that, when preparing delegated acts, the commission shall ensure that the relevant documents are transmitted to the european parliament and to the council. the report is therefore acceptable.
in writing. ‒ the amended proposal is satisfactory and will help to preserve cod, herring and sprat. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the multiannual plan for the baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat and the fisheries exploiting those stocks. the plan, the first to be drawn up under the new fisheries policy, requires management of fish stocks at maximum sustainable yield, which, according to the text, is assessed according to a range of values.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this multiannual management plan for the baltic stocks of cod, herring and sprat, concerning the fisheries exploiting these stocks. this management plan is the first to be drawn up under new rules resulting from the common fisheries policy, reformed in 2013, which requires, inter alia, the management of fish stocks at maximum sustainable yield (msy).
in writing. ‒ the baltic sea stocks of cod, herring and sprat are now in danger due to overfishing. - scientific advice has established that current stock exploitation is incompatible with the objective of maximum sustainable yield. - the commission did not want to wait for further studies by the ices (international council for the exploration of the sea) before implementing the multiannual plan. - the draft provides for the delegation of many technical measures to the commission. the draft, as amended by the members of the committee on fisheries, insists that the most recent ices studies be taken into account and that the relevant advisory councils be consulted. it is also provided that, when preparing delegated acts, the commission shall ensure that the relevant documents are transmitted to the european parliament and to the council. i therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ in view of the legal uncertainty regarding the property rights of international couples, the commission has been working on a proposal for a european regulation to harmonise the legal rules on matrimonial property regimes. i voted against this proposal for a regulation because the eu is not meant to legislate on family law. it remains the exclusive competence of the member states, which may, if they so wish, conclude international conventions to lay down rules of cooperation with other states. this is therefore an unjustified interference with national legislation on the family.
in writing. ‒ parliament adopted its position on these regulations during the last term. the council took a long time to take a position. we welcome the enhanced cooperation and hope that other member states will decide to join this process. this regulation will make life much easier for european international couples and guarantee them greater legal security.
in writing. ‒ in 2010, the commission identified uncertainty about property rights for international couples as one of the main obstacles eu citizens face in their daily lives. after the negotiations were blocked, since any agreement on family law had to be unanimous, this proposal was sent to parliament in the form of enhanced cooperation involving only 17 member states. the regulation enshrines the principle of the unity of the applicable law, the same law for all property owned by the couple, wherever it is located. the regulation also allows the choice of the applicable law, provided that it is closely related to the situation of the spouses. the eu is not meant to legislate on family law. member states are free to conclude international conventions to lay down rules of cooperation with other states. it is therefore an unjustified interference with national legislation on the family. i therefore voted against the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ this report concerns a regulation determining the competent court and the law applicable to applications in matters of matrimonial property regimes. apart from the fact that there is already a convention on this subject, the convention of 14 march 1978, under the aegis of the hague convention, there is nothing to give the eu the right to legislate on family law. member states are free to conclude international conventions to lay down rules of cooperation with other states. it was therefore an unjustified interference with national legislation on the family which called for a negative vote.
in writing. ‒ i have chosen to oppose this report and the proposal for a council regulation on jurisdiction, applicable law and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in matrimonial matters. i consider this intrusion into national family law unacceptable. in addition, although the situation of international couples must of course be considered, particularly as regards their property rights, i would remind you that there is already an international convention on the subject, the one of 14 march 1978, which all member states are free to ratify. the regulation in question adds nothing to the existing framework, since it excludes from its scope matters concerning the capacity of spouses, the existence, validity or recognition of a marriage, as well as maintenance obligations and the succession of the deceased spouse.
in writing. ‒ this text is undoubtedly a prerequisite for the standardisation of the legal rules on the matrimonial regimes of international couples, whether they are married or linked by a registered partnership. there is a fear that national legislation on the family will be tampered with in the future. i therefore voted against.

in writing. ‒ in 2010, the commission announced a proposal for a regulation to make it easier for international couples to know which courts have jurisdiction over their property rights and which legislation applies to them. after the negotiations had come to a standstill, this proposal was referred back to parliament in the form of enhanced cooperation involving only 17 member states. the regulation covers jurisdiction and the applicable law in matters of the property effects of registered partnerships. the text also allows the choice of the applicable law, provided that it is the law of the state of which one of the partners is a national or the state in which he has his habitual residence. the partners may also choose the law of the state of registration of the partnership. although the regulation states that it excludes matters relating to property rights (capacity, maintenance obligations, succession, etc.), it will inevitably enable the partners to anticipate possible bottlenecks and to circumvent the obstacle. this is in particular the case with the generously provided possibility of choosing the applicable law. the autonomy of the member states in family law is therefore not ultimately safeguarded. it is therefore an unjustified interference with national legislation on the family. i therefore voted against the report.

in writing. ‒ this report assesses the implementation of the energy efficiency directive with a view to its revision. the rapporteur stresses the potential energy savings to be achieved, in particular those linked to the renovation of the building stock. although calling for more binding measures, the text stresses the flexibility that must be granted to member states in transposing european directives. unusually, this text even addresses the problem of the competitiveness deficit of our energy-intensive industries in relation to their non-community competitors, but without ever challenging the general free trade which exacerbates unfair international competition. finally, the text includes a paragraph calling into question the current austerity which prevents member states from financing the investments needed to achieve energy efficiency targets. i have, however, abstained on this text, which calls for more binding measures.
in writing. ‒ implementation of the energy efficiency directive is essential to reach the eu's 20% target for 2020. the union has made enormous progress in this area even though the directive has not yet been transposed into the law of all member states. the first thing to do is to monitor the application of the directive in the member states. this will ensure the consistency of the union's energy efficiency policy. i voted against this report because i was not in favour of a binding 40% energy efficiency target by 2030. we must respond appropriately to environmental challenges. we will not achieve our aims by setting ourselves binding, unattainable objectives which will undermine the competitiveness of our enterprises. it is true that we must make considerable efforts in energy efficiency, but we must do so gradually. other components, such as competitiveness, jobs and growth, need to be taken into account.
in writing. ‒ the cheapest energy is the one you do not consume. energy efficiency must therefore be seen as a fully-fledged energy source which represents the amount in nw (negawatts) of energy saved, as the recent history of the world and europe has irrefutably demonstrated. in this sector, as in others, citizens' initiatives and those taken at local level are of the greatest relevance and european legislation must accompany and facilitate them. i share the view of the authors of this resolution that the potential for energy savings at local level should be exploited much better, given that local and regional authorities have a central role to play in achieving energy efficiency and in the energy transition in general. it is also at this level that the issues of equal access and energy poverty can best be addressed, and we must be extremely vigilant to ensure that the savings from 'energy efficiency' are not reserved for those (individuals and businesses) who can afford to make the necessary investments.

in writing. ‒ energy efficiency is the european union's priority in combating global warming. improving energy efficiency by 20% with a 20% increase in the share of renewable energy and a 20% reduction in co2 emissions is one of the european 2020 targets in terms of sustainable development. between 1990 and 2014, greenhouse gas emissions fell by 23%. at the same time, the union's gdp increased by 46%. so this is proof, if any, that by reducing their impact on the environment, citizens and businesses have generated a surplus of growth. contrary to the claims of those who advocate environmental disregard, the ecological transition and energy management are not a brake on economic growth, but an adjuvant. the 40% efficiency target by 2030 set by parliament instead of the originally planned 27% is therefore a good thing. a cheap environmental policy cannot satisfy the desire to build a sustainable and prosperous europe. it is by embarking on the path of ecological transition that europe will effectively achieve its economic, social and environmental objectives.

on behalf of the enf group. mr president, reducing emissions requires constant efforts and a transformation of our production machinery. the report before us is aimed at this objective and some of the ways in which it is proposed are good. however, this text is much more restrictive than the existing rules and will leave even less room for manoeuvre for the member states. we cannot continue on this path while europe is increasingly unequal and our industrial activities are stagnating. nevertheless, the eu is strengthening its regulatory grip, which is shackling manufacturers or pushing them to circumvent the legislation. moreover, the transition period from 2018 to 2020 is too short. the smaller producers will have great difficulty in changing their models and will live in fear of new texts that will hamper their projects in the medium and long term. more importantly, under the guise of 'harmonisation' and 'better market surveillance', the report accelerates the alignment of our standards with us standards. but what can we expect, ladies and gentlemen? that by doing so we will increase the opportunities for our industries across the atlantic? let us be realistic in the face of social crisis, economic stagnation for decades and trade wars. let's not shoot each other in the foot! let's give our builders a break and turn our eyes first to research and investment! this is a positive and constructive approach to environmental policy, this is the real european pooling of our resources, the opposite of technocracy.
in writing. the european union is only interested in integrating 'refugees' into the labour market, without looking for an alternative solution, even though immigration is a tragedy whose first victims are the immigrants themselves: an unprecedented number of deaths, poor housing or exploitation. the very notion of 'refugee' remains more than ambiguous. there is still no concrete definition because although the eu distinguishes between three categories of 'legal beneficiaries', it does not give a real definition. the eu also recognises that welcoming refugees is a palliative to europe's demographic problems: 'the eu's working age population is expected to fall by 7.5 million by 2020'. how shameful to think so when we see the unemployment figures! it is a shame that we do not prefer a birthist policy to mass immigration. the eu states that refugees "can undertake and generate economic activity that has a positive impact on host communities" without any certainty or concrete figures. in addition, integration is mentioned but assimilation is not. integration implies "demanding" and "communitarianism" whereas assimilation implies adaptation and recognition.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this agreement between the european union and peru on the short-stay visa waiver. this text provides for a visa-free travel regime for citizens of the union and peruvian nationals travelling to the territory of the other contracting party for a stay of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the policy of liberalization which the commission is constantly trying to impose on us in the context of the migration crisis currently affecting the european union seems to me completely out of place. the commission argues that the fight against organised crime, in particular drug trafficking and human trafficking, will be greatly strengthened. on the one hand, i do not see any substantial advantages in these areas with this agreement. on the other hand, i am concerned that the commission, despite a clear view of the risks posed by such an agreement, may insist on wanting to open the borders of the european union.
in writing. ‒ given the mass immigration facing european states, i am opposed to any visa liberalisation. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the agreement of 14 march 2016, which is provisionally applied pending the approval of the european parliament, provides for a visa-free travel regime for citizens of the european union and peru for a maximum stay of 90 days in any 180-day period. this visa exemption will benefit all categories of individuals except those who are gainfully employed. the agreement is expected to boost tourism and help strengthen trade relations between the two sides. although the situation regarding illegal migration from peru has improved, it seemed highly inappropriate to conclude such an agreement at a time when the member states of the european union are experiencing an unprecedented influx of migrants. therefore, i consider it essential that peru remains a key partner in the fight against organised crime without liberalising visas for its nationals. i therefore opposed this text.

mr president, this report is a good thing: it proposes to introduce the standards of the international labour organisation into international trade agreements. that's very good! since we are at this point, i have a suggestion to make: since the european treaty prohibits social harmonization, why, for example, could we not say that all the member countries of the european union are obliged to sign the conventions of the international labour organization? this is of great importance for the future, especially for the tafta agreement we are preparing, because if we make the standards of the international labour organisation mandatory in our international treaties, then we will be obliged to ask the united states of america to ratify the main conventions of the international labour organisation. you may not know this, but the united states has not signed the convention on freedom of association and protection of the right to organize, the convention on the right to organize and collective bargaining, the convention on equal pay for men and women, the convention on discrimination, or the convention on the minimum age for admission to employment. they have not signed the convention on the rights of persons with disabilities or the convention on the rights of the child. i would now like to conclude by saying that, since we have set ourselves this objective, we must support the un initiative which envisages the establishment in the treaties of environmental and social standards to be imposed on multinational companies. we must help instead of deserting the table, instead of voting against at the un, and i would like to commend the courage of mrs maría fernanda espinosa, who is now in charge of these negotiations, and the president, and the courage of her action and that of the government of rafael correa.

challenge. youth unemployment, migration crises, refugee crisis, cop 21, agricultural crises, underinvestment, internal security: unfortunately, in the last two years, new challenges and emergencies priorities, its limits have been reached, all the instruments of flexibility have been called upon to deal with the various crises and, without revision, we will continue to strip peter to dress paul. cuts have been made in key programmes - this is the case in horizon 2020, this is the case in the connecting europe facility - and a freeze of commitments to combat youth unemployment has been decided, while the ceilings, especially those for heading 3, have exploded. i think i can say that this report rejects the idea of a compromise between trust funds and facilities. it refuses to allow the proliferation of financial instruments to become the rule at the expense of the waning democratic control. and then, of course, there are the payments: the payment crisis is coming at the end of the period. if we do not make changes, we must stop acting like ostriches and run away from our responsibilities in this situation. the credibility of our institutions is at stake and, more the rapporteur. madam president, thank you also to the commission for being here. ladies and gentlemen, the vote on my report on coast guard cooperation is quite simply a victory. since 2011, i have been asking for coastguard cooperation to make the european union more effective in responding to crises at sea. crises at sea can be many: marine pollution, illegal fishing, the influx of refugees in dangerous boats. in all these cases, when i first proposed european coastguard cooperation, my aim was not only to prevent disasters but also to enable the european union to act in a coordinated and effective manner. we've identified 316 civilian and military authorities from the coast guard. this fragmentation has so far prevented joint action and the exchange of information. the three european agencies - the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard - now have complementary mandates, which obviously increase the eu's response capabilities at sea tenfold. the agencies will coordinate the 316 authorities responsible for coast guard functions. we will improve the capacity of the european union to act, and i believe that is what the european citizens want today. the agencies are now pooling their response capacity and information systems and working in a coordinated way to rescue at sea and prevent illegal immigration. their mandates are extended; support all national or local authorities with coast guard functions through the sharing of human and operational resources. through this decision, we are creating real synergies between agencies to provide more efficient services, also in terms of costs. in 2015 and 2016, the european union experienced strong pressure at its external borders. over the last two years it has become clear that the schengen area without internal borders is only viable if the external borders are effectively protected and guaranteed. this is only possible with joint, united and responsible action by all member states. through the cooperation of the three agencies to support member states in protecting our borders, we are building a more united europe because it is more responsive, more efficient and more secure. i would also like to point out that we are only extending the mandate of the european fisheries control agency. the agency's primary task is, of course, to monitor fisheries in europe in order to ensure that a common fisheries policy is put in place to combat illegal fishing effectively. however, the agency may also be called upon in the event of other crises at sea. europe is gaining speed, efficiency and coordination in border control.

in writing. ‒ the intervention concerns the second reading (without final vote) of this report on the directive of the european parliament and of the council on measures to ensure a high common level of security of network and information systems in the union: this directive, which is part of the digital strategy for europe, is relatively satisfactory overall, despite a glaring lack of data and a lack of research on the actual expected impacts. we can only encourage any measures to protect ourselves from the cyberattacks that are currently on the rise. this growing digital insecurity needs to be taken seriously. however, this text still deserves further study, particularly in its more binding than voluntary regulatory approach, including obligations to cooperate with european commission bodies on pain of sanctions, its lowering of certain security standards to overcome the legislative weaknesses of certain countries, or its lack of personal protection against digital service providers. this text has real potential but is (too) heavily underused (and too restrictive in respect of the principle of subsidiarity).

in writing. ‒ at a historic moment when it is important to improve the security of online environments and to strengthen cooperation between member states and the european institutions in this field, this resolution will make progress on the necessary common rules, standards and mechanisms. the resolution therefore sets out tools for cooperation and response to cybersecurity incidents. it also lays down security and notification requirements for market players, i.e. operators of essential services (such as energy, transport, health, banking, drinking water supply and distribution, etc.) and providers of digital services (such as search engines, clouds, etc.). these two categories of actors are required to take organisational and technical measures to manage risks and to notify incidents.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of the text strengthening the european means of action and reaction in the fight against cybercrime. we are not always aware of the seriousness of this new form of crime, which can be disastrous for a company and reveal worrying security flaws in the proper functioning of a state. from 2018, all infrastructures providing essential services (internet service providers, energy, transport, financial markets, health and public administrations) will be obliged to notify a cyber attack and take appropriate measures to ensure network and information security (nis). the diversity of regulatory frameworks and the highly uneven resilience of member states facilitated the spread of online attacks and viruses. common rules will now harmonise the response of states, since each member state will be required to set up an authority responsible for ihr, have emergency response teams and draw up strategic plans. we must absolutely avoid incidents like the attack on the french-language tv channel tv5 by russian hackers in april 2015 from happening again in more strategic sectors that put our security at risk and make us vulnerable to cyberterrorists.

in writing. ‒ the adoption of this directive on the security of network and information systems is an important step as it will allow the first eu-wide rules on cybersecurity to enter into force. the text aims to establish an open, safe and secure cyberspace and provides for security obligations for 'operators of essential services' in sectors such as energy, transport, health, banking and drinking water supply. some providers of digital services, such as search engines and cloud services, will also need to take measures to ensure the security of their infrastructure. in addition, member states should establish one or more authorities responsible for network and information security, define national strategies in this area and set up it emergency response teams. this text is not perfect. it is regrettable that the council has not been more ambitious on the level of cooperation between member states, given the increasing frequency of cyberattacks. but it is still a step in the right direction and some notable progress is to be noted.
in writing. ‒ the nis directive is the first eu-wide legislation on cybersecurity. its main objective is to improve security in the online environment and to strengthen cooperation between member states and the european institutions in this field, in order to overcome the current fragmentation. it involves the establishment of national strategies by member states, the designation of competent authorities and a dedicated incident response team. it also aims to improve cooperation between member states by networking and establishing cooperation groups. finally, it lays down certain obligations for operators of essential services and digital service providers. they shall take organisational and technical measures to manage the risks to the security of network and information systems and to prevent and mitigate the impact of incidents that compromise the security of those systems. i supported this directive in voting for this report.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this legislative report is to create a european border agency that can ensure integrated european management of external borders in the face of migratory challenges and potential external threats. to this end, cooperation between the european fisheries control agency, the european maritime safety agency and the european border and coast guard agency will be strengthened in order to pool their efforts in fisheries control, rescue at sea and maritime security as well as migration management and surveillance of the external borders of the union. i would like to recall that this was one of the election promises of the ump in 2014; i'm glad this project finally came to fruition. i supported this report, considering that this effort to pool resources is essential in order to respond more effectively to the challenges of migration and the security of european waters.
in writing. the creation of a european border and coast guard is a strong measure that i have supported for years. in the midst of the explosion of the migration crisis, it is essential that the european union should take up this essential instrument without further delay to strengthen the external borders of the european union. with this vote, we are not only delivering on our campaign promises, but also reaffirming our commitment to a stronger europe in the face of the migration challenge. the new agency, while respecting the sovereignty of the member states, will have the necessary means of action to deal with potential shortcomings in external border controls, but also in particular to organise return operations for irregular migrants within the european union. it is now essential that this european border and coast guard should become operational as soon as possible, as early as the autumn.
in writing. ‒ i fully support this report which aims to create a european border control system. the system described in the pabriks report is expected to be in place by october. the new border and coast guard agency thus created will have new tasks such as the surveillance of the external borders of the european union and will also benefit from increased human and financial resources. by supporting this report, i wanted to send a strong signal to the european citizens that protecting their security is one of our priorities. moreover, i welcome the establishment of this system which will act exclusively at the request of the member state in difficulty or failing, thus not creating a situation of interference. while it is important to act on border controls, it is equally important to preserve the sovereignty of the member states, especially on a sensitive issue such as this.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which will create a european border and coast guard corps to ensure integrated european management of external borders. this creation, together with the re-establishment of frontex's missions as part of a renewed agency, was necessary in the face of the influx of migrants, in order not to blow up the schengen agreements and not to leave responsibility for the external borders to a few member states in the front line. this new agency with additional human resources and with greater involvement of the european parliament should be more responsive. it will now have a mandate to act in search and rescue operations at sea and in humanitarian assistance. in addition, as regards respect for the fundamental rights of individuals, a complaint mechanism is created by this new text which also reaffirms the rule of the prohibition of the transfer of personal data in the management of migrants to european law enforcement authorities, except where strictly necessary in the detection, prevention, investigation and prosecution of serious crime.
in writing. the european union and its member states must share responsibility for the surveillance of their external, maritime and land borders. as we have been asking for years, it is therefore urgent that europe should have a european coast guard to guard its borders, with appropriate and substantial means: reconnaissance planes, boats, helicopters. the establishment of a union border control system bringing together the european agency frontex and national border management authorities is a first step. member states with pressured borders will be able to ask the european border and coast guard agency for assistance. the agency, which will not have its own teams, will then be able to call on guards provided by the member states to deploy teams rapidly at the borders concerned. i hope that this system, which is based on the goodwill of the member states, will work. but we still think that a genuine european system of coastguards and border guards, like the one in the united states, would have been much more effective.

in writing. ‒ on wednesday 6 july, i voted in favour of this report to create a european border and coast guard corps, which should become operational at the beginning of october and mobilise up to 1 500 men. the new border and coast guard agency, which will replace frontex, will have strengthened capabilities and tasks, including control of the union's external borders and the return of irregular migrants. this border guard corps will only intervene at the request of a failing country and member states will be able to re-establish internal border controls in the event of laxity or disengagement by their neighbours. this agreement responds to the concerns of citizens who want more security and control while respecting the will of the member states.
in writing. i voted for this reform of frontex because it will allow the agency to participate in a more european and more efficient management of our external borders. the agency will have increased resources to react more rapidly and collectively, including a reserve of 1 500 border and coastguards. it will be able to detect emergencies and provide the best possible assistance to the member states 'on the front line' at our external borders, which is essential. my group has, however, taken care to introduce certain safeguards into the functioning of the agency. frontex will be carrying out search and rescue operations which will now clearly be part of its missions. frontex will have to carry out all its missions in full respect of fundamental rights and will have a new complaints mechanism as a flagship, something that the parliament and the european ombudsman have long advocated. it will also have to develop specific training tools for the protection of minors and vulnerable persons. i therefore supported this text, which makes it possible to make the management of our borders more european and solidary, and which introduces guarantees for respect for fundamental rights.
in writing. ‒ the commission's proposal to create a european border and coast guard corps to operate at the borders of the member states without their consent was an option i rejected as a whole. for me, there was no question of having a supranational agency that imposed itself on the member states in defiance of their sovereignty. i therefore welcome the final agreement reached in the interinstitutional negotiations. we now have a new agency, the border and coast guard agency, which will replace frontex and will be given additional human and financial resources to protect our borders effectively. the agency will only intervene at the request of a state which is overwhelmed or failing and will mobilise up to 1 500 national border guards, the number and profile of whom will be decided annually by each member state. if a state refuses the agency's assistance but its laxity threatens the stability of its neighbours' borders, they can reinstate internal border controls. finally, the agency will be responsible for returning irregular migrants. this is a welcome step, given that less than 40% of return decisions to europe are actually enforced. in my view, this agency is a good synthesis between the necessary european cooperation and solidarity and respect for national sovereignty.

in writing. - i voted against this text. the purpose of this text is to extend cooperation between the frontex agency and the european maritime safety agency. the change of nature of frontex into the european border and coast guard agency requires the maintenance of the working agreement between the two institutions. the rapporteur, mep marie-christine arnautu, tabled several amendments which focused on the very subject of the text: the fight against illegal immigration. it is important to be aware that often the tools put in place to combat immigration (such as the use of surveillance drones) become the instruments of immigration. why? because the purpose changes. for the drones, for example, it becomes the route for illegal immigrants to italy, greece, etc. these amendments were not adopted. we oppose this report, which distorts the primary purpose of these institutions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of parliament's recommendations on the preparation of the post-election revision of the multiannual financial framework (mff) for the period 2014-2020. a review of the mff is necessary to take stock of the budgetary implications of the challenges that have emerged over the last two years, such as the migrant and refugee crisis, youth unemployment, the crisis in the agricultural sector, environmental challenges and internal security to respond to the terrorist threat. since the ceilings of the mff are insufficient to cope with these crises, the union has had to resort to special instruments, the proliferation of which has created a problem of accountability and democratic control. we recommend, in particular, the creation of a permanent crisis reserve of the union in the budget to avoid the use of ad hoc instruments, the increase of the financial envelope of the flexibility instrument and the emergency aid reserve, or the improvement and simplification of the functioning of the cfp and the reduction of the administrative burden. it is also important to emphasise the importance of implementing measures to avoid the accumulation of an outstanding backlog of invoices and thus prevent a new payment crisis at the end of the mff.

in writing. ‒ the second special committee on tax returns (taxe 2) was set up to enable meps to continue their work on taxation in europe. the number of documents made available to members by the european commission was indeed very large. in this report, the european parliament welcomes the tax transparency package proposed by the commission. it is a good start in the fight against tax evasion in the union. it is essential that multinational companies as well as individuals pay their taxes where they do business. the luxleaks and panama papers scandals have exposed some of the shortcomings of european tax law. the mandate of the committee on taxation has come to an end and we will now continue our work in the committee of inquiry into the panama papers, of which i am a member. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report is the final report of the special committee on tax remissions and other measures similar in nature or effect (taxe 2). this report aims to examine ways of putting an end to unfair tax practices and thus combating tax evasion in europe. considering that this report is an extension of the report of the first special committee taxe 1 and that the european union needs to implement reforms in order to combat tax evasion and tax rewriting, i supported this report.
in writing. ‒ this text continues and elaborates on the roadmap drawn up by the taxe 1 committee (initiated in the european parliament in the wake of the luxleaks scandal). the aim is to tackle the loopholes in which multinationals operate and to restore equality in taxation. it proposes a series of recommendations, including the rapid establishment of a common consolidated corporate tax base. it stresses the need for a list of tax havens with sanctions, for strict control of tax advisory firms and for measures to eliminate tax opacity (european register of final beneficiaries, public country-by-country reporting, etc.). i also welcome the criticism of the tax credit system in this text. these tax schemes too often allow large groups to recover considerable expenditure under the label of 'research and development' in order to maximise their tax relief. in this case, i advocate support through grants to better control the real destination of public money allocated to r&d.
‒ tax dumping by multinational companies represents a significant loss of revenue for the states. it is damaging to economic activity and disadvantaging the smes that make up the european economic fabric. it is unacceptable that a multinational company pays 30% less tax than a company established in one state! the european tax system must be fairer and clearer. this is why our parliament calls for the fight against tax fraud and evasion to be stepped up, by introducing sanctions against non-cooperative jurisdictions, but also directly against banks and companies. it also recommends that measures be taken to increase transparency. this is crucial because it is the secrecy surrounding fraudulent companies that allows them to prosper. the establishment of a blacklist of tax havens and a european register of beneficial owners are essential for a future european legislative initiative in this area. these provisions provide a basis for more effective action against tax evasion and aggressive planning by certain companies. however, european leaders must bear in mind that effective european tax legislation cannot be achieved without further harmonisation of national legislation. it's an emergency.
in writing. ‒ this text concerns the final report of the taxe 2 special committee against aggressive tax optimisation, which has made it possible to hear a number of companies on their arrangements. it was thus possible to obtain from the states and the european commission documents which they had not delivered and to examine the mechanisms of patent boxes or the liability and conflicts of interest of consultancy firms in the assembly process. the report reaffirms the european union's commitment to combating this type of tax evasion, fraud or tax optimisation. a country like france, whose tax attractiveness is low because of unstable legislation and high compulsory levies, has much to gain from common tax rules. it is regrettable that the commission should be asked to create a european-level withholding tax, to give a commission body the task of monitoring national tax policies, or to create a register of the assets of individuals and companies. while defending the rule of unanimity of the member states for the regulation of the union in tax matters, i voted for this text which is in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ vote for: we think it is consistent to continue supporting the text without making any legislative progress, while voting against a number of proposals that are ambiguous or too much in the direction of integration.
in writing. ‒ i voted for the taxe 2 special committee report for the same reasons as i voted for the taxe 1 committee report. created after the luxleaks scandal, which revealed the exorbitant tax benefits granted by luxembourg to certain companies at the expense of tax revenues from other member states, these two commissions, whose successive work spanned a year, helped to better identify the amoral, if not illegal, practices used by multinationals to avoid tax. i do not agree with all the proposals in the text, but i support the principle. a country like mine, france, has much to gain from common tax rules against tax evasion, fraud and optimisation... it is true that the current government, which is surprised that the city banks are reluctant to move to paris after brexit, has done much to make it a poor or even non-fiscal attraction. it is time he thought about softening the fiscal hell that is ruining the middle classes and jobs.
in writing. ending tax injustice: this is what guided my vote in favour of the final report containing the recommendations of the special committee taxe, set up in the wake of the luxleaks scandal. the report sets out a new set of recommendations to make corporate taxation fairer and more ethical. it calls, inter alia, for the immediate protection of whistleblowers, including from legal prosecution, for a public country-by-country accounting of multinationals, for a european public register of beneficial owners of companies, for a blacklist of tax havens, for sanctions against non-cooperative tax jurisdictions, for action against the abuse of tax regimes favourable to patents (intellectual property income), and finally for a withholding tax on profits leaving the union. in particular, the commission is called upon to propose without delay a common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb), the most direct and effective tool to prevent aggressive tax optimisation by multinationals and tax dumping by member states. with my colleagues, i will continue to act as a catalyst for europe to put an end to fraud, tax evasion and tax optimisation.
in writing. ‒ taxe 2 has enabled a number of additional companies to be heard on their arrangements, to obtain from the states and the european commission documents they had not provided and to delve into certain issues, such as patent box mechanisms or the liability and conflicts of interest of consultancy firms in arrangements. the report reaffirms the european union's willingness to take a firm stand on the problem of multinational companies evading taxation by ingenious schemes exploiting the flaws in bilateral agreements or the generosity of tax laws in our neighbours. we have always expressed our support for all the observations and the principle of a strong reaction. pragmatism for national public finances encourages acceptance of the pooling of certain solutions, while reaffirming the uncontested maintenance of unanimity among member states for the regulation of the union in tax matters. i therefore thought it was consistent to support this text.

in writing. ‒ the vote on this report closes the work of the special committee taxe, set up in the wake of the luxleaks scandal. less than a week after the convictions of those who raised the alarm, this text allows the european parliament to put forward proposals to end the impunity of tax fraudsters. among its many recommendations, the report proposes whistleblower protection, country-by-country accounting reporting, a european public register of beneficial owners of companies, a blacklist of tax havens, sanctions against non-cooperative tax jurisdictions, a code of conduct for banks and tax advisers, tax rules for good governance in all eu trade agreements and withholding tax on profits leaving the eu. as a socialist, i am in favour of a fairer and more ethical taxation of companies. i therefore vote in favour of this report.
in writing. - i voted for this report. this is the final report of the taxe 2 special committee, which follows up on the special committee set up in february 2015 to formulate proposals against aggressive tax optimisation. some provisions of this text, which is broad in the sense of greater tax harmonization between member states, call for certain reservations. in particular, this concerns the harmonisation of the corporate tax base, leading eventually to a distribution of tax revenue according to the methods of calculation by country, the possible creation of a withholding tax at european level and the establishment of a european observatory of the tax policies of the member states. however, pragmatism must prevail: the legal loopholes allowing certain multinationals to abuse the diversity of national tax systems must be reduced.
in writing. ‒ the european union, as we know, often gets the battle wrong when it spends more time recommending budget cuts than fighting inequalities. if there is one area where this is not the case, it is taxation. the union's real progress in this area over the past two years is worthy of note. at the instigation of the european parliament, in the econ committee, in the special committee taxe 1 and now taxe 2, a real roadmap was drawn up to correct the shortcomings of multinationals and restore equality in taxation. with a clear reminder of the demands we have been making since the beginning of the legislature, such as an immediate and comprehensive common consolidated corporate tax base, a list of tax havens with sanctions, rigorous control of tax advisory firms, and detailing all the future steps to be taken to remove tax opacity (european register of final beneficiaries, country-by-country reporting to the public, etc.), and despite some regrets, such as the lack of a proposal for an effective minimum tax rate for multinationals, the taxe 2 report is a solid living document proposed to the commission and reminded to the member states. i voted in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report of the taxe 2 special committee, set up on 2 december 2015 to examine harmful corporate tax regimes and practices in certain european countries and at international level, in order to combat tax evasion and tax avoidance. the work of this committee has highlighted the need for a legislative package to combat tax evasion, addressing the optimisation techniques and the legal gaps that allow them. the members of the taxe 2 committee also stressed the importance of revising the directive on administrative cooperation between national authorities of the member states. in addition, the key role of whistleblowers should be welcomed and we call for a harmonised legal regime to clearly define whistleblower status and provide for an adequate level of protection. the fight against tax evasion and tax optimisation is a constant battle, which will ensure that our companies that respect the rules do not suffer unfair competition.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect. the panama papers scandal has once again demonstrated the need to combat tax fraud and evasion, which are carried out to the detriment of the general public and smes and whose scale is estimated at €1 trillion per year. the european parliament has decided to take up its responsibilities through a series of recommendations: the development of a blacklist of tax havens, a european tax levied at source and collected by the member states, a union code of conduct for all tax advisory services and binding union legislation to combat the misuse of patent-friendly tax regimes for tax evasion. the text also calls for a clear legal framework to ensure effective protection of whistleblowers. finally, we call for deterrent measures such as sanctions to be imposed on the countries on the blacklist, as well as on the companies, banks, law firms, accountancy firms and tax advisers who are complicit in these fraudulent activities.

in writing. ‒ i supported the report by my colleagues jeppe kofod and michael theurer, whose realistic assessment of tax policies shows that europe is not committed to equality before tax. the aggressive tax optimisation of multinationals, the convictions of whistleblowers acting in the public interest and the complacency towards tax havens are all elements that weaken the link between citizens, tax and europe. the european parliament has therefore adopted a series of recommendations for fair taxation. the creation of a common consolidated corporate tax base, country-by-country reporting, reform of the body for coordination between member states on tax practices in respect of companies and the protection of whistleblowers are all essential steps towards greater tax and social justice. globalisation and the development of multinationals have weakened the ability of states to raise taxes. let us not be mistaken: it is at european level that action is needed to restore our public finances and ensure equality for all in the face of taxation. this report is an indispensable step on the long road to building a just europe.

in writing. ‒ the fight against tax evasion is a priority and the report tax 2 indeed raises elements in this direction. for example, he criticises the favourable treatment of multinationals, which pay less tax than smes and benefit from tax avoidance strategies implemented by some countries, known as tax optimisation. lack of information on final beneficiaries, ineffective exchange of information, non-compliance with control requirements: all these shortcomings stem from the ineffectiveness of the current legislation and this report has the merit of highlighting them. but it does not go far enough: the people responsible for the situation are cleared and the real solutions are neglected. public control of the banking and financial system, restrictions on capital movements and a common action plan are needed to put an end to tax havens. the commission has already made a number of proposals, and i am sure that the commission will be able to support them.

in writing. ‒ this is an own-initiative report to enable the application of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. the anti-discrimination directive, which has been blocked in the council for eight years, would thus be brought to an indirect conclusion. the council would then be obliged to apply in full the decisions related to the union's accession to the convention in 2010. the idea is generous and seems positive at first. however, if we look at it more closely, the initiative here is to enhance the role of the commission by obliging the council, on a (social) subject outside its direct competence, to consider the union as a state in its own right. many of the stumbling blocks are also due to the differing definitions of disability, the reasonable use of public and private spaces, etc. finally, the report extends the concepts of disability to include gender equality and the reception of migrants. we are opposed to the method used by the union in its disability policy and to its systematic attempts to extend it to other concepts. i therefore opposed the report.

in writing. ‒ the figures are sobering: 15% of the world's population, or approximately one billion people, live with a disability. 80% of these people live in low-income countries. 50% of disabilities are preventable and are due to poverty. about 98% of children with disabilities living in developing countries are out of school. in europe there are 80 million disabled people, one sixth of the population. according to the ilo, the unemployment rate of disabled people can reach 80% in some countries. people with disabilities are too often marginalised and discrimination against them takes many forms, from denial of educational opportunities to exclusion and isolation. so yes, action is needed to at least try to reverse the trend, if not by a profound change in attitudes and behaviour. even if i do not agree with the proposed text in all its aspects, i will always be in favour of texts which aim to eliminate discrimination against disabled people in all areas of life.

in writing. ‒ by ratifying the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, the european union has established a framework for promoting, respecting and monitoring the convention. the five bodies responsible - parliament, commission, ombudsman, fundamental rights agency and european disability forum - must work towards its implementation in european legislation and actions, thus aiming at a better integration of disabled people. several levels of action need to be considered. first, the labour market. it is necessary to ensure that businesses and administrations have the facilities to employ disabled people and are encouraged to do so. secondly, access to education. progress is still needed in terms of accessibility to infrastructure and recreational and sporting activities, which are also drivers of integration. the eu must also ensure that gender equality is better integrated into its disability policy. finally, there will be a need to ensure regular monitoring of the implementation of the convention and an evaluation of the progress made.

in writing. the integration of disabled people into our society remains a challenge. the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, ratified by the eu in 2010, takes stock of its implementation and the final observations of the un committee on the rights of persons with disabilities. the report finds, not surprisingly, that many disparities remain, particularly between member states. disabled people face multiple forms of discrimination and violence, which can add up to one another, particularly when they are women, children or refugees. the creation of a european framework could provide guarantees for the effective implementation of the rights of persons with disabilities, the promotion of their personal autonomy, accessibility, access to employment, social integration and autonomy, and the elimination of all forms of discrimination. the emphasis is also on accessibility to transport and buildings in new construction projects. this report is a proposal and shows the long way to go. i voted in favour, hoping that this type of proposal could be implemented by the member states. unfortunately, this is far from a priority and in reality the eu has little influence on these issues.
in writing. ‒ this is an objection to a commission proposal based on a positive (or even a targeted) opinion of the european food safety authority (efsa) on caffeine products. it is believed to have major therapeutic or health benefits, for concentration, endurance, etc. caffeine is often found in sweet or fatty foods. the rapporteur is concerned that the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work should be rejected. the commission is trying to reassure consumers by claiming that it will limit the caffeine-friendly labels to products intended for adults only, but it does not specify how it will force retailers to distribute them only to adults. in addition, the report points to the shortcomings in the efsa study: lack of gender distinction in the evaluation of effects on metabolism, lack of analysis of side effects, etc. the commission's proposal appears to be based on a few simple public health grounds. so naturally i supported that objection.
in writing. ‒ this objection concerns health claims that may be made for products containing caffeine. these products may be either solid foods or beverages. caffeine products do not need claims to be sold and are not really the work of french industrialists. the proposed claims (caffeine improves endurance, alertness and concentration) are a real problem with energy drinks as they can lead to dangerous consumption (especially when mixed with alcohol), however, the french coffee union told us that these claims were expected by companies (some of them french) to revive coffee consumption among young people and that no french company manufactures energy drinks. that is why i abstained from voting on this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this objection which seeks to ban 'health claims' on products containing caffeine. the european food safety authority (efsa) has allowed claims such as 'caffeine helps to improve concentration' to be used. however, there is no information on the side effects of high caffeine intake, such as incontinence, or on the dangers of mixing caffeine and alcohol. however, these claims are necessary to revive coffee consumption among young people, who often prefer energy drinks to more serious health effects, a revival all the more important than expected by a significant number of companies.
in writing. ‒ this report concerns an objection under article 106 on permitted health claims made on foods. this concerns products containing caffeine. efsa gave a favourable opinion on several claims (caffeine increases alertness, concentration, endurance, etc.). however, this opinion has several shortcomings (doses taken into account, no difference between men and women, no consideration of side effects, etc.). the rapporteur, however, points out that the consumption of these caffeine-based products also affects the youngest, that these are often very sweet drinks and that more than one third of young europeans are already overweight. the commission is introducing restrictions to protect this young audience.

in writing. ‒ in 2015, revelations by us researchers of software cheating to mask nitrogen dioxide emissions from diesel engines led to the volkswagen scandal. this process allowed the world's leading car manufacturer to export to the united states despite strict limits on nitrogen dioxide emissions. on 17 december 2015, a committee of inquiry was set up in the european parliament to examine allegations of breaches of union law or maladministration in the application of union law. this interim report sets out the methodology and hearings that constitute parliament's inquiry into emissions in the automotive sector. the hearings themselves will continue until autumn 2016, after which meps will work on the final report. this short and very neutral text encourages the committee of inquiry to continue its work and invites the conference of presidents, the commission and the authorities of the member states to cooperate in good faith, so that no element of the inquiry escapes the committee. i therefore voted in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ rosario crocetta was a member of the european parliament when he made the controversial remarks and the record of the debates in which mr crocetta participated shows that he has always been very active in the fight against organised crime. it is also clear from the documents provided to the committee on legal affairs and the hearing before it that mr crocetta's statements have a direct and obvious link with his parliamentary duties. so i voted to defend his immunity.

in writing. ‒ the proposed action concerns the issuing in 2011 by the thessaloniki city council of allegedly illegal public domain occupancy permits for the purpose of installing terraces on pedestrian paths. sotirios zarianopoulos is being prosecuted as a former member of that municipal council. the prosecution in question is clearly unrelated to sotirios zarianopoulos' status as a member of the european parliament, but rather to his previous term as a member of the thessaloniki city council. nor does it concern an opinion or vote delivered by a member in the exercise of his duties as a member of the european parliament within the meaning of article 8 of protocol no 7 on the privileges and immunities of the european union. there is therefore no reason to assume that the prosecution envisaged was inspired by the intention to harm the political activity of the member of parliament (fumus persecutionis), especially since the prosecution concerns all the members of the municipal council of the time (judicial proceedings for prevarication committed jointly (articles 13bis, 45 and 259 of the criminal code) against 34 municipal councillors who voted in favour. so i voted to waive immunity.

in writing. ‒ the winkler report was intended to convey to the council the european parliament's recommendations on the way forward for adjusting the concessions offered to china by the eu at the wto following the accession of croatia to the european union. while it foreshadows the type of (reverse) adjustments the eu will have to make following brexit, the file is mainly technical in that it is about changing, according to established practice, customs duties on industrial products and quotas for agricultural products, in proportion to the size of the croatian market, to take account of the enlargement of the european single market. the changes are minor: customs duties on entry into the european market for rubber shoes from china will rise from 17% to 16.9%. similarly, china will have the opportunity to export an additional 650 tonnes of mushrooms to europe. i voted for this report because i believe that it is not appropriate to engage in a needless confrontation with china. on the other hand, i will continue to fight at parliamentary level for the european union to increase its tariffs on the dumped products that beijing dumps in europe: steel, ceramics, chemicals, paper, etc.

in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 471/2009 concerns community statistics on external trade with third countries. the purpose of this decision is to specify the powers of the commission and to lay down the appropriate procedure for the adoption of measures for external trade statistics under those powers. the general objective is to remove, by the end of the seventh parliamentary term and in all legislative instruments, all provisions referring to the regulatory procedure with scrutiny and to replace them with procedures with delegated acts and implementing powers. regulation (ec) no 471/2009 of the european parliament and of the council confers on the commission the power to implement certain provisions of that regulation. in order to align regulation (ec) no 471/2009 with articles 290 and 291 tfeu, the implementing powers conferred on the commission by that regulation should be replaced by the power to adopt delegated and implementing acts. the abolition of regulatory procedures with scrutiny and their replacement by delegated acts and implementing powers is a technical measure made mandatory by the adoption of the tfeu. so i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation provides for compulsory collection of statistics on the prices of electricity and gas supplied to private individuals, whereas this collection was previously voluntary. for companies, a 2008 directive already made this collection compulsory. this proposal is an accessory to the energy liberalisation packages adopted in the years 2004-2012. the stated aim is to produce european statistics and then to encourage the creation of transnational european and then transatlantic oligopolies which, "put into competition", will "lower prices". the commission has forced france to increase edf's tariffs from 2007 onwards in order to artificially create a competitive electricity market. as regards gas, it is a challenge to believe that private actors, not backed by governments, will guarantee a secure and affordable supply. beyond this general consideration, three criticisms can be made of the text: the choice of the regulation over the directive; a delegation of power (articles 9 and 10) without a time limit; an additional reporting system which will burden the management of the undertakings concerned. that is why i voted against this proposal.
