in writing. ‒ i voted against the report entitled 'towards a new organisation of the energy market'. firstly, the report calls for the acer to be given greater powers in the name of greater coordination at regional level (paragraphs 70 and 72), with the aim of gradually moving it from the role of coordinator between national regulators to a supranational regulatory role. the report also maintains the illusion of an integrated energy market and the energy union (points 3 and 4), blaming the member states for not moving fast enough in the change process. it also opposes national capacity mechanisms (point 9) and puts the market before security of supply, as all european texts in this field do. as usual, ecology (in this case renewable energies) is a pretext for strengthening european federalism and destroying national enterprises in the name of the fluidity required by intermittent energies.
in writing. ‒ the progressive approach mentioned is a way of limiting the competences of the member states a little more, in an almost painless way. moreover, the energy market is logically a natural monopoly, even though the states have almost no room for manoeuvre on matters governed by the treaties. the states, whatever the rapporteur says, are always the losers, whatever the dress and the formulas used. ecology is, as is too often the case, used as a pretext for strengthening european federalism and for destroying national enterprises in the name of the fluidity required by energy sources. i could only vote against that resolution.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to clarify the european parliament's position on the european commission's legislative proposal on a new energy market organisation due to be published in december 2016. given the evolution of our energy supply (methods and locations of production, development of renewable energy, etc.), the market must necessarily adapt to these changes. this report sets out options for achieving a more fluid, open and integrated energy market. it proposes, for example, to increase interconnections so that energy services and supplies flow across national borders on the basis of local and regional needs. the energy supply for 500 million europeans is a crucial issue; i therefore vote in favour of this report, which has a broad consensus in parliament and respects the approach of our political group.
in writing. - i voted for this text. despite the incentive to invest in the network, we criticise the enhanced powers granted to the supranational regulator, the european agency for the cooperation of energy regulators (acer), at the expense of the authority of the states. market ideology takes precedence over the security of supply of states. for these reasons, we cannot support this report.
in writing. ‒ the evolutionary approach mentioned is a way of limiting the competences of the member states a little more in a painless way. moreover, the energy market is logically a natural monopoly, and the states have almost no room for manoeuvre on matters governed by the treaties. the states, whatever the rapporteur says, are always the losers, whatever the dress and the formulas used. ecology is, as too often, a pretext for strengthening european federalism and for destroying national enterprises in the name of the fluidity needed by energy. i therefore voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ this langen report towards a new energy market organisation deals with the new energy market brought about by the changes brought about by the energy union. the report has some positive aspects (investment in the grid, reiteration of national competence on the energy mix, etc.). however, other points are tainted by the report, such as the strengthening of the powers of acer, the endless promotion of the energy union, all tinged with liberalism. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the new energy market organisation. i support in particular the desire to make it more flexible and to strengthen the security of supply, which is fundamental for our continent, in particular by creating an interconnected market at european level.

in writing. ‒ the report has a very centrist tone: it is a caress of the hair of the states on issues regulated by the treaties (energy mix), it is based on an evolutionary approach to gnaw at the competences of the states and it is based on a so-called energy market, which is, despite what the rapporteur says, a natural monopoly. as usual, ecology (in this case renewable energies) is a pretext for strengthening european federalism and for destroying national enterprises, in the name of the fluidity required by intermittent energies. i therefore vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which encourages the strengthening of the internal energy market, in particular by allowing the free movement of electricity, in conjunction with cross-border competition which will stimulate appropriate investments for the sector. regional cooperation and coordination on energy policies are needed. the report also points to the possibility of implementing capacity mechanisms to ensure security of supply for european citizens. the energy union is a good example of the usefulness of cooperation between states in a sector where the national perspective alone is not sufficient to meet the expectations and needs of citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, the main objective of which is to make the energy market more flexible, particularly the electricity sector. the report calls for a reorganized electricity market, combined with the implementation of existing legislation. in this sense, the regulatory framework needs to be amended to allow for the improvement of the share of renewable energy and to fill existing gaps in regulation at cross-border level. it is regrettable that there are still significant gaps in the interconnection between member states. new approaches are needed to overcome bottlenecks and achieve a smart distribution network that allows for the proper integration of the various energy market players. i supported this report because it recalls the importance of a more flexible energy market, targeting renewable energy and better integrated within the union.

in writing. ‒ this report aims to make the eu the world's leading producer of energy from renewable sources. that would be a good thing in itself if it were not contradicted by facts and actions. if it were really a question of allowing the development of renewable energies and ending dependence on both nuclear and fossil fuels, i would be totally in favour. in reality, the eu spends a lot of money on nuclear energy and very little on renewable energy, including research. it is developing free trade agreements all over the world which lead to aberrations in export policy, particularly with regard to the carbon footprint, supposedly to break prices, but which above all break the rights of workers and workers themselves, and i am not talking about the multitude of armed conflicts to ensure control of fossil fuels. this text does not create any illusions and when it claims that the internal energy market will better protect consumers by fighting against price regulation and subsidies, my indignation knows no bounds, as if energy poverty linked to the growing increase in poverty were not a growing scourge in europe.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. heating and cooling account for about half of the eu's final energy demand. this is why it is so important to reduce demand and make the sector more efficient, in order to reduce our dependence on energy imports, reduce emissions and lower costs for consumers, especially those at risk of energy poverty.
in writing. ‒ despite the good measures proposed, france does not need the eu's recommendations to define its energy policy, in this case in the field of heating and cooling. the problems of central europe, with its often outdated and/or highly polluting facilities, are not the same as those of our own country and the interpretation of the text could well be against our interests by imposing heavy constraints on individuals and by accelerating the disfigurement or outright destruction of our heritage. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it sets out a european union strategy for heating and cooling, setting out proposals to reduce energy use in buildings. i believe that renovating buildings is one of the simplest ways to use energy more efficiently and to achieve significant reductions in co2 emissions.
in writing. ‒ this text, written by a polish author and mainly concerned with eastern european countries, poses potentially serious threats to our architectural heritage. there is a caution for historic buildings . however, in addition to the fact that the concept remains vague (given the different legislation on heritage protection, with only 44 000 buildings protected in france against more than 1 000 000 in germany), paragraph 23 for example asks the local authorities to deal with the specific problems of rural buildings, which are generally older, less energy-efficient and less beneficial to health and provide less thermal comfort. you mean the outside insulation? this risk to our heritage (in the broad sense) is all the greater as the current trend in france is to give more and more decision-making power to local buildings, which generally do not have the required skills and which can hardly withstand the various pressures (in particular from the btp), to the detriment of the architects of the buildings of france. this text therefore risks accelerating the disfigurement and even the outright destruction of our heritage in the name of energy efficiency.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the eu heating and cooling strategy because the measures it proposes risk endangering our architectural heritage, especially in rural areas. while energy efficiency is a worthy goal, the text urges local authorities to take action on rural buildings, which are considered to be older, less energy-efficient and less beneficial for health. in addition to the danger that such measures would pose to our assets, it should be remembered that the constant change in standards poses a certain cost problem, particularly for individuals who have to invest, according to the report, in reversible heat pumps or in thermal insulation works. while there are attempts in the text to be cautious about 'historic buildings', this precaution is fragile given the legal vagueness surrounding this definition. it should also be noted that despite the precaution included in the energy transition act for the protection of the old building in insulation operations, the implementing decree was quick to mitigate this assurance as much as possible.
in writing. ‒ this text calls on member states and local authorities to save energy for heating and cooling. energy saving is here considered as the first clean fuel. in paragraph 23 it emphasizes rural buildings with a clear risk to the rural heritage of france. i voted against this paragraph as it was adopted.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to increase energy efficiency and encourages the use of renewable energy for heating and cooling with a target of 100% by 2050. to achieve this, the report proposes to rely on geothermal energy, the production of biomethane, the priority use of local raw materials or the recovery of industrial heat. although it is necessary in the member states to tackle energy waste in order to reduce our energy bill, there is still the question of financing the infrastructure to achieve this, such as thermal insulation and reversible heat pumps. however, there is a concern that this work will be carried out by private individuals despite the existence of a subsidy system. the report also recommends that energy saving studies be carried out in historic buildings to improve their energy performance. there is no guarantee that adequate work will ensure the protection and preservation of our cultural heritage. that is why i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report is about the european commission's proposal to launch its first strategy to tackle massive energy consumption, which is considered one of the priorities of the energy union. the parliament's report underlines the importance of urban energy networks and calls on member states to reduce the use of boilers. it also stresses the importance of investing in research and innovation in this area. considering that more efficient use of energy must help the union to achieve the objectives of cop21 and help european citizens to reduce their energy bills, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. this report on the european union's heating and cooling strategy sets out the european parliament's recommendations to address the massive energy consumption in this sector. with almost 50% of final energy demand in the european union used for heating and cooling, guidelines are needed to improve energy efficiency, mainly in buildings. i believe that there is a particular need to encourage research and innovation in this area in order to enable not only better insulation, which will generate energy savings, but also to develop the use of renewable energy.
in writing. ‒ this text extends the pieper report on energy efficiency adopted in brussels in june. the stated objective is to achieve 100% renewable energy. despite this seemingly laudable objective, there are fears that a form of energy austerity is being imposed on the peoples of europe. in addition, this text puts our heritage at serious risk by advocating an improvement in their energy performance at the expense of preserving their heritage value. i therefore voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ 40% of the eu's energy consumption is used for heating and cooling buildings. although i am convinced that this is an important source of energy savings and probably of savings in the short and long term, i voted against this report. because hell is paved with good intentions, but also with many of the measures proposed. the 'smart boilers', for example, are reminiscent of the controversy surrounding the smart meters, which are concerned with health problems, privacy, untimely power cuts and without even the assurance of real savings. germany has decided to do without it. it's a sign. the new equipment is also recommended, which will inevitably be very expensive for households. and there is also the encouragement, if not the obligation, of the external insulation of old buildings. this obligation already exists in french law, via a highly controversial decree implementing the law on energy transition. it risks destroying many of the picturesque facades that give charm and beauty to many of france's towns and villages. there is no guarantee of effectiveness. this lucrative market could bring in €800 million for professionals. it's the price of ugliness.

in writing. ‒ the eu trust fund for africa (eutf), launched on 12 november 2015 at the eu-africa summit in valletta, aims to foster political stability in the different regions of the african continent and to contribute to better management of migration flows. more specifically, the eutf aims to address the root causes of forced displacement and irregular migration by promoting resilience, access to employment, equal opportunities, security and development. while the report welcomes the initiative, it stresses that the eutf, which is largely funded by the european development fund, cannot be used for security or border control purposes. the eutf should give priority to supporting access to education and employment, good governance and environmental projects. this is the driving idea which is perfectly reflected in the final text, and i therefore support this report.
in writing. - i abstained on this text. we approve of the reasons why this aid is being released. the european union trust fund aims to tackle the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and illegal migration. it is committed to promoting resilience, economic opportunities, security and development. but on the one hand, there is no control of this aid and, on the other hand, it is part of a blind financing logic, which we are fighting against.
in writing. ‒ a new form of european funds is becoming fashionable in brussels. to 'combat the root causes of irregular migration' from africa, states and the commission agreed on an urgent 'trust fund'. it will redirect the financing of eu instruments and state aid for development policy towards a board of directors which will be responsible for deciding on projects to be financed, ranging from the return of migrants to security and defence operations. in the most complete opacity, outside the community budgetary framework and therefore at the expense of development projects. parliament is obviously not a member of this council and can only point out these risks here, by requesting monitoring and impact reports. it called for an increase in development contributions within the community budget, over which it has a say, in order to focus more on the development of local economies and the fight against unemployment, which, along with crises, are the main drivers of displacement. i acknowledge this critical and supportive work, but i am totally opposed to this fund, which it endorses. i vote against it.
in writing. ‒ as is often the case in this committee, good intentions (such as development aid to the countries of emigration to stop the migration bleeding), but mixed with too few concrete proposals in terms of monitoring of this aid, evaluation of results and real political will to stop the migration influx. therefore, i abstained on this matter.
in writing. ‒ the main objective of the european union trust fund for africa is to promote stability in these regions and to help better manage migration. it aims to address the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and irregular migration by ensuring the promotion of resilience, economic opportunities, security and development. despite its voluntarist aspects, this report is part of a blind funding logic, without any a posteriori or a priori checks on the proper use and management of funds, the eu preferring to shift the burden onto local authorities and a partnership with the private sector. the report sees population growth as an asset in developing areas, while youth employment and training policies are lagging far behind the development goals and the future is uncertain for the younger generations, who are more likely to desert their countries for a better life in the west than to build the future of the west. abstention from voting.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the european union trust fund for africa as regards its implications for humanitarian development aid. the fund provides assistance in three african regions to manage migration, security and development issues. in this respect, it is based on three pillars: economic programmes, resilience, migration management and stability and governance.
in writing. ‒ the european union trust fund for africa was signed by the president of the european commission, 25 member states, norway and switzerland and launched at the valletta summit on migration on 12 november 2015. it is intended to address the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and irregular migration by ensuring the promotion of resilience, economic opportunities, security and development. despite its voluntarist aspects, this report is based on a blind funding logic, without any a posteriori or a priori checks. the eu prefers to shift the burden onto local authorities and partnership with the private sector, in the hypothetical hope of transferring the burden. the report sees population growth as an asset in developing areas, whereas youth employment and training policies are lagging far behind the development goals, and the future is uncertain for younger generations, who are inclined to leave their countries. i therefore prefer to abstain on this report, which, wrapped in good moral intentions, ignores reality and spends millions of euros without results.
in writing. ‒ the european union trust fund for africa was established in november 2015, following the valletta summit on migration, to provide support to african states most affected by irregular migration. four regions are particularly targeted: the horn of africa, the sahel, the lake chad basin and, more generally, north africa. i voted in favour of this report, which notes the difficulties involved in setting up this fund in terms of financing, implementation and control. through this text, we call for greater transparency and consistency, both in the preparation of programmes and in the implementation of projects. development effectiveness must be a priority, and all stakeholders (the eu, its member states and african states) must therefore fully assume their responsibilities to make this trust fund a useful tool in resolving this unprecedented migration crisis.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the financing, implementation and control of the european union trust fund for africa. the fund was created at the valletta summit on migration in november 2015 and has a budget of €1.8 billion. the main objective of this fund is to promote stability in the region and to contribute to better managing migration. it also aims to address the root causes of destabilisation, forced displacement and irregular migration, with a focus on promoting resilience, economic opportunities, equal opportunities, security and development. this report calls for transparency and clarity to better achieve the objectives. it is essential that the fund respects the principle of coherence and avoids any contradiction between development and security objectives, humanitarian and migration policies. in using this fund, the union and the member states should set as long-term objectives the consolidation of peace and the strengthening of governance in the beneficiary countries.

the rapporteur. madam president, we hear it all the time: europe is in crisis and we know that one of the reasons for this crisis is that we have a single market, freedom of services, capital, people who can move, but we have completely different social systems and we know that social dumping is taking place. for a long time it was not possible to define what social dumping was and we have now come to an agreement that there was a set of illegal and abusive practices which led to a profound undermining of the dignity of workers. dignity when you are housed in a humiliating way, when you are not paid for the work you have done, when you work all day or all week and when you do not respect rest periods. but it is also a financial and budgetary problem, because social dumping is draining resources from our social protection systems and is making them poorer by the day. finally, it is an economic problem, because it tends to weaken labour income, as we know, and obviously to push towards a deflationary tendency. i would add that this is a huge political problem and that european citizens, who consider that europe does not protect them but, on the contrary, weakens them by accepting these social dumping practices, are increasingly sceptical or even turn against europe by deciding that we must vote for parties which today want to destroy it, that many states today are beginning to say that we must question the internal market and question the existing directives, sometimes even unilaterally. how do you answer that? of course, this report is just a stone, but it is a stone that is still necessary and important. firstly, by applying existing legislation. to do this, we must increase the means of control, we must ensure that there is cooperation at european level to enable labour inspectors to work together, to have the means of translation. it is important to establish genuine crossborder cooperation which makes it possible to combat drifting enterprises today. the existing legislation must also be improved, and that is why a number of measures are needed, for example to combat the famous letterbox companies which do not exist, or which exist at one time and disappear immediately afterwards. these companies must have a real business to be able to employ people today, to send them off to another country, for example. we need a road transport agency and this is very important, because how can we fight social dumping in the road sector today if there are no instruments at european level to do so? a blacklist is needed so that companies which have seriously failed, which have seriously infringed european and national legislation, cannot now claim contracts which would be dangerous to award to them. finally, we must record, for example, the declarations of secondment in a european register, if only so that we can know exactly who is being seconded and when. finally, we must work towards social convergence. there are specific measures to be taken, for example at european level, on the situation of women, who are often the first victims of fraudulent secondment or even of abusive exploitation. we must also work on the question of wages and, while we know that a single minimum wage is impossible today in europe and even undesirable, a national minimum wage of about 60% of the average wage would obviously be a very important step forward. i want to end by saying something to you. these discussions lasted thirty hours. they have made it possible to overcome the divisions, to bring together the forces of progress to work together, but also the political divisions within this house. they have also helped to bridge the geographical gaps between north, south, east and west. it is now necessary to ensure that the european parliament supports this proposal to combat social dumping.

in writing. today i voted in favour of the report by my colleague, mr guillaume balas, on the fight against social dumping in the european union. this report sends a clear message to the commission and calls for concrete measures to combat social dumping. the drawing up of a blacklist of companies which do not comply with social legislation, the registration of declarations of secondment in a european register, the strengthening of controls or the limitation of secondments over time are all proposals which would strengthen the social dimension of the internal market. the commission must now act, this vote shows that there is a parliamentary majority to move forward on these necessary measures. i also welcome the fact that the report calls for the establishment of a 60% threshold of the national average wage as a reference for setting the minimum wage in the member states. finally, on road transport, which is the epitome of social dumping, the report also goes in the right direction by calling on the commission to set up a european road transport agency to ensure compliance with the rules.
president of the committee on budgets. mr president, this late debate on the draft budget for 2017, as a consequence of the timetable chosen by the united kingdom to hold its brexit referendum, comes on the eve of two expected events. first, the state of the union address by the president of the commission, followed by the presentation of the draft mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020. my dear colleagues, we can still dream. he dreams that the 2017 budget will no longer be just an annual tranche of the financial framework. our budgetary hemiplegia prevents us from deliberating on the revenue. as for our field of work, expenditure, 1% of european gdp, is distributed at a rate of 80% to the member states. so only 20% is left for supranational actions, which is the essence of the european budget. but a third of that 20% is already pre-empted to finance the institutions - the commission, parliament, council, court of justice, court of auditors, agencies. how can we respond to crisis situations and prepare for the future? yes, ladies and gentlemen, less than 14% of our budget is allocated to the research programmes horizon 2020, erasmus, the programme for the interconnection of infrastructure in europe, to control our external borders, to welcome refugees with dignity, to combat terrorism, unemployment, especially among young people, to regulate agricultural production, to combat tax havens and fraud of all kinds, to meet our humanitarian obligations in the regions devastated by war, to reduce the sources of economic migration through an ambitious policy of development aid, particularly in africa. the financial framework, which is a mirror of the past, is outdated and lacks any significant flexibility. this is the zero degree of politics. the situation is so miserable that the commission is multiplying budgetary satellites - efsi, trust funds, budgetary facilities for turkey - which are like galaxies beyond parliamentary control. our budget is a spectacle of impotence, an illegible budget, a budget that is incomprehensible to the citizens, an illustration of the european union's inability to speak to the europeans. i hope that the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework will bring our budget out of the simulation it has been in for years. let us be vigilant about the appropriations made available to the member states and the cohesion funds that are sanctioned by nature. the payment forecasts are revised downwards because commitments are not being decided on quickly. why would you do that? i think it is because the new cohesion programmes and our regulations have become so complex that they are repelling public investors and local actors. that means that there is an urgent need for a drastic revision of our financial regulations. perhaps also because, however important, european aid covers only part of the expenditure, forcing operators to go into debt as if europe were becoming a catalyst for public spending and debt. in conclusion, at this stage of the budgetary procedure, we remain confident. we look forward to designing and voting budgets that give the union the means to show its power, budgets that speak to europeans, budgets that demonstrate to public opinion the effectiveness of the european union's added value.
for the gue/ngl group mr president, mr minister, commissioner vella, i do not know whether we should talk about wildlife trade, or whether it would be more appropriate to talk about wildlife trade, since when it comes to wildlife trade, wildlife is on the side of humanity. i also do not know whether we should talk about trade, but rather about crime, the crimes of humanity against endangered species. we always tend to wait for tragedy to happen before we act, and the decline of these species has now become tragic. as you said, the african lion is declining by almost half its population and is disappearing from 12 european countries. almost all of africa's elephants are being slaughtered for their ivory. millions of pangolins and rhino are being poached for their scales and horns, and the forests of madagascar, near my home island of réunion, are being plundered for their rosewood. we must take the time factor into account. it's late, very late, but not too late to both stop the sixth wave of species extinction, but also to stop the decline in wildlife.

in writing. ‒ following the accession of croatia, the european union must update its agreement with switzerland on the free movement of persons. under the agreement, which was signed in june 2002, nationals of both parties can enter, reside, settle and study in the territory of the other party as easily as a national resident. the new protocol gives switzerland the possibility of restricting access to its labour market for croatian nationals for a period of seven years. a safeguard clause even provides that at the end of this period, switzerland may, for a further three years, unilaterally limit the number of residence permits that allow croats to come to work there. i am opposed to the free movement of people, which is the main cause of social dumping, and i voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ this social dialogue at the summit is presented as essential to reinforce the legitimacy of economic governance with a strengthened 'social pillar'. however, it only involves partners who are all the more dependent on the institutions as they are an integral part of the system. the ultra-liberal line of these discussions is clear and strongly encourages structural reforms. in addition, the schengen area is considered untouchable, and the integration of migrants is seen as an opportunity for europe. not only is the 'social dialogue' rigged, and the desire to relaunch the process at member state level a mere formulation of principle, but this social guarantee serves to legitimize the governance that is imposed, without any consideration for national and democratic institutions, starting with national parliaments. i voted against it.

in writing. the eu-sadec agreement is the first economic partnership agreement signed between the european union and a group of acp countries, botswana, lesotho, swaziland, namibia, south africa and mozambique. economic partnership agreements (epas), intended to replace previous trade preference agreements that expired in 2007, are more ambitious than traditional trade agreements. under the terms of the agreement, the six states, all members of the southern african development community (sadc), will benefit from positive discrimination, i.e. immediate duty-free and quota-free access to the european single market for their exports. protective measures have been added at the request of the european parliament to ensure that this cooperation will really benefit africans. this agreement contains an appointment clause providing for the mandatory review of any epa after 5 years and its possible amendment. this should make it possible to assess the impact of the elimination of customs duties on a country-by-country basis, also measuring the impact of progress made and, if necessary, making adjustments and improvements, in a spirit of mutual trust.

in writing. ‒ this text sets out the provisions for implementing the labour convention for the fisheries sector. as regards crew in particular, ships must have sufficient personnel of sufficient quality and number to ensure safe navigation and operation of the ship. a minimum rest period for fishermen must be fixed, and it may never be less than 10 hours per 24-hour period and 77 hours per 7-day period, according to the provisions on rest time. in addition, every fishing vessel must have a crew list on board. finally, a fisherman's commitment agreement must be signed between the fisherman and the shipowner. these measures seem to me to be an acceptable minimum and make it possible to limit the social dumping to which french fishermen may be subjected.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the implementation of the convention on labour in fisheries, established in 2007 by the international labour organisation (ilo). this text is a reminder of the importance of paying particular attention to workers in the european fisheries sector. the overall requirements of the convention on work in fishing are therefore minimal and thus allow member states to adapt measures to national specificities in favour of fishermen.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the implementation by the union of the international labour organisation's convention on work in fishing. with the integration of the social partners' agreement on the ilo fisheries labour convention into european law, the union will be able to promote its implementation in partner countries around the world, thus contributing to the establishment of a level playing field in the fisheries sector at global level and to the fight against the worst forms of exploitation of fishermen.
in writing. ‒ today, more than 100 000 people are employed in the fisheries sector. yet it is one of the most accident-prone sectors in europe, with the number of accidents at work sometimes 15 times higher than in other sectors. lack of sleep, old or broken equipment and long working hours are just a sample of the difficult conditions faced by fishermen, which can quickly lead to human catastrophe. in 2007, the ilo adopted the convention on work in fishing, to ensure adequate protection for fishermen worldwide. unfortunately, at this stage only france has ratified this convention at the level of the european union. in an unusual procedure, the social partners therefore asked the european commission to implement the agreement on the ilo convention by a council directive. i am glad that the social partners have reached an agreement that is acceptable to all parties, after almost four years of negotiations. while the transport sector was very quick to implement the necessary transpositions, such a legal vacuum in the fisheries sector was no longer tolerable.
in writing. ‒ in 2002, the international labour organisation (ilo) started global discussions on a comprehensive and updated set of international standards for the fisheries sector, to ensure adequate protection for fishermen worldwide. these discussions culminated in 2007 with the adoption of the convention on work in fishing. in its public consultation, the commission consulted the european social partners to examine the possibility of a joint initiative to promote the application of the provisions of the convention in the eu. the european commission's aim is to improve the working and living conditions of fishermen working on board vessels flying the flag of an eu member state. the resolution currently under consideration seeks to request the application of the agreement concluded between cogeca, the etf and europêche on the implementation of the ilo convention on labour in fisheries, 2007. i voted yes. it should be noted that france is the only member state to have ratified this convention. this ratification is dated 28 october 2015, but has not yet entered into force.

in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 requires the initiators of insurance-based retail investment products (a €10 trillion market in europe) to prepare key information documents for these products. the european supervisory authorities have been asked to develop regulatory technical standards on the presentation and content of key information documents. the commission therefore submitted a delegated act on 30 june 2016 containing all the elements to be presented in the key information documents. the delegated act was strongly criticised by all financial market participants and investor associations from the time of its publication. these new key information documents are criticised for being opaque and misleading, especially in relation to the presentation of performance and its calculation. in addition, the formulas used on the spreadsheet are not realistic enough and do not place enough emphasis on the risks of loss for the investor, and the presentation of costs is based on overly favourable assumptions. i therefore voted in favour of the objection tabled, which calls on the commission to introduce new technical standards and to postpone the entry into force of the regulation.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 (priip regulation) requires the originators of insurance-based retail packaged investment products (priips) (a €10 trillion market in europe) to prepare key information documents (kids) for these products before they are made available to retail investors. a delegated act proposing regulatory technical standards (rts) on the presentation and content of kids has been submitted by the commission. these standards are often criticized, but they leave a lot of room for subjectivity. we voted in favour of the objection put forward by pervenche berès, asking the commission to introduce new technical standards and to postpone the entry into force of the regulation. it is worth noting that this is the first time in the history of the european union that the european parliament has rejected regulatory technical standards (rts).

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the commission delegated regulation supplementing regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 on key information documents for retail and insurance-based investment products (priips). the regulation requires the originators of these products, which represent a €10 trillion market in europe, to prepare 'key information documents' (kids) before they are made available to retail investors. the esas have been requested to develop regulatory technical standards (rts) on the presentation and content of the kids. the commission therefore submitted a delegated act containing all the elements to be submitted. the delegated act was strongly criticised by all financial market participants and investor associations. in particular, these kids are criticised for being opaque and misleading, especially in relation to the presentation of performance and its calculation. past performance is suppressed in favour of future performance scenarios built around 3 hypotheses (unfavourable, moderate, favourable) which leave a lot of room for subjectivity and do not take into account past crises.
in writing. ‒ objection to the technical standards presented by the commission under the priip regulation on kids available to retail investors for insurance-based retail packaged investment products (priips). these standards remove references to past performance of products in favour of subjective predictions of future performance. moreover, the formulae used on the plaque are not sufficiently pessimistic and do not sufficiently emphasise the risks of loss for the investor. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 (priip regulation) requires the originators of insurance-based retail packaged investment products (priips) (a €10 trillion market in europe) to prepare key information documents (kids) for these products before they are made available to retail investors. this objection, which was voted unanimously in committee, criticised these new kids for being opaque and misleading, especially with regard to the presentation of performance and its calculation. past performance is suppressed in favour of future performance scenarios built around 3 hypotheses (unfavourable, moderate, favourable) which leave a lot of room for subjectivity and do not take into account past crises. the presence of past statistics is the only way to highlight the likely gains and losses in an objective way. we therefore support the objection put forward by pervenche berès, who asks the commission to introduce new technical standards and to delay the entry into force of the regulation.

in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 1286/2014 (priip regulation) requires the originators of insurance-based retail packaged investment products (priips) (a €10 trillion market in europe) to prepare key information documents (kids) for these products before they are made available to retail investors. these new kids are criticised for being opaque and misleading, especially in relation to the presentation of performance and its calculation. past performance is suppressed in favour of future performance scenarios built around 3 hypotheses (unfavourable, moderate, favourable) which leave a lot of room for subjectivity and do not take into account past crises. the presence of past statistics is the only way to highlight the likely gains and losses in an objective way. in addition, the formulas used on the spreadsheet are not pessimistic enough and do not place enough emphasis on the risks of loss for the investor, and the presentation of costs is based on overly favourable assumptions. i therefore support the objection put forward by pervenche berès, who asks the commission to introduce new technical standards and to delay the entry into force of the regulation.

in writing. ‒ the priip regulation requires the originator of insurance-based retail investment products to prepare key information documents (kids) for these products before they are made available to retail investors. the esas have been requested to develop regulatory technical standards (rts) on the presentation and content of the kids, including methods for calculating and presenting the risks, remuneration and costs to be included in the kids. the commission therefore submitted a delegated act on 30 june 2016 containing all the elements to be presented in the kids. the delegated act was strongly criticised by all financial market participants and investor associations from the time of its publication. these new kids are criticised for being opaque and misleading, especially in relation to the presentation of performance and its calculation. i therefore supported the objection raised by pervenche berès, who asks the commission to introduce new technical standards and to postpone the entry into force of the regulation.

in writing. ‒ the revision of the prospectus directiveis part of the capital markets union, launched by jonathan hill, which aims to boost alternatives to bank financing for businesses. facilitating access to financial markets has therefore been one of the commission's priorities. the term prospectus refers to the documentation that issuers of financial products with public call for tender must make available to investors. overly stringent information requirements can create an administrative burden and the risk of dissuasive litigation, particularly for smes. it is therefore necessary to provide investors with relevant and synthetic information, differentiating between professional and lay investors, without creating excessive obstacles. on a strictly technical level, the recasting of the 'prospectus' directive may be justified. on the philosophy of the text and the capital markets union, it is more questionable to want to finance more the financing of enterprises, especially smes. the main beneficiaries will be market firms and commercial banks. i am more in favour of long-term business partnerships with banks focused on their business and loans to the real economy than speculation and market operations. i'd rather not.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report setting out the european parliament's position on the rules applicable to the issuance of a prospectus for the placing of securities. in november 2015, the european commission published a proposal for a european regulation to replace directive 2003/71/ec on prospectuses. the reform, which is part of the creation of a single capital market, aims to reduce investment barriers and facilitate the raising of funds on financial markets. it should be noted that smes will be the main beneficiaries of this simplification of documentation, national regimes will be harmonised and the centralisation of information at the level of the european securities and markets authority (esma) will be increased.

in writing. ‒ this resolution provides a number of recommendations to the european commission and member states in the run-up to the next international conference on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) next month. its convention helps to combat wildlife crime and illegal trade. the illegal trade in these species is the fourth largest black market in the world. the text supports many proposals by states to protect new species increasingly threatened by human activity and global warming or to ban the trade of certain others, such as elephants, for example, whose ivory trade supports many paramilitary groups. it called on the member states of the union and the commission to go beyond the existing international provisions. it called for greater transparency and vigilance in cites' decision-making process, its potential conflicts of interest and its proven cases of internal corruption. i welcome this resolution, to which my friend younous omarjee has made a major contribution. i vote for it.
in writing. ‒ this resolution welcomes the eu's accession to cites, whereby the eu will now vote on behalf of the 28 member states, all of whom were already parties to cites. the eu cannot replace the role of sovereign states in major issues of international cooperation, so i voted against this resolution.
in writing. ‒ this resolution sets out the key objectives of the eu as a participant in the 17th conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). it is true that there is an urgent need to regulate this trade and to protect species, in particular by strengthening the permit system. but cites welcomes the eu's accession to the convention as the sole representative. none of the 28 member states will be able to speak and vote on it, as it is now a matter for the eu. this situation is an attack on the sovereignty of states, and we are voting against this resolution.
in writing. ‒ since the eu cannot replace the role of sovereign states in major issues of international cooperation, i am voting against this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which sets out parliament's indications on the key objectives of the next convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, to be held in johannesburg at the end of september 2016. the text recalls that it is essential for biodiversity to protect endangered species, in particular by combating poaching and illegal trade in these species, of which europe is a hub.
in writing. ‒ this resolution sets out the eu's key objectives as a participant in the 17th conference of the parties to the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites) to be held in johannesburg from 24 september to 5 october. it is certainly urgent to regulate this trade and protect the species by strengthening the permit system and completing the classification of cites annexes i, ii and iii, which reflect the seriousness of the situation. unfortunately, this resolution welcomes the eu's accession to cites, whereby the eu will now vote on behalf of the 28 member states, all of whom are already parties to cites, on matters falling within the eu's competence. this was not the case before the eu joined cites in 2015. the eu cannot replace the role of sovereign states in the major issues of international cooperation, so i am voting against this resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which sets out the european parliament's position on the key objectives of the 17th conference of the convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora, to be held in johannesburg at the end of september. the text stresses the importance of protecting these species, which are threatened by illegal trade, poaching and organised crime, and which fuel corruption and trafficking in some countries around the world. the european union cannot remain a hub for this illegal trade.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which takes up parliament's indications on the key objectives of the forthcoming convention on international trade in endangered species of wild fauna and flora (cites). the 17th conference of the parties to cites will be held in johannesburg, south africa, at the end of september. as the resolution recalls, it is crucial to protect species threatened by international trafficking and poaching. moreover, it is undeniable that organised crime plays a major role in organising this illegal trade, which is a source of corruption. i supported this text because it stresses the need to punish the customers of this trade as much as the poachers.

in writing. ‒ this report concerns the application of the directive on postal services, which have been fully subject to competition since 2008. the use of e-mails reduces the number of letters sent, but the use of the internet and online shopping increases the number of parcels delivered to the benefit of online sellers and parcel delivery companies. the report proposes a series of contradictions and the end of the postal public service. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competition' in the context of the directive on the protection of the environment. the report, however, reaffirms the need to maintain universal service, ignoring the fact that this requirement is contrary to the ideal of competition. the report also calls for the elimination of public subsidies and thus, in the end, of universal service. as a rural person, and being even more concerned about these issues, i voted against this text.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this report was for the european right to call on the commission to revise the postal services directive in order to accelerate the liberalisation of the sector, in particular by strengthening the regulatory authorities and the control of universal service operators. for the s&d group, the challenge was to defend and ensure the universal service in a sustainable way. at the end of the negotiations, the text remains a measured approach and draws attention to points which are essential in my view, such as guaranteeing territorial cohesion while maintaining certain access points. however, it casts an unacceptable suspicion on the universal service, which i regret as vice-president of the intergroup on the common good and public services.
in writing. ‒ this report on postal services markets deplores the fact that international intra-eu trade is no longer developing. the committee therefore calls on the commission to ensure that domestic prices in the member states are closer to international prices, at the risk of raising the price of national consignments to compensate for the fall in international prices. the report multiplies the contradictions. it calls for the functions of postal operator and postal regulator to be completely separated. the most important objective is to ensure competition, not efficiency, accessibility or public service. it asks the commission to combat social dumping and wage-based labour exploitation, while at the same time it wants more competition, and it is precisely this competition which is at the origin of social dumping, the use of posted workers and even disguised work. finally, the hunt for public subsidies is reaffirmed. he explained that the aim is to achieve an integrated postal sector in the long term, through interoperability and a european definition of minimum standards to be respected. i therefore voted against this standardisation from below.

in writing. ‒ mr ferber looks at the situation of postal services, which were fully liberalised in 2008. as soon as the commission wanted to liberalise a public service, it hammered out the following argument: more competition would necessarily lower prices while guaranteeing the quality of the service. in 2008, the french bought their stamp for 0.55 euros to send a letter to france, as in many neighboring countries. in 2016, it costs them 0.80 euros for a letter to france and 1 euro to belgium, for example. this is a 45% and 80% increase respectively. for mail that comes in slower. as for the universality of the service, ask the many french people who live in towns and villages where post offices have disappeared or reduced their opening hours. the rapporteur believes that the market is still not liberalised, and regrets the predominance of the incumbent operator, while competitors concentrate on the most profitable geographical areas and segments. the national front's long-awaited market is being scrapped. the same is true of the precariousness of employees in all operators, due to competition, and the slow erosion of the very notion of public service. stop the slaughter.

in writing. ‒ the 2008 postal services directive has achieved its objectives of liberalising postal services. the report before us is concerned with ensuring that the conditions of competition are properly respected. it recalled that 'the vat exemption for postal services must be applied in a way that reduces distortions of competition between the old monopolies and new entrants to the market'. while some of the findings are realistic, the report does not suggest any way forward. the report thus merely 'notes' 'the increase in the number of parttime employees, temporary workers and self-employed in the sector'. or to deplore 'attempts to circumvent existing minimum wage regulations by increasing the workload to such an extent that it cannot be performed during paid working hours'. the few elements conceded on employment, such as the demand for a guarantee of 'decent working conditions', cannot therefore make us forget the social disaster that accompanied the liberalisation of this sector (11,700 jobs lost at the french post office in 2010). i am voting against this text which is satisfied with that.

on behalf of the enf group. mr president, special report no 13/2015 of the european court of auditors describes the failure of the european programme to support timber-producing countries in the fight against illegal logging. this scourge threatens not only the world's forest heritage but also the indigenous peoples who depend on the forest for their livelihood. the reasons for this illegal slaughter are varied. first, in indonesia, a large number of trees are being cut down to make way for plantations for paper or palm oil, thus destroying biodiversity. in south america, illegal logging is used to export timber to organizations that sometimes have ties to corrupt officials, who, of course, want to enrich themselves by supplying the international demand for timber. the loggers are being persecuted while they are victims of a system that exploits them, and of course the decision-makers are never arrested. in addition to corruption, the fight against illegal logging is not always the priority of the government of the country in question. the expansion of palm oil or soybean fields to support intensive agriculture is part of the problem. finally, the last problem is that of the traceability of products on the market. for example, 80 to 90 percent of peru's timber exported to china and other asian markets is illegal, representing a loss of approximately eur 86 million. finally, i think that expanding and strengthening the traceability imperative would be a good solution. given the complexity of the problem, knowing where the wood comes from and knowing the logging company is obviously a credible and entirely feasible solution.

on behalf of the enf group. mr president, mrs jourová and the members who have just spoken are all clearly in favour of this draft directive, and i regret that i have to break this fine consensus. what's this about? the aim of this directive is to guarantee access to a lawyer for all persons prosecuted for criminal offences. in particular, it is a matter of forcing states to provide legal aid to people who are too poor to pay their lawyer in full. so, in itself, legal aid is obviously a good system, but the states do not need the european union to enforce it. if i take the example of france, you should know that this system is introduced in our country by a law of 22 january 1851. that is, if france is two centuries ahead of you. the european union's inherent interference in this text is based in particular on article 47 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union, which provides precisely for this right to legal aid. but it is precisely the invoking of this charter, which i consider to be a highly questionable instrument, that is problematic. if we really want to protect human rights at european level, i think the european convention for the protection of human rights is more than enough. in reality, the charter is a wolf for human rights. he's the ultra-liberal wolf in the human rights fold. the justification for interference is given in the directive. the aim, she said, was 'to build confidence in the criminal justice systems of other member states'. i think that the objective has been missed, however, because this interference is taking on such proportions in criminal matters that it will certainly cause concern among the peoples of europe. you have learned nothing from brexit, and you have learned nothing from the hungarian referendum of 2 october. you also say that this text applies to the european mandate, which is not reassuring. the european mandate is a much less protective system than extradition. in french law, extradition is not a judge-to-judge procedure, but a procedure involving the judges, the investigating chamber, on the one hand, and the government, the decree, on the other. this means that the individual has two chances instead of one to escape extradition. in the final analysis, this text is a regression and, in my view, does not represent any progress at all.

‒ 4 october 2016 is a big day. i voted for the eu to ratify the paris agreement, which is the culmination of a long battle for binding targets to fight, together at global level, the greatest challenge of the 21st century, global warming. with the adoption of the paris agreement in the european parliament, as the un secretary-general ban ki-moon said, we are making history by bringing it into force. it is a great step for humanity and the planet and as a member of the european parliament i am proud that the european union has played a leading role in bringing this agreement to fruition. now we must look to the future, the entry into force of the paris agreement is only the beginning of a long struggle. this vote is not a mere formality but a political signal to translate our commitments into action. at european level, several pieces of legislation are on the table to translate the paris agreement, and parliament will have to live up to the challenge by adopting ambitious emission reduction targets.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european parliament's approval of the paris agreement. the agreement marks a historic turning point in the global fight against climate change. limiting the rise in global temperatures is ensured by confirming the warming threshold below 2°c, as well as setting an ambitious indicative target of 1.5°c. the planned nationally determined contributions (ndcs) of the signatory parties ensure global and collective action, while a new dynamic mechanism will allow the objectives set by the agreement to be revised upwards every five years. the text also provides for a strengthened transparency and accountability framework. finally, the agreement includes a solidarity clause requiring industrialised countries to finance aid to poor countries vulnerable to rising temperatures. the european parliament's approval of the paris agreement opens the way for the european union to ratify the text. this act demonstrates europe's leading role in the fight against climate change and its unwavering commitment to the clean energy transition.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which constitutes the european parliament's ratification of the paris agreement concluded at the end of cop21 in december 2015. the agreement is the first universal and legally binding global climate agreement in terms of environmental protection and reducing greenhouse gas emissions. this ratification must be followed by concrete and effective implementation involving and involving all public and private actors. the european union must continue to be a central international actor and a leader in the fight against climate change. this agreement is a step in the european union's action, not an end in itself.
in writing. ‒ the paris agreement, concluded in december 2015 at cop 21, is a historic agreement. it sets binding standards to stop the ravages of climate change, as illustrated by the increase in the number of people displaced by climate change. with this ratification, the european union, through the voice of its parliament, is living up to this historic requirement. by limiting the rise in temperature to less than 1.5°c and the emission of greenhouse gases, this agreement commits the international community to the future, even if the means of this transition to a new model of development that is more sustainable and decarbonised still have to be implemented in order to combat climate warming effectively. this should not be the latest good intention, but a new stage in an ambitious european strategy which requires a substantial european budget with its own resources to achieve the ecological and economic transition and to make europe's commitments a reality.

in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of this report. at a time when the emphasis is on creating as many new criminal law instruments as possible to combat terrorism and other forms of crime, it is important to remember that the basis of a union based on the rule of law is to guarantee respect for the fundamental rights of the defence of those accused or suspected by our criminal justice systems.
in writing. ‒ while the commission's proposal would only guarantee the right to 'provisional' legal aid, the libe committee suggested that the scope of the proposed directive be extended to include the right to 'ordinary' legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and for persons whose surrender is sought in proceedings relating to the execution of a european arrest warrant. member states should ensure in particular that: ordinary legal aid is provided at all stages of criminal proceedings; systems are in place to ensure the quality and independence of lawyers practising as barristers, in particular an accreditation system, as well as initial and continuing vocational training; the suspect, the accused person or the person whose surrender is sought has the right to request the replacement of the lawyer of his own choice assigned to him. this is a new step in the development of european criminal law, although it is a matter for the member states. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ judicial europe is on the move but it is moving slowly. yet this is one of the areas where europe can demonstrate its added value to its citizens. free movement within the union and the division of judicial powers at national level is a boon for offenders. it is obvious that something must be done about it. trust in the respective legal systems is based on trust in the member states' legal aid systems. that is why i voted for this resolution.
in writing. according to this text, suspects and persons prosecuted in criminal proceedings should have an effective remedy if their rights were to be infringed. however, i am against this legal aid which is a new stage in the development of european criminal law, whereas it is a matter for the member states.
in writing. ‒ i opposed this report by the libe committee, which takes the european commission's ambition to develop a genuine european criminal law to the detriment of national law even further. the report advocates the establishment of a right to 'ordinary' legal aid for persons prosecuted in criminal proceedings, as well as for persons whose surrender is sought in proceedings relating to the execution of a european arrest warrant. the approach of the europeanists is perverse, since it is to attack the sovereignty of the member states from the point of view of individual rights. the european nations, if this directive is followed, would now be confined to a role of verification: to ensure that ordinary legal aid is provided at all stages of the criminal proceedings; the commission has also proposed that the court of justice should be consulted on the interpretation of the provisions of the treaty. but the member states are already states of law and most of them have already been ensuring such practices at national level, in france since 1841! a draft directive which therefore has no usefulness other than its ideological scope.
in writing. ‒ this text is a new step in the development of european criminal law, although this is a matter for the member states. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ this report advocates extending the scope of the european commission's proposal for a directive to include the right to ordinary legal aid for individuals prosecuted in criminal proceedings. the member states would thus be obliged to provide such legal aid at all stages of the criminal proceedings and to guarantee the quality and independence of lawyers hired on their own initiative. the law also grants suspects the right to request, at one sitting, the replacement of the lawyer appointed for them and the right to appeal against a decision refusing such legal aid. i voted against this report, which is a new step in the development of european criminal law, whereas this is a matter for the exclusive competence of the member states.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it allows the establishment of common minimum rules on the right to legal aid for suspects, accused persons and persons whose surrender is sought. the report, with its common minimum rules, helps to strengthen the confidence of member states in the criminal justice systems of other member states. it also facilitates the mutual recognition of decisions in criminal matters. member states are encouraged to take measures to improve the quality and efficiency of legal aid services. this report requires member states to grant access to legal aid, beyond provisional legal aid, because persons whose surrender is sought are not always deprived of liberty. this will also strengthen mutual trust and make effective the right to a double defence in european arrest warrant proceedings.
in writing. ‒ this legislative report follows the european commission's proposal of november 2013 for a directive on legal aid. the aim of this text is to strengthen the rights of european citizens by establishing common minimum standards in all member states for the right to legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings. i voted in favour of this text, considering that it will ensure better protection for european citizens and strengthen mutual trust between states in the field of justice.
in writing. the adoption by a very large majority of this text on legal aid for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and for persons whose surrender is sought in european arrest warrant proceedings is an important step towards strengthening the procedural rights of european citizens. as rapporteur on this text for my political group, the epp, i have insisted that strong minimum standards for access to legal aid be guaranteed for any suspect or accused person deprived of liberty in any of the member states of the european union. this harmonization of our criminal procedures is essential to the construction of the europe of justice which i defend.
in writing. the right of access to legal aid gives any person prosecuted for a crime the possibility of obtaining legal aid, such as a lawyer or an interpreter, regardless of his or her income. this right is one of the fundamental principles enshrined in article 6 of the european convention on human rights and article 47 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. since 2009, the union has had legislation to guarantee this right of access to all its citizens throughout europe. although all member states recognise this legal instrument, there are still some differences in the quality of the aid provided. with the adoption of the revised directive, european citizens will now be able to fully benefit from this right without distinction of income, regardless of the member state in which they are at the time of their arrest.
in writing. ‒ vote against: a new stage in the development of european criminal law, although this is a matter for the member states.
in writing. i voted in favour of this text, which is part of a package proposed by the european commission to improve procedural rights and harmonise them at european level. that report shall lay down the common minimum rules under which a person accused or suspected in criminal proceedings or subject to a european arrest warrant may apply for legal aid. two tests to be carried out by the member states will enable an independent authority to decide on the right to legal aid, based on, among other criteria, the resources and situation of the person and the seriousness of the offence. i welcome the fact that the european parliament has succeeded in applying these rights to aid throughout the criminal proceedings and that a right of appeal can be exercised in the event of refusal. parliament has also made it possible to make information on this aid available, which is important because all citizens must know their procedural rights.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the strengthening of legal mechanisms in europe with the agreement by the european parliament and the council on a set of common minimum rules governing the right to legal aid. in france, this system already exists, but in other eu countries, the effective right of access to a lawyer was not always guaranteed for persons prosecuted or suspected of having insufficient resources. legal aid will now be available for suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings but will not apply to minor offences because of the excessive financial burden this would have imposed on member states. it should also be clarified that this assistance will apply to persons whose surrender is sought in the context of european arrest warrant proceedings. finally, each state will remain free to apply the criterion it considers most relevant - resource or merits - in determining whether or not legal aid can be granted.

in writing. ‒ europol has entered into a strategic cooperation agreement with the ministry of public security of china to increase efficiency in the fight against organised crime. these strategic agreements provide for exchanges of information on expertise, general reports, the results of strategic analyses, criminal investigation procedures, crime prevention methods and the provision of advice and support in specific criminal investigations. although these strategic agreements effectively exclude the exchange of personal information, i opposed this text to protect member states from a potential risk of industrial espionage by china. the fight against crime must not be at the expense of safeguarding our jobs and industries. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes that the european parliament give its consent to the conclusion by the council of the strategic cooperation agreement between europol and china. china hosts several organized crime groups and is considered an important transit country for organized crime. considering that this technical and strategic cooperation between the union and the people's republic of china will strengthen the fight against organised crime networks, i supported this report.

in writing. ‒ the report refers here to the conclusion of a strategic agreement between europol and china. strategic agreements involve exchanges of information other than personal data, while operational agreements include the latter. our group often abstains when it comes to strategic agreements, while we oppose operational agreements in order to avoid any disclosure of personal data. in this case, the agreement is certainly strategic, but it concerns a country from which we can fear certain risks, such as industrial espionage for example. therefore, i opposed the agreement.
in writing. ‒ china, with its 1.3 billion inhabitants, has several criminal organisations, which it combats by developing the fight against organised crime: measures against aid to illegal immigration, human trafficking, money laundering, counterfeiting of the euro, and corruption in sport. europol, the european intergovernmental criminal police agency, needs to work with china. this strategic agreement will allow, in particular, the exchange of expert opinions, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods, as well as training and advisory activities in the context of specific investigations. the agreement also categorically excludes the exchange of personal data. the agreement with china will facilitate and intensify the fight against organised crime and help to strengthen international police cooperation, while ensuring the protection of personal data. i therefore vote in favour of this agreement.
