in writing. ‒ when we hear the recurrent debates on china in the european parliament, it is surprising to say the least that we are being asked to ratify a police cooperation agreement with china. this strategic cooperation agreement between europol and chinese intelligence services is intended to prevent serious forms of crime. while it explicitly excludes the exchange of personal data, which i welcome, this agreement is similar to most cooperation agreements with europol and is therefore characterised by a high degree of vagueness as to the type of information that will be exchanged. what types of information on criminal investigation procedures are we talking about? what kind of strategic analysis results are we talking about? what are the agreed retention periods? what purpose? once again, it's all fuzzy. and in an agreement with a state where respect for human rights is at least a real issue, we can expect much more transparency. i am voting against this text, which was adopted by the epp and the conservative and socialist groups, with the liberals abstaining in a large majority.
madam president, the agreements on so-called economic partnerships with the african, caribbean and pacific countries arouse reluctance on the part of all governments, regardless of their political colour. in truth, they are not partnership agreements. it is an incredible machine for producing immigration, since it immediately triggers a decline in the revenues of the states concerned and, therefore, in the health, social, educational and equipment measures for these countries, and above all an invasion of our goods, which has the result of killing the local economy, increasing unemployment and pushing the rural populations to the cities - those countryside where food crops are ruined by the products of our countries' agriculture. this mechanism increases the production of monocultures, which cause damage by pollution and a mutilation of all traditional cultivation methods in these regions. finally, it is obvious that it is causing the population to move from the countryside to the city and from the city to the outside. i believe that history will judge very harshly the blindness we show at a time like this in voting for agreements of this nature and putting absolutely unbearable pressure on the governments of this area.
in writing. ‒ the european union wants to perpetuate what it sees as the advances of the cotonou agreements. these are based on three pillars (development, trade relations and political dialogue). apart from the fact that the union does not need to have any form of diplomacy, the cotonou accords were a disaster for africa. by replacing a system of gradual free trade with a paternalistic system where the northern countries agreed to pay higher customs duties to allow the accelerated development of this area, the cotonou agreements contributed with other factors such as the policy of international institutions to delay the creation of african industries protected by high customs duties, which was the objective of france with the cooperation project. instead, the gigantic african cities, particularly because of a massive rural exodus, are real centres of consumption but essentially not centres of production. finally, one can only be surprised at the lessons that the union is allowing itself to teach in this text on corruption. i therefore opposed this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution, which has been the subject of an opinion of the committee on budgets. the simultaneous expiry of the cotonou agreement and the multiannual financial framework provides an opportunity to decide on the budgetisation of the european development fund. this suggestion will help to promote the acp-eu special relationship.
in writing. ‒ by replacing a gradual free trade system with a system deemed paternalistic where the northern countries agreed to pay higher customs duties to allow for the accelerated development of this area, the cotonou agreements contributed, along with other factors, such as the policy of international institutions, to delaying the creation of african industries protected by high customs duties. the african cities, which have become gigantic as a result of a massive rural exodus, are simply centres of consumption rather than centres of production. we must work towards cooperation that is more beneficial to all parties.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this text, which is a glaring example of european blindness to the failure of its own policies. the report seeks to endorse the alleged advances made by the cotonou agreements, which have had many negative consequences for african countries. the main 'progress' of these agreements was to impose a brutal free trade regime on the acp countries, preventing them from developing or protecting their industries by means of customs duties, which could have allowed the accelerated development of this area, as france wanted with the cooperation project. this policy has led to a massive rural exodus, with large african cities becoming centres of consumption but also deserts of production. what's the outcome? 80% of the 'least developed' countries are in the acp area. at the same time, the union, which is trying to replace the member states in its diplomacy, has avoided a genuine policy of co-development which would not only enable these countries to flourish economically but also offer a future to young africans who are now being forced to leave their homes by emigration.
in writing. ‒ this report aims to extend the cotonou agreements beyond 2020. these free trade agreements have been particularly damaging to the acp area, preventing states from encouraging the emergence of local industries, given the absence of protective customs duties. direct cooperation between the member states and the acp countries is much more effective than the european union commission's interference in the internal affairs of the acp area, and it also propagates an ideology that is not well suited to african realities. for all these reasons, i vote against.
in writing. ‒ with this report, the european union wishes to maintain its relations with the acp countries (africa, caribbean and pacific) before 2020, the date on which the cotonou agreements expire. these agreements were intended to contribute to the development of the acp countries by promoting their integration into international trade, establishing a constructive dialogue with their national authorities and involving economic and associative actors in the implementation of projects. these agreements have proved to be disastrous in those countries which have been forced to adopt a gradual free trade system which prevents them from protecting their nascent industries and agriculture by means of tariff barriers. in this context, the european union no longer has any diplomatic legitimacy to establish relations with third countries, especially since this is the exclusive competence of the member states. that is why i voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ the cotonou agreement's acquis is the result of a combination of factors. it brings together a large number of states parties through development cooperation, political cooperation and economic and trade cooperation, and has a common institutional framework and a large budget: the european development fund. this partnership is based on a set of core values and principles, including respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms, democracy based on the rule of law and transparent and accountable management. i voted in favour of this report because the relevance of the cotonou agreement has not yet been demonstrated. the report emphasises several key objectives for 2030: making the new agreement a political project based on the principle of ownership and abandoning the donor-recipient mentality; strengthening political dialogue; strengthening the autonomy of local and regional governments; allow private sector financing in the development process under certain conditions; use economic partnership agreements as tools for regional development and integration.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report follows the public consultation launched by the european commission on the future of the partnership between the european union and the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states after 2020. the cotonou agreement has strengthened political ties between the two parties and developed close cooperation to combat poverty, but the results are still insufficient. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat the spread of the virus and to ensure that the virus is contained in the body. the report stresses the need to maintain the cotonou agreement by establishing a legally binding framework agreement based on three main principles: political dialogue, cooperation and trade. considering that the acp states are important political and trade partners for the european union and that it is necessary to draw the lessons of past partnerships in order to improve future relations with the acp states, i supported this report.

in writing. the cotonou agreement, which governs relations between the european union (eu) and the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) group of states, expires at the end of 2020. the situation in both the european union and the acp countries has changed over the past 20 years, due to internal developments but also to external challenges such as climate change. it is therefore important, as we approach 2020, that the framework for eu-acp relations focuses on environmental protection, migration management and the fight against inequalities within and between countries. this strategic cooperation should take into account the objectives of co-growth and co-development. to do this, we need to identify priority areas for action, such as africa's energy independence, sustainable management of natural resources or diversification and strengthening of its economic fabric.

in writing. ‒ this report aims to perpetuate what the european union considers to be the advances of the cotonou agreements. signed on 23 june 2000, they are based on three pillars: development, trade relations and political dialogue. for my part, i think that the cotonou agreements have not advanced africa. before these agreements, the countries of the north paid higher customs duties to allow for the accelerated development of the zone. a system considered 'paternalistic' by the western world. the cotonou agreements have replaced this with a gradual free trade system. the direct consequence is a huge delay in the development of african industries, an unprecedented rural exodus and the creation of ultra-concentrated megacities, which are gigantic centres of consumption, not of production. finally, the moral lessons that the eu is constantly teaching, especially on corruption, are surprising to say the least. for these various reasons, and above all to sanction these agreements which are not the success they promised, i voted against.
in writing. the cotonou agreement, adopted in 2000, will expire in 2020. it is the legally binding framework for relations between the european union and the african, caribbean and pacific (acp) countries. it now provides a reference framework, based on values and priorities shared by 107 countries. it is the largest international partnership agreement, both in terms of the number of signatories and in terms of the political, developmental, economic and trade dimensions it covers. the future of eu-acp relations is a key issue in view of the political and strategic challenges it poses in the long term. in order to adapt the partnership to new international challenges, the report calls for the preservation of the previous achievements of the cotonou agreement beyond 2020. the report also stresses the urgent need to incorporate the outcomes of the major international conferences of 2015: new sustainable development goals, new development financing framework, paris climate agreement/cop21. i am convinced that the future of the eu-acp relationship is a major issue and i am voting in favour of this text.

in writing. ‒ the cotonou agreement, which governs relations between the states of europe, africa, the caribbean and the pacific - 107 countries! - is the most extensive international cooperation agreement in existence. signed in 2000, it expires in 2020. while the european commission is reflecting on the future of this eu-acp partnership, it was important that the european parliament set its conditions for the renewal of a possible cotonou ii agreement. i personally believe that it is essential that eu-acp relations remain balanced and that their commercial aspect does not take precedence over the pillars of political cooperation and development aid. this aspiration is shared by the neuser report, which sets strict conditions (and currently not respected by the commission) for the negotiation of eu-africa trade agreements. the report also recalls that the cotonou partnership is primarily intended to promote common values (democracy, the rule of law) and shared objectives (the un sustainable development goals, cop 21), without obscuring the indispensable political dialogue symbolised by the joint parliamentary assembly, particularly on human rights. conversely, the european union must not skimp on development aid vis-à-vis its acp partners. i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ the eu is trying to perpetuate and justify the cotonou agreements. these are based on three pillars (development, trade relations and political dialogue). the aim here is to develop structures and to deepen procedures, such as the political dialogue of articles 8 and 96 or the new form of epas (economic partnership agreements). it should be stressed that the eu has no diplomatic competence, in any form. it should also be remembered that the cotonou agreements were a disaster for africa. by replacing a system of 'progressive' free trade with a system considered too paternalistic, where the northern countries agreed to pay higher customs duties to allow the accelerated development of this area, the cotonou agreements helped to delay the creation of 'african industries protected and perpetuated by high customs duties', which was france's objective with the 'cooperation project'. today, increasingly large african cities, a phenomenon promoted by rural exodus, have become real centres of consumption, but not yet centres of production. so i objected to this file.

member of the commission. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, the current commission, the juncker commission, is very firmly committed to respecting its obligations as set out in the treaties and in the code of conduct for commissioners. among these obligations are the independence and integrity of the members of the commission. the commission stresses two major concepts: transparency and exemplary behaviour. parliament and all citizens must be assured that the commissioners act exclusively in the interests of the european union and that the necessary transparency is guaranteed. it is therefore essential to avoid any conflict of interest. the treaties - i would like to remind you of this - lay down the obligations of independence and integrity to be respected by the members of the commission throughout their term of office. article 245 of the treaty also provides that members of the commission are to observe the duty of honesty and discretion in accepting, after leaving office, certain other duties or benefits. the code of conduct for commissioners contains provisions which give concrete expression to the obligations imposed by the treaties. it aims to prevent any risk of conflict of interest by prohibiting members of the commission from exercising any other duties during their term of office, with the exception of strictly honorary duties or political activities, of course without a mandate. the members of this commission are men and women of conviction and political commitment. the code also provides for a procedure for authorizing activities planned after the end of their mandate. these are strict rules, compared with those which apply to members of the other european institutions or those in force in the member states. i'm beginning to have a rather long political life, at least a fairly respectable one; i have held many offices - as a member of parliament, as a member of the european parliament, as a local elected official, as a minister in my own country - and i can indeed testify that the rules laid down for commissioners are rather more robust than any i have had to live with before. this code has been revised several times, each time to be more precise and rigorous. these revisions have always been aimed at strengthening these provisions. i would like to dwell briefly on the post-mandate activities which have generated a great deal of interest. according to the code of conduct, when commissioners intend to pursue a professional activity, therefore, former commissioners, within 18 months of the end of their term of office, these members or former members are obliged to inform the commission of these activities. this 18-month period is in line with european and international standards and is intended to avoid situations of conflict of interest at the end of the mandate. in this configuration, the commission consults the ad hoc ethics committee when the proposed activity is related to the portfolio and then decides on the compatibility of the proposed activity on the proposal of the chair. in practice, this means that in the 18 months since the end of the previous commission, this commission - i am speaking of the juncker commission - has consulted the ad hoc ethics committee on 40 of the 114 activities notified by the members of the previous commissions. the committee adopted five negative opinions. in the event of a negative opinion, the members concerned have always, on each occasion, preferred to withdraw their notification rather than risk receiving a negative opinion from the commission as well. i think this shows how well the ethics committee works and how strong the rules are. all the decisions adopted by the commission are publicly available - i should like to say this - through its minutes. in order to ensure greater transparency, the commission has set up a web page where each decision is reproduced with a direct link to the corresponding minutes as soon as they have been adopted. criticisms of laxity or lack of transparency are therefore unfounded. we are facing debates which are serious enough and which public opinion considers important enough not to add to them or to imagine other types of failure. moreover, no rule, even the strictest, can substitute for the individual responsibility of the members of the commission. if we consider - and you mentioned two communications, which i have in fact grouped together - the recent cases of former commission president barroso and former vice-president kroes, no extension of the obligations imposed by the code of conduct could have prevented their choice of professional development. there may be some misunderstanding about the individual responsibility of some. the declarations of interests of the commissioners are the responsibility of each individual. the statement must be accurate and complete in order to allow for effective consideration of the risks of conflict of interest, and again it must be precise, up-to-date and to the point. i would like to conclude by saying that the president is following the implementation of the code of conduct closely and personally and considers that at this stage no change in the code would have prevented the cases which are now the subject of particular attention by parliament and public opinion, which does not, of course, prevent discussion and the formulation of some of the assessments which the president has also had the opportunity to make known.

president-in-office of the council. – mr president, the author of the question rightly reminds us that this proposal has been on the table for quite some time, for three years exactly. i remember when it was placed under the leadership of madam reding. it is no surprise that this has been on the table for some time, given the sensitivity of this proposal, because in fact the regulation deals with many complex issues which lie at the heart of the criminal law systems of the member states. let me update you on the state of play of our work. after very intensive and constructive work, we have now reached a point where the member states agree on most of the provisions in the draft regulation, and it looks possible that negotiations in council can be concluded in the near future. the presidency is treating the discussions with the highest priority with the objective of closing the file by the end of the year. in this context, we are ready to work – let me underscore this –very closely with parliament. let me briefly mention one issue that has been raised in earlier contacts with parliament and which is very important for all of us, namely the need to ensure that the office is both independent and efficient. let me explain in more detail: the current structure of the office builds on the idea that the college member of a given member state will be in charge of investigations and prosecutions in his or her member state of origin, and will supervise them. this organisation has been chosen mainly for practical reasons, in particular with a view to ensuring the efficiency of the office. the legal systems and cultures of the member states still vary to a considerable degree, and it is clear that only a prosecutor with his or her background in a given legal system will be able to know exactly what actions are most appropriate and efficient in that given state. i can assure you that the council wishes to ensure that there is no ambiguity on these issues. the council remains convinced that the structure proposed in the current text fully ensures the independence of each european prosecutor and of the office as such. i also believe that the current council text is, by and large, in line with the main wishes and expectations of parliament. a detailed picture of the state of play on the draft european public prosecutor’s office (eppo) regulation, containing all the provisions of the regulation that ministers have preliminarily agreed upon, is freely accessible. this draft should be very close to final outcome. however the documents still do not include a number of provisions: on judicial review, cooperation between the eppo and eurojust and relations with third countries. these provisions will be included in a new consolidated version, which will hopefully be completed in the coming weeks. the main task of the presidency is now to ensure that outstanding reservations are resolved and that the few remaining gaps in the text are filled. in other words, the council is relatively close to an agreement on the full text. as noted in your question, it is also clear that the eppo regulation must be made coherent with the eurojust regulation and with the directive on the protection of the union’s financial interests or ‘pif directive’. the council adopted its general approach on the eurojust regulation in march last year and is ready to start negotiations with parliament at any time. certain provisions need to be coordinated with the eppo regulation, but we do not foresee major difficulties. the council agrees with the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe) that it would be useful to ensure that the pif directive is adopted before or at least around the time of adoption of the regulation. the negotiations on the pif directive have been on hold since last year, but i am confident that the council and parliament will find a compromise solution in the near future. as regards the financial analysis, the commission is studying this important but complex issue, and it is likely that the commissioner is better placed to reply to this question. from the point of view of the council, i would like to underline that it is generally agreed that eurojust must continue to have sufficient resources to fulfil its tasks in an efficient manner. the eppo regulation should, for this reason, a priori not have any significant impact on the eurojust budget. finally, the exact nature of the operational, organisational and administrative links between the eppo and eurojust is one of the last issues which are still under discussion in the council. the council is working on a model according to which the eppo may rely on the support and resources of the administration of eurojust, and where eurojust will provide certain services to the eppo. whether there is a need to define these services, or if this could be left to the two bodies, is still under discussion. it is thus still too early to give a detailed account of the links between the eppo and eurojust. we will come back to you with a more precise reply in the coming months. let me however assure you that our aim is to ensure that the bodies complement each other, and that there is no duplication of work. the creation of the eppo must not lead to any weakening of eurojust.
member of the commission. – mr president, honourable members, as we all know, we face some crucial challenges in europe in the area of security, but also regarding our prosperity. we have a problem because crime does not know borders, as mr voss said before. this goes for big scope crime against eu money, including big cross—border vat fraud. crime is harming our economies and decreasing taxpayers’ trust. it is our duty to fight against this crime, which can be done only by joining forces. i am speaking about a pan-european issue that cannot be resolved by national authorities only. as you may know, eurojust and olaf are not equipped to lead criminal investigations and prosecutions, and national authorities are facing limits in addressing fraud cases, either for political or resources reasons. that is why i see the european public prosecutor as a specialised body dealing with financial crime in the eu, having the necessary competence to investigate and prosecute. we need a european public prosecutor to deal with the alleged fraud cases we all read about in some cohesion countries, but we also need it to tackle the big vat fraud cases, especially in the cross-border context – our very conservative estimation is around eur 50 billion in revenues lost every year due to vat fraud, and the real figure is probably much higher. we need an effective answer to these negative impacts on the eu budget, but also on national budgets. so, where are we on this? i know, replying to questions one and two, we are – as you also heard from the presidency – in the final stages of our negotiations, and the commission fully supports the efforts of the slovak presidency to achieve a political deal on this by the end of this year. we are hopeful that the council will be able to finalise the remaining chapters of the proposal for a regulation on the establishment of the eppo, in particular the provisions on the judicial control of the office and on relations with third countries and international organisations, with non-participating member states and relations with eurojust, in october. provisions with respect to staff matters relating to the setting—up of the eppo would also need to be added. at the justice and home affairs council on 14 october, the slovak presidency will present a complete consolidated text to seek the conceptual support of the council on the revised provisions. from the perspective of the commission, the current council text should still be improved on several points. two should be highlighted in particular at this stage. the first one relates to competence. the priority competence of the eppo on cases of fraud affecting the union’s financial interests demands that the eppo have access to information on all pif cases. the eppo needs to have competence to fight at least serious cross-border vat fraud. also, the rules on ancillary competence must not lead to a restriction of the eppo’s core competence in the pif area. the second point is on efficiency, because the efficiency of the eppo requires a flexible mechanism to redistribute work at central level between the european prosecutors, even if the general principle that european prosecutors supervise cases being handled in their respective member states is maintained. as already stated on numerous previous occasions, the eppo can only be launched with confidence if we streamline the rules concerning its competence, and strengthen the guarantees of independence, as well as the provisions on procedural rights. in addition, given that its material competence is defined by reference to the pif directive, finalising the directive is essential for setting up the eppo. now let me reply to questions three and four. the eppo, as a specialised body for financial crime, is to be seen as part of our overall structure in the european union to combat crime effectively. since eurojust will no longer work on financial crimes against the eu budget (so-called ‘pif cases’), it will be able to focus on the fight against terrorist threats or other crimes such as trafficking, drugs, and in our cooperation with neighbouring countries. in accordance with article 31 of the financial regulation, the commission’s services undertook an analysis of the financial impact of the changed eppo structure and competence following the council compromises. this paper, with initial working estimates, will be shared with you in parallel with ministers, at the justice and home affairs council on 14 october. this estimate also takes into account the synergies and the future relationship between the eppo and eurojust. the council model chosen for the eppo, based on governance by a college, will create the need for new posts in the eppo’s central office, but as a result of the eppo’s shared, rather than exclusive, competence it will overall lead to a reduction of posts at central level when compared to the original commission proposal. this will have an impact on costs. the cost implications of european delegated prosecutors (so-called edps) are still under discussion. it depends on how many edps will be appointed by the member states. as regards benefits, the commission expects that the inclusion of vat fraud into the eppo’s competence will bring considerable benefits in comparison to today’s situation where especially large intra-community vat fraud cases often remain undetected or are not followed up effectively. as regards the involvement of national parliaments, the council supports the approach proposed by the commission whereby the european chief prosecutor or one of the deputies may be requested to appear before national parliaments to give account of the general activities of the eppo. such appearances should be without prejudice to the eppo’s obligation of discretion and confidentiality as regards individual cases and personal data. axel voss raised a lot of other questions here, and i can confirm what you also heard from the minister that we are ready to come back between october and december, when we will go through a decisive period for the final version of eppo and reply to all your questions, both regarding the text and regarding the relation between the eppo, eurojust and olaf, and all the other practical matters, especially the financial conditions. i only wanted to declare here today that we are working on the cost—benefit conditions for the eppo, with full regard and full respect to the value of money, which means that we need to do the right thing, to do it in the right way, and to do it for the least possible money. so this is our aim, and that is also why we are working now on a very precise financial analysis. as for eurojust, i am not someone who would like to establish a new body for combating serious crime in europe by devastating the other one. i see the clear picture of combating crime in europe, standing on three very strong legs: one is olaf, which has to continue its work; the second is eurojust, which should focus more on crimes other than financial crime; and the third is the eppo, with full prosecuting competence. i believe that for the near future, from 2019 we will be able to do this reorganisation so that we will be able at european level to address all of the serious crime which the member states cannot investigate and prosecute efficiently. it is all about this. we are not replacing here the prosecution at national level; we are setting up a layer above it so that we are jointly more successful. finally, let me thank madam viviane reding, who is the mother of the proposal, for giving me the chance to continue what she started. i can only declare here that i will try to be a good stepmother to this proposal and i will do my best to push it to a successful result.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, 40 years ago the idea of creating a european public prosecutor's office was born. 40 years later, and since 2013, a legislative proposal has been on the table. today, after three years of negotiations between the states and the council, what is left in the end? three or four points. firstly, we wanted a european prosecutor's office with jurisdiction for major crossborder crime, transnational crime, transnational terrorism cases, because if criminals and crimes have no borders, our investigations and criminal prosecutions should have none either. it is a popular saying that the gendarmes should have at least the same weapons as the thieves. what's left? firstly, a european public prosecutor's office which will only be competent to protect the financial interests of the union. it is true that in the present context, with the increase in large-scale organized crime and criminal networks, it was time to limit the powers of such a prosecutor's office. secondly, a european public prosecutor's office, which is moreover limited within this very competence to combat fraud against the financial interests of the union, since the council has introduced limiting thresholds. thus, in the case of co-financing, if the union does not contribute more than 50% of the amount invested, the public prosecutor's office will not be competent. but everyone knows, and especially the european institutions, that the union usually finances projects at less than 50%. thirdly, a european public prosecutor's office has no jurisdiction when fraud is linked to another form of crime, such as trafficking or money laundering. fourthly, a european public prosecutor's office with no jurisdiction over vat fraud. madam commissioner, you have recalled the principle of this and the estimated loss of revenue that this represents, since the council refuses to incorporate vat into the directive on the protection of the union's financial interests. this is crossborder fraud par excellence. secondly, and this is obvious, we want an independent european prosecutor's office which can conduct its investigations and inquiries in full independence from national interests. what's left there, too? a european prosecutor's office with a decentralised structure, a complex organisation linked by the omnipresence of the national link, a prosecutor's office which will not have jurisdiction as a last resort, since in the event of conflicts of jurisdiction between a national authority and the prosecutor's office, it is the national authority which will decide as a last resort. the result of the negotiations in the council, commissioner, is simply worrying. the council has peeled away the original proposal and emptied it of its meaning, that of a european prosecutor's office which is strong, ambitious, efficient and, above all, independent. many of us in this house are wondering about the added value of this floor. the chapters on skills should definitely be reopened. in conclusion, please note that parliament's approval of the prosecution is not a given. yes, we are in favour of the establishment of a european prosecutor's office, but not at any price.

on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, madam commissioner, i thank you for having already, in your opening statement, cleared up many of the points of concern to this parliament. i would also like to thank my colleague, theodor stolojan, who is leading our working party with great efficiency and intelligence. the accounting standards developed in the wake of the financial crisis - as you recalled - were originally intended for banks, as the financial crisis revealed the need to strengthen the soundness of the global financial system, including through these accounting standards. it is in this spirit, and in line with the conclusions of the g20 in london in april 2009, that accounting regulators have been working on the replacement of ias 39. this reflection led to the publication by the iasb in july 2014 of the final version of ifrs 9, which aims to ensure greater transparency on credit risk in financial statements by adopting an approach to asset impairment that should be more responsive to changes in the credit cycle. ifrs 9 is designed to apply first to banking institutions and therefore raises two questions: first, in the absence of a real impact assessment, there are concerns about the potential effects of the application of this standard on investment, as it could introduce volatility in the accounts unrelated to the economic reality of a long-term lender. in a certain sense, we wish to refer here to the concept of 'public good' as developed by maystadt in his report. is not long-term investment the public good par excellence, especially in these troubled times? secondly, we are concerned - as you have mentioned - about the impact of this standard on the banking and insurance sector, and we obviously want to continue our work and collaboration in this area in good faith with efrag and its new president.

mr president, the main points of migration policy still need to be addressed. the agreement with turkey is effective, but it only concerns syrian refugees. in the meantime, the flow from africa through libya - as you know, mr president - has picked up again. now, these migrants are mostly from west africa, which is generally at peace, and not from war-torn countries like somalia or sudan, so controlling the migration flows requires that the problem be dealt with from the top down at the european level. this begins with a common foreign policy: a policy of partnership with the countries of origin and transit, if they are at peace, and a policy of restoring peace, if they are at civil war. secondly, we need a european border guard corps. it is beginning to take shape, but it must be a permanent body and not just partial reinforcements in times of acute crisis. then it was time to imagine a new kind of european solidarity to help the member states that were geographically most exposed. authoritarian relocation is definitely not working! but there can be other forms of solidarity - real solidarity, as the president of the commission says - in the form, for example, of a contribution of personnel, material or money to the implementation of asylum policy. we can then begin to devise a common policy for economic migrants, based on quotas for each country of origin and each country of destination. all the legal tools are now available. will the 27 have the political will to use it? answer is "blue cardboard". thank you for this question, which is very relevant. my personal position on the problem of development aid is that we are wasting a considerable amount of that aid. the european budget allocates some €9 billion to development cooperation each year, and this is added to by almost ten times the sum of the national aid allocated to development cooperation by the 28 countries. i think it is time to coordinate better and to concentrate this aid on those countries which need it most, with political conditions attached to it; we do not dare to provide for them in treaties, and when, by chance, we write them down, we do not dare to apply them.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction was established in 1980. all the member states of the european union are signatories to this convention. this private international law legislation imposes a uniform legal basis for the abduction of a child by one of the parents in the event of a bi-national separation. sometimes a parent abducts a child and is given legal custody in their home state. the other parent is then obliged to comply with this decision because of a lack of legal uniformity between the two states of which the parents are nationals. such situations must not happen again. we must do everything possible to ensure that children's rights are applied in the same way all over the world. i voted in favour of peru's accession to the hague convention.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision authorising austria and romania to accept, in the interest of the european union, the accession of peru to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. by establishing the primacy of the jurisdiction and laws of the state in which the child resides, the convention plays a key role in resolving issues surrounding child custody in the event of the separation of binational couples. the convention is an indispensable tool for the international protection of children and has also allowed the development of an accelerated procedure for the return of child abductees. however, for the convention to be applied, it is necessary that the accession of a state is accepted by the other states parties to the convention. although peru joined in 2001, austria and romania have not yet accepted this accession. in order to protect children linked to the peruvian community from abduction, we call on the council to adopt as soon as possible a decision authorising austria and romania to accept peru's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction.
in writing. every year, several thousand children are abducted by one of their parents. in the absence of cooperation between the child's state of origin and the state of residence, some cases cannot be resolved. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a legal instrument which recognises the jurisdiction of the courts of the state where the child resides. a dialogue can thus be established between the states parties to this convention to facilitate the return of the child who has been abducted. the european union supports the accession of third states to the 1980 convention so that its member states can build on a common legal framework to deal with international child abduction. in addition to the general objective of developing judicial cooperation, this regulation pursues the general objective of protecting the rights of the child. so the accession of peru to the convention is good news.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states to settle cases of international child abduction. it has been ratified by all eu member states. in many cases, these problems arise when a couple separates. if the mother and father are from different states, there is a temptation to exploit the lack of cooperation between the states in order to secure custody of the child. it is common for the courts in both states concerned to declare that they have jurisdiction and to award custody of the child to the parent who is a national of their state. the purpose of the convention is to resolve such situations at the international level by establishing that the competent courts and the applicable laws are those of the child's state of residence. the convention also introduces a system to ensure the immediate return of abducted children. i am in favour of the adoption of this text because kazakhstan has chosen to apply for this accession. i therefore vote in favour of the text.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980, ratified by all the member states of the european union, establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states to settle cases of international child abduction. in most cases, these abductions are linked to the divorce of the parents, in an attempt to exploit the lack of cooperation between states in obtaining custody of their child. this convention stipulates that the competent courts and the applicable laws are those of the child's state of residence. the purpose of this text is to give the european parliament's opinion on the entry into force of the convention between south korea and the union, which now has exclusive external competence in this area. although i disagree with the loss of sovereignty of the member states, which leave it to the union to adopt this type of agreement for them, i voted in favour of this text. on the one hand, this convention promotes the return of children to their homes, and on the other hand, the accession of south korea is welcome news.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a council decision authorising certain member states to accept, in the interest of the european union, the accession of the republic of korea to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction. by establishing the primacy of the jurisdiction and laws of the state in which the child resides, the convention plays a key role in resolving issues surrounding child custody in the event of the separation of binational couples. however, for the convention to be applied, it is necessary that the accession of a state is accepted by the other states parties to the convention. although the republic of korea acceded in 2013, all eu member states, with the exception of the czech republic, ireland and lithuania, have still not accepted this accession. in order to protect children linked to the korean community from abduction, we call on the council to adopt as soon as possible a decision authorising those member states of the union which have not yet done so to accept the accession of the republic of korea to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction.
in writing. every year, several thousand children are abducted by one of their parents. in the absence of cooperation between the child's state of origin and the state of residence, some cases cannot be resolved. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a legal instrument which recognises the jurisdiction of the courts of the state where the child resides. a dialogue can thus be established between the states parties to this convention to facilitate the return of the child who has been abducted. the european union supports the accession of third states to the 1980 convention so that its member states can build on a common legal framework to deal with international child abduction. in addition to the general objective of developing judicial cooperation, this regulation pursues the general objective of protecting the rights of the child. the accession of south korea to the convention is therefore good news.

in writing. ‒ the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction establishes a system of cooperation between contracting states to settle cases of international child abduction. it has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention's main purpose is to resolve childcare situations at international level by establishing that the competent courts and the applicable laws are those of the child's state of residence. the convention also introduces a system to ensure the immediate return of abducted children. the eu now has exclusive external competence in this area as confirmed by the court of justice in its opinion 1/13. after ratification, the convention will enter into force between these three countries and the european union as a whole. i therefore support the adoption of this text because these countries have chosen to apply for membership.

in writing. ‒ in september, the us construction equipment manufacturer caterpillar announced its intention to close its only belgian plant in gosselies, resulting in the loss of 2 200 jobs in the already disaster-stricken charleroi area. alstom has announced the closure of its belfort site, which specialises in the construction of railway equipment. the company explained its decision by the decline in orders from sncf, which preferred bombardier as the supplier for the ters. the french government has announced a solution to maintain employment in belfort by ordering new tgv trains to run on the intercity network. the majority groups took advantage of the media coverage of these cases to revive the idea of a european industrial policy, "without protectionism". the proposals in the resolution promote free trade and demand reciprocity and the opening up of public procurement by other powers. no community preference is in sight for the railway, which is a sovereign industry. we want green growth but without massive investment, which is only possible through monetary creation for the benefit of the real economy. social europe is a mirage that even its promoters no longer believe in. i therefore voted against the joint motion.

in writing. ‒ the successive decisions by the management of alstom and caterpillar to close sites and cut jobs in france and belgium are emblematic of the crisis facing european industry. in addition to the specificities of each country, the european industry is under pressure from a triple dumping: social, fiscal and environmental. many actors benefit from europe's ideological attitude, which imposes on itself a liberalism that no other great power respects. the issue is our public procurement open to international competition without limitation. the commission is prepared to grant china market economy status, removing even more protection from its exports and, ultimately, from its social dumping. finally, as we vote this week on the ratification of the paris agreement, it should also be remembered that if european industry is at a disadvantage vis-à-vis its asian competitors, it is also because it is trying to comply with environmental legislation that is absolutely crucial for the energy transition. the 'carbon adjustment at borders' mechanism is therefore urgently needed. i voted for this resolution which recalls these ambitions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the reindustrialisation of europe in the light of the recent caterpillar and alstom cases. at european level, the challenge is above all the requirement of reciprocity in the opening up of public procurement, which our businesses need. in addition to its social and environmental constraints, europe is opening up its public procurement markets to subsidised foreign companies. other countries close their markets or impose conditions on local production. we therefore call for reciprocity in market access, the establishment of a border adjustment mechanism and anti-dumping measures of the same type as those we have obtained against china in respect of steel.
in writing. ‒ on 2 september 2016, the us construction equipment manufacturer caterpillar announced its intention to close its only belgian plant in gosselies, resulting in the loss of 2,200 jobs (6,000 if subcontractors are included) in the already disaster-stricken charleroi area. the company alstom announced on 12 september the closure of its belfort site, which specialises in the construction of railway equipment. the company explained its decision by the decline in orders from sncf, which preferred bombardier as the supplier for the ters. on 4 october, the french government announced a solution to maintain employment in belfort by ordering new tgv trains to run on the intercity network. the majority groups want to take advantage of the media coverage of these cases to revive the idea of a european industrial policy, 'without protectionism'. their proposals are incoherent and based on the absurd idea that it would be a good thing to transfer industrial policy to the commission as part of ever deeper integration. i believe that only sovereign and democratic states are capable of defining an effective industrial policy which respects the interests of their people and the environment. i therefore vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ in view of the difficulties faced by european companies, such as recently caterpillar or alstom, establishing a european reindustrialisation policy is a priority. it is in this spirit that i voted for this text. too often, when large firms in difficulty are 'saved', they are the subject of often artificial recovery plans. the case of alstom in france is a case in point. the question must therefore be considered more globally: how can we tackle the structural challenges that are currently holding back the economic growth of our continent? global competition is fierce, and no growth will be possible without trade defence and the promotion of harmonised rules in globalisation. today, europe remains open to foreign players. this openness will only continue to be beneficial if, in return, we ensure that we obtain the same development opportunities beyond our borders. but i am saying this clearly: until certain national governments, like the socialist executive in france, become aware of the need to reduce the administrative burden, the social and employer burdens on our companies, and to put in place a clear strategy for foreign trade, no industrial policy worthy of the name will be effective in france and in europe.
in writing. ‒ today, in response to the announcements of the closure of caterpillar's plants in belgium and alstom's in france, the european parliament adopted, on the initiative of the socialist and democratic group, a resolution calling for a genuine re-industrialisation strategy for europe. i voted in favour of this resolution, which contains a number of concrete elements to revive european industry in the face of unfair foreign competition, to defend jobs better and finally to call for a reorientation of the austerity policies that undermine public investment. the resolution also sends a strong message to punish multinationals, such as caterpillar, which favour blind financial profitability at the expense of an industrial approach. the european parliament, for example, thanks to the commitment of the socialists, has voted in favour of sanctions for companies that practice redundancies. i also welcome the fact that the resolution calls for the florange law, adopted in france, to be transposed at european level, to oblige multinationals to look for a buyer in advance in the event of the closure of an industrial site. the commission must now make proposals to the european parliament to revitalize the european industrial fabric which is a vital pillar of our economy.
in writing. ‒ i supported the european parliament resolution, initiated by the socialists and democrats, which stresses the urgent need to define a european policy for reindustrialisation. the announced redundancies at caterpillar and alstom demonstrate the pressures on european industry, due to unfair global competition and unacceptable financial practices. the resolution calls on the commission to adjust the union's trade policy to combat anti-competitive practices. it also calls for a redefinition of competition law rules, in particular to ensure that relevant markets are defined at global level. furthermore, the resolution urges contracting authorities to base their decisions on the award of public contracts on the principle of the most economically advantageous tender. in particular, it stresses the need for effective social dialogue in the event of restructuring and the application of strict rules to combat redundancies without real economic grounds. finally, the more efficient use of european funds, the intensification and rationalisation of research and development efforts, the targeting of the regions most affected by deindustrialisation and the consideration of training, health and working conditions are given priority.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution which recalls the urgency and need for the european union to adopt a policy of reindustrialisation, particularly in the light of the closure of caterpillar in belgium and alstom in france. europe needs a forward-looking industrial strategy to improve the conditions under which businesses operate, to make better use of existing european financial instruments and, above all, to protect workers. european industry needs a stable social and fiscal environment that will be conducive to investment and thus to competitiveness. the european reindustrialisation strategy must be accompanied by a trade policy with modernised trade defence instruments that are more efficient, faster and more accessible, especially to smes. the european union must be the guarantor of fair competition for our industries. i supported this resolution because it also recalls the importance of sustained social dialogue based on mutual trust in order to find consensual solutions and to develop common perspectives in the management of restructuring processes. europe must support european workers while being a driving force for reindustrialisation.
in writing. ‒ the sudden announcement of the closure of alstom's plants in france and caterpillar's in belgium, which were disastrous for the employees of these plants and the territories, led the european parliament to react. i commend the work of my colleagues marie arena and edouard martin on this initiative. with this vote we reaffirm our desire to save industries and jobs in the european union by implementing the principle of sanctions against companies that practice redundancies on the market with the reimbursement of public aid. we also call for the adoption at european level of a 'florange law', to oblige multinationals that abandon sites to look for a buyer. we propose a 'carbon adjustment at the border' to combat unfair competition, particularly from countries with high carbon production facilities. we call for the revival of public investment in europe and the exit from austerity policies. this new european industrial policy must also be accompanied by social and fiscal harmonization between member states to avoid any dumping situation.

in writing. this report is a clear signal to the european commission and to consumers! chemicals in materials intended to come into contact with food, such as packaging, cookware, dishware, etc., can endanger human health or significantly alter the composition of products consumed, and it is essential that the european commission address this issue. it is important to harmonise at european level the different measures taken by the member states, but also to reflect on the gaps in the existing legislation. we must work towards better legislation on this matter, legislation which aims to inform and protect the citizen properly. finally, i would like to raise the question of the prohibition of bisphenol a (bpa) in all materials intended to come into contact with food. bpa is a chemical that is endocrine disrupting and toxic to the reproductive organs. it is found in many everyday products. it is important that this ban be made at european level in order to protect all european citizens!
in writing. regulation 1935/2004 of 27 october 2004 covers all materials coming into contact with food at all stages of the production and consumption chain: containers, packaging, cutlery, etc. it limits the alteration of the composition, taste or texture of food. in its first annex, the regulation lists 17 materials which may be the subject of specific european or national regulations. at present, only four of them are subject to european regulation. the first objective of the draft report is therefore to harmonise european regulations for all these materials. the draft report also aims to take account of the following elements in the above regulation: interference with regulation 1907/2006 on the registration, evaluation and authorisation of chemical substances; interactions between and the reaction introduction of complementary substances. other elements are positive, such as the protection of pregnant women or technical measures on bisphenol. for all these reasons, i supported this far-sighted text on the action of the commission and the european food safety authority.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report promoting accounting standards that ensure financial stability, sustainable growth and long-term investment. a thorough reform of the process of developing and approving accounting standards is fundamental to ensuring transparency and accountability.
in writing. ‒ ifrs 9 applies to financial instruments and is intended to address the difficulties of ias 39 (international accounting standards), which is the current standard. the big change is mainly due to the concept of fair value , which allows the assets and liabilities of large enterprises to be valued at their market value or, failing that, at their value calculated by the discounted sum of the expected income streams from their use. the resolution drafted by the econ committee calls on european and international financial regulators to produce studies on the impact of ifrs 9 standards on the banking, financial and insurance sectors. the proposal raises concerns about the lag between the entry into force dates of ifrs 9 and the new accounting standards for insurance products, ifrs 17. this could lead to serious inconsistencies for companies using these two types of products. i voted in favour of this essentially technical proposal, which follows the very low feedback the european parliament receives from regulators and the european commission on requests for impact assessments of ifrs 9.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe that ifrs 9 is one of the necessary responses of the iasb to the financial crisis.
in writing. ‒ the international accounting standards board (iasb) aims to develop a set of accounting standards that are applicable worldwide, and thus to create a common language for financial reporting worldwide. these standards are called international financial reporting standards (ifrs). since 2005, the ias regulation requires eu listed companies to prepare their consolidated financial statements in accordance with these standards. i support this technical resolution proposal, which mainly calls on international financial and banking regulators to make available studies on the impact of ifrs9 accounting standards (for financial products) on the banking, financial and insurance sectors.
in writing. ‒ since 2005, the ias regulation requires eu listed companies to prepare their consolidated financial statements in accordance with these standards. ifrs 9 is the standard that applies to financial instruments and is intended to address the difficulties of ias 39 (international accounting standards), which is the current standard. ifrs9 therefore introduces changes in the methods for calculating 'fair value', but there is very little impact analysis of these new standards. the resolution here calls on financial regulators to produce studies on the impact of ifrs9 standards on the banking, financial and insurance sectors. in addition, the proposal addresses concerns about the delay in the entry into force of ifrs9 and the new insurance product standards (ifrs17). it is therefore a very technical issue, following the limited feedback received from regulators and the european commission on the impact assessment requests. so i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ in july 2014, the international accounting standards board (iasb) published the final version of ifrs 9 - financial instruments. ifrs are international financial reporting standards designed to standardise the presentation of accounting data exchanged internationally. they are thus intended to enable investors to determine the financial position of a company. this new standard replaces ias 39 - financial instruments: accounting and measurement, with the aim of avoiding further financial crises such as the one in 2008. the report makes some criticisms about the complexity of the new standard and the lag between the entry into force of ifrs 9 and the future standard on insurance contracts (ifrs 17). i am afraid that these new financial standards, which are based on the anglo-saxon accounting model and are drawn up without democratic control, will not change the harmful financialisation of the economy. to think that crises depend on an accounting standard is the height of ridicule. i shall abstain on this text, however, because i am uncomfortable with some of the additional information requirements which will now be imposed on banks.

in writing. ‒ the international accounting standards board (iasb) aims to develop a set of accounting standards that are applicable worldwide, and thus create a common language for financial reporting worldwide. since 2005, the ias regulation requires eu listed companies to prepare their consolidated financial statements in accordance with these standards. ifrs 9 applies to financial instruments and is intended to address the challenges of ias 39, which is the current standard. the big change is mainly due to the concept of 'fair value', which allows the assets and liabilities of large enterprises to be valued at their market value or, failing that, at their value calculated by the discounted sum of the revenue streams expected from their use. this accounting standard is in contrast to the 'historic cost' valuation standard, which values assets and liabilities at the date of purchase on the markets. but this 'fair value' has also been blamed for a large part of the 2007 crisis, because of its very powerful procyclical impact on the banking and financial system. i voted for this essentially technical proposal.

in writing. by ratifying the paris climate agreement, the first ever universal and legally binding global climate agreement, the european union and its member states have sent a strong signal just weeks before the opening of cop22 in marrakech. this was all the more necessary as the eu had to have ratified the agreement in order to be able to participate in the first decisions as a stakeholder. the eu must seize this opportunity to continue its leadership in the global fight against climate change. this implies a more ambitious strategy, in the medium and long term, to reach the zero emission target by 2050. the union should further promote green finance and set stricter limits on emissions from the international civil aviation and maritime transport sectors. the european union must also continue its efforts within itself and with partners in third countries on the creation of financial transaction taxes, part of whose resources could support the adaptation of developing countries to climate change.

in writing. ‒ this resolution affirms that the paris agreement is 'ambitious, balanced, fair and legally binding', while acknowledging that most of its provisions are non-binding and that the historical challenges that needed to be addressed were largely missed. the resolution also acknowledges that the sum of 'nationally determined contributions' at global level 'does not even come close to the objective' of limiting global warming to a maximum of 2°c, and that this limit, which is unattainable in the state, 'does not guarantee that serious impacts on the climate will be avoided'. it would almost be laughable if the stakes weren't so high. the text also makes the 'carbon market' the alpha and omega of the fight against climate change, whereas emissions trading systems have largely proven to be ineffective and dangerous. and what about the vain demands made to 'developed countries, especially those in the union, to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions in a draconian manner, beyond current commitments', when we know that in practice they are doing exactly the opposite as we see in france with the government's persistence in maintaining the notre dame des landes project. so i chose to abstain.

in writing. food contact materials are found in the everyday lives of europeans, whether in the form of food packaging, cooking utensils or dishes. these materials have chemical properties which, if left unchecked, can sometimes be hazardous to health. only four of these products (including plastics and ceramics) are currently subject to specific safety measures at european level, with the control of the other 13 listed materials left to the discretion of the member states. in view of the risks to public health and the environment, the union needs to harmonise its controls more. in addition, the total ban on bisphenol a, which is limited to a few member states such as france or sweden, should be extended to the whole of the union.
