in writing. ‒ this initiative is in response to the report published annually by the european commission, pursuant to articles 16 and 17 of the tfeu, to present the main trends in the eu pilot procedure and in infringement procedures against member states. the 2014 report highlights in particular that the environment, transport and the internal market for services are the areas of public policy where infringements are still most numerous. the juri report also sought to build on the work of its working party on administrative law by suggesting that a regulation on administrative procedure within the institutions could contribute to a better application of union law. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the report recalls or advocates a number of points to which we are opposed, namely, in particular, the eu charter of fundamental rights as equal to the treaties, compliance with eu law as a political priority and the suggestion of greater involvement of the parliament in the correct transposition of eu legislation in each member state as well as for the candidate countries. the report stresses that 'when applying eu law, member states should avoid adding unnecessary constraints to eu law, as this leads to a misconception of eu legislative activity and fosters unjustified euroscepticism among citizens' (sic). i therefore opposed the report.
in writing. - i voted against this text. the 2014 annual report of the committee on the enforcement of eu law takes stock of the infringement procedures initiated against member states. the text we have voted recalls or advocates several concepts that we oppose: the equal value of the charter of fundamental rights of the union to the treaties, compliance with union law as a political priority, etc. the report stresses that 'when applying eu law, member states should avoid adding unnecessary constraints to eu law, as this leads to a misconception of eu legislative activity and fosters unjustified euroscepticism among citizens'. we are of course opposed to this concept.
in writing. ‒ every year, the commission takes stock of the application of the treaties: the transposition of european legislation into national law and infringement procedures against recalcitrant states. the environment is the most important issue. france has been repeatedly in the red for its air pollution rate of fine particles for example. without the impact of german coal mines being incriminated. i guess so. the report notes that there are fewer infringements, supports citizens' petitions and complaints and denounces the setting of often unrealistic deadlines. i welcome the fact that it recalls the possibility of setting 'higher social and environmental standards in the member states than at union level'. but above all, he asks the commission to 'apply more 'dissuasive financial sanctions' to 'creatively' assess the union and thus combat 'unjustified euroscepticism among citizens'. the commission is thus seeking to incorporate the sanctions of the european semester, the so-called golden rules, into the marble of the treaties. i vote against it.
in writing. ‒ the report recalls or advocates a number of points to which we are opposed, namely, in particular, the eu charter of fundamental rights as equal to the treaties, compliance with eu law as a political priority and the suggestion of greater involvement of the parliament in the correct transposition of eu legislation in each member state as well as for the candidate countries. the report stresses that 'when applying eu law, member states should avoid adding unnecessary constraints to eu law, as this leads to a misconception of eu legislative activity and fosters unjustified euroscepticism among citizens' (sic). i therefore opposed this report.
in writing. ‒ this report recalls or advocates a number of points that we are fighting against, namely, in particular, the equal treaty value of the charter of fundamental rights of the union, compliance with union law as a political priority, the suggestion of greater involvement of parliament in the correct transposition of union legislation, in particular in each member state as well as for the candidate countries, the link between the effective application of union law and the strengthening of the credibility of the union institutions. i have no choice but to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which is the annual publication of the european commission on the application of eu law in the member states. unfortunately, the areas of public policy where the most serious infringements occur are those related to the internal market, transport and the environment. for policies decided at union level to be coherent and effective, they must be applied and respected in all european territories.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which takes stock of the year 2014 on the monitoring of the application of eu law. this text emphasises the essential role played by the european commission in monitoring the application of community law, while recalling the primary role of the european parliament in exercising political supervision over the commission's implementing measures. the report points out that the application of eu law is not sufficiently transparent and that the environment, transport and the internal market for services are the areas of public policy where infringements are still most numerous.
in writing. ‒ the commission's annual report 2014 on the monitoring of the application of union law takes stock of the infringement procedures brought against member states for delayed or incorrect transposition of union directives by the commission, in the context of its role as 'guardian of the treaties'. the most problematic areas were health, the environment, consumer protection and transport. in 2014, the court of justice of the union delivered 38 judgments against member states. it ordered italy, greece, portugal, spain and sweden to pay the costs. this report recalls or advocates a number of points that we are fighting against, namely, in particular, the equal value to the treaties of the charter of fundamental rights of the union, compliance with union law as a political priority, the suggestion of greater involvement of the parliament in the correct transposition of union legislation in particular in each member state as well as for the candidate countries. i am voting against this text.
in writing. ‒ we oppose the authorisation of the cultivation of this gm maize. bt11 maize is tolerant to the herbicide glufosinate-ammonium. in addition, it should be recalled once again that the rules on the authorisation of gmos are not democratic, as jean-claude juncker himself has admitted. it is therefore up to parliament to play its part in promoting transparency and democracy. no new proposal for rules on the import of gmos appears to be proposed by the commission. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the environment. our objective remains the same: no genetically modified food will be validated by the european parliament in committee until the commission has proposed a new framework for the import of gmos, in order to take account of the fact that gmos are the majority in europe. it is a question of democracy and also a way of enforcing the european parliament's choices in the institutional game.
in writing. ‒ five objections are raised by parliament on authorisations to grow or import gm maize or wheat. despite systematic objections, the commission continues to issue authorisations for cultivation or imports of gmos. parliament is still objecting, but in vain, because the commission is not taking this into account. these objections help to expose the hypocrisy of the majority parliamentarians (who maintain the commission) in the face of the totalitarianism of the eu. i therefore voted in favour of these new objections.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection to ban the import and placing on the market of herbicide-resistant maize. its use could have adverse effects on users and consumers.
in writing. ‒ parliament has tabled five objections to authorisations for the cultivation or import of gmos with different properties. gmos tolerating one or two herbicides that are about to be banned are of little interest and, moreover, are dangerous for biodiversity. monitoring of effects on nature is insufficient, efsa's evaluation is still minimal and also contrary to food sovereignty. in this case, i voted in favour of this objection to the placing on the market of genetically modified maize bt11 seeds.
in writing. ‒ despite systematic objections, the commission persists in issuing authorisations for crops or imports of gmos. the object is to object to the placing on the market of seeds of genetically modified bt11 maize for cultivation by the manufacturer syngenta. the issues raised are glufosinate, which is due to be banned in 2017 (ownership is therefore useless) and the destruction of biodiversity. so i voted for it.
in writing. ‒ the present report proposes to adopt five objections to authorisations for the cultivation or import of gmos, including those from monsanto. these objections highlight the hypocrisy and double-talk of the meps of the majority groups who vote against what they promise to their constituents. i voted in favour of these objections.
in writing. ‒ the object of this objection is to oppose the placing on the market of the gmo bt11. i object to this because the european commission has respected its mandate within the framework of the implementing powers granted to it by the european parliament and the council. i regret that this ideologically motivated resolution does not take into account the many precautionary measures adopted by the european legislator in relation to the authorisation of new products to be placed on the market, as well as the positive scientific opinion given by the european food safety authority. for these reasons, i voted against this objection.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this objection to refuse the placing on the market of genetically modified maize seeds for cultivation. the objection is based on an allegation that the commission exceeded the implementing powers conferred on it by this authorisation. however, the commission has complied with the existing procedure for the authorisation of gmos. it first requested an analysis from the european food safety authority (efsa) to verify that the maize seed was not hazardous to human and animal health and the environment. i therefore believe that this objection is unwarranted and merely reflects a desire to ban all gmos systematically, whereas this is a matter for the member states.
in writing. currently, genetically modified organisms (gmos) can be grown in the european union after the seed companies that hold the gmo have obtained a marketing authorisation in accordance with european regulations. the european parliament has chosen to use its right of objection to ask the european commission to withdraw its authorisations for the use of genetically modified bt11 maize seeds tolerant of glyphosate, a herbicide classified as a 'probable carcinogen' by the world health organisation (who). in the future, the authorisation process for gmos will need to be revised, which should not be possible without the support of a qualified majority of member states and the opinion of the parliament.

in writing. ‒ the report opposes the commission's decision to authorise the placing on the market of genetically modified maize bt11 seeds. this variety is developed by syngenta. it gives resistance to certain insects (maize bollworm). but of course there is also tolerance to herbicides containing phosphinotricine (ppt), such as ammonium glufosinate, a substance classified as toxic to reproduction. and it's actually banned from use on corn in the eu. the report criticises the assessment made by the european food safety authority (efsa). in particular, it points to the arbitrary introduction of the concept of an 'acceptable local mortality' level for non-target lepidopteran species. the corn is known to kill insects other than the corn borer, which it is supposed to be specialized in. i am voting for this text.

in writing. ‒ the safety of gmos is far from proven. the danger of many of them, both for the environment and for consumers, is well established. the precautionary principle should therefore prevail. however, the european commission regularly authorises them. the current procedure does not allow the blocking of marketing authorisations for gmos granted by the european commission. as far as the cultivation of gmos authorized by the commission is concerned, it can only be blocked by the member states on their territory. but we all know that pollen does not stop at frontiers, nor do insects that have become resistant. so, with a large majority of my colleagues, we have just challenged the authorisation and renewal of the authorisation of five gmos, including the famous monsanto gm maize. i welcome this vote even though it is essentially a political position to put pressure on the commission to propose new legislation. but i have no illusions about what the european commission will do. that is why i call on our citizens to use this vote to press for and enforce the precautionary principle in the eu.

the commission has already submitted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. madam president, commissioner, as rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on international trade, i am pleased that we have been able to take part in the examination of customs matters normally reserved for the imco committee. this approach has been both effective and complementary. it is important to take account of the place of the internal market in a global context, because our partners have already pointed out the inconsistencies of our internal market. we can learn from them. although the customs union is considered to be the backbone of the single market, there is still no integrated approach. the idea of approximating the definitions and penalties for customs infringements is a good one. especially in 2016. we should say: "it's about time". however, the issue is caught between the exclusive competence of the european union in customs matters and the principle of subsidiarity of the judicial or administrative sanctions of the states. this balance must therefore be preserved. the lack of vision on the part of some politicians in europe, who do not understand the challenges we face today, is appalling. only the european union can develop a common approach to implementing customs legislation, which does not please mr magnette, who may seek to complicate the trade facilitation we are putting in place. more seriously, we must put in place a grand strategy that gives a direction, a course to the economic world of the european union. this type of initiative is useful in bringing coherence to both the internal market and our external trade. our customs are doing a great job. they must be able to rely on a flexible structure and a rigorous framework, which is not uniform across europe. let us support this kind of initiative, whose aims of simplification, harmonisation, fairness and firmness must be emphasised in order to give a better understanding of the challenges facing the european union.
on behalf of the s&d group. madam president, i would like to thank the rapporteur and all the fictitious rapporteurs with whom the work on this dossier has been very effective and very fruitful. this was all the more difficult because it was a very technical subject on which compromises were sometimes difficult to obtain, but we really worked in a very constructive spirit. i think we can be happy with the result. we welcomed the commission's proposal because the customs union is the backbone of the internal market, the other side of the internal market. it is one of the first harmonized policies of the european union and the adoption of the customs code is a signal of even greater integration in this area. however, even though this is a highly integrated policy of the european union, inconsistencies remain, particularly with regard to sanctions. the paradox is that the rules may be the same, but depending on the country in which you carry out your customs formalities, if you break the rules you may be liable to penalties ranging from a fine in one member state to a prison sentence in another. it is clear that this situation of inconsistency and disparities creates opportunities for customs competition between states, not in terms of rules but of the sanctions attached to them. therefore, to prevent this circumvention of the common rules of the internal market, which leads to a loss of several hundred million euros due to fraud, we believe it is absolutely necessary to harmonize the sanctions. in this respect, i think we have reached a very good compromise which avoids unfair competition between member states. we have clarified and strengthened the legal basis. we have clarified definitions, in particular the notions of negligence or intentional fault. we have also clarified a number of points on the nature of the sanctions. we have removed the criminal sanctions which remain the exclusive competence of the member states, who can introduce them if they wish. finally, we have brought the sanctions and thresholds into line with the directive on the protection of financial interests in the european union. i welcome this harmonization. as regards the method of determining the amount of the penalties, i also think that the compromise we have reached is satisfactory, with a floor for serious infringements and a method of calculation based on the amount of the duties to ensure proportionality of the penalty. but i think we could have gone a little further on this point, by specifying certain criteria to ensure the deterrent side of the instrument. we also support the possibility for member states to introduce sanctions other than fines, such as the suspension of economic operator status or the revocation of an import authorization. in addition, the commission proposal was strengthened by the introduction of a distinction between major and minor infringements, based on objective and contextual factors, in order to protect smes whose infringements are allegedly unintentional due to a lack of knowledge of customs rules. finally, we welcome the introduction of the amicable settlement procedure and the maintenance of the four-year limitation period. the harmonization of customs sanctions is clearly essential to better combat fraud, to better guarantee compliance with european rules and also to better feed the budget of the european union, for which customs duties are one of the few own resources. in this context, it is regrettable that the work has not yet begun in the council. this is a case which unfortunately illustrates the contradictions which are too frequent between the discourse of the member states in general and the positions taken in the council. in the case of customs sanctions, as in the case of other policies, namely fiscal or social policies, it is clear that the lack of harmonization which leads to a situation of competition between states is harmful, undermines the application of common rules and deprives citizens of legitimate resources. so parliament now has a strong, coherent position which i think is a good basis for work. it is now up to the council to take up its responsibilities and move towards harmonizing customs sanctions. i would like to thank the rapporteur and my colleagues again for the excellent work they have done and i hope that the council will make rapid progress on this matter.
on behalf of the enf group. madam president, the aim of this directive is to establish a common legal framework for the member states of the european union in order to eliminate the disparities between the various national systems which are applied. in other words, it is a question of harmonizing the national application of customs legislation in order to complete the implementation of the customs union. national disparities in the implementation of this customs union do affect the level playing field in that they provide an advantage to those who do not comply with the legislation in a member state with a more lenient customs sanctions regime. the risk to infringers therefore varies according to the gateway to the single internal market. these distortions of competition are indeed commonplace in this single internal market, whether they are social, environmental, financial, economic or political in nature. the french experience this bitterly every day. in short, the scheme is simple. member states continue to transpose european directives into national law in accordance with their own interests. while i see this as a patriotic act, the rapporteur explains that some member states are dragging their feet. for the commission and the european institutions, however, it is a mortal sin. on the contrary, we need more europe. despite the economic crisis in the euro zone, the widening of the migration crisis, the clear rejection of this concept of european integration by the peoples of europe, as evidenced by brexit or the rejection of ceta by belgium, the juncker commission is still advocating more and more integration. as the proverb says, errare humanum est, perseverare diabolicum, to err is human, to be stubborn is diabolic. this dream of a harmonized and homogeneous single market is being shattered by economic, political, geographical and therefore national realities. i think that's great news for the future.

directive and adoption of the new european union data protection package in april earlier this year; the new europol regulation adopted in may; and the new cepol regulation providing for better action plan on strengthening the fight against terrorist financing, we would propose by the end of the year a number of legislative proposals, such as a proposal for a directive on criminal offences integrity policies. this goes in parallel with our work in the framework of the european semester of economic governance. at this stage the commission is working with member states to follow up and take forward the conclusions of the first anti—corruption report and will inform parliament by the end of the year how the commission sees this work progressing. to conclude, the commission welcomes i'm the reporter. mr president, i would first of all like to thank in particular the fictitious rapporteurs who accompanied me on this report, their assistants and the group advisers and marion, my own collaborator, without whom this report could not have been made. we have been working there for almost a year, and their support has been invaluable to me despite the many vicissitudes we have gone through, the worst of which was what i would call the test of languages. in the droi sub-commission, translations are partly outsourced, which must be relatively expensive; we should expect a service rendered to the highest standards. it was a nightmare. we discovered that some of them were machine translations. i therefore urge the ad hoc committees of the european parliament to investigate this matter. this report deals with human rights and migration in third countries and therefore does not deal with the union's migration policies. our parliament has produced a report on this subject, that of mrs metsola and mrs kyenge, which was adopted by a large majority, and is preparing another on foreign policy. we have therefore focused on the situation in third countries, with the aim of putting migration back into its global context. this report emphasizes the evolution of migration policies, which are increasingly globalized but also regionalised, and their causes, which are increasingly multiple and complex: 244 million international migrants, or 3.3% of the world population, compared with 2.9% in 1990; 80% of movements now take place between countries with common borders, and increasingly south-south. most countries in the world today are countries of origin, transit and destination, including europe. these migrations increasingly involve women and children, including isolated minors and, therefore, vulnerable persons who are entitled to special protection on the increasingly dangerous routes of migration. they are also graduating more and more: already 59 million in 2010, and it is africa that is paying the heaviest price for this brain drain. the question of refugees is of particular importance in this report. the number of uprooted, refugees and displaced people now stands at 65 million according to the unhcr, with a 10% increase in one year, mainly in the number of displaced people. in our proposals we wanted to start with respect for human rights, as they are recognised and protected by international conventions, and to see how the european union, in its policies of partnership with third countries, can act to ensure better respect for human rights, including by setting an example on its territory and enforcing ad hoc international conventions. the international convention on the protection of the rights of all migrant workers and members of their families has not been signed by any member state of the european union. all migrants have rights, whatever their situation, as the un special rapporteur on migration has repeatedly said. respect for human rights means, for example, refusing forced readmission of migrants to countries where they risk ill-treatment and torture; refusing mass expulsions and refoulements that are contrary to international law; the european union is committed to the principle of subsidiarity, and to the principle of subsidiarity. these are just a few examples. such a wish may seem like a pious wish. some here say that this report is too progressive. we have seen in the foreign affairs committee that the european union should do more in this area, working with its main partners to implement legislation that respects the rights of migrants, starting with the right of asylum. we believe that the eidhr is a good instrument for moving forward and that it is time to adopt specific guidelines for the rights of migrants. we all know that migration issues are increasingly taking up space in the european union's dialogues with third countries. we also know that an increasing proportion of these policies are beyond the control of parliament. this is why this report proposes, in particular, to assess and monitor all agreements and funds in this area, starting with the eu-turkey agreement and the khartoum and rabat processes. there are many other subjects in this report which i cannot go into and i regret that. i would like to conclude by thanking all those who have contributed, and especially all those who have contributed, since the vast majority of the fictional rapporteurs were women.

complaint has been heard on the docks: that the control of fishing should be less strict in neighbouring countries than in one's own country. a rumor never meant that there was any truth to it, but its persistence made it worth investigating. i have therefore conducted the inquiry with the support of my colleagues in the committee on fisheries of the european parliament and have drawn up an own-initiative report on this basis. this feeling of inequity due to the differentiated application of the regulation by country raises the question not only of the efficiency but also of the credibility of the european union. the regulation is supposed to apply to everyone and it is not acceptable that it does not apply in the same way. however, compliance with the rule is a condition for the results of sustainable and modern fishing. in this report i have tried to analyse the shortcomings in the regulation and its application, the shortcomings which lead to this feeling of injustice. the second objective of this report is to propose solutions to harmonize the control of the common fisheries policy, which, i would remind you, is supposed to be one of the most integrated policies in europe. i am of course pleased with the constructive work carried out in committee, where everyone's contribution has made it possible to draw up an almost complete picture of the situation of control in europe. i am of course particularly grateful to the fictitious rapporteurs. this report highlights the chameleon nature of the control regulation in that it applies differently depending on the colour of the country, whether it is the scope of the control regulation or the procedures and strategies. the report also reveals that each member state has its own standards for training inspectors, that fishermen are not trained in the same way and that there is not always any training for inspection. the overly limited mandate of the fisheries control agency, whose main role should be to harmonise practices, is also highlighted. it therefore appears appropriate to establish a european training course for controllers and to develop a single control reference framework. training for fishermen should also be strengthened. the procedures should also be europeanised and the role of the vigo agency strengthened by increasing its resources and broadening its scope. i also believe that it is urgent that the control procedures should be transparent and standardised, and that the various control bodies should be coordinated within the same geographical area. but the most serious dysfunction is that member states may transpose the regulation differently because of a large number of optional provisions within the 'control' regulation itself and the inapplicability of some of them, which can lead to a subjective interpretation of controllers. it will therefore be essential to remove the optional entries and to clarify and simplify existing community legislation when the next revision of the control regulation is carried out. court procedures and penalties also differ across the union. for the same offence, the sanction may be of an administrative or criminal nature. it seems legitimate to implement a regulation in the future where the same penalty will be applied for the same offence and to introduce incentive measures. the instruments, tools and financial means used to carry out the checks also vary from one member state to another. the most urgent point, according to the auditors we have heard from all the countries, is the data and the compatibility of the instruments. the databases used by member states are not always shared, but they are essential for risk assessment and control strategy. i will close with the issue of pleasure, which will be put to the test during this week's votes. if we are to achieve a balance between fishing rights and the state of the fishery resources, it is essential that this activity also be controlled. we are a few steps away from the revision of the fisheries control regulation announced by the commission. i have no doubt that the recommendations adopted by parliament will be taken into account in the future proposal.

the agenda calls for the debate on the report by sophia in 't veld, on behalf of the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs, containing recommendations to the commission on the establishment of a union mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights (2015/2254(inl)) (a8-0283/2016).
on behalf of the enf group. madam president, article 7 of the treaty on european union provides for a mechanism of sanctions against member states which do not respect human rights. the report in 't veld today seeks to complete it. this report raises both a legal and a political problem. the legal problem is that it overturns article 7. as explained by the council's legal service in an opinion of 27 may 2014, article 7 gives the council, and it alone, the power to find that a member state is violating human rights. the in 't veld report, however, ignores this exclusive competence of the council by seeking to give the brussels commission a competing power of assessment by adopting reports and recommendations. on the other hand, the in 't veld report raises a political problem in particular, by dealing a new blow to the sovereignty of states. it allows experts without democratic legitimacy to rate states as children according to three grades of rating symbolized in its initial presentation by a game of three colors: green for good students, yellow for those who can do better and red for those who must be punished. the member states which must be punished are, of course, those which dare to resist the dictates of the european union, in the spirit of the report in 't veld. the report does not even hide this fact, since it openly aims to punish two states: hungary, guilty of resisting the eu's migration policy, and poland, guilty of refusing to let its family policy be dictated by the lgbti lobby. the report in 't veld is therefore a further step in the forced march towards the sovietization of the union. that is why i tabled an amendment rejecting this liberty-killing text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text on the amendment of regulation (eu) no 1303/2013 as regards certain provisions relating to financial management for certain member states experiencing or likely to experience serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability. the budget-neutral text is intended to help member states such as greece and cyprus, which are experiencing financial difficulties, to implement projects co-financed by european funds at national level. in concrete terms, the aim is to increase the rate of european co-financing applied to erdf, esf and cohesion fund projects in these countries. this will enable projects that have been stalled due to difficulties in mobilising national funds to be relaunched.
in writing. ‒ under pressure from the european commission, member state governments are implementing austerity policies to reduce their public deficits to 3% of gdp, which has led to a fall in public investment, notably in greece, portugal and cyprus, where national authorities are no longer able to co-finance projects eligible for eu structural funds. regulation no 1303/2013 provides for an increase in the co-financing rate to be granted to states which have received financial assistance from the european union after 31/12/2013. in view of their debt burden, these member states are unable to finance public investment that would help to boost economic growth. although these increases may prove positive in the short term, they do not solve the structural problems of the greek and cypriot economies (lack of competitiveness, over-indebtedness) but are instead aimed at making them even more dependent on the european structural funds. finally, with constant payment appropriations, these increases will be made at the expense of other member states such as france, which will suffer even more significant delays in payment. in these circumstances, i would therefore prefer to abstain because i disapprove of this foolish policy but do not wish to penalise the people who suffer because of the eu.
in writing. ‒ this report validates a commission legislative proposal to facilitate an additional support mechanism in the implementation of the union's regional policy for countries experiencing severe financial difficulties. they do not have sufficient resources to co-finance these programmes. if no decisions were taken, regional policy would have declined only partially in these territories. i am glad that i voted for this report, which has a neutral budgetary impact in the end.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report amending regulation (eu) no 1303/2013 on the financial management of certain member states experiencing serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability. today, some member states are facing budgetary difficulties and are no longer able to provide national co-financing for projects linked to cohesion policy, formerly regional policy. it is important to emphasise that european law provides for the possibility for the european institutions to help member states in financial difficulty. the purpose of this text is to extend the deadline for the commission to grant additional support. the report will enable the commission to supplement payments to a member state under an adjustment programme by adding up to 10 percentage points to the co-financing rates applicable to the priorities of the european social fund, the european regional development fund or the cohesion fund programmes. it is important to note that this extension has no budgetary impact.
in writing. ‒ this text provides for the granting of aid and derogations in the european financial regulatory system to member states experiencing serious difficulties with respect to their financial stability. although these increases may prove positive in the short term, they do not solve the structural problems of the greek and cypriot economies in particular. on the contrary, they are intended to make them even more dependent on the european structural funds. i therefore chose to abstain on this report.

in writing. ‒ the directive aims to establish a common legal framework for the 28 member states of the european union to eliminate disparities between the different legal systems applied and thus contribute to equal treatment of economic operators in the eu. the commission would retain the right to define the nature of the infringements, to determine whether they are minor or major, and to monitor and supervise the application of the regulation by the member states. i was against it because the problems of the internal market always follow the same logic. the member states have a common regulatory framework (eu) but the application of laws (transposition of directives, etc.) varies widely between member states, depending on the interests of some or the economic and political (in) capabilities of others. thus, distortions of competition are indeed commonplace within the single internal market itself, whether they are of a social, environmental, financial, economic or political nature. the chimerical implementation of a harmonized and homogeneous single internal market thus inevitably clashes with national and geographical realities.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this directive is to harmonise the way in which member states implement community customs legislation. to achieve this, the directive establishes a common legal framework for the 28 member states of the union in order to reduce disparities between the different legal systems, which would lead to distortions of competition within the single market. on the one hand, the european commission would, through this directive, claim the right to define the nature of infringements, the right to determine their degree of importance and the right to monitor the application of the regulation in each member state. on the other hand, distortions of competition resulting from disparities between national legal systems are far less harmful than those resulting from social, environmental and fiscal dumping practiced by certain member states within the european union itself. dumping which contributes to the acceleration of deindustrialization in western countries with the consequent increase in unemployment, poverty and social inequalities. that is why i voted against this text.
in writing. i support the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the union legal framework for customs offences and the sanctions applicable to them. it is inadmissible that the sanction for a customs offence in the union should depend on the frontier at which it was committed. in addition, the existence of different regimes is a hindrance to cooperation between national customs services. it creates potential differences in treatment which tarnish mutual trust between member states. with a common framework governing customs offences, the different customs services of the member states will operate within the same system, allowing them to cooperate in an optimal way.
in writing. the customs union is one of the first guarantees of the european single market, with its common customs tariff vis-à-vis third countries. its rules cover all aspects of trade policy, such as preferential trade, health and environmental controls, common agricultural and fisheries policies, and the protection of our economic interests through non-tariff instruments and external policy measures. these common rules must be applied by all member states. however, differences persist between member states as regards customs control procedures, the definition of customs offences, the legal nature of those offences, or the penalties applied, which may range from simple fines to imprisonment. these disparities can threaten the interests of europeans. the harmonization and simplification of these rules at european level is therefore a step in the right direction.

in writing. ‒ mrs kallas' report is a typical example of the european union's tendency to centralize. the european union is a customs union: customs rules are community rules and provide a legal framework for controls and cooperation between national administrations. since the regulation is based on directives, and therefore on an obligation to produce results, its application, like the penalties for infringement, is the responsibility of the states (freedom of action). consequently, the definition of such offences and the sanction for them may vary from one member state to another depending on legal systems and administrative practices. the commission considered that this would create distortions of competition between international traders. to remedy this, european definitions are now being proposed, i.e. a harmonisation of criminal and administrative law, which goes far beyond the commission's prerogatives. the commission has also decided to initiate proceedings under article x (3) of the gatt agreements, which require each party to apply its customs legislation in a uniform manner. i cannot vote for an illegitimate harmonization under international dictates.
in writing. ‒ the eu is once again faced with the test of hard reality. while all member states are governed by the same regulatory framework, laws apply to them differently, given their different economic, political, social, environmental and financial make-up. the illusion of promoting a single and harmonised internal market thus stumbles on a heterogeneity of national characteristics. i voted against it.

in writing. ‒ the customs union does not have an integrated approach to the enforcement of its customs legislation. this means that the rules are the same but that when the rules are broken, the penalties applied differ considerably. this encourages importers to operate in the member states with the lowest penalties, thus creating a distortion of the market. to address this, the commission proposed in 2013 a directive on the union legal framework governing customs offences and the sanctions applicable to them. the report before us improves the commission's proposal by distinguishing between administrative and criminal sanctions, which remain subject to national legislation. but in the end, the directive is a major infringement of the judiciary. the directive sets minimum and maximum penalties and lists possible aggravating and mitigating circumstances. it also sets out how judges will have to calculate fines, leaving no room for manoeuvre for judicial institutions. for these reasons, i abstain.

in writing. - that's a balanced and common sense report. iran is a great country and the heir to this great persian civilization which, in the years to come, can and must play a leading role in the middle east in order to counterbalance the predominant influence of the sunni countries of the muslim world. yes, the nuclear deal must bring iran back into the concert of nations. yes, a large economy like iran must be allowed to join the wto. let us welcome this opening, even if everything is not perfect today in tehran. the rapporteur is right to point out the imperfections of the iranian political and legal system. it is true that iran is not yet a state governed by the rule of law as we conceive it. too many political prisoners are still languishing in iranian jails. but is it any different in the other countries of the region? is saudi arabia, our great ally, a state of law? what about yemen? what about turkey? what about qatar?

in writing. ‒ the report on the fight against corruption and the follow-up to the crim resolution is very positive overall. i simply wish to explain why i voted against paragraph 42 (b) of this report. although i support the idea of temporarily banning people convicted of corruption from holding public office or running for election, the wording of paragraph 42 (b) is unfortunately not clear and precise enough. as it is drafted, it also applies to persons who have participated in acts of corruption, which does not correspond to a well-defined category and thus undermines legal certainty. it would have been more fair to limit this proposal to only those 'convicted' of corruption or organised crime. furthermore, the wording of paragraph 42 (b) is not sufficiently precise in that it may concern any person who is the subject of a conviction, whether or not it is related to corruption. such a reading of the text could, for example, prevent certain environmental or trade union activists from running for office or holding public office, which is obviously too restrictive and contrary to the aim pursued.

in writing. ‒ the title of ms vergiat's report is a pretext for singing the praises of immigration, a good thing for migrants themselves, for the host countries and for the countries of origin. its basic axiom is: 'everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own'. it is true that dictatorships, especially communist dictatorships, have always narrowly limited the possibility of obtaining passports to a handful of apparatchiks, the vast majority of the population being in a sense under house arrest. but freedom of movement is not an absolute right to emigrate and settle wherever one wishes in order to enjoy the many rights listed by ms vergiat (education, employment, housing, health, etc.). western societies, already overwhelmed, cannot cope. ms vergiat advocates that developing countries hosting displaced people should align themselves with the lax and outrageously generous regulations of the european union, even as they struggle to guarantee these rights to their own citizens. i demand for them what i demand for my country: the right to choose whether or not to accept migrants and to discriminate in favour of their own nationals.

in writing. ‒ apart from the interference in our energy policy with the strengthening of the power of the commission and its agencies, and the systematic desire to liberalise the energy market, this report, which speaks four times of the union's 'energy diplomacy', seems above all to be the result of geopolitical orientations which are not ours and which take precedence over any other considerations. that is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ this is a very clear text in favour of the gas sector, whose development should allow a smooth ecological transition, with good economic prospects at the heart, particularly in terms of jobs that cannot be relocated thanks to biomethane. in this case, the report deals more specifically with the lng sector, in particular interconnections and storage capacities. it also involves increasing the diversification of sources and supply routes; the lng offers even more flexibility. nevertheless, the strengthening of the power of the commission and its agencies in the field of energy policy seems to me to be contrary to the interests of france, as does the systematic desire to liberalize the energy market. the report also mentions the eu's 'energy diplomacy' four times, and geopolitical orientations, which i dispute, therefore take precedence over all other considerations. for all these reasons, i am voting against this report.
in writing. ‒ liquefied natural gas (lng) is a cooled natural gas, which facilitates its storage and transport, with one third of the world's gas passing through in the form of lng. the advantages are many: reduced geopolitical problems because lng does not transit through traditional pipelines, reduced isolation and energy dependence, increased cleanliness when it comes to fuel (less co2, sox and nox). i voted in favour of this text, which shows that an internal energy market fully integrating lng will contribute to the emergence of an efficient energy union.
in writing. ‒ in this text, the rapporteur makes good recommendations, such as the one to promote domestic energy sources or the one to promote liquefied biogas. the rapporteur, however, points out that the european union must decide our energy policy in the name of energy diplomacy. this is unacceptable and highly questionable, especially since this energy diplomacy is aimed at american shale gas and qatari liquefied natural gas against russian sources, historical and reliable sources. i therefore voted against.

in writing. to join the eu, candidate countries must respect the rule of law, democracy and fundamental rights. however, within the eu, compliance with these principles is difficult to monitor and enforce. the tools created by the union, such as article 7 teu or the rule of law mechanism, may come too late, be difficult to apply or even be misunderstood. the hungarian and polish cases have shown this. the european parliament therefore proposes that the eu should establish a mechanism for regular assessment of the respect for the rule of law, fundamental rights and democracy in the member states and the three main eu institutions. including relevant interlocutors and experts and based on objective criteria, the pact is designed as a prerequisite to article 7 and suggests easier activation of sanctions - including financial ones. i supported this report because it is essential not to compromise on the rule of law, especially when the respect of economic rules is subject to regular and recurrent european checks. i also welcome the fact that this report proposes an awareness campaign for european citizens and residents about their fundamental rights.

european parliament with great effort in 2013, have proved to be a lifesaver in the first years of the mff's implementation in order to cope with the unforeseen events and crises we are experiencing. how could we have predicted in 2013 the current migration phenomenon, brexit or the new challenges of internal security? these flexibility tools have been very much in demand and, without revision, they will simply not be enough to meet the commitments we have made to our fellow europeans. our resolution welcomes the commission's proposals for flexibility extensions, although we believe that further steps will be needed, particularly to strengthen the emergency aid reserve and the flexibility instrument. as regards the union's crisis reserve, we welcome the fact that this idea, proposed by parliament - as you said, madam vice-president - has been taken up by the commission. the scope and funding of the programme will have to be considered further. budgetary flexibility is neither a luxury nor a whim, and this has been demonstrated. it is a powerful tool in long-term budgetary planning, which is designed to respond to situations which we cannot anticipate. we also support the proposals for the use of the automatic appropriations in the european budget. these appropriations, which are intended to be spent under the union budget, must logically be kept in that budget and not taken out of it. as for payments, we said in july that the ostrich policy would lead to serious disappointments at the end of the period. we have to take responsibility. the credibility of the european institutions is at stake, but, more seriously, the situation of the beneficiaries, whether local and regional authorities, businesses or students on erasmus mobility, who would have to wait for the european union to be able to pay their bills. this hidden deficit, if i may use the expression, is contrary to the treaty. the revision should make it possible to solve this problem by calculating special instruments, excluding ceilings, and by making the overall margin for payments more flexible. the solutions are on the table and the discussion must now begin with a common objective: every union bill must be paid on time. however, let me make a few criticisms. we regret in particular that the commission's draft does not propose to raise the expenditure ceilings for heading 1a on competitiveness for growth and employment, heading 1b on economic, social and territorial cohesion and headings 3 and 4. we need to break the deadlock of unfunded advertising. i will take only one example: the fight against youth unemployment. it's a shared priority. the commission has just given a positive assessment of the youth employment initiative, which is recognised as a success, not a complete one, but never a complete one. however, while the six billion appropriations for this programme are exhausted, the commission's proposal provides for only one billion euro of reinforcement until 2020. this is notoriously inadequate in the face of the tragedy experienced by 25% of young europeans under the age of 25. at least the same amount, namely eur 6 billion, must be added to the end of the budget period. the debate on the merits of the revision is just beginning. we in parliament are ready to open negotiations. we know that the commission is also. we are now waiting for the council and, as we said in july and as we reiterate in the resolution which i hope will be voted on tomorrow, parliament wishes to conduct the negotiations on the 2017 budget and the revision of the multiannual financial framework in parallel. the letter of amendment no 1 on the 2017 budget demonstrates this: the revision will necessarily have consequences for the 2017 budget. these two dossiers must therefore be negotiated at the same time. madam president, i have only my conclusion to say, if i may. to this end, parliament has set up a single negotiating team on these two subjects. we have our mandate, adopted in july, which we are completing today. it is now up to the council to speed up. there is no time to lose for our fellow citizens and for europe.

madam president, madam vice-president, ladies and gentlemen, i too am surprised that the council is not here. i would like to pay tribute to the outstanding work of our co-correspondents, isabelle thomas and jan olbrycht. they set out here, by way of resolution, the basic principles of negotiation with the council. i feel that we are coming to the end of a cycle and that the revision of the multiannual financial framework must put an end to two hypocritical practices. the first concerns the flexibility levers, the so-called special instruments. during the negotiations on the financial perspective for 2014-2020, it was agreed that these special instruments, in response to exceptional circumstances and crises, would be above the ceilings. then, as we tried, we found that the council did not want to accept that if there was subscription above the ceilings for commitments, there must be corresponding subscription above the ceilings for payments. the council rejects this version and that is how the remaining balance is being worked out and how we are going to find ourselves faced with a major difficulty tomorrow. the second hypocrisy concerns the practice of hiding our impunity by multiplying the budgetary satellites: the juncker fund for strategic investments, the facilities for turkey and other trust funds. this practice is contrary to the principle of budgetary unity and creates a dead end for parliamentary control. the resulting galaxy is a mirage. the revision of the multiannual financial framework is an opportunity to put the budgetary house in order and to instill sincerity in a budget which has lost all readability. let us beware: a union whose budget is not understandable to its citizens is a union in danger. it is therefore urgent that the commission's intelligent proposal for a revision be given substance.

in writing. ‒ the vote on the 2017 budget is an important moment for the european parliament. the context is clear: political priorities are increasing (security, migration, employment, youth, investment), but the eu council wanted to propose reductions in many areas. it is understandable that some member states, which are experiencing budgetary difficulties often due to failing national public policies, would like to reduce the eu budget. but at the same time, these states and their citizens are increasingly demanding more efficiency at european level. we must therefore be consistent, and that is why i voted in favour of the draft general budget of the eu for 2017, which revised upwards, as far as possible, the proposals made by the council. for example, we decided to increase the youth employment initiative to €1.5 billion in commitment appropriations, to release an additional €600 million in commitment appropriations for the agricultural sector to support farmers affected by the dairy crisis, and to counter the adverse effects of the russian embargo. a europe that acts and protects is also, and above all, a europe that knows how to prioritise its spending.
in writing. ‒ the budgetary debate is an important moment in the evaluation of european policies. the 2017 meeting is an opportunity to recall the council's promise to review the multiannual financial framework and to review funding to meet the challenges facing the union. i welcome the fact that the european parliament has included the reception of refugees and their integration and the ecological challenge among these. this report is part of the dialogue with the council which, as usual, is calling for arbitrary budget cuts in programmes such as erasmus+ and cosme, which are among the most representative of what the european union should be. the same applies to cohesion policies, which are supposed to restore regional balances, but which are increasingly subject to austerity policies, and i am thinking in particular of the structural funds such as the esi or life, which are seriously threatened by the council's cuts. the question is not therefore to approve the final budget as a whole but to ensure that the council stops distorting european policies to conform to what i shall call national egoisms. i therefore abstained on this report pending the final outcome of the negotiations before i can make a final decision.

in writing. ‒ in the negotiation of the multiannual financial framework (mff) 2014-2020, the european parliament had obtained a mid-term review. this is what the commission proposed when it presented the draft revision on 14 september. the text begins by recalling the shortcomings of the current mff in the face of the challenges that have emerged since its adoption. it recommended raising the ceilings for the headings which are in dire need of new liquidity: competitiveness for growth and employment, economic, social and territorial cohesion, security and citizenship and europe in the world. the report, which also proposes measures to avoid a payment crisis, stresses the importance of continuing to fund the youth employment initiative, but also of offering greater budgetary flexibility. in the face of the humanitarian catastrophe caused by the refugee crisis, the deep economic and social crisis in europe and the growing terrorist threat, this text calls for the eu to provide a budget that is up to the challenge. i therefore support this report.
in writing. ‒ faced with a monetary union which deprives the monetary and exchange rate policy instruments, the fiscal union is still in its infancy. the european union's budget for seven years (the multiannual financial framework, mff) is limited to 1% of its gdp. in the last parliament it was even lowered below that figure! since then, the greek crisis, the launch of the juncker plan, the refugee crisis and the fight against youth unemployment have led to a stronger commitment by the union. this commitment cannot be expressed in financial artifices or "off-the-record" arrangements. in the resolution on the mff, the social democrats succeeded in getting the european parliament's own-initiative report on this issue to remain firm: it is imperative to create eu own resources to respond to the payments crisis. each year, the member states agree to open appropriations for commitments, but refuse to increase or even often reduce the appropriations for payments (cash). this is because the union budget is too dependent on national contributions. this resolution is clear on these points, and i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ this report finally opens the debate, promised in 2014 during the european elections, on a revision of the european budgetary framework for the period 2014-2020, which had been adopted in 2013. this budgetary framework is marked by austerity, since it has eliminated 50 billion appropriations. meanwhile, the eu population has increased by 10 million inhabitants compared to the previous programming! the report repeats its demands for a revision of the 2014-2020 framework, in the same terms as parliament has been saying since 2013... in vain. but it has no consequences for the commission and the council. it welcomed the commission's decision to propose an amended financial framework regulation. the commission is proposing only redeployments and no increase in the budgetary ceilings, whereas parliament considered them too low. and the report calls, in a totally hypocritical way, for the 'revised framework' finally achieved to be incorporated in the 2017 budget. but at the same time it supports the commission's 2017 budget proposal which does not incorporate this 'revised framework'. i vote against this nonsense which endorses emptiness and submission.
in writing. ‒ the text calls for more financial resources to be made available to the eu by increasing the ceilings of the mff, in particular to deal with the 'challenges' of migration and terrorism (and thus by increasing the contributions of states). the idea of an open approach is also mentioned in relation to the increase in the eu's own resources and thus the idea of a european tax. i therefore voted against this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which follows the proposals of the european commission, because i wanted to send a clear message: the european union's long-term multiannual financial framework (mff) must be adaptable and resilient to crises. as in the budgetary approach for 2017, the revision of the mff must be done in the light of the emerging priorities for european public action. clearly, the current financial resources at european level are not sufficient and new mechanisms need to be put in place, such as a permanent financial reserve that could be mobilised in case of crisis (migration, humanitarian, agricultural...). the european commission's desire to simplify the mobilisation and use of the various financial instruments is also to be welcomed, and this is therefore part of an ambitious revision of the general financial rules.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution calling for a reconciliation of the union's political objectives and its means. faced with the chronic investment deficit, youth unemployment, the migration crisis and the climate emergency, the eu budget must provide an operational response to all these challenges. the multiannual financial framework is now obsolete because of the multiple crises affecting the european union. it will therefore have to be revised at the same time as the 2017 eu budget is adopted. this is the meaning of this resolution, which gives parliament a mandate to obtain from the council the flexibility proposed by the european commission, the increase in ceilings and additional funds for a number of priority programmes. parliament called for the negotiations to include the next financial perspective, in order to put an end to the structural shortage created by the growing imbalance between the weakness of own resources and national contributions. the message from parliament is therefore clear: the member states must now take a stand for a budget that finally meets our needs!
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which sets out parliament's priorities in the context of the mid-term review of the multiannual financial framework for 2017-2020. the text stresses that the european union must update its long-term financial framework in order to better withstand unforeseen crises and respond to new priorities that have emerged in recent years. it is crucial that the union budget is more flexible in order to respond more quickly and effectively to current challenges such as terrorism, internal security, the migration crisis, the agricultural crisis and high unemployment. the resolution welcomes the fact that the commission has incorporated in its draft review of the cfp the parliament's proposal to create a permanent reserve in the european budget which could be mobilised in the event of a crisis. finally, i supported this text because it calls for the revision of the mff to be used as an opportunity to make commitments for the period after 2020, such as a reform of the union's own resources system.

in writing. - i was one of the first to sound the alarm about xyllela fastidiosa, the chestnut cynip or the olive fly. our farmers must be better protected against the entry of these pests which cause serious damage to their crops. in order to combat such health threats, i had consistently advocated a border protection system to better control the entry of plant pests into the european union. it's done now. the european union will finally apply reciprocal rules on health with its major trading partners! we were calling for a risk management-based import control system. this draft regulation will make it possible to put in place a genuine preventive strategy. a preliminary assessment will identify plants and plant products with a high risk and prohibit their import until a phytosanitary risk assessment has been carried out. this text will allow for better protection of plant health and, consequently, of our ecosystem and the biodiversity of the european union.
in writing. ‒ the general objective of this text is to respond to the risks to plant health caused by new pests and diseases imported from third countries. the criticism of globalisation and its effects on trade has thus been largely ignored. the text aims to modernise control instruments, both within the internal market (improved traceability) and in trade with third countries, while reinforcing a risk-based approach. to this end, the draft lays down rules for determining the phytosanitary risk posed by any species, strain or biotype of pathogenic animal or plant parasite harmful to plants, and the measures to reduce this risk to an acceptable level. the text increases controls on the entry and movement of new organisms into the internal market, but it also increases the commission's powers. it will be responsible for drawing up the list of harmful organisms and deciding on the eradication of affected plants, as it did this year with the olive trees affected by xylella fastidiosa in puglia. i abstained on the rejection amendment.

in writing. ‒ i abstained on the report on protection measures against organisms harmful to plants. the aim of this text is to respond to the risks to plant health caused by harmful organisms from third countries. on the positive side, it should be stressed that this text calls globalisation and its excesses into question. it also called for more controls, both within the internal market (in particular on traceability requirements) and in trade with third countries. this is done by reinforcing a risk-based approach. the main problem with this text is that it leaves the commission with the task of analysing and taking decisions. in short, it will be responsible for drawing up the list of organisms harmful to plants, for establishing the various quarantine possibilities and for arbitrarily deciding what measures to take. as a recent example, the radical and unilateral decision taken by the commission on the xylella fastidiosa problem in puglia is based on total interference, coupled with a precautionary principle which is detrimental to italy and beneficial to a third country (tunisia).
in writing. ‒ the general objective of this text is to address the risks to the health of plants. it is threatened by new pests and diseases from third countries. the criticism of globalisation and its effects on trade and on the issue of climate change is therefore a foregone conclusion. the text aims to modernise the control instruments, both within the internal market (improved traceability) and in trade with third countries. to this end, the draft resolution lays down the rules for determining the phytosanitary risk posed by any species, strain or biotype of a plant pathogen, animal or plant parasite harmful to plants and the measures to reduce this risk to an acceptable level. however, this project also increases the commission's power. it will be responsible for drawing up the list of harmful organisms and may even decide on the eradication of affected plants. there is no final vote on second reading, but i abstained on the rejection amendment tabled by the alde group.

in writing. ‒ my colleague mireille d'ornano, from the envi committee, was a co-author of this motion for a resolution. it is imperative to limit the content of trans fatty acids, given their now proven harmful effects on human health. our group stressed that naturally occurring trans fats are not harmful, that regulation of the content of trans fats in foodstuffs must take into account national specificities (consumption habits, gastronomy) and that incentive measures for agri-food businesses should not be neglected. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution. the proposal aims to strengthen european legislation on the standards and identification of the content of trans fats in food, particularly in the agri-food industry, due to their harmfulness to human health. the enf group is co-author of the standards and insists that national dietary habits be taken into account when adapting the standards.
in writing. ‒ trans fatty acids (tfa) are unsaturated fatty acids found in dairy products and meat as well as in industrially produced vegetable oils. these agt are used by the food industry for their specific characteristics (consistency) and especially for their low production cost. they're found in fast food, prepared meals and basically all sorts of processed foods. according to the european food safety authority (efsa), increased consumption of these products increases cholesterol and triglycerides and is a risk factor for cancer. the resolution advocates limiting agt by introducing a % limit for each type of product. i am voting for this text, although i regret that the impact of industrial processes is not more strongly questioned in the food and health sector.
in writing. ‒ my colleague mireille d'ornano of the envi committee was a co-author of this motion for a resolution. it is imperative to limit the content of trans fatty acids in view of their now established harmful effects on human health. our group stressed that naturally occurring trans fats are not harmful, that regulation of the content of trans fats in foodstuffs must take into account national specificities (consumption habits, gastronomy) and that incentive measures for agri-food businesses should not be neglected. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.

the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner, this is the first time in 54 years that the subject of employment and the cap has been directly addressed. we are in the midst of a paradox: the budget for the common agricultural policy represents almost 40% of the budget of the european union and employment is at the very beginning of our priorities, the first we have set within the institutions of the european union. for more than 50 years, the common agricultural policy has shaped agriculture by directing it towards the intensification of its production (s) towards international markets and the development of increasingly concentrated and specialised farms. these choices have been marked by a dramatic increase in labour productivity, which has had a considerable impact on agricultural employment. in 1957, in a europe of six, farmers accounted for 20% of the total workforce in the european union. today, they are only 4% in a union of 28. in the last ten years, we have lost a quarter of our farms. if we continue with this policy, we will not be able to attract young people in the years to come. the cap has also gradually lost its legitimacy over time. today it no longer meets the needs of farmers and is being challenged by all our european citizens. the elements which have long structured the common agricultural policy are no longer appropriate today, and the liberal choice applied to this policy since the 1990s has led us to a dead end. this model destroys many jobs in production and in the territories, especially in the most fragile. we must rethink the cap in depth, and it must remain a common policy for all european agriculture. we are facing several challenges today: the food challenge, the environmental and climate challenge and the territorial challenge. on the food challenge, the cap must give priority to ensuring food security for europe's 500 million citizens and giving everyone access to sufficient food in quantity and quality. the question of human health and the nutritional aspect must be at the heart of the future reform of the common agricultural policy. one in two europeans is overweight or obese. as for cancer, the new forms of the disease among young people in europe, young men and women, especially in rural areas, cannot leave us indifferent to the policies we must implement. the environmental and climate challenge and the productivity model show us every day their limits in terms of sustainability. above all, it is important to produce, but to produce better by managing more efficiently and better protecting natural resources and biodiversity, which can play a positive role for the climate through soils. this implies changes in our production methods, which will have to be adapted to each region and each ecosystem. we cannot forcefully grasp the territorial challenge. we need to re-territorialise agriculture. agriculture is an essential component of the development of rural and peri-urban areas. these areas also contain important resources for diversifying agricultural and forestry activities. we need to reinvest in short circuits, circular economies and organic farming. the answers to these challenges involve three specific responses: a main policy of aid for the settlement of young people; a policy of regulation of agricultural markets; the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the quality of the environment and to improve the quality of life in the european union.
