in writing. - i voted against this text. the text has many positive points (efficient support for small and medium-sized farms, defence and promotion of protected designations of origin (pdo) and protected geographical indications (pgi), local priority, etc.), but, moving away from the substantive issues, it takes a position on gender issues and the social and economic integration of migrants and refugees. we oppose these positions in the present context of crisis in the agricultural sector.
in writing. ‒ like the vast majority of the european parliamentary left (social democrats, ecologists, united left) and unlike the right and the national front, i voted in favour of the andrieu report on the future of the common agricultural policy, which calls for a reform of the cap in a more employment-friendly direction. i share both the diagnosis and the recommended solutions. the text starts with a well-known but still relevant observation: the cap, despite the budgetary envelope at its disposal, is misdirected. it serves productivist and intensive agriculture rather than family farming, promotes export competition rather than short circuits and weakens territorial cohesion and ecosystems. the cap needs to be reformed to respond to these ecological and social challenges (1/5 of european farms disappeared between 2007 and 2013) and to embark on a strategy to renew the generations those under 35 years of age currently represent only 7% of farms. the solutions exist but are neglected by the liberal right at the helm of europe: better regulation of markets, increased support for small farms, promotion of the circular economy. this report calls for a shift towards greater political voluntarism in agricultural matters.
in writing. ‒ this report provides a critical overview of eu agricultural policy. in an integrated approach, it considers that the 'development of the agricultural sector is also linked to the diversification and maintenance of other economic activities, such as forestry and handicrafts, and to the development of small and medium-sized enterprises and integrated production capacities, rural tourism, recreational, educational and sporting activities'. this promotes a model based on small farms rather than agro-industry. the report also highlights that 'trade agreements under negotiation such as the transatlantic trade and investment partnership (ttip), the eu-canada comprehensive economic and trade agreement (ceta) and the eu-mercosur free trade agreement threaten employment and the creation of favourable conditions for farmers'. finally, the report calls for the common agricultural policy (cap) to 'support organic and biodynamic farming more effectively'. i vote in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report has several positive points: efficient support for small and medium-sized farms, defence and promotion of pdos and pgi, local priority in markets and employment, questioning of free trade agreements (in their agricultural components), willingness to reuse price regulation tools on markets, etc. nevertheless, this report was tainted by the opinions of the femm and empl committees, which therefore incorporated the usual claims about migrants and gender issues. in this respect, paragraph 77 which promotes the social and economic integration of migrants and refugees (and their wives) into rural employment is demagogic, off-topic and therefore unacceptable, all the more so in a dual context of the agricultural and employment crisis. for this reason, and despite the elements of the agreement, the vote will be unfavourable.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the contribution of the cap to rural employment. the report is more about the socialist rapporteur's vision of the common agricultural policy than it is about genuine solutions to promote employment, crisis management, rebalancing aid between farms and territories and support for niche producers.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report. it is important, in the context of the forthcoming reform of the common agricultural policy, to make it an instrument for employment. tools to regulate markets and combat price volatility must therefore be put in place. finally, i very much share the report's stated aim of 'reterritorialising' agriculture around short circuits and the circular economy.
in writing. ‒ we must ask ourselves what the political motives are behind this non-legislative own-initiative report, which was opposed by a large number of members, with a large number of abstentions. the text is based on a systematic opposition of agricultural models, thus offering an unrealistic view of agriculture, supposedly based on small farms withdrawing into themselves while european agricultural exports are important. we have understood that the socialist rapporteur has used this report to propose a kind of re-foundation of the cap. yet his french socialist colleagues, and particularly stéphane le foll, have been conspicuous in their failure to speak for france in dealing with the unprecedented agricultural crisis in our country. the commission's proposal for a regulation on the common organization of the market in bananas is a very good one. like many colleagues, including michel dantin, i was opposed to this text, which promotes a gas-fired plant when our farmers are asking for simplicity and stability to be the keywords of agricultural policy.
in writing. ‒ in the face of the many crises facing the agricultural world, this report addresses the subject of the cap and employment for the first time. it advocated making the cap a genuine instrument for employment, while ensuring that the greatest number of people had access to healthy food. the report proposes to support the establishment of young farmers to promote generational renewal, but also to reactivate, by adapting them, the tools for regulating markets and combating price volatility, and to put an end to the laissez-faire of markets, which is devastating for farmers, employment and the economy of the territories. the aim is clear: to strengthen small and medium-sized farms to better support employment and sustainable development, as well as harmonious land use. as the cap review approaches, this report sets the stage for an agricultural policy that combines rural and modernity: innovation, apprenticeship, vocational training and collective organisation must be used to meet the challenges facing agriculture at the beginning of the 21st century! i voted for this report.
in writing. ‒ although there has been much debate on agricultural policy since the treaty of rome in 1957, the employment aspect of the policy had never been discussed until the report by eric andrieu. between 1957 and today, the agricultural population has risen from 20% to 4% of the total labour force in the european union, and more than one in five farms in the eu disappeared between 2007 and 2013. the analysis of eric andrieu, which i share, shows that the cap, by encouraging the outsourcing of production and the concentration of farms, has had a significant negative impact on rural employment and family farming. the report calls for a new social contract between farmers and citizens, which transforms the cap into a genuine instrument for employment, but also for healthy food, accessible to the greatest number. it must also enable young farmers to settle down, to ensure the renewal of farms. in this sense, small and medium-sized farms, which account for a very large share of production and are the most successful in terms of employment and sustainable development, deserve special attention.
in writing. ‒ the report starts from the observation that the economic crisis is particularly affecting rural areas and even more so territories with geographical handicaps. to address this, it calls on states to increase support for the cultivation of plant proteins (for which the eu depends on imports from third countries) and for the cultivation of local species (which contributes to the protection of biodiversity). it also called for the promotion of short supply chains and the development of quality systems, geographical indications and organic farming, which all share the same localised logic. i welcome these proposals and the affirmation, particularly welcome in the present context, of the positive role of migration in stimulating economic growth and social cohesion in rural areas. i would nevertheless like to express my disappointment (but not my surprise) that recital t of the version put to the vote, which stressed the negative consequences that ttip, as the commission itself admits, could have on rural areas by actually harming traditional agriculture, was deleted from the text by a vote of the epp, s&d and alde groups. i voted for it, though.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text in order to ensure, in particular, greater legal certainty for union fishermen. the court of justice of the european communities has supported the european parliament in stating that multiannual fisheries management plans, taken as a whole, constitute policy choices which should be decided on in the ordinary legislative process, in accordance with article 43 (2) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which is the legal basis of the treaty of lisbon for measures pursuing the objectives of common policies in the field of agriculture and fisheries. following that judgment, our socialist group has contributed constructively to the rapid development of a revised cod-fishing plan which is fully in line with the principles of the reformed cfp and can enter into force on 1 january 2017.
in writing. ‒ council regulation no 1342/2008 of 18 december 2008 was adopted before the entry into force of the tfeu and therefore confers decision-making powers on the council (articles 10 and 11). as the tfeu no longer allows for this possibility, the commission has therefore suggested an amendment to that regulation. the proposal is essentially aimed at improving and clarifying the provisions of the regulation. it implements the principles of the new common fisheries policy and supports its implementation. in substance, the old 2008 plan contained a complicated system of fishing effort (days at sea) that did not allow the stocks to be restored. i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ council regulation no 1342/2008 of 18 december 2008 was adopted before the entry into force of the tfeu and therefore confers decision-making powers on the council (articles 10 and 11). as the tfeu no longer allows for this possibility, the commission has therefore suggested an amendment to that regulation. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal, which is essentially aimed at improving and clarifying the provisions of the 2008 regulation, which seems to me to be in the right direction, both for the conservation of cod stocks and for the fisheries exploiting those stocks.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the long-term plan for cod stocks and the fisheries exploiting those stocks, amending council regulation no 1342/2008 of 18 december 2008. the principles of the new fisheries policy seem to us to be designed to preserve marine biodiversity.
in writing. ‒ regulation no 1342/2008 of 18 december 2008, which was adopted before the entry into force of the treaty on the functioning of the european union (tfeu), confers decision-making powers on the european council. since the tfeu no longer allows for this possibility, the european commission wanted to suggest an amendment to this regulation. the main purpose of this proposal is to clarify the provisions of the regulation and to implement the principles of the new common fisheries policy. i voted in favour of this amendment to the directive which should help to rebuild cod stocks.

in writing. - i abstained on this report. this text concerns the annual review of the activities of the european central bank (ecb). unlike the 2015 report for the year 2014, the european parliament decided this year to take a slightly more critical approach towards the ecb. the rapporteur therefore asks questions about the macroeconomic situation in europe and the latest measures taken by the central bank. it makes few favourable value judgments about the policy in place and expresses some relevant reservations. however, it does not go far enough to call into question the existence and the way the ecb works. it also remains blind to the consequences of austerity policies and the abandonment of monetary sovereignty by member states.
in writing. ‒ this annual report acknowledges that 'the effects on the real economy (of the ecb's actions) have been very limited'. but that doesn't mean that i question their logic. the report defends the independence of the ecb. it even asks governments to 'avoid statements calling into question the role played by the institution in the context of its mandate'. clearly, the ecb does what it wants and there is no complaining about it! above all, the report does not propose to finance the real economy directly and prefers to continue to fuel speculative bubbles by bailing out the banks. i am voting against this text.
in writing. ‒ this annual report reviews conventional and unconventional monetary policy instruments. the report is written in a polite tone and contains few value judgments in favour of the ecb's policy. it is clear that there are reservations about the transmission of quantitative easing (qe) to the real economy, about the questionable quality of collateral provided in exchange for cash, about the non-conditionality of some programmes in terms of lending to the real economy, about the risks of zero rates on the life insurance business model, about the risk of a bond crash in the event of a rate hike, about the delicate management of a qe exit (tapering), about the necessary sharing of tasks with the eba, etc. even if this opinion does not praise the actions of the president of the european central bank, mario draghi, our criticisms of the ecb's business model would go far beyond the mere reservations expressed in this report. that's why i abstained on this one.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this green paper is to launch a debate on how the european market for retail financial services could be further opened. the main recommendation is to establish mutual trust, in particular by ensuring consumer protection and the free movement of businesses in their cross-border activities. we oppose this desire to further expand the single market because it has proved to be more problematic and inconvenient than beneficial, in particular because of economic, cultural and regulatory disparities. we therefore fear that the establishment of the single market for retail financial services will cause serious damage to our national economy and that future market disparities will be corrected by even more technocratic administration and control from brussels. moreover, crossborder purchases of retail financial services are a serious threat to our banking sovereignty and to the future of our citizens in the event of the euro's demise. this single market is intended to appear as a means of offering more freedom to the consumer, but it is above all an additional chain that the commission wants to throw on the member states to force them not to leave the euro area or the european union. i therefore voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ this green paper aims to strengthen the european market for retail financial services such as current accounts, retirement savings solutions, real estate project financing and personal or property insurance. the project would increase competition between financial institutions in favour of customers' purchasing power. to achieve this, the text advocates establishing mutual trust by ensuring consumer protection and the liberalisation of banking/insurance in crossborder areas. we believe, on the contrary, that the establishment of the european single market highlights above all the economic, legislative and regulatory disparities that exist between the member states. we are therefore rightly concerned that the european commission will correct these disparities by strengthening european regulation and legislation to the detriment of our national sovereignty. the single market is therefore, above all, a further step in the economic, monetary and financial integration of the european union. i therefore opposed the report.
in writing. ‒ the commission published a green paper and a public consultation in december 2015 to assess the feasibility of a european market for retail financial services. the commission's objective is to identify the remaining obstacles to cross-border activities in the area of retail financial services, taking into account the digitalisation of these services and technological developments. this report is therefore the european parliament's contribution to the debate on the creation of a european market for retail financial services. a european market for retail financial services will have very positive consequences for consumers, investors, smes, fintechs and businesses. however, it seems difficult to achieve in the present state of affairs. many barriers, which cannot be overcome by the digitalisation of services alone, persist, such as regulatory barriers (different tax, social, health systems, etc.), geographical and cultural barriers (languages). it is also important not to rush into legislative work in order to avoid creating duplicates with the european legislation that has recently been created in this field. i voted in favour of this report, for which i am the rapporteur for the epp.

in writing. ‒ in 2002, the monterrey conference was supposed to move us from an era of concern about the volume of development aid to one of questioning the quality of it. in 2005, the paris declaration promised to align donor countries with the development goals of recipient countries. in 2011, the global partnership was to work towards decoupling the provision of this aid from any conditions imposed by the donor country. it is 2016 and the failure of these ambitions is clear. not only has the volume of aid not reached the level requested since 1970, but far from being aligned with local needs, aid is increasingly being used to serve the interests of european businesses, including in the fight against climate change, when it is not diverted to migration control. this report only very partially reflects this reality. it also takes a position which is contrary to the principles it sets out by claiming to decide what the aid should be used for in the first place. i abstained.

in writing. ‒ the report consists of a series of amendments by the envi committee concerning the reduction of national emissions of directive 2001/81/ec setting national ceilings for certain air pollutants. the purpose of this text is to replace the abovementioned directive, in particular in line with the international commitments of the european union (gothenburg protocol, 1999). the ceilings imposed on member states are intended to achieve 70% of the maximum technically feasible reduction in health effects, as defined by the who. they shall be determined unilaterally by the commission. i cannot support the inclusion of methane in the scope of the directive, because such an inclusion would constitute an unacceptable constraint on the agricultural sector, let alone the gas sector which includes a growing share of biomethane.

in writing. ‒ this report aims to amend directive 2001/81/ec which sets national emission ceilings for certain air pollutants such as sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxide, ammonia and methane. the revision calls for the member states to tighten up their legislation in order to achieve ambitious targets for 2020 and 2030. on the one hand, this report considerably strengthens the regulatory power of the commission and the prerogatives of the european union in the development of emission reduction programmes to the detriment of our national sovereignty. the rapporteur also calls for a reduction in methane emissions, which will increase the pressure on the agricultural sector, which is already facing serious difficulties due to the fall in the price of raw materials, the russian embargo and the proliferation of free trade agreements. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the reduction of national emissions of air pollutants, which is part of the commission's legislative package on improving air quality. this is a first reading agreement on the downward revision of national emission ceilings for five pollutants for 2020. ambitious emission reduction commitments are needed to address the health and environmental impacts of air pollutants. the agreement reached in the trilogue excludes the emission of enteric methane from ruminants from the scope of the directive. this withdrawal helps to protect european agriculture and to maintain coherence between the union's policies, in particular environmental policy and the common agricultural policy.
in writing. ‒ this report proposes to adopt the outcome of the interinstitutional negotiations on the directive on national emission ceilings for pollutants (necd). the aim of this text is to replace the current eu regime for the annual capping of national emissions of air pollutants and to ensure that the national emission ceilings for member states apply until 2020. i fully share the objectives of this text, which aims in particular to reduce the impact on human health of pollutant emissions, which cause a large number of deaths each year. i was also particularly committed, in the agri and envi committees, to ensuring that these limits were nevertheless reasonable and realistic as regards methane (ch4) and more particularly enteric methane. enteric methane, which is a waste product exclusively from ruminant farming, is very difficult to reduce unless the animals are confined all year round. i am glad that enteric methane is no longer included in the ceilings in question and that at the same time the level of ambition of this legislation has remained very high. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. i supported the directive on the reduction of national emissions of certain air pollutants. since air quality is a common problem for all member states, the fight against air pollution is one of the main missions of the european union. this directive will allow us to step up our efforts by limiting the emissions of europe's biggest air pollutants with binding targets for 2020, 2025 and 2030. while air pollution is responsible for around 400 000 premature deaths in the european union each year, i welcome the ambitious target we have set to reduce by 2030 the mortality due to air pollution by almost 50%.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the revision of a directive setting national emission ceilings for five pollutants. it is important that regulations protect european citizens from environmental pollution, which is a public health problem to be taken very seriously. the directive sets ambitious targets, such as the reduction of deaths due to air pollution by 50%. but at the same time it includes realistic national emission ceilings which respect the principle of subsidiarity of the member states. thus, each country can and must commit to reducing its emissions of air pollutants. i am also pleased that enteric methane has been excluded from the substances listed in this directive. it seemed relatively difficult to integrate it in a consistent way, as emissions of this methane are very difficult to measure. this exclusion was essential in the interest of european farmers.

in writing. ‒ air pollution is the number one environmental health risk in europe, causing more than 430 000 premature deaths in europe each year, including more than 50 000 in france. in response to this, the european commission presented its 'air quality' legislative package in december 2013. the main objective of this draft legislation is to address the health risks and environmental effects of air pollution. despite the good intentions of this report on emissions of certain pollutants, it is disappointing in several respects: firstly, it lacks ambition on the emission thresholds for pollutants. on the other hand, the overseas territories are excluded from the scope of the draft legislation on which the report we are voting on today is based. this differential treatment between the metropolis and the overseas territories cannot be tolerated; all citizens, whether local or european, should be able to benefit from the same protection of air quality. i therefore vote against this text.
in writing. - i voted against this text. the aim of this report is to amend directive 2001/81/ec setting national ceilings for certain air pollutants. it aims to increase the limits imposed on member states and make all reduction commitments binding by 2025. we cannot accept this text which considerably strengthens the regulatory power of the commission, as well as the prerogatives of the european union over the member states in the elaboration and implementation of national emission reduction programmes.
in writing. ‒ in december 2013, the european commission adopted a set of proposals to improve air quality in europe, called the 'air quality package'. the proposal before us revises this directive to introduce controls on the various types of air pollution in each member state. the aim is to halve the number of premature deaths - estimated at 400 000 per year in the eu - caused by air pollution by 2030. however, during the negotiations with the council, key elements of the proposal were deleted. thus, methane and mercury are no longer covered by emission limits. member states will be allowed to average their emissions over three years in the event of a dry summer or a cold winter. finally, the binding interim (2015) targets proposed by parliament were removed. in short, the proposal is devoid of substance. good job on the lobbyists! you deserve your pay. i am voting against this text which ignores the public health objectives.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this text is to bring it into line with the european union's international commitments (gothenburg protocol, 1999). the aim of this revision is to set targets for 2020 and 2030 for the reduction of emissions of the main polluting gases: sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, non-methane volatile organic compounds and ammonia. this report is not, in my view, satisfactory because it considerably strengthens the regulatory power of the commission and the prerogatives of the european union over the member states in the development and implementation of national emission reduction programmes. furthermore, we cannot support the inclusion of methane in the scope of the directive, as such inclusion would constitute an unacceptable constraint on the agricultural sector. i therefore voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ the report consists of a series of amendments by the envi committee concerning the reduction of national emissions within the meaning of directive 2001/81/ec setting national ceilings for certain air pollutants. the aim of this revision is to set targets for 2020 and 2030 for the reduction of emissions of the main polluting gases. we are not satisfied with this report in many respects. it significantly strengthens the commission's regulatory power and reinforces the eu's prerogatives over the member states in the development and implementation of national emission reduction programmes. the text also abolishes certain facilities previously granted to states. in particular, we cannot support the inclusion of methane in the scope of the directive, because such inclusion would constitute an unacceptable constraint for the agricultural sector. i vote against.

in writing. ‒ the basel committee develops prudential rules in the form of recommendations which can be transposed into national and european law by the competent authorities. since the 2008 financial crisis, these rules have been aimed at forcing banks to increase their own funds in order to improve their solvency, with the aim of making them more resilient to financial instability scenarios. the report considers that the new regulations, which are aimed at increasing the solvency ratios of european banks, must not undermine the competitiveness of our banking sector. in conjunction with the capital markets union, the application of basel iv could increase the competitive disadvantage of our banks. i voted in favour of this text which warns european and national authorities against the consequences of overly restrictive regulation.

in writing. this resolution endorses the state of play of the discussions on the new global banking standards known as basel iii. they were set out in 2010 and were supposed to respond to the 2008 crisis, but have not yet entered into force because of a lack of agreement on how to implement them. the basel committee is an oligarchic institution composed only of the central bankers of the countries with the largest banks. the ecb is represented, but the national regulators of the majority of eu countries are not! the resolution does not say a word about the questionable legitimacy of such an institution. she's also clueless about the diagnosis of the financial system. it says nothing about speculation and makes only marginal reference to the dangers of securitisation. it gives priority to the assessment and compensation of financial risks but not at all to their prevention. the resolution also says nothing about the misappropriation of central bank liquidity without the real economy ever seeing the colour. on the contrary, it grants a credit to the ecb. i am voting against this resolution which makes no useful proposal in the face of the increased dangers of financial capitalism.

in writing. ‒ this text is an objection by the envi committee to the renewal of the active substance bentazone. bentazone is a commonly used pesticide, particularly for peas, beans and potatoes. doubts remain about its harmfulness to humans and the environment, despite several encouraging studies. in particular, bentazone may infiltrate surface and groundwater. in addition, there are still doubts about the danger of bentazone to human health, although according to the conclusions of several scientific studies, including those of the world health organisation, this is dependent on the absorption of very high doses of bentazone. in view of the importance of this information, the 'confirmatory information' procedure is contrary to the precautionary principle and cannot be used as a basis for granting an authorisation for a period of 15 years (the maximum period). for all these reasons, the enf group supports the objection calling on the commission to carry out the additional assessments necessary for the renewal of bentazone before renewing it. i therefore voted in favour of this objection.

in writing. - i voted against this bentazone objection. this substance, which is one of the only effective ones, is used on certain vegetables to control toxic plants such as date palms, blackberries and redwoods. it has also been approved as safe by the european food safety authority. the political groups which have tabled this objection are more in favour of their dogmatic positions than the interests of farmers and, more broadly, of european citizens.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which recommends not to renew the authorisation of the herbicide bentazone. bentazone can easily reach groundwater and could be toxic to human reproduction. the european commission must take into account all the necessary data confirming the safety of a given substance before issuing authorisations, especially since the european food safety authority (efsa) collegial review has proposed that the active substance bentazone be classified as toxic for reproduction category 2.

in writing. ‒ bentazone is a pesticide commonly used, particularly for peas, beans and potatoes. there are concerns about its harmfulness to humans and the environment:- bentazone can infiltrate surface and groundwater. this contamination depends in part on the type of soil and its porosity and is hampered by the rapid photodegradation of this substance. - there are also doubts about the danger of bentazone to human health, although according to the conclusions of several scientific studies, including those of the who, this is dependent on the absorption of very high doses of bentazone. the objection rightly points out that many assessments remain necessary for the grant of authorisation: these include assessments of the risk to the consumer and the possibility of infiltration of groundwater and surface water. in view of the importance of this information, the 'confirmatory information' procedure is contrary to the precautionary principle and cannot be used as a basis for granting an authorisation for a period of 15 years (the maximum period). i therefore voted in favour of this objection.

create an even greater instability. i will not go into what is happening in jordan, but the economic and social consequences of what is happening around that country are obviously considerable. tourism has plummeted, exports have slowed because jordan's natural trade outlets, syria and iraq, are totally devastated, growth is stalling, unemployment has skyrocketed. so we have a country that is both politically stable but in great difficulty economically and socially. in spite of this, jordan faces another challenge, a colossal and considerable one, that of welcoming hundreds of thousands of refugees from these warring countries, who are fleeing persecution and poverty. i would remind you that in jordan, the refugees are less in camps than in cities, where the jordanian authorities are trying to integrate them, to allow them to work, and all this with great dignity. this should be a challenge to those of us who know a little about the situation in this country, as europeans also faced with this refugee crisis, but with responses that sometimes take a long time to come and in any case a generosity that we do not really show. so, faced with this exceptional situation, the european institutions have obviously decided to provide aid, relief to jordan through what is called 'macro-financial assistance' (mfa). of course, there are other ways to help this country, this is not the only one. the commission is also working to make the rules of origin for jordanian products more flexible and there is talk of negotiating a trade agreement which is both asymmetrical and progressive. but in any case, we discussed this macrofinancial assistance in the inta committee and reached an initial agreement. there were technical elements, since we had to accept the amendments introduced by the council to the commission's text. this did not take us long, but of course we mainly discussed the amount. there was unanimity in the inta committee, both right and left, to try to propose a much higher amount than the one suggested by the commission, which was only 200 million euros. there was an interesting debate. we felt that the jordanians' financing needs were great and the rapporteur. mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin by thanking my co-rapporteurs for the quality of their contribution, the warmth of our reports and the ability to reach a very broad consensus. it should be recalled that transport, which is essential for the movement of people and goods, is a fundamental element of the internal market. in addition to the often troubled public transport, smes in the transport sector - or should i say 'mobility' - represent a key and often the main activity of the sector, a key element of mobility, especially in urban centres, and a dynamic source of growth and therefore of job creation to meet the ever-increasing demand for mobility. the challenges facing european transport smes as a whole are of different kinds. they face a regulatory challenge firstly due to the complexity, inherent costs and wide disparity of access rules to regulated professions; secondly, an economic challenge linked to the high costs and the perennial problem of financing with difficult access to credit for limited investment capacity; thirdly, an environmental challenge resulting from congestion, emissions and dependence on fossil fuels; fourth, to a technological challenge with the emergence of the new economy, intermediation platforms, empowerment, automation and vehicle connectivity. the last point leads me to emphasize the emergence of a new phenomenon in this context. it was in the transport sector that the collaborative economy first made its most spectacular breakthrough. the term "uberization" is a testament to this. this new economy brings positive technological and commercial breakthroughs, but also poses some problems for traditional players and regulators. the advances brought about by the collaborative economy are numerous: improvement of the quality and fluidity of existing services; security of the actors for the benefit of the consumer; i am talking about the gains in trust generated by the identification and mutual notification of the consumer and the service provider; enhancing the security of transactions; the creation of a new type of selfemployed, often low-income, who contribute both to growth and to the reduction of unemployment. however, we should not forget the challenges posed by this platform economy, starting with the definition and management of the relationship between these platforms and service providers, both for taxation and social protection or the security of legal stability. secondly, should the nature of the service offered by the provider to the private individual be described as 'commercial' or 'cost-sharing' in the context of co-consumption? in addition, and as a consequence of the above, the question arises of the tax and social status of the actors in the collaborative economy and the differentiation between the sharing economy for non-profit providers and the for-profit platform economy. data protection is obviously an important subject, not to mention relations with the so-called "classic" transport economy and corporations. access to regulated professions is often complex, restricted and varies across member states. the answer to all these problems implies, on the one hand, improving the environment for smes in the sector by reducing their administrative burden, by simplifying their access to credit, and even to research, by modernising the status of the professions and by facilitating access to new technologies for traditional players. this response also implies the convergence between the classical economy and the new collaborative economy at european level by the harmonisation of the statutes and rules of access to the professions, by the determination of what is a matter of sharing and what is a matter of profit in a commercial activity, by the harmonisation of tax and social regimes in order to ensure identical rules between the classical economy and the new economy and by the progress towards european frameworks that define the status of the professions and their economic framework. my dear colleagues, these are the challenges ahead. i am glad that this report has received very broad support from my colleagues in the committee on transport. i hope it will be useful in moving towards greater efficiency, growth, employment and sustainability in the service of citizens and i look forward to listening to your speeches with great interest.
for the greens/efa group mr president, commissioner, every day european citizens ask themselves about their transport, about their daily life. they live, as we do, with this digital wave which is a positive evolution and which brings the multiplication of platforms that heat our existing models. among these platforms, we find new ethical business models that pursue values of sharing, climate protection and social connection. this is a little bit of what the collaborative economy should be based on and, from this, we should think that a collaborative economy can benefit everyone, whether it is the manufacturer, the driver, the passengers or the environment. our role as legislators is to anticipate technological change without inhibiting innovation. that is why i want to say that there is an urgent need for a strict regulatory framework and i am making this appeal to the european commission because there are still too many legal uncertainties which are hindrances to the development of the collaborative economy. in this regulatory framework, we must, on the one hand, define what a platform for the collaborative economy is based on cost sharing as opposed to platforms that provide professional services and, on the other hand, harmonise the rules at european level. there are two other reasons why the sharing economy needs to be regulated. firstly, to protect it from itself, because it is a sector which is still immature and which has a tendency to monopolize. secondly, rules should be established to ensure that competition is not unfair and does not encourage fiscal or social dumping. this risk of dumping exists. it's when a small category of people use collaborative platforms to make a business out of it. it is therefore on this condition that the collaborative economy can flourish within a regulatory framework... member of the commission. – mr president, this was a really good and constructive discussion and i thank the honourable members for all their contributions and comments and for the debate. it shows me that parliament is taking a position in many respects very similar to that of the commission, especially when it comes to modernisation of the regulatory frameworks. among other things, emerging business models may indeed raise problems of legal uncertainty with regard to the application of the existing legal framework. we also agree that we need to distinguish between profit-making and cost-sharing activities. this is, again, in line with the commission’s communication on the collaborative economy. in that communication, besides a clear definition of terms, the commission also made very clear that operators in the collaborative economy should comply with rules that are well designed to ensure consumer protection, safety and security, adequate working conditions and training and fiscal compliance. with this report, parliament calls on the commission and member states to combat anti-competitive practices. the reaction of member states to the emergence of new players has indeed been diverse and the commission is following the developments. whether or not the commission needs to intervene will depend on case-by-case assessment. when appropriate, the commission may use its competition-policy tools to guarantee the proper functioning of the market with access for smes. we take note of parliament’s call on the commission to continue monitoring the developments and impact of the collaborative economy and the digital agenda. monitoring exchanges of best practices and enforcement are among the key actions that the commission intends to pursue, as explained in the communication of 2 june 2016. here, i can also assure you, once again, that we keep smes constantly in mind. not long ago, i was one of them. therefore we will be paying special attention to ensure open systems and access to customers, especially in the digital age, while at the same time ensuring that safety is not compromised.
the rapporteur. mr president, dear commissioner, dear violeta, dear colleagues, first of all i would like to thank you for your contribution to the clarity and quality of the contributions that have been made, and for the excellent spirit that has guided the preparation of this report. beyond the large public transport companies, the majority of transport in europe is therefore provided by these millions of craftsmen, self-employed people and smes who have to face environmental challenges and technological advances that upset their working and living conditions. europe should support their adaptation to these rapid changes by improving their environment and by focusing its action on the following priorities: more effective, simpler and cheaper regulation; more legible, stable and attractive taxation; access to credit that needs to be simplified, accelerated and more effective; and social protection and tax equality. the explosive development in transport of these new technologies of the platform economy also requires a rapid and powerful effort on our part, namely a harmonisation of the regulations of access and exercise which are sometimes corporatist and differ greatly from one territory to another, as well as an effort of convergence towards a european definition and regulation of the activities of digital platforms in transport. a word on amendment no 37, which has been mentioned several times. it is not a question of regulating, much less over-regulating, but of asking the commission to look into a new problem, that of light commercial vehicles in international transport. this totally unforeseeable but new phenomenon has caused enough concern in a number of member states for nine of them to address the commission with a letter co-signed by nine ministers. i think it is not a question of regulating, but of seeing clearly and, if new elements are introduced, of thinking about them together. finally, this own-initiative report - this modest report, madam commissioner - is intended to encourage the european commission to propose as quickly and effectively as possible the necessary measures to support the harmonization and convergence of all types of undertakings in the field of transport.
in writing. the impact of the digital economy and the rapid development of platforms in transport is a reality that the european legislator can no longer ignore. the issues are many, from the protection of workers' rights to access to the profession of driver to the legal responsibility of platforms. the report before us contains positive elements in the fight against social dumping, the training of drivers and the fight against monopolies. i also welcome the distinction between platforms that generate real benefits and the collaborative economy, which is fundamentally based on cost sharing. however, i regret that this report does not take into account the risks of driver insecurity using platforms such as uber. i also disagree with the paragraphs that seek to limit the ability of states to regulate these platforms; this is contrary to the message sent in favour of a modernised regulatory framework. finally, i believe that carriers using these platforms should be regulated as 'transport companies'. the digital medium is only a tool for the service provider who offers a well-defined service: passenger transport!
on behalf of the enf group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, energy security based on federalism is putting our peoples in an energy insecure situation. you are denying the states the fundamental freedom to contract, to ensure their own energy security in full sovereignty, which is contrary to subsidiarity, but above all to efficiency. only long-term contracts with the state, by virtue of the economic visibility they give, allow for long-term investment in private or state capacity. the liberalization of energy leads us into the short-term cheap-sell mentality and thereby undermines long-term security and profitability. by subjecting the energy diplomacy of the states to the good will of brussels through short-term thinking, the liberalization of a natural monopoly and your political diplomacy, you are committing to total energy insecurity.
mr president, i would like to congratulate the ombudsman on her work. i wanted to ask you about two things: access to documents and the problem of the links of interest between the commission's experts, particularly the euratom treaty. as regards access to documents, you know that the commission refused to give the documents, either to greenpeace or to pan europe, concerning glyphosate, the active substance in roundup. the court, and in particular the court of justice of the european union, had said that access to these documents should normally be granted. the commission had appealed. yesterday, and for that reason this report is timely, the court of justice of the european union gave the associations a victory. this shows that when you are caught, you are given even more power to access the documents of the commission, but also of agencies such as efsa. the second point concerns the links of interest between the experts. madam ombudsman, i called you to ask for the names of the experts and the interests of the euratom treaty experts who had been the origin of the maximum permissible limits in the event of a nuclear accident. i got the names, but not the connections of interest, and you told me that it's up to the panel to decide whether to communicate, yes or no, those connections. so i really ask you, and the commission and the states, to make sure that you have more power to ensure that we have access to this information.
mr president, madam ombudsman, i am going to go off the beaten track. i want to raise awareness of a subject that has never been discussed and yet there is much to be said and done. i am talking about the european parliament. hundreds of parliamentary clerks work in this institution, and the precariousness of their employment contracts means that they have little interest in complaining. they can be thanked simply by a declaration of no confidence, and this is at the discretion of the member. it's cool! yet sexual harassment is a reality, and there is no listening, counselling or alerting structure here. it's a lack, it's a pain! sexual harassment has no color, it has no smell and it has no political color. it is therefore urgent to put in place monitoring tools to help victims so that the omerta is no longer a problem here. we need a real status for parliamentary staff so that they can better defend their rights. we cannot be the world's disciplinarians here without putting our own house in order. the victims are therefore counting on you, madam ombudsman, and i hope that you will take a strong initiative.
for the gue/ngl group mr president, the guarani-kaiowá people are one of the symbols of the struggle of indigenous peoples. for decades they have fought against the plundering of their ancestral lands and paid a heavy price for it. the demarcation of their territory, which was recognized in 1988, is still not a reality. the amazon lands are very appealing. deforestation, land grabbing for food, energy, forestry, and mining industries, intensive livestock farming, and huge dams have destroyed a third of the amazon rain forest. while they are a bulwark against climate change, they are the first victims of it via the agrofuel frenzy. the european union is an important trade partner of brazil its first partner and therefore has responsibilities. it cannot turn a blind eye to the human and environmental costs of the policies it promotes and the products it imports, nor can it escape the responsibility of european multinationals. it's time to act.

in writing. ‒ in the face of the financial crisis, the ageing population, the increase in the amount invested in occupational pension by capitalisation, and the capacity of the sector to invest in long-term assets, the commission proposed a review of the iorp1 in 2014 which presents several dangers: the creation of a single occupational pension market will enable iorps to offer their products in all member states by removing regulatory barriers to cross-border activities. this will give a definite advantage to european countries with a long experience of pension funds, in particular the benelux whose financial centres have already anticipated the benefits that this new european market could offer; new rules on the placement of risky assets which will encourage risk-taking by institutions that do not have the financial and human resources to make such investments; the introduction of rules allowing the creation of european pension funds on the american model, with the risks that the latest financial crisis has brought to light; the commission has also proposed that the pension scheme should be gradually replaced by a system of capitalisation pensions, which the french have rejected. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which provides for the continuation of efforts towards the establishment of an internal market for occupational pension schemes at european level. the purpose of this directive is to propose minimum harmonisation in this area in order to facilitate the mobility of workers between member states.
in writing. ‒ this recast of the directive proposes to support the development of a european occupational pension market and to deregulate existing standards to copy the so-called american model of pension funds. the text also goes in the direction of creating a single market for occupational pensions, and the risks are many: favourable regulation for large investment funds, rules for placing assets that are too risky or the promotion of capitalised pensions. i voted against it.
‒ i opposed this report and the commission's proposal, which are aimed at creating a single occupational pension market. i am certainly aware of the issues surrounding occupational pension institutions, as there are currently 125 000 occupational pension funds across the european union, holding eur 2 500 billion in assets on behalf of 75 million europeans. i note some good ideas from the commission, such as the obligation to monitor remuneration, a better estimation of risks and improved information for savers. however, behind its good intentions lies the real desire to deregulate existing standards in favour of the emergence of an 'american model', which will have the real consequences of favouring large investment funds and rules for placing assets that are too risky, but also, and above all, it will lead to the promotion of pension systems by capitalisation and therefore, ultimately, to a challenge to national pension systems by distribution. this is a debate that we are entitled to have, but at the national level, and not imposed by brussels in order to realize its dream of americanization of europe.
in writing. ‒ on 27 march 2014, the commission proposed a recast of directive 2003/41/ec on the activities and supervision of institutions for occupational retirement provision (pension funds). the aim of this revision is to modernise the legislation on pension funds to make it more closely aligned with demographic developments and, in particular, with the ageing of the population. furthermore, pension funds were severely affected by the economic and financial crisis of 2008. it was important to put in place a regulatory framework that would strengthen their resilience. a pension fund is an investment fund which invests the retirement savings of many employees to make them grow. it is essential to ensure their good governance. i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ this codecision report aims to facilitate the development of occupational retirement savings. considering that this new regulation improves the governance of pension funds, increases transparency of information for members and beneficiaries of pension schemes, improves the supervision of pension funds and sets new rules for transfer activities and transfers, i have decided to support this report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the proposal for a directive on the activities and supervision of institutions for occupational retirement provision. with ageing populations, institutions, known as occupational pension institutions, are developing, using financial markets to provide retirement benefits. since this phenomenon affects all the member states of the union, it is essential that we update the european regulatory framework on the supervision of these institutions. by achieving minimum harmonisation, in particular by clarifying the procedures allowing these institutions to carry out cross-border activity, we are protecting european citizens more and are encouraging the development of the activity of these institutions throughout the european territory.
in writing. ‒ vote against: this directive can be seen as part of a desire to gradually replace divided pensions with capitalised pension systems, which has always been rejected by the french.
in writing. ‒ it is perhaps not without reason that a text on occupational pension funds and another calling for the promotion of a european market for retail financial services, including voluntary retirement savings for individuals, are voted on in the same session. this is two of the three possible levels of old age insurance with public schemes. the aim is to create a european occupational pension market and to change existing standards on the model of us pension funds, in particular by facilitating cross-border activities and international portfolio transfers within the single market, despite the diversity of social and labour rights. of course, some concessions are made in terms of prudential or governance rules, or in terms of information for savers. but all this does not compensate for the shortcomings of the text, in particular the widening of the asset classes in which these funds could invest, increasing the risk. nor does it succeed in concealing its underlying philosophy: the promotion of capitalised pensions at the expense of public systems based on distribution. it is true that the stakes are enormous and that the appetite is high. it is for the states, and the states alone, to define the nature, extent, organisation and functioning of their social protection.
in writing. ‒ this recast of the directive proposes to support the development of a european occupational pension market and to deregulate existing standards to copy the us model of pension funds. the danger of favourable regulation of investment funds, of rules on the placement of assets which are too risky and of the promotion of capitalised pensions is obvious. the latter is obviously a first step towards challenging the national pensions system by distribution. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report by my colleague brian hayes on occupational pension schemes. these institutions are bodies which provide employment-related pension benefits in parallel with public pension and social security systems. the report, which is based on the principles of free movement of capital and freedom of provision, seeks to provide a framework for these entities to guarantee a secure occupational pension system for citizens. the rapporteur therefore calls for a more healthy remuneration policy, a reduction in the gender pension gap and more transparency towards members. i welcome the fact that this report was adopted by a large majority.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which aims to facilitate the development of occupational retirement savings with the dual objective of modernisation and transparency. the text improves the governance of pension funds, increases transparency in the provision of information to members and beneficiaries of pension schemes, improves the supervision of pension funds and lays down new rules for transfer activities.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it proposes to support the development of a european occupational pension market and to dismantle the pension branch of social security to copy the american model of pension funds. such a system would probably be acceptable to françois fillon and his friends in the lr who voted for it, but not to me.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the activities and supervision of occupational pension institutions. the commission's objective is to create a single market for occupational pensions which will enable all iorps to offer their products in all member states. the aim is therefore to remove the regulatory barriers that hinder crossborder activities, which will give a definite advantage to countries with long experience of pension funds. in addition, the new rules on asset placement are also dangerous because they encourage risk-taking by institutions that do not have the financial and human resources to make such investments. and the quantitative prudential requirements required are insufficient to cover the beneficiaries of supplementary pension schemes. the ultimate aim of this recast directive is to introduce rules to allow the creation of european pension funds on the american model, with the risks that the last financial crisis has brought to light. this directive can also be seen as part of a desire to gradually replace divided pensions with capitalised pension systems, which has always been rejected by the french.
in writing. ‒ this recast of the directive proposes to support the development of a european occupational pension market and to deregulate existing standards to copy the us model of pension funds. the text also goes in the direction of creating a single market for occupational pensions, and there are many risks: favourable regulation for large investment funds, rules for placing assets that are too risky or the promotion of capitalised pensions. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ pension schemes (public pillar one, private pillar two and three) and in particular those in the second and third pillars form a significant part of the financial sector. the proposal aims to use these available resources to stimulate investment. it takes account of the operation of pension funds following the deepwater horizon case, when the us authorities asked bp and shell to compensate for environmental damage. and that impacted the investment of pension funds in these companies. the proposal therefore takes environmental and social risks into account in the risk analysis. it promotes the establishment of an effective information system for all beneficiaries... but the responsibility of private institutions is very little questioned. similarly, pension funds are treated as financial products which must be treated as marketable goods on the eu financial markets. finally, the proposal does not allow for a clear separation between the private and the public pension systems, as my group has called for. the report does improve the commission's proposal, so i shall abstain.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal concerns a recast of directive 2003/41/ec on occupational pension institutions, known as iorp1. in the face of the financial crisis, the ageing population, the increase in the amount invested in occupational retirement by capitalisation, and the sector's ability to invest in long-term assets, the commission proposed a review of iorp1 in 2014 with the following objectives: to improve governance, to improve saver information through the introduction of the pbs, to facilitate cross-border activities and international portfolio transfers within the single market, to encourage long-term investment by allowing iorps to invest in more asset classes. the proposal for a directive aims to support the development of a european occupational pension market and to deregulate existing standards to replicate the us model of pension funds. the dangers are: favourable regulation for large investment funds, rules on investing too risky assets and the promotion of capitalised pensions. i therefore voted against the commission proposal and the legislative resolution.
in writing. ‒ the reform of the iorp directive would largely introduce funded pension schemes. the risk for a country like france is that it is preparing to abandon the distribution model to which the citizens are attached. again, the aim is to promote financial markets and established players in professional savings products, mainly in luxembourg or belgium. the risk on funded pensions, in a time of negative rates and high market volatility, is too high to be encouraged further. i vote against.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposal concerns a recast of directive 2003/41/ec on occupational pension institutions, known as iorp1. this directive suggests a desire to move a little more towards a private funded pension system. i therefore vote against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the directive of the european parliament and of the council on the activities and supervision of institutions for occupational retirement provision. the aim of this text is to modernise this legislation so that it is fairer and more in line with demographic developments and, in particular, the ageing of the population. it provides in particular for clarification of the procedures allowing institutions to carry out cross-border activity and for the removal of unnecessary obstacles to such activity, in order to improve the functioning of the internal market in this field.
in writing. pension schemes constitute a significant part of the financial resources available within the union and the purpose of this directive is to use these resources to motivate investment. in order to ensure worker mobility, the directive seeks to unify pension systems in order to facilitate worker mobility within the eu. while significant progress has been made in the development of the text, such as the inclusion of environmental and social data in the fund's investments, aimed at increasing transparency and information for beneficiaries, the nature of the pension fund remains and parliament's requests to further restrict investment opportunities to ensure its security have not been heard. in fact, despite some positive progress, the result is not satisfactory, which is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which provides for greater protection, transparency, information and security in the way occupational pension funds are managed. providers of occupational pension schemes wishing to move their operations across national borders will now have to receive the approval of a majority of their members and the support of regulators in both the home and the beneficiary countries.
in writing. ‒ this recast of the directive proposes to support the development of a european occupational pension market and to deregulate existing standards to copy the us model of pension funds. however, the pitfalls are: regulations that are too favourable to large investment funds, rules on investment of assets that are too risky, promotion of pension by capitalisation (as opposed to the distribution model). i voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted for this resolution to make the fight against violence against women and girls a priority for all! 45% of women in europe have experienced gender-based violence at least once in their lives. because of the lack of harmonisation of policies in this area at european level, they are not protected in the same way depending on the country in which they live. there is a tool to better protect women, prevent violence and prosecute those responsible: the council of europe's istanbul convention, the first international legally binding instrument on the subject. although all the member states have signed the convention, only 14 of them have ratified it, including france. for this reason, the european commission proposed in march 2016 that the european union could accede to the istanbul convention. this would be a very important step forward in further harmonising measures to combat this unacceptable gender-based violence which persists in europe today.
in writing. ‒ the council of europe convention on preventing and combating violence against women is an international treaty adopted in 2011 in istanbul. it aims to eradicate all acts of gender-based violence which cause women physical, sexual, psychological or economic harm or suffering. it imposes a binding legal framework prohibiting forced marriage, female genital mutilation, forced sterilization and sexual harassment. it should also be noted that the convention includes more questionable objectives, particularly on abortion. by august 2016, 42 countries had signed it, including all member states, and 21 countries had ratified it, including 14 member states, including france. the joint motion for a resolution calls on the council and the commission to speed up the negotiations with a view to acceding to the convention and calls on the member states to ratify it. the text also emphasises the protection of refugees and women seeking asylum. the eu has no diplomatic legitimacy to ratify such a convention. once again, this is an attack on the sovereignty of the member states, which will now be forced to ratify it. i therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ the guarantee and promotion of equality between women and men is an indisputable objective of the european union, guaranteed by the treaties. the accession of the union to the istanbul convention will help the union to ensure a coherent legal framework to prevent and combat violence against women. for this reason, i welcomed the commission's proposal to sign and conclude the accession and therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. ‒ while the aim of this resolution is laudable, i consider that the european union has no diplomatic legitimacy to ratify such a convention, which would impose it on the member states, who should be the ones to decide. the european union would once again overstep its bounds and undermine the sovereignty of states, which is why i voted against the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote against this motion for a resolution on the accession of the european union to the istanbul convention on preventing and combating violence against women. in my view, the signing of international conventions and treaties must remain the prerogative of sovereign states, the only ones capable of playing an effective and legitimate diplomatic role at international level. i would remind you that france has already ratified the istanbul convention. of course, some forms of violence, especially against women, are intolerable, such as female genital mutilation and forced sterilization. i am surprised, however, that other types of violence are not included in the same bag, such as the submission to the veil and religion in some communal areas in europe, or the impossibility, for some women who wish to have access to alternative solutions to abortion. finally, i found it difficult to see how women refugees and asylum seekers could be entitled to greater protection and consideration than european women, as appears to be the case in this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the istanbul convention on preventing and combating violence against women aims to eradicate all acts of gender-based violence that cause physical, sexual, psychological or economic harm and suffering. among the laudable goals are the prohibition of forced marriage, female genital mutilation and forced sterilization in the signatory countries. the joint motion for a resolution recommends that the council and the commission ratify the convention and allocate sufficient financial resources to combat this violence effectively. we consider that the european union has no diplomatic legitimacy to ratify such a convention. this is a further attack on the sovereignty of the member states. the european union must first ensure that women have their first right: the right to security. the development of fundamentalism in europe and the current migration flood, reinforced by the mechanism of compulsory distribution of migrants, directly threaten the freedom and physical integrity of women. this is evidenced by the explosion in the number of sexual assaults, particularly in cologne and sweden. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ i have spoken in favour of the european union's accession to the istanbul convention. accession to this convention will ensure a coherent european legal framework to prevent and combat violence against women and gender-based violence and to protect victims of such violence. the aim is not only to combat such violence but also to provide the means to prevent it, in particular through the implementation of relevant union legislation, programmes and funds for monitoring. the convention will help to improve the collection of data on violence against women and gender-based violence at union level. accession strengthens the union's responsibility at international level and exerts political pressure on the member states to ratify this instrument.
