in writing. i voted in favour of this report which presents a complete and balanced picture of the situation of fundamental rights in the european union in 2015. the european union is built on a foundation of common values which we must defend. as rapporteur for my political group on the state of prisons in europe, i felt it was particularly important to denounce the inhumane and degrading conditions of detention in some member states where prisons are all too often overcrowded and in an explosive situation. it was also essential to stress in this report the need for better cooperation and exchange of information between member states in the face of radicalisation and terrorism for a genuine security union, of course in full respect of fundamental rights and freedoms. i also support the proposal that member states should have a simple procedure for citizens to report hateful content online.
in writing. the european union ensures respect for the principles inherent in democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights, both within the union and at international level. these values are enshrined in the treaty and the eu charter of fundamental rights. however, violations of these rights occurred in europe in 2015, primarily against migrants and refugees. they must be able to be received in dignified conditions and enjoy the rights they enjoy under international conventions. it is essential that the union and its member states contribute to the promotion of european values of solidarity and integration. this is the very meaning of the european pact on fundamental rights which the european parliament called for last october. the commission must be able to take more systematic action against a member state which does not respect our european values.

in writing. ‒ one of the strengths of the european economy is its capacity to create and innovate. the cultural and creative industries sector contributes 39% to the union's gdp. it employs more people than the automotive sector and is highly competitive internationally. in order for this sector to continue to develop, it is essential that it receives adequate political and financial support. however, compared to other european industries, it has relatively few financial support instruments at its disposal. to remedy this imbalance, two approaches should be advocated. on the one hand, the establishment of a genuine industrial policy framework to support culture in the long term. on the other hand, national policies that work in support of this european framework. our legislation must also provide answers to the problems raised by the digital revolution. for example, copyright must be modernised to protect creators and empower hosts and intermediaries, and thus enable everyone to enjoy the cultural offer in a fair and sustainable way. finally, it should be remembered that preserving the vitality of european culture is essential to the intellectual dynamism of our societies and helps to define our identity.

in writing. ‒ the union's eastern partnership policy is directed at six post-soviet states: armenia, azerbaijan, belarus, georgia, moldova and ukraine. this report constitutes a clear attack on the european union in the institutional, political, economic and social systems of the countries concerned. the text does, however, denounce all forms of violence against women, including trafficking in human beings for sexual exploitation and all forms of violence against women. but this report sets out a typology of women to be defended in priority, especially those from ethnic minorities or those from the lgbti group. it also called for the countries concerned to introduce a policy of positive discrimination in favour of women through a quota system and to promote family reunification. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report focuses on the role of women in the stabilisation of the european neighbourhood policy. in particular, the report assesses the situation of women in several areas of crucial importance such as women's participation in decision-making processes, women's economic participation, violence against women, and the role of women in the peaceful settlement of conflicts. i think that this report is balanced and i have voted in favour of it.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on women's rights in the eastern partnership states. the eastern partnership, launched in 2009, is a joint initiative between the union, its member states and armenia, azerbaijan, belarus, georgia, the republic of moldova and ukraine. gender equality is one of the strategic priorities of the european neighbourhood policy for the period 2014-2020. calls in particular on the partner countries of eastern europe and the south caucasus to ratify the istanbul convention on preventing and combating violence against women and to put in place national strategies. finally, efforts must be made to involve women more in the peaceful resolution of conflicts and in decision-making processes.
in writing. ‒ the eastern partnership aims to strengthen political association and economic integration between the union and six central european countries: armenia, azerbaijan, belarus, georgia, moldova and ukraine. this cooperation implies the sharing of fundamental values such as democracy, the rule of law and human rights, but also gender equality. the legal systems of the partner countries enshrine women's rights, but unfortunately practices remain discriminatory. women are underrepresented in the political sphere, with only 14% of ministers and 16% of parliamentarians, and in the economic sphere, the pay gap ranges from 24 to 50% depending on the country. over the past five years, €103 million has been allocated to 121 projects and programmes promoting gender equality in the european neighbourhood, including €5 million for the 'women in business' programme in the eastern partnership countries. the union must continue to promote gender equality with its partners. this includes, for example, technical assistance and the sharing of good practice in the field of governance and public administration reform.

in writing. ‒ for the past three years, the uzbek authorities have been working in cooperation with the international labour organisation (ilo) to end forced and child labour in the country. significant progress has been made. the most significant is child labour, which according to the latest ilo reports has now been virtually eradicated. it is in the light of this progress and the uzbek authorities' awareness of the importance of respecting international labour standards and human rights and the implementation of a strategy to this end that the european parliament has given its backing to the inclusion of textiles in the areas of trade cooperation covered by the partnership and cooperation agreement between the european union and the republic of uzbekistan. it remains essential to monitor developments with the utmost vigilance. it should be noted that cases of forced labour are still observed in uzbekistan. we therefore expect the authorities to continue to step up their efforts to put an end to it. thus, any deterioration in the situation of human rights and labour law will necessarily lead to an immediate suspension of the preferences granted under these agreements.
in writing. - i abstained on this text. the resolution was adopted by a large majority with a view to adopting a non-legislative resolution on the eu-uzbekistan textile protocol. the aim is to call for traceability efforts in the clothing sector. the text also calls on uzbekistan to: - put an end to forced labour and child labour; - respect fundamental rights and democratic principles; - give ngos more freedom of action. these requirements, which are indeed fundamental rights, are interference in the internal affairs of a sovereign state. the text, however, calls for the ratification of the agreement on trade in textiles.
in writing. ‒ abstention: we vote against free trade agreements, including textiles, but this agreement will have very little impact on france and allows this poor and landlocked country to find outlets for its cotton.
in writing. ‒ welcoming uzbekistan's continued efforts to improve the situation of forced child labour, the european union is once again interfering in the internal politics of a third country by promoting economic modernisation, gender equality and labour inspection in line with imported ilo standards. the defence of rights and freedoms is certainly commendable but must not be accompanied by too deep intrusion into the affairs of a country. i chose to abstain.
in writing. ‒ the current restrictions on uzbek cotton are justified by the practice of forced labour for the cotton harvest. during the harvest season, local people and even children are requisitioned, as well as people hired by the local authorities to harvest cotton and thus reach production quotas. the current authorities are trying to change this assessment, but not necessarily the practices. it is true that an ilo evaluation mission was authorised, as were some local ngos. the latter conclude that there has been an improvement, particularly in the government's speech announcing measures against these practices. but in reality, we are still very far away: the monitoring missions were remote-guided by the uzbek authorities and there are still serious doubts about the independence of the local ngos. other ngos have also provided us with conflicting information on forced labour. in the end, there is still a long way to go and better access to the european market will strengthen a very large-scale industrial cotton crop in uzbekistan, which is already responsible for the drying up of the aral sea. that is why i opposed this agreement.

in writing. ‒ in 2011, the commission proposed to extend the eu-uzbekistan partnership and cooperation agreement to textile trade. the inclusion of the textile protocol in this partnership agreement - which is largely symbolic in view of the volumes involved - does not represent a major economic issue for the european union. at the time, however, the european parliament had (rightly) decided to make its consent conditional on a clear improvement in the human rights and labour law situation in uzbekistan. at that time, child labour in the cotton fields was common, as was forced labour. the uzbek government has since partnered with the international labour organisation (ilo), allowing it to send several observation missions to the field. five years later, according to the ilo, the situation has improved: child labour has almost disappeared and forced labour has declined markedly. that is why my colleague, marie arena, supported by my political group, has proposed that the conclusion of the textile protocol should finally be given the go-ahead, while reserving the right to ask for its suspension if the situation of fundamental rights were to deteriorate. i voted yes.

in writing. ‒ unlike the various eu-africa partnership agreements, which i have consistently opposed, the protocol of accession of ecuador to the colombia-peru agreement is a pro-development agreement. it is decidedly asymmetrical - after 17 years, the ecuadorian market will be 60% open, compared with 95% for the european market - and takes into account the needs of ecuador. it should help to support the social efforts of the correa government, and translate into a gdp increase of 0.5% on the ecuadorian side. at the same time, the agreement will allow european industries and producers to gain a foothold in the ecuadorian market: access to public procurement is extended, customs duties in the automotive sector are significantly reduced, and some 100 european protected designations of origin are recognised. however, by dismantling the high tariff (the entry price for ecuadorian bananas on the european market will be set at eur 75/tonne), the agreement could put the caribbean banana sector at risk, whose good health is decisive for the prosperity of these territories. while it is true that the stabilisation mechanism specifically for bananas will be strengthened in the near future, there are doubts about its applicability. so i refrained.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this text, which represents the ratification by the european parliament of the trade agreement between the european union and its member states, on the one hand, and colombia and peru, on the other, to take account of the accession of ecuador. the agreement will remove customs duties on many products and once the agreement is fully implemented, it is estimated that eu exporters will save at least €106 million a year in customs duties. it should also be noted that some 100 eu geographical indications will be protected on the ecuadorian market. nevertheless, we were concerned about the impact of this agreement on our european banana producers, given that ecuador is the world's leading producer of bananas. we have thus ensured, through the trialogue held the day before the ratification of the agreement, that it will be accompanied by a safeguard clause and a stabilisation mechanism for bananas. these arrangements will enable us to obtain better information and support our producers in the event of market disturbances.
in writing. ‒ unlike many trade agreements, this protocol of accession for ecuador takes into account the country's specific development needs. it is estimated that the ecuadorian market will be 60% open at 17 years, compared with 95% for the european market. this is an important step forward in the european union's design of its trade policy: to ensure fair trade that does not destroy the partner's economy. but this progress must not come at the expense of fragile european production. by further dismantling the tariff regime for banana trade, the agreement risks destabilising the economy of the eu's outermost regions (such as the french dom). i am particularly keen to defend the economy of these territories, which are subject to unique social, environmental and regional factors. we must be vigilant about the impact of trade agreements on these territories. however, the safeguard clause to protect banana production from falling prices, provided for in this type of agreement, is not automatic and far too long to implement. i therefore decided to vote against this text.
in writing. ‒ ecuador will no longer benefit from the gsp+ system as from 31 december 2016. in order not to lose the benefit of this tariff preference, ecuador had to resume negotiations on the free trade agreement which the eu had already adopted with other countries of the andean community of nations, putting them in competition while claiming the opposite. ecuador had good reason to leave the negotiating table in 2010. the country's ambition was to move from an economy based on exporting raw materials to a high value-added economy based on innovation and renewable energy. the country also had to maintain considerable fiscal flexibility, as it had no currency of its own. blackmail and pressure, coupled with a significant drop in oil prices, have overcome ecuador's resistance. i am opposed to free trade agreements on principle, and i have serious doubts about the long-term benefits that ecuadorians will derive from them. for these reasons i have chosen to abstain as i have had the opportunity to do in similar situations.
in writing. ‒ on 19 december 1966, denmark, norway and sweden signed an agreement on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat up to four nautical miles from their respective baselines. this agreement coexisted with the 1980 eu-norway fisheries agreement. following developments in fisheries law (the 1982 united nations convention on the law of the sea and the 1995 united nations fish stocks agreement), norway denounced the agreement on 29 july 2009. norway and the eu signed a new agreement in 2015 on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat. the new agreement is adapted to changes in international law and ensures that the two member states concerned and norway maintain reciprocal access to the respective waters of the other parties in the skagerrak area, while ensuring the implementation of conservation and fisheries management measures in that area. it also allows for the adoption of control measures in accordance with the principles of the normal jurisdiction of the coastal state. so i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ in december 1966, denmark, norway and sweden signed an agreement allowing reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat up to four nautical miles from their baselines. this was necessary in view of the convergence of national laws and for practical reasons. following the accession of denmark and sweden to the european union in 1973 and 1995, the commission took over the management of the agreement on behalf of the two member states. the new agreement in question is designed to take account of changes in international law and to guarantee reciprocal access for the two member states concerned and norway to the respective waters of the other parties. the new agreement will also help to protect fishery resources in the area. that is why i voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement between the union and norway on reciprocal access for vessels flying the flags of denmark, norway and sweden to fishing activities in the skagerrak. in view of developments in international fisheries law, the 1966 agreement between denmark, norway and sweden, supplemented in 1980 by an eu-norway agreement, has been brought into line with the united nations conventions on the law of the sea. a new agreement was therefore signed on 15 january 2015. the new agreement maintains the exclusive access enjoyed by the vessels of denmark, norway and sweden to their respective waters beyond four nautical miles from the baselines. it ensures that the two member states concerned and norway maintain reciprocal access to the other parties' respective waters in the skagerrak and kattegat area, while ensuring the implementation of fisheries conservation and management measures in that area.
in writing. ‒ this non-legislative report concerns reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak, a strait between southern norway, south-eastern sweden and north-western denmark. norway, a non-eu country, has entered into formal negotiations with the european commission to secure reciprocal access to this highly prized fishing area, which is also exploited by eu members sweden and denmark. the agreement includes provisions for the sustainable management of fisheries in this area and control measures in line with the principles of coastal state jurisdiction. considering that this agreement ensures the rational exploitation and sustainable management of fish stocks in this international fishing area and that it will provide new opportunities for european fishermen, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the agreement between the european union and norway on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak. on 19 december 1966, denmark, norway and sweden signed an agreement on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat up to four nautical miles from their respective baselines. following developments in fisheries law, in particular after the adoption of the 1982 united nations convention on the law of the sea and the 1995 united nations fish stocks agreement, norway denounced the latter on 29 july 2009. it therefore expired on 7 august 2012. the new agreement is adapted to changes in international law and ensures that the two member states concerned and norway maintain reciprocal access to the respective waters of the other parties in the skagerrak area, while ensuring the implementation of conservation and fisheries management measures in that area. it also allows for the adoption of control measures in accordance with the principles of the normal jurisdiction of the coastal state.
in writing. - i voted for this text. this report concerns the approval of the agreement between norway and the european union on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat. the agreement signed by the european commission and norway is an update of the fisheries agreements previously existing between norway and the european community and between norway and other scandinavian countries. the new agreement is adapted to changes in international law and guarantees the maintenance of reciprocal access to waters in the skagerrak and kattegat area for sweden, denmark and norway. it also ensures the implementation of fisheries conservation and management measures in this area.
in writing. ‒ this resolution endorses the agreement between the european union and the kingdom of norway on reciprocal access for vessels flying the flags of denmark, norway and sweden to fishing activities in the skagerrak. it stresses in particular the better integration of the objectives of sustainable fisheries management with the introduction of the landing obligation and the maintenance of stocks above levels that allow maximum sustainable yield to be achieved. i am voting for this text.
in writing. ‒ on 19 december 1966, denmark, norway and sweden signed an agreement on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat. the 35-year agreement was extended for two five-year periods until 2012 and could be terminated by either party on three-year notice before the expiry of either of the two five-year periods. following the denunciation of the agreement by norway, a new agreement was signed on 15 january 2015 with the european union. the agreement, adapted to changes in international law, guarantees the maintenance of reciprocal access by the two member states concerned and norway to the respective waters of the other parties in the skagerrak area, while ensuring conservation and fisheries management measures in that area and also allows for the adoption of control measures in accordance with the principles of normal coastal state jurisdiction. i therefore voted in favour of this agreement.

in writing. ‒ an agreement signed in 1966 between denmark, norway and sweden on reciprocal access to fishing activities in the skagerrak and kattegat entered into force on 7 august 1967. with the accession of denmark and sweden to the european union in 1973 and 1995 respectively, the commission took over the management of the agreement on behalf of these two member states. in the light of more recent developments in international fisheries law, norway considered that the existing agreement was no longer in line with the provisions of the law of the sea and with modern conservation and management principles. a new agreement was proposed in 2014: it guarantees the maintenance of reciprocal access of the two member states concerned and norway to the respective waters of the other parties in the skagerrak and kattegat, while ensuring the implementation of conservation measures and sound fisheries management in this area. the approval of the european parliament is required for the conclusion of this agreement. i vote for it.

in writing. ‒ the treaty of paris was signed on 18 april 1951 and established the european coal and steel community (ecsc). it entered into force on 23 july 1952 and was to last for 50 years, expiring on 23 july 2002. the remaining assets of the former ecsc were then transferred to a new research fund for coal and steel (frca) which provides approximately €50 million in research and development funding each year for the coal (27.2%) and steel (72.8%) sectors. while the european steel industry is in a particularly critical situation, the european commission's text considers that 'the frca has achieved its objective of supporting competitiveness'. under the pretext of 'facilitating access to funding for beneficiaries' (simplification, transparency, harmonisation), the text is of course aimed above all at giving the ec full powers so that it can finally 'manage the frca programme alone'. for this reason i voted against the commission proposal and abstained on parliament's motion for a resolution.

in writing. ‒ visa liberalisation is an important aspect of the union's foreign policy. it is therefore essential to update this policy to adapt it to the new challenges facing the european union today. this is especially true as discussions on visa liberalisation are currently underway, in particular with ukraine, georgia, kosovo and turkey. for these reasons, a revision of the suspension mechanism was necessary in order to make it more flexible. the commission will now be able to re-introduce the visa requirement for third-country nationals in a number of cases: in the event of a sudden and substantial increase in irregular immigration, unfounded asylum applications, rejection of too many readmission applications or in the event of a threat to security in the territory of the union. i voted in favour of the revision of the readmission mechanism.
in writing. ‒ this legislative report concerns the reintroduction of a visa requirement by member states for third-country nationals who are hitherto exempt from a visa requirement. this measure applies to nationals of georgia and ukraine and responds to the exceptional situation faced by the member states, namely the substantial increase in irregular immigration and security risks. this suspension could apply in the event of a significant increase in the number of georgian or ukrainian nationals refused entry to, or staying illegally on, the territory of the union. this flexibility instrument should enable member states to better manage migration flows and to strengthen security on european territory, while ensuring respect for human rights; i therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. i supported the revision of the suspension mechanism under the regulation allowing visa liberalisation with third countries. the mechanism had not been activated since 2013 due to the rigidity of the criteria and the complexity of the procedure. by reintroducing a more flexible visa waiver suspension mechanism, the european union has finally abandoned its policy of unconditional liberalisation. it will now have the necessary tool to be able to effectively temporarily reinstate the visa requirement for third-country nationals in the event of sudden spikes in irregular immigration, unfounded asylum applications, a lack of cooperation with the european union on readmissions or in the event of a threat to public policy or internal security related to the third-country nationals concerned. while the current discussions on further visa liberalisation, notably with turkey, but also with georgia, kosovo and ukraine, raise many concerns in view of the migration and security challenges, we had to ensure that the mechanism was working properly.

in writing. ‒ we vote in favour of this resolution, which calls for more phytosanitary controls on citrus fruit imports to avoid the import of organisms harmful to our plantations. imported fruit should meet the following conditions: registration of the production area, packaging facilities, exporters and any other operators involved in the handling of the specified fruit, the presence of documents issued under the supervision of the national plant protection organisation during transport and, for certain fruits, the use of pre- and post-harvest treatments. these controls, which will help to avoid contamination of our citrus production, are also a means of protecting it against increasingly aggressive competition from many third countries.
in writing. ‒ i am voting for this proposal, which is also a way of protecting our citrus growers from the import of cheaper products from third countries.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objection to the european commission implementing directive amending annexes i to v to council directive 2000/29/ec on plant health protection measures in the union. the text calls on the commission to refrain from relaxing the requirements for the import of fruit intended for industrial processing into juice, to tighten its requirements for the import of fruit originating in countries where phyllosticta citricarpa is present, or to take measures to prevent the introduction of the insect thaumatotibia leucotreta.
in writing. ‒ the measures envisaged in the commission's draft directive on plant protection do not sufficiently prevent the risks of importing exotic pests. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution which proposes to amend this directive. we call for better protection of citrus growers against pests by increasing the requirements for importing fruit for processing, especially when it comes from countries where exotic pests are present. sample controls should be strengthened and contaminated fruit should be treated before import into the union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection, considering that the measures envisaged to combat the introduction of plant pests are not sufficiently stringent to protect eu producers. we cannot accept that the european commission does not act by proposing simplified and lighter measures. we must maintain the requirements for imports from third countries, regardless of the destination of the product.
in writing. ‒ the resolution proposed here aims to increase controls on the introduction into the european union of fruit, in this case citrus fruit, originating in third countries. this resolution calls for citrus fruit from third countries to be accompanied by a phytosanitary certificate proving that the fruit originates from a production field which has been subjected, at the appropriate time, to treatments against various diseases affecting citrus fruit in particular. this proposal calls for increased controls on these fruits which could contaminate european production. i choose to support this objection because it is a way of protecting our citrus growers from the importation of cheaper products from third countries.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal because i also believe that parliament should be involved from the outset in the negotiation of international aviation agreements. it is therefore necessary for the commission to provide parliament with information on the launch of certain negotiations and with the information necessary for the analysis of these agreements.
in writing. ‒ this oral question from the committee on transport, which calls for more transparency in the negotiations vis-à-vis parliament, is certainly in the right direction, but it is far from covering the whole subject. the transfer of sovereignty from the member states to the european union in the negotiation of traffic rights ipso facto leads to a reversal of the balance of power with third countries: they gain access to the whole of the vast european market, while they can only concede a few things in exchange, most of which have already been conceded. this type of negotiation therefore considerably weakens the position of european airlines in relation to those of third countries. i therefore vote against this oral question. on the contrary, i am voting for the resolution by the efdd and the enl.
in writing. for an international aviation agreement to enter into force, it must be approved by the european parliament. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy. as several negotiations are about to begin on international aviation agreements, in particular with china, japan and mexico, i voted in favour of this resolution to remind the commission of the role of the european parliament in approving such agreements and to ensure effective negotiations.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the tran committee's motion for a resolution. in december 2015, the commission presented an aviation strategy for europe, involving, inter alia: - the opening of safety agreements with japan and china; - the opening of air services agreements with china, turkey, mexico, the six member states of the gulf cooperation council, armenia and the association of southeast asian nations. the aim of these agreements is to replace existing bilateral agreements with a single european agreement, enabling european carriers to compete with emerging countries, particularly those in the gulf. however, the commission is still unclear as to the conditions for these negotiations. in addition, the precedents in this area have not been favourable to the european union, notably with regard to the united states (2007) as regards reciprocity (acquisition of voting shares in american companies of up to 25%, compared to 49.9% in europe, prohibition of cabotage, etc.). the enf group, on the other hand, called for more transparency in these negotiations.
in writing. ‒ vote for the efdd and enl motions for resolutions which not only require the commission to be fully transparent but also to guarantee fair and equitable competition between air carriers through specific legal clauses.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution. it will encourage the adoption of our standards in the aviation sector in order to ensure the safety of european passengers as much as possible and to establish fair competition with third countries. this resolution rightly provides for technical and scientific collaboration between the eu and the other parties in reducing greenhouse gas emissions from aircraft, which are increasingly contributing to global warming.
in writing. ‒ in a context of tough competition between our aviation and the airlines and hubs of the gulf and turkey, it is essential to assess the stakes of this agreement and to ensure its reciprocal application by the other parties. the commission is not clear on the non-negotiable points that guarantee fair and just competition, and i think it is essential to be firm in addressing the substantive issues inherent in these 'open skies' agreements with the commission, rather than simply calling for transparency on its part with parliament. i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which calls on the commission to involve the european parliament fully and to inform it fully of any international agreement on aviation. it is important that our institution, which represents the peoples, be kept informed in real time of all the information relating to the negotiations in this major area. this is important to remember, as the commission has proposed in its aviation strategy for europe to open, for example, negotiations on civil aviation safety with japan and china or air services agreements at union level with turkey, china, etc.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because it merely asks the commission to be transparent with parliament without ever addressing the substantive problems raised by the 'open skies' agreements (reciprocity, investments, rules for controlling airlines, working conditions, traffic rights, clauses guaranteeing fair and just competition, etc.).
in writing. - i voted against this text. the resolution, which was put to the vote by the committee on transport and tourism, aims to increase the level of transparency of the european commission's actions in the field of international aviation agreements. we support this principle but we cannot accept that the rapporteurs should limit themselves to this request. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the airlines are able to operate in the gulf. we have proposed an alternative resolution, which we consider to be insufficient. the motion for a resolution tabled by our group in parliament stressed the need to ensure fair and fair competition between air carriers by means of specific legal clauses. it was unfortunately rejected by parliament.
in writing. ‒ this is a motion for a resolution from the tran committee on international aviation agreements with, inter alia, the association of southeast asian nations, turkey, qatar, the united arab emirates and armenia. the resolution simply seeks clarification of the objectives and issues of the negotiations which have begun, since, as with ceta, tafta and tisa, the commission is very discreet on this subject. i therefore voted against the first tran resolution, since it simply asks for clarification. i voted for the efdd and enl resolution which, in addition to calling for more transparency from the commission, also calls for the guarantee of fair and equitable competition in the air transport sector through specific legal clauses.
in writing. ‒ since december 2015, the commission has been undertaking to amend the rules on international air agreements. despite the fact that the chicago convention has enshrined the sovereignty of states over their airspace, the commission is trying to obtain new negotiating mandates to simplify line openings and develop air links by replacing existing bilateral treaties with a single european agreement. the oral question put to the vote was therefore intended to remind the commission of the serious problems facing european airlines in maintaining their shares in the long-haul market, particularly as a result of unfair competition from the gulf countries. parliament also criticised the total opacity of the negotiations between the commission and the countries with which new agreements were to be signed, such as ceta, tisa and tafta. however, this oral question has been emptied of its content by the epp and ecr, and only asks for more transparency from the european commission. we shall therefore vote against.
in writing. ‒ the oral question was welcome in view of the crucial issues at stake in these negotiations for the future of european aviation, particularly french aviation. as a reminder, as early as the early 2000s, air france had alerted the european and national authorities to the threat of unfair competition from gulf carriers. it is essential to send a clear and very strong political message to the commission to ensure that it adopts a transparent approach towards the european parliament and the national authorities. it is right to deplore him, given his philosophy on competition and his disastrous record on deregulation. i therefore vote against the tran motion for a resolution which merely calls for the commission to be transparent with parliament and i vote for the efdd and enl motions for resolutions which not only call for full transparency from the commission but also call for the commission to guarantee fair and fair competition between air carriers through specific legal clauses.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on international aviation agreements. the text reminds the european commission that it must involve the european parliament from the outset of the procedure for negotiating aviation agreements with third countries so that meps can freely decide whether or not to give their consent.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it recalls that parliament must be kept fully informed of all the progress of the negotiations on aviation agreements. i say this as rapporteur for parliament on the agreement currently being negotiated on aviation safety between the european union and japan. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's aviation strategy and will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's aviation strategy. when the agreements are concluded, we will have the final say in whether or not to approve the final agreement. we must therefore know now where the negotiations are going so that we can redirect the discussions if necessary.
on behalf of the enf group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the customs code is an outdated document before it is even fully implemented. it is based on ideological, free trade and globalist foundations, which have been promoted since davos and the wto. this ideology has been rejected by many peoples and by the citizens of the world's leading economy, the united states. with donald trump, trade is for national development and protection of industry. customs duties are necessary to balance trade in the spirit of the havana charter for peace in trade. your customs code of the union starts from a presupposition: the general abolition of these duties to facilitate trade. so we need to keep reducing the control rate. in the age of protectionism and tariff rearmament, the european union is still a step behind. in addition to the commission's new contribution to the liquidation of our monarchical states, by giving importers greater freedom to clear customs wherever they wish, particularly with centralised clearance, you are encouraging them to shop among the customs administrations for the most lax and least-discriminatory. you are also weakening our states and making them insecure. your technological instruments - ecs, ics - which claim to put customs fraud into the digital equation will never replace the instinct, experience and knowledge of the customs field: the investigation, the chain of custody, systematic protection. by accelerating the destruction of our customs protections, you continue to hand over our economies to unfair competition, to the social dumping that our fellow citizens are already suffering, you also hand over our societies to criminal organizations, to whom you guarantee a perpetual income by your inefficiency. then we have the christmas hope, eternity in the face of the temporal bankruptcy of a world that needs saving. merry christmas to you!
